cantonese: 终须有日龙穿凤，唔通日日裤穿窿
jyutping: zung1 seoi1 jau5 jat6 lung4 cyun1 fung6, m4 tung1 jat6 jat6 fu3 cyun1 lung4
mandarin_meaning: 总有一天（会发生某件事/一次极端经历），又不是每天都会发生（比喻不可能天天重演）
english_meaning: There will be a time when it happens, but it won't happen every day — used jokingly to say something inevitable won't recur daily.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语带有幽默或讽刺意味，表示某件事终有发生的那一天，但不应期望它每天都发生。句中有轻微的下流/玩笑成分，用以强调不可能天天重演。
explanation_english: A humorous/ironic colloquial saying meaning that something will happen eventually, but you shouldn't expect it to happen every day. It often carries a playful or mildly risque undertone and emphasizes that an extreme event won't recur daily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔使太心急，终须有日龙穿凤，唔通日日裤穿窿？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 sai2 taai3 sam1 gap1, zung1 seoi1 jau5 jat6 lung4 cyun1 fung6, m4 tung1 jat6 jat6 fu3 cyun1 lung4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不用太着急，总有一天会发生，又不是每天都裤子破洞吧？
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so impatient — it'll happen eventually; it's not like your trousers will have holes every day, is it?

jyutping: ging1 jat1 si6 coeng4 jat1 zi3
mandarin_meaning: 經一件事就能增長智慧／從經驗中獲得教訓
english_meaning: To become wiser from experience; to learn a lesson from going through something
explanation_mandarin: 指經歷過一件事之後會獲得經驗或教訓，從而增長智慧，以後處理類似事情會更好。
explanation_english: An expression meaning that people gain wisdom or learn lessons through experience; every time you go through something you become a bit wiser.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好灰心，經一事長一智，下次會做得更好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 fui1 sam1, ging1 jat1 si6 coeng4 jat1 zi3, haa6 ci3 wui5 zou6 dak1 gang3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別灰心，經一事長一智，下次會做得更好。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be discouraged; you learn from experience, and you'll do better next time.

jyutping: lok3 zyu6 si2 kut3 diu3 geng2
mandarin_meaning: 陷入無法脫身的麻煩或困境（粗俗說法）
english_meaning: To get oneself into a nasty, inescapable mess or trouble (vulgar slang).
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話俚語，字面意思是「被卡在糞坑裡要上吊」，比喻把自己弄得很麻煩或陷入無法脫身的困境或窘境，帶有強烈的口語與粗俗語氣。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang expression. Literally 'caught in a shit pit and hanging oneself', it figuratively means to have gotten oneself into a serious, inescapable mess or predicament. It is coarse and used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日咁做，遲早會絡住屎窟吊颈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 gam2 zou6, ci4 zou2 wui5 lok3 zyu6 si2 kut3 diu3 geng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是這樣做，遲早會把自己弄得很麻煩、無法脫身（粗俗說法）。
examples.english_sentence: If you keep doing that, you'll sooner or later get yourself into a messy, inescapable situation (vulgar slang).

mandarin_meaning: 缩在一起；挤在一起；缩成一团
english_meaning: to huddle together; to bunch up; to curl up into a lump
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語或俚語，指人或動物靠得很近或收縮成一團，常用於形容因寒冷、害怕或空間擠迫而聚攏在一起的狀態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to huddle or bunch together (literally “shrink together into one lump”). Often used to describe people or animals clustering close for warmth, out of fear, or because of limited space.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天氣咁凍，大家縮埋一嚿取暖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 hei3 gam2 dung3, daai6 gaa1 suk1 maai4 jat1 gau3 ceoi2 nyun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天气这么冷，大家缩在一起取暖。
examples.english_sentence: It's so cold; everyone is huddling together to keep warm.

mandarin_meaning: 小气；吝啬；抠门
english_meaning: to be stingy; to be tight-fisted; to skimp
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語的口語說法，指在人情或金錢上吝嗇、抠门、不愿意多给或多帮忙，常用于抱怨某人小气。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to be stingy or miserly — to withhold money or generosity, often used to complain that someone is tight-fisted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢借人錢成日縮埋一字角，唔肯借多啲幫襯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ze3 jan4 cin2 sing4 jat6 suk1 maai4 jat1 zi6 gok3, m4 hang2 ze3 do1 di1 bong1 can3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他借钱给别人总是很抠门，不肯多借一点帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: When he lends money he's always stingy and won't lend a bit more to help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 食飯AA，佢又縮埋一字角，只肯出一半錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sik6 faan6 AA, keoi5 jau6 suk1 maai4 jat1 zi6 gok3, zi2 hang2 ceot1 jat1 bun3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 吃饭AA制，他又抠门，只肯出一半的钱。
examples.english_sentence: We split the bill, and he was stingy again — only willing to pay half.

cantonese: 缸瓦船打老虎，尽地一煲
jyutping: gong1 ngaa5 syun4 daa2 lou5 fu2 zeon6 dei6 jat1 bou1
mandarin_meaning: 把不同的人或事物全部混在一起、不加區別地一概而論
english_meaning: To lump everything or everyone together indiscriminately; to mix different things/people in one pot without distinction
explanation_mandarin: 形容把不同的人、情況或事物不加分別地混爲一談或一併處理，帶有批評概念。
explanation_english: Describes treating different people, situations, or things as the same—lumping them together or handling them all in one way—often with a critical connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁樣講，唔好將人哋缸瓦船打老虎，尽地一煲咁講晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 joeng6 gong2, m4 hou2 zoeng1 jan4 dei6 gong1 ngaa5 syun4 daa2 lou5 fu2 zeon6 dei6 jat1 bou1 gam2 gong2 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要這樣說，不要把別人一概而論。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say that; don't lump people together indiscriminately.

mandarin_meaning: 漏洞；疏漏
english_meaning: loophole; omission; oversight; flaw (also to have a slip-up or leak)
explanation_mandarin: 「罅漏」在廣東話裡常用來指事務上的漏洞、疏忽或破綻，也可指資訊或液體的滲漏；在口語中也可用作指出別人做事有失誤或疏漏。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "罅漏" commonly refers to a loophole, omission, oversight, or flaw (and can also mean a literal leak). Colloquially it is used to point out mistakes or lapses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢有啲罅漏，成日錯漏百出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 jau5 di1 haa6 lau6, sing4 jat6 co3 lau6 baak3 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事有些疏漏，經常錯漏百出。
examples.english_sentence: He's sloppy at work and often makes many mistakes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份合約有罅漏，律師話要修訂先可簽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 hap6 joek3 jau5 haa6 lau6, leot6 si1 waa6 jiu3 sau1 ding6 sin1 ho2 cim1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份合約有漏洞，律師說要先修訂才能簽署。
examples.english_sentence: This contract has loopholes; the lawyer said it needs revision before signing.

mandarin_meaning: 模仿金屬撞擊或敲擊發出的鏗鏘聲（擬聲詞）
english_meaning: An onomatopoeic word imitating a metallic clanging or clanking sound (e.g., clang, clank)
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示金屬碰撞、敲擊等發出的鏗鏘聲，可重疊使用如「鐺鐺／罉罉」，常見於描述門鉸、鍋蓋、金屬器物等發聲。
explanation_english: Used to represent the metallic clanging or clanking sound produced by collisions or strikes. Often reduplicated (e.g., "dong-dong") and used to describe noises from hinges, lids, metal objects, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一拉開大門，門鉸就鐺一聲，好響。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 laai1 hoi1 daai6 mun4, mun4 gaau3 zau6 dong1 jat1 seng1, hou2 hoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一拉开大门，门铰就“当”地一声，很响。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as he pulled the big door open, the hinge went 'clang' — very loud.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚廚房個鍋蓋跌落地，鐺鐺兩聲，把我嚇醒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 cyu4 fong4 go3 wo4 goi3 dit3 lok6 dei6, dong1 dong1 loeng5 seng1, baa2 ngo5 haak3 sing2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上厨房的锅盖掉到地上，‘当当’两声，把我吓醒。
examples.english_sentence: At night the pot lid fell to the floor with a couple of clanging sounds and woke me up.

cantonese: 罗汉请观音，人多好担当
jyutping: lo4 hon3 cing2 gwaan1 jam1, jan4 do1 hou2 daam1 dong1
mandarin_meaning: 人多力量大 / 众人拾柴火焰高（人多好分担、事情容易办成；有时也含有人多可以互相推诿的讽刺意味）
english_meaning: Many hands make light work; with many people it's easier to share the load (can also imply people can shift responsibility among themselves)
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语。字面是“罗汉请观音”，用来表示人多可以分担工作或责任，事情容易办成。根据语境也可带讽刺意味，指多人在场时容易互相推诿或借助众人之力掩饰问题。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb. Literally 'Arhats invite Guanyin', used to say that when many people are present it's easier to share work or responsibility and get things done. Depending on context it can also be used sarcastically to mean people in a crowd can shift blame or hide responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 搬屋嗰日大家一齊幫手，真係羅漢請觀音，人多好擔當。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baan1 uk1 go2 jat6 daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 bong1 sau2, zan1 hai6 lo4 hon3 cing2 gwaan1 jam1, jan4 do1 hou2 daam1 dong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 搬家的那天大家一起帮忙，真是罗汉请观音，人多好担当。
examples.english_sentence: On moving day everyone helped together — truly 'many hands make light work'.

mandarin_meaning: 陷阱；圈套（古字）
english_meaning: trap; snare; net (archaic)
explanation_mandarin: 罧為古字，原指用作捕捉動物或拘捕人的網具、陷阱，亦可引申指圈套或設下的陷阱。
explanation_english: An archaic character referring to a trap or snare (a net or device used to catch animals or to entrap people); it can also be used figuratively to mean a scheme or trap.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人設咗個罧，結果就中招喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 sit3 zo2 go3 waan4, git3gwo2 zau6 zung1 ziu1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人設下陷阱，結果就上當了。
examples.english_sentence: He was set up in a trap and ended up getting caught.

mandarin_meaning: 篮子；编织的簸箕/筐（用于装蔬菜、鱼虾等）
english_meaning: a woven basket (used to hold vegetables, fish, shellfish, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 罶為傳統的編織容器，類似籮或簍，常用以盛放農作物、海產或雜物。
explanation_english: A traditional woven container similar to a basket or hamper, commonly used to hold produce, seafood, or miscellaneous items.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個罶係用嚟裝蔬菜嘅，唔好亂放其他嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 lo4 hai6 jung6 lai4 zong1 so1 coi3 ge3, m4 hou2 lyun6 fong3 kei4 taa1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个篮子是用来装蔬菜的，不要随便放其他东西。
examples.english_sentence: This basket is used to hold vegetables; don't put other things in it carelessly.

mandarin_meaning: 陷阱、圈套
english_meaning: trap; snare; ambush (figurative)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指設下的陷阱或圈套，引申為騙局或會讓人上當的安排。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for a trap or snare; used figuratively for a scheme or setup intended to deceive or catch someone out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話份工好穩定，我覺得有罾門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 fan6 gung1 hou2 wan5 ding6, ngo5 gok3 dak1 jau5 zang1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說那份工作很穩定，我覺得有陷阱。
examples.english_sentence: He says the job is stable; I think there's a trap.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 買二手車要小心，可能有罾門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai5 ji6 sau2 ce1 jiu3 siu2 sam1, ho2 nang4 jau5 zang1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 買二手車要小心，可能有圈套。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful when buying a used car; there might be a scam.

mandarin_meaning: 一种大捕鱼网；比喻为圈套或陷阱
english_meaning: a large seine/net used for fishing; figuratively, a trap or snare
explanation_mandarin: 罾𥯆原指漁民用來圍捕魚蝦的大型網具，也可引申指設下的圈套或陷阱；在廣東話語境中可作實物或比喻用法。
explanation_english: Originally refers to a large fishing seine used by fishermen to encircle and catch fish/shrimp. It can also be used figuratively to mean a trap or snare. In Cantonese it appears both as a concrete noun and in a metaphorical sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋今日出海，用咗條罾𥯆捕到成籮魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 dei6 gam1 jat6 ceot1 hoi2, jung6 zo2 tiu4 zang1 fung1 bou6 dou3 seng4 lo4 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们今天出海，用了条罾𥯆捕到一大篮鱼。
examples.english_sentence: They went out to sea today and used a seine to catch a whole basket of fish.

mandarin_meaning: 臨時用來遮陽或遮雨的棚蓬（字面為傘與帳的結合），屬於方言或舊時用語，現代較少使用。
english_meaning: a temporary canopy/awning or umbrella-shaped tent used for shade or shelter (literally 'umbrella-curtain'); a dialectal or archaic term, now uncommon.
explanation_mandarin: 「羅傘帳」字面由「羅/羅網」、「傘」與「帳」組成，指臨時搭起用以擋風、擋雨或遮陽的棚蓬或帳篷。此詞在廣東話口語或舊時描述中偶有出現，但現代日常用語較少見，常可用「帳篷／遮陽棚／遮雨棚」等代替。
explanation_english: Literally combining characters for net/mesh, umbrella, and curtain/tent, '羅傘帳' denotes a temporary canopy or umbrella-like tent used to block wind, rain, or sun. It appears in some Cantonese dialectal or older usage and is uncommon in contemporary everyday speech; synonyms like 'awning' or 'tent' are typically used instead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊時街市啲小販會搭個羅傘帳擋太陽同落雨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 si4 gaai1 si5 di1 siu2 faan6 wui5 daap3 go3 lo4 saan3 zoeng3 dong3 taai3 joeng4 tung4 lok6 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 過去，街市的小販會搭起羅傘帳擋太陽和雨水。
examples.english_sentence: In the past, market hawkers would set up a '羅傘帳' to shield themselves from the sun and rain.

mandarin_meaning: 小羊；小羊羔（也可作比喻，指單純、天真的人）
english_meaning: lamb; young sheep (also used metaphorically for someone innocent or naive)
explanation_mandarin: 「羊仔」是廣東話用語，主要指年幼的羊（即小羊羔）。在口語中有時也用作暱稱或比喻，形容人單純、天真或溫和。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "羊仔" refers to a young sheep (a lamb). Colloquially it can be used as an affectionate nickname or metaphor to describe someone who is innocent, naive, or gentle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 村入面啲羊仔好可愛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyun1 jap6 min6 di1 joeng4 zai2 hou2 ho2 oi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 村子裡的小羊很可愛。
examples.english_sentence: The lambs in the village are very cute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細個嗰陣好似羊仔咁天真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 hou2 ci5 joeng4 zai2 gam2 tin1 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她小時候像小羊一樣天真。
examples.english_sentence: When he/she was young, he/she was as innocent as a lamb.

mandarin_meaning: 楊桃（星形的熱帶水果）
english_meaning: starfruit (Averrhoa carambola)
explanation_mandarin: 楊桃，一種熱帶水果，切開橫剖面呈星形，味道酸甜，可鮮食或榨汁。『羊桃』多為誤寫或俗寫，正確常用字為『楊桃』。
explanation_english: Starfruit, a tropical fruit whose cross-section is star-shaped when sliced. It has a sweet-tart flavor and is eaten fresh or made into juice. '羊桃' is often a nonstandard or mistaken spelling; the usual character is '楊桃'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗啲羊桃返屋企，準備切開嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 di1 joeng4 tou4 faan1 uk1 kei2, zeon2 bei6 cit3 hoi1 lai4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我買了一些楊桃回家，準備切開來吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some starfruit and brought them home to cut up and eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天飲一杯楊桃汁好清涼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 jam2 jat1 bui1 joeng4 tou4 zap1 hou2 cing1 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天喝一杯楊桃汁很清涼。
examples.english_sentence: A glass of starfruit juice is very refreshing in summer.

mandarin_meaning: 對女性的貶義稱呼（類似「賤女人／婊子」）
english_meaning: Derogatory Cantonese slang for a woman (similar to 'bitch' or 'cheap woman')
explanation_mandarin: 「羊牸」字面是母羊，但在廣東話中是粗鄙的貶義用語，用來罵討厭、粗魯或下流的女性。屬於地域性粗口用語，使用時需注意場合。
explanation_english: Literally 'she-goat', but in Cantonese it is a coarse, derogatory slang term used to insult a woman as unpleasant, rude, or morally loose. It's regional vulgar language and should be used with caution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做羊牸啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 joeng4 zaa1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別當個羊牸（別當個討人厭的女人）。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a bitch.

mandarin_meaning: 迅速用手抓走、奪取（口語）
english_meaning: to snatch; to grab quickly with one's hand (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，指迅速用手把東西抓走或奪取，常見於香港日常會話中，帶有倉促或突兀的動作意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to quickly grab or snatch something with the hand, often implying a sudden or hurried action; commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一見塊餅就翕手拎走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 jat1 gin3 faai3 beng2 zau6 hip6 sau2 ling1 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一看到那塊餅就一下子抓走了。
examples.english_sentence: He snatched the cake as soon as he saw it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路成日翕手走人哋啲玩具。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Sai3 lou6 sing4 jat6 hip6 sau2 zau2 jan4 dei6 di1 waan4 geoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩經常會把別人的玩具搶走。
examples.english_sentence: Kids often snatch other people's toys.

mandarin_meaning: 悶塞、阻滯（常用來形容胸悶、呼吸不順或事務進展緩慢）
english_meaning: stuffy, obstructed, stagnant (often describing chest congestion/difficulty breathing or slow/stalled progress)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某處不通暢或感覺悶塞、滯留。可指身體上的不適（如胸悶、呼吸不順）或比喻事務運行緩慢、被阻礙。
explanation_english: Describes a condition that is blocked, stuffy, or stagnant. Can refer to physical sensations (e.g., chest congestion, difficulty breathing) or be used metaphorically for things that are slow or impeded.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近天氣咁悶熱，我成日覺得胸口好翳滯，呼吸唔太順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 tin1 hei3 gam2 mun6 jit6, ngo5 seng4 jat6 gok3 dak1 hung1 hau2 hou2 ngai3 zai6, fu1 kap1 m4 taai3 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近天气这么闷热，我总觉得胸口很闷滞，呼吸不太顺。
examples.english_sentence: Lately with the humid heat, I often feel my chest is stuffy and my breathing isn't smooth.

mandarin_meaning: 遮蔽；蒙蔽；眼睛的混濁物（如白內障）
english_meaning: to cover/obscure; a film or opacity (especially on the eye, e.g. cataract); obscurity, shade
explanation_mandarin: 古漢語和醫學用字，表示遮蔽、遮蓋或眼睛上形成的混濁。現代可指使視線模糊的障礙（如眼翳＝白內障）。在文言中也用於比喻隱蔽、蒙蔽。
explanation_english: An older literary and medical character meaning to cover or obscure; specifically can mean a film or opacity over the eye (as in cataract). Also used figuratively to mean concealment or obscuration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個眼有翳，要去睇眼科。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 go3 ngaan5 jau5 ji6, jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ngaan5 fo1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他眼睛有翳，需要去看眼科。
examples.english_sentence: He has a film over his eye and needs to see an ophthalmologist.

mandarin_meaning: 悶熱、令人透不過氣
english_meaning: stuffy; oppressively hot and suffocating
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容天氣或室內空間悶熱、不通風，讓人感到呼吸不順或煩悶的狀態。
explanation_english: Used to describe weather or an indoor space that is hot, stuffy, and poorly ventilated, causing discomfort or a feeling of being unable to breathe.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日咁翳焗，企喺街度都覺得透唔到氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 gam2 ai3 guk6, kei5 hai2 gaai1 dou6 dou1 gok3 dak1 tau3 m4 dou2 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天這麼悶熱，站在街上都覺得透不過氣。
examples.english_sentence: It's so hot and stuffy today I feel like I can't get enough air even standing on the street.

mandarin_meaning: 翹班／翹課（曠工、曠課）
english_meaning: to skip work or class; to bunk off; to play truant
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，指無故不去上班或上課，逃避工作或課堂義務，與「翹班」「翹課」類似。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to absent oneself from work or class without permission — similar to 'skip work/class' or 'bunk off.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日又翹釘，唔知去邊度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 jau6 kiu4 ding1, m4 zi1 heoi3 bin1 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天又翹班，不知道去了哪裡。
examples.english_sentence: He skipped work again today; I don't know where he went.

mandarin_meaning: 回去 / 走開（口語、粗魯或命令語氣）；（也可指）翻過去、翻轉過去
english_meaning: to go back / go away (colloquial, often dismissive); also to flip/turn over
explanation_mandarin: 「翻去」在廣東話中常用作口語/俚語，表示叫人回去或走開，語氣可以較為粗魯或強硬。亦可指把物件翻轉過去（如翻頁、翻起來）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "翻去" is a colloquial/slang verb meaning to go back or go away (often dismissive or forceful). It can also mean to flip or turn something over.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你翻去啦，唔好再煩我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 faan1 heoi3 laa1, m4 hou2 zoi3 faan4 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你回去吧，不要再烦我。
examples.english_sentence: Go back / leave, don't bother me again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到狗吠就即刻翻去屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou3 gau2 fai3 zau6 zik1 hak1 faan1 heoi3 uk1 kei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他听到狗叫就立刻回家。
examples.english_sentence: He immediately went back home when he heard the dog barking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你將報紙翻去睇下後面有冇好嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoeng1 bou3 zi2 faan1 heoi3 tai2 haa5 hau6 min6 jau5 mou5 hou2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你把报纸翻过去看看后面有没有好东西。
examples.english_sentence: Flip the newspaper over and see if there's anything good on the back.

jyutping: faan1 zaa1 caa4, mou5 lei4 mei6 dou6
mandarin_meaning: 粗俗、沒品味；低質、廉價的感覺
english_meaning: Tacky or tasteless; lacking refinement or class (literally like re-steeped tea with dregs, implying low quality/cheapness).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人、打扮或事物庸俗、沒有品味、顯得低質廉價。字面意象像是喝回泡、有渣的茶，暗指質素差。
explanation_english: Used to describe a person, dressing, or thing as tacky, tasteless, and low-quality. The literal image—drinking re-steeped tea with dregs—implies cheapness and poor taste.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇佢啲裝扮，真係翻渣茶，冇厘味道。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 keoi5 di1 zong1 baan6, zan1 hai6 faan1 zaa1 caa4, mou5 lei4 mei6 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看他的打扮，真是又俗又沒品味。
examples.english_sentence: Look at the way he dresses—it's really tacky and has no taste.

mandarin_meaning: 翻面；過一會兒、不久（口語）
english_meaning: to flip/turn over; shortly/after a short while (colloquial)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞（字面義）；副詞（口語用法）
explanation_mandarin: 1) 字面義：把物件翻轉、翻面（如煎食物時將其翻面）。2) 口語義：表示短時間之後、不久（相當於「一會兒」「一轉眼」）。
explanation_english: 1) Literal: to flip or turn something over (e.g., turning food to cook the other side). 2) Colloquial: indicates a short time later or shortly afterward (similar to "in a moment").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 煎魚嗰陣要翻頭，唔好煎到一面焦晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zin1 jyu4 go2 zan6 jiu3 faan1 tau4, m4 hou2 zin1 dou3 jat1 min6 ziu1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 煎鱼的时候要把它翻面，别把一面煎糊了。
examples.english_sentence: When frying fish, remember to flip it so one side doesn't burn.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱出門，翻頭佢就打嚟講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aam1 aam1 ceot1 mun4, faan1 tau4 keoi5 zau6 daa2 lei4 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我刚出门，不一会儿他就打电话来有事要说。
examples.english_sentence: I had just left the house, and shortly after he called to say something.

synonyms: 一陣/一會兒 (jat1 zan6 / jat1 wui5) (用於時間義)

mandarin_meaning: 回去 / 返回 / 再
english_meaning: to return; to go back; to do something again
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，「翻/返」常用作動詞，表示回到原處或返回，也可作副詞/動態助詞表示「再、重新」。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "翻/返" is commonly used as a verb meaning to return or go back; it can also function like an aspect/particle meaning "again" or "re-".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要返屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 faan1 uk1 kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我明天要回家。
examples.english_sentence: I have to go home tomorrow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢返公司做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faan1 gung1 si1 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他回公司上班。
examples.english_sentence: He returned to the office to work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可唔可以講返多次？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 faan1 do1 ci3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以再說多一次嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Can you say that again?

cantonese: 老人怕激气，嫩木怕损皮
jyutping: lou5 jan4 paa3 gik1 hei3, non6 muk6 paa3 syun2 pei4
mandarin_meaning: 老人害怕被激怒，嫩木害怕树皮受损。比喻对待年长或年幼（或脆弱者）都要小心、温和。
english_meaning: The elderly fear being provoked; young wood fears its bark being damaged. A proverb advising that both the old and the young (or the vulnerable) should be treated gently and with care.
explanation_mandarin: 用比喻说明年长者和幼小者各有脆弱之处：老人因体质或情绪较易受刺激，嫩木若树皮受损会影响成长。因此提醒人们与老幼或弱势者相处时要小心、温和。
explanation_english: The saying uses a metaphor: elderly people are vulnerable to being provoked, and young wood is vulnerable if its bark is damaged. It reminds people to treat both the elderly and the young (or other vulnerable people) gently and attentively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 照顧小朋友同老人要有耐性，老人怕激氣，嫩木怕損皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ziu3 gu3 siu2 pang4 jau5 tung4 lou5 jan4 jiu3 jau5 noi6 sing3, lou5 jan4 paa3 gik1 hei3, non6 muk6 paa3 syun2 pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 照顾小朋友和老人要有耐心，老人怕被激怒，嫩木怕树皮受损。
examples.english_sentence: Be patient when caring for children and the elderly; the elderly are easily provoked and young wood fears bark damage — meaning we should treat the vulnerable with care.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）年紀較大的人看起來或行為像年輕人；常用來形容經過護理、整容或保養後變得年輕或舉止像年輕人。
english_meaning: A colloquial/slang expression meaning an older person looks or behaves like a youngster; often used jokingly to describe someone who has been rejuvenated (e.g. by treatments) or acts more youthful.
explanation_mandarin: 用於非正式語境，形容年紀較大的人經過保養、整容或改變行為後，看起來或表現得像年輕人。語氣通常帶有驚訝或調侃。
explanation_english: Used in informal contexts to describe an older person who, after treatments or lifestyle changes, looks or behaves like a younger person. The tone is usually surprised or teasing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯整完皮膚療程，真係老人成嫩仔，睇落年輕咗十年。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 zing2 jyun4 pei4 fu1 liu4 cing4, zan1 hai6 lou5 jan4 sing4 nan6 zai2, tai2 lok6 nin4 hing1 zo2 sap6 nin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 伯伯做完皮膚療程後，真的從老人變成嫩仔，看起來年輕了十年。
examples.english_sentence: After the uncle finished the skin treatment, he really went from an old man to a youngster — he looks ten years younger.

mandarin_meaning: 老兄 (lǎo xiōng)：口语中用于称呼男性朋友或熟悉的人，相当于“兄弟”“哥们儿”；也可作感叹用，带有亲切或半开玩笑的语气。
english_meaning: bro; buddy; mate; an informal way to address a male friend or to call someone’s attention; can also be used as an interjection.
explanation_mandarin: 用于以轻松、亲切或略带玩笑的语气称呼男性朋友，也可用作感叹词表示惊讶、责备或呼唤注意。
explanation_english: Used to address a male friend in a casual, familiar, or jocular tone; can also function as an interjection to express surprise, mild reproach, or to get someone's attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老兄，你好耐冇見喇！
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 hing1, nei5 hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老兄，你好久不见了！
examples.english_sentence: Hey bro, long time no see!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老兄，今次真係多謝你幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 hing1, gam1 ci3 zan1 hai6 do1 ze6 nei5 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老兄，这次真的谢谢你帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: Bro, thanks a lot for your help this time.

jyutping: lou5 gung1 bok3 sin3, cai1 (cai1) loeng4
mandarin_meaning: 丈夫冷淡，妻子凄凉（“妻”与“凄”同音，含讽刺意味的俗语）
english_meaning: A saying that describes a husband being indifferent or neglectful, leaving the wife miserable (the phrase plays on the homophone of 'wife' and 'miserable').
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東俗語用誇張的畫面（老公拨扇、妻子凄凉）表達丈夫對妻子冷淡或忽視，經常用來批評婚姻中一方被冷落或感情不和。括號標示“妻”與“凄”同音，帶有雙關和諷刺意味。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying uses a vivid image (the husband waving a fan while the wife is miserable) to convey that the husband is indifferent or neglectful toward his wife. It's often used to criticize situations where one partner is neglected or the relationship is cold. The parenthesis highlights the homophone between 'wife' and 'miserable', adding ironic wordplay.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢日日返到屋企都冇理老婆，真係老公拨扇，妻（凄）凉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat6 jat6 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 dou1 mou5 lei5 lou5 po4, zan1 hai6 lou5 gung1 bok3 sin3, cai1 (cai1) loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他每天回到家都不理老婆，真是老公拨扇，妻（凄）凉。
examples.english_sentence: He comes home every day and ignores his wife — truly a case of 'the husband waves a fan, the wife is miserable.'

mandarin_meaning: 指關係非常親密、可以互相幫助和信任的朋友（死黨、摯友）
english_meaning: a very close friend or bosom buddy; someone you trust and rely on
explanation_mandarin: 「老友兼死党」是粵語口語說法，用來形容彼此關係非常親密、互相扶持和信任的好友。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression for a friend who is extremely close — someone you trust implicitly and who would have your back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我老友兼死党，咩事都會幫我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 lou5 jau5 gim1 sei2 dong2, me1 si6 dou1 wui5 bong1 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我的死党，什麼事都會幫我。
examples.english_sentence: He's my bosom buddy; he'll help me with anything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同佢細個已經係老友兼死党，依家都仲係咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 sai3 go3 ji5 ging1 hai6 lou5 jau5 gim1 sei2 dong2, ji1 gaa1 dou1 zung6 hai6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我和他從小就是死黨，現在仍然如此。
examples.english_sentence: He and I have been bosom buddies since childhood, and we still are.

mandarin_meaning: 不停地咬、啃；（引申）糾纏、嘮叨、反覆糾結某事
english_meaning: to gnaw or nibble repeatedly; figuratively, to nag, pester, or keep dwelling on something
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的口語擬聲詞，字面上指一直咬或啃的動作（例如狗啃骨頭）。在口語中也可引申用來形容對人或事情反覆糾纏、唸叨或放不下，帶有有點煩人的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese onomatopoeic expression. Literally it describes continuous gnawing or nibbling (e.g. a dog gnawing a bone). Figuratively it can describe someone persistently nagging, pestering, or repeatedly dwelling on an issue, often with an annoying nuance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰條狗成日老嚙嚙隻骨頭，啲牙都磨到光晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 tiu4 gau2 sing4 jat6 lou5 nip6 nip6 zek3 gwat1 tau4, di1 ngaa4 dou1 mo4 dou3 gwong1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那只狗老是咬著那根骨頭，牙都被磨光了。
examples.english_sentence: That dog keeps gnawing the bone; its teeth are worn smooth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日老嚙嚙呢啲細節，講一次就算啦，唔使咁嘮叨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 lou5 nip6 nip6 ni1 di1 sai3 zit3, gong2 jat1 ci3 zau6 syun3 laa1, m4 sai2 gam2 lou4 dou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要总是对这些细节念念不休，说一次就算了，不必这么唠叨。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep fussing over these small details; say it once and that's enough—no need to keep nagging.

mandarin_meaning: 老太婆；老女人（带贬义）
english_meaning: old woman; old hag (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗稱，用來指年紀較大的婦人，常帶有不尊重或貶低的語氣。屬口語、俚語用法，常見於香港地區的非正式語境中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term for an older woman, often used pejoratively. Informal and commonly heard in Hong Kong speech; conveys disrespect or disparagement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁講，叫佢做老姆婆好傷人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 gong2, giu3 keoi5 zou6 lou5 mou2 po4 hou2 soeng1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別那樣說，叫她老姆婆很傷人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say that — calling her '老姆婆' is hurtful.

mandarin_meaning: （我的）姪子；口語上也可用來親暱或戲稱年輕男子
english_meaning: nephew; colloquially a kid/young man (used affectionately or teasingly)
explanation_mandarin: 「老姪」字面上指某人的姪子（男性旁系後輩）。在廣東話口語裡，也可用作對年輕男性的稱呼，常帶親暱或戲謔的語氣。
explanation_english: Literally 'nephew'. In Cantonese, it refers to someone's nephew and is also used colloquially to address or refer to a younger male, often with an affectionate or teasing tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個老姪今日嚟探我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 lou5 zat6 gam1 jat6 lai4 taam3 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的姪子今天來看我。
examples.english_sentence: My nephew came to visit me today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個老姪成日打機，唔鍾意出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 lou5 zat6 seng4 jat6 daa2 gei1, m4 zung1 ji3 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個姪子總是打電動，不喜歡出門。
examples.english_sentence: That nephew is always playing video games and doesn't like going out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老姪，你快啲返嚟幫手啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 zat6, nei5 faai3 di1 faan1 lai4 bong1 sau2 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小子，你快點回來幫忙啦！
examples.english_sentence: Hey kid, hurry back and help!

jyutping: lou5 po4 daam1 ze1, jam1 gung1
mandarin_meaning: 老婆拿著傘，老公倒楣；比喻在家庭或關係中一方受委屈或吃虧
english_meaning: Literally 'the wife holds the umbrella, the husband is unlucky' — used to describe someone being left in the lurch, treated unfairly, or made to suffer (often within a relationship).
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面指老婆拿著遮（傘）保護自己，而老公反而受雨淋；引申用來形容在夫妻或其他關係中有人被忽視、吃虧或倒楣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying. Literally it means the wife holds the umbrella (protecting herself) while the husband ends up unlucky/left out. Figuratively it describes someone being neglected, shortchanged, or made to suffer (often within a marriage or close relationship).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強話結咗婚之後成日都係『老婆擔遮，陰公』，覺得自己好食虧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 waa6 git3 zo2 fan1 zi1 hau6 sing4 jat6 dou1 hai6 'lou5 po4 daam1 ze1, jam1 gung1', gok3 dak1 zi6 gei2 hou2 sik6 fai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强說結婚後總覺得「老婆拿傘，老公倒楣」，覺得自己很吃虧。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung says that since getting married it's always 'the wife takes the umbrella, the husband is unlucky' — he feels he's being shortchanged.

mandarin_meaning: 表面看起來老實、低調，但實際很厲害／有實力（香港俚語）
english_meaning: Looks honest/low-key on the outside but actually very impressive or formidable (HK slang).
explanation_mandarin: 「老实威」是香港廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人外表看似老實、低調或乖巧，但實際上很有能力、很厲害。既可作描述，也可作感嘆（表示佩服）。
explanation_english: “老实威” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang describing someone who appears honest, quiet, or low-key outwardly but is actually very capable or formidable. It can be used descriptively or as an exclamation to express admiration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢望落好老實，但其實好威，真係老實威。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mong6 lok6 hou2 lou5 sat6, daan6 kei4 sat6 hou2 wai1, zan1 hai6 lou5 sat6 wai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看起來很老實，但其實很厲害，真是老實威。
examples.english_sentence: He looks very honest/low-key, but he's actually impressive — truly 'low-key but powerful'.

mandarin_meaning: 老來俏（晚年仍然嬌俏或在晚年獲得寵愛）
english_meaning: Becoming attractive or finding affection/romance in old age; flourishing or being doted on in later life
explanation_mandarin: 指年紀漸大但仍然有魅力，或在晚年重新受到寵愛、獲得幸福。常用來形容老年人晚年風采或晚年得寵。
explanation_english: Refers to remaining attractive or finding affection/romance in later life; used to describe elderly people who remain charming or enjoy renewed happiness and attention in their later years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家晚年仲老來俏，打扮得好有精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 maan5 nin4 zung6 lou5 loi4 ciu3, daa2 baan6 dak1 hou2 jau5 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她現在晚年仍然老來俏，打扮得很有精神。
examples.english_sentence: They are still attractive in their later years and dress very spiritedly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢老來俏，仲搵到個愛人，生活好舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lou5 loi4 ciu3, zung6 wan2 dou3 go3 oi3 jan4, sang1 wut6 hou2 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老來俏，還找到了伴侶，生活很舒適。
examples.english_sentence: He/She found a partner later in life and now lives comfortably.

mandarin_meaning: 用慢火長時間熬煮的廣東滋補湯（慢炖的靓汤）
english_meaning: a Cantonese slow-simmered (nourishing) soup, simmered for a long time over low heat
explanation_mandarin: 「老火靓汤」是廣東話的烹飪詞，指用慢火長時間熬煮、通常含骨頭、中藥材或蔬菜的滋補湯品，味道清鮮且有補益作用，常見於家庭或粵菜館。
explanation_english: “老火靓汤” refers to a Cantonese practice of slow-simmering nourishing soups (often with bones, herbs, and vegetables) over low heat for a long time. The result is a clear, flavorful, restorative soup commonly made at home or served in Cantonese restaurants.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我阿媽煲咗一煲老火靓汤，好滋補。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 aa3 maa1 bou1 zo2 jat1 bou1 lou5 fo2 leng3 tong1, hou2 zi1 bou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我媽媽煲了一鍋老火靓汤，很滋补。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight my mum simmered a pot of slow-cooked nourishing soup; it's very restorative.

mandarin_meaning: 老狗（字面：年老的狗）；俚語、辱罵用語，指『老家伙／壞人／可惡的人』，帶貶義
english_meaning: Old dog (literal: an aged dog); slang/insult used to call someone an 'old scoundrel' or 'dirty old man', pejorative
explanation_mandarin: 「老狗」可指年紀大的狗；在廣東話口語中常作貶損的稱呼或罵人用語，用來表示輕視、憤怒或不屑，語氣粗俗。要注意場合，常帶冒犯性。
explanation_english: Literally an old dog. In Cantonese colloquial speech it's often used as a derogatory term to insult someone (e.g. 'old scoundrel' or 'dirty old man'). It conveys contempt and is coarse; avoid in polite contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你呢個老狗，竟然食晒我嘅零食！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ni1 go3 lou5 gau2, ging2 jin4 sik6 saai3 ngo5 ge3 ling4 sik6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这个老狗，竟然把我的零食都吃光了！
examples.english_sentence: You old dog, you actually ate all my snacks!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講大話，真係個老狗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6, zan1 hai6 go3 lou5 gau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是说谎，真是个老狗。
examples.english_sentence: He lies all the time — really an old dog.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市入面有隻老狗，好可憐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 jap6 min6 jau5 zek3 lou5 gau2, hou2 ho2 lin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 菜市场里有一只老狗，很可怜。
examples.english_sentence: There's an old dog in the market, very pitiful.

cantonese: 老狗嫩猫儿，食死冇人知
jyutping: lou5 gau2 non6 maau1 ji4, sik6 sei2 mou5 jan4 zi1
mandarin_meaning: 老男人與年輕女人在一起（常指荒唐或祕密的男女關係），別人看不到真相
english_meaning: An old man paired with a much younger woman (often implying a scandalous or secret relationship); what they do in private nobody knows
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句粵語俗語/俚語，帶有貶義或調侃意味，通常用來形容年長者與年輕異性在一起的關係（特別是男女年齡懸殊且帶有祕密或不光彩的含義），強調旁人看不到或不清楚其私下情況。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase, often pejorative or teasing, describes an older person paired with a much younger partner (especially an older man with a young woman) and implies secrecy or scandal. It emphasizes that outsiders don't know what happens in private.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲人成日講佢哋係老狗嫩猫兒，食死冇人知，街坊都喺背後講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 jan4 sing4 jat6 gong2 keoi5 dei6 hai6 lou5 gau2 non6 maau1 ji4, sik6 sei2 mou5 jan4 zi1, gaai1 fong1 dou1 hai2 bui3 hau6 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大家總說他們是「老狗嫩貓兒，食死冇人知」，街坊私下都在議論。
examples.english_sentence: People keep saying they're 'an old dog with a young cat — what they do in private nobody knows', and the neighbors gossip behind their backs.

mandarin_meaning: 比喻受到过教训以后变得很谨慎（类似“吃一堑长一智”）
english_meaning: Once bitten, twice shy — someone who has been burned before becomes cautious
explanation_mandarin: 字面是“老猫被烫到胡须”，用来形容经历过挫折或教训后变得小心谨慎，不再轻率行事。
explanation_english: Literally 'an old cat burns its whiskers.' Used to describe a person who, after suffering a setback or lesson, becomes more careful and avoids taking the same risks again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢投資蝕咗一次，依家老貓燒鬚，唔敢再亂嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 zi1 sik1 zo2 jat1 ci3, ji1 gaa1 lou5 maau1 siu1 sou1, m4 gam2 zoi3 lyun6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他投资亏过一次，现在老猫烧须，不敢再乱来。
examples.english_sentence: He lost money on an investment once; now he's been burned and won't act recklessly again.

synonyms: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井繩

mandarin_meaning: 老番凉茶（字面：外國人的涼茶；口語用法，多用作商品名或戲稱，帶有文化混搭或貶義色彩）
english_meaning: ‘Lao faan liang cha’ (literally ‘foreigner's cooling herbal tea’). A colloquial/slang label sometimes used as a product name or joking/derogatory reference to a Westernized or foreign take on Chinese herbal cooling tea.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞彙，字面意為「外國人的涼茶」。並非固定成語，常見用法包括作為飲品或店名，或戲謔地指中西混合、或嘲諷外國人喝中醫涼茶。需注意「老番」帶貶義或冒犯意味，使用時要小心語境與對象。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning 'foreigner's cooling herbal tea.' It's not a set idiom — it is often used as a playful product name or joking/pejorative label implying a Westernized version of traditional herbal tea or poking fun at foreigners trying Chinese remedies. The term '老番' can be derogatory, so be cautious with usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間茶餐廳新推出一款叫「老番涼茶」嘅飲品，賣相同味道都有啲特別。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 san1 teoi1 ceot1 jat1 fun2 giu3 "lou5 faan1 loeng4 caa4" ge3 jam2 ban2, maai6 soeng6 tung4 mei6 dou6 dou1 jau5 di1 dak6 bit6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间茶餐厅新推出一款叫“老番凉茶”的饮品，外观和味道都有点特别。
examples.english_sentence: This cha chaan teng just launched a drink called 'lao faan liang cha' — its look and taste are a bit unusual.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話嗰杯老番涼茶藥味好重，唔係佢鍾意嘅口味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 go2 bui1 lou5 faan1 loeng4 caa4 joek6 mei6 hou2 zung6, m4 hai6 keoi5 zung1 ji3 ge3 hau2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說那杯老番凉茶藥味很重，不是他喜歡的口味。
examples.english_sentence: He said that cup of 'lao faan liang cha' tasted very herbal — not his kind of flavor.

mandarin_meaning: （方言／口語）堆積的舊雜物、破爛（罕見或地區性詞）
english_meaning: An informal/colloquial term for accumulated old junk or scattered clutter (rare/regional usage)
explanation_mandarin: 「老積散」並非標準書面詞彙，屬口語或地區性用語。字面可理解為「積存已久而散亂的東西」，常用來形容房間或地方堆滿舊雜物、破爛，使用時有時會有人不熟悉此說法。
explanation_english: Not a standard written term; a colloquial/regional expression. Literally suggests things that have accumulated over time and lie scattered. It is used to describe a place filled with old junk or clutter. Usage is informal and may be unfamiliar to some listeners.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成間屋都係老積散，唔知道點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 gaan1 uk1 dou1 hai6 lou5 zik1 saan3, m4 zi1 dou3 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 整個房子都是老積散，不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: The whole house is full of old junk/clutter; I don't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 守舊、老派、頑固（也可指事物過時）
english_meaning: old-fashioned; conservative; stuck in one's ways (can also mean outdated)
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗稱，通常用來形容人思想守舊、不願接受新事物或固執，也可用來形容東西過時、老土。常見於香港粵語口語中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term usually describing a person who is conservative or stubborn and unwilling to accept new things; can also describe something that is old-fashioned or out of date. Commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁老積，點會試下新嘢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 lou5 zik1, dim2 wui5 si3 haa5 san1 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼守舊，怎麼會嘗試新東西？
examples.english_sentence: You're so old-fashioned; how would you try something new?

mandarin_meaning: 爸爸；父親
english_meaning: dad; father
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語稱呼父親的詞，屬非正式用法。寫作「老竇」或「老豆」，在香港常見，帶有親暱或俗稱的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for one's father. Informal—often written as 老竇 or 老豆—commonly used in Hong Kong with a familiar or slangy tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我老竇今日唔喺屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lou5 dau6 gam1 jat6 m4 hai2 uk1 kei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我爸爸今天不在家。
examples.english_sentence: My dad isn't home today.

mandarin_meaning: （可能是「老竇」的誤寫或變體）爸爸、老爸
english_meaning: dad; father (colloquial) — likely a misspelling or variant of '老竇'/'老豆'
explanation_mandarin: 「老脰」並非標準或常見的書寫形式，經常被視為錯寫或個別地區的變體。更常用且標準的粵語口語寫法為「老竇」或「老豆」，意思是父親，屬於口語、非正式用法。
explanation_english: Not a standard or widely used written form. '老脰' is likely a misspelling or regional variant of the Cantonese colloquial term '老竇'/'老豆' (lou5 dau6), meaning 'father' or 'dad'. Usage is informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 其實「老脰」通常係寫錯或者變體，真正常用嘅寫法係「老竇」，意思係爸爸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: kei4 sat6 「lou5 dau6」 tung4 soeng4 hai6 se2 co3 waak6 ze2 bin3 tai2, zan1 zing3 soeng4 jung6 ge3 se2 faat3 hai6 「lou5 dau6」, ji3 si1 hai6 baa4 baa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 其实“老脰”通常是写错或地区变体，常用写法是“老竇”，意思是爸爸。
examples.english_sentence: '老脰' is usually a misspelling or variant; the standard colloquial form is '老竇', meaning 'dad'.

mandarin_meaning: 表面強勢但不親自出手，借用他人或他力去做強勢或欺壓行為（廣東話俚語，使用範圍有限）
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who appears strong but does not act personally, instead using others or borrowed force to do the dirty work or bully others
explanation_mandarin: 「老虎借豬」是廣東話口語、俚語，常用來形容某人表面上看似兇猛或有氣勢，但實際上不親自出手，透過借助他人、他力或代理去完成強勢或欺壓的行為。此詞較為地方性、非正式，使用時需注意語境。
explanation_english: "老虎借豬" is Cantonese slang used to describe someone who projects toughness but does not act personally, instead relying on others or borrowed means to carry out forceful or bullying actions. It is informal and regionally used; context matters when using it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做老虎借豬，唔親自出面，淨係搵人代佢出手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zou6 lou5 fu2 ze3 zyu1, m4 can1 zi6 ceot1 min6, zing6 hai6 wan2 jan4 doi6 keoi5 ceot1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常做老虎借豬，不亲自出面，只找别人代他出手。
examples.english_sentence: He often plays the 'tiger borrows pig' — not confronting personally, but getting others to act on his behalf.

jyutping: lou5 fu2 tau4 soeng6 ding1 sat1 naa5
mandarin_meaning: 自找麻烦、惹来祸端（在虎头上钉虱子）
english_meaning: to ask for trouble; to court disaster; to do something reckless or pointless that invites trouble
explanation_mandarin: 比喻做出危險或愚蠢的事，等於自找麻煩或找死，像是在老虎頭上釘虱子一樣不智且危險。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression meaning to take a dangerous, foolish, or self‑defeating action — like trying to nail a louse onto a tiger's head; essentially asking for trouble or courting disaster.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做喺老虎頭上釘虱乸，係自找麻煩㗎！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 zou6 hai6 lou5 fu2 tau4 soeng6 ding1 sat1 naa5, hai6 zi6 zoek3 maa4 faan4 gaa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣做是在虎頭上釘虱子，簡直是自找麻煩！
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing is like nailing a louse on a tiger's head — you're just asking for trouble!

mandarin_meaning: 連最厲害/看似真的東西也是假；一切都是假的（表示懷疑或不信任）
english_meaning: Even the supposedly real or impressive things are fake; everything's fake (expresses skepticism or distrust)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來表示對某些物品、資訊或情況完全不信任，覺得連「看似可靠或厲害」的東西也不是真實的。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to say you don't trust something at all — even the things that appear strong, authentic, or impressive are fake. It's used to convey skepticism or cynicism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家邊樣唔係真嘅？老虎蟹都假啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 bin1 joeng6 m4 hai6 zan1 ge3? lou5 fu2 haai5 dou1 gaa2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在有什麼是真的？連老虎蟹都是假啊。
examples.english_sentence: What's real anymore? Even the supposedly real things are fake.

mandarin_meaning: 父母；雙親
english_meaning: parents; one's mother and father
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用語，指自己的父親和母親。帶有口語或親切色彩。括號內的「襯」為部分口語或書寫的變體，發音略有不同。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term referring to one's parents (mother and father). It carries an informal or affectionate tone. The variant written with 襯 is a regional/colloquial variant with a slightly different pronunciation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要多啲照顧你啲老親，佢哋年紀大㗎啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 do1 di1 ziu3 gu3 nei5 di1 lou5 can1, keoi5 dei6 nin4 gei3 daai6 gaa3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要多照顧你的父母，他們年紀大了。
examples.english_sentence: You should take better care of your parents; they're getting old.

jyutping: lou5 dau6 joeng5 zai2, zai2 joeng5 zai2
mandarin_meaning: 父母養育孩子，孩子長大後也會養育自己的孩子；強調代際延續或各自負責
english_meaning: A proverb meaning parents raise their children, and when grown the children will raise their own; emphasizes generational continuity or each generation taking care of its own.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，表示生活和照顧會代代相傳，或暗示不必過分擔心未來，因為下一代會自生自立或養育下一代。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying that expresses intergenerational continuity — parents raise children, and those children will in turn raise their own. It can also imply that each generation is responsible for itself or that one need not worry excessively about future provision.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家經濟咁差，佢都唔擔心，話「老豆養仔，仔養仔」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 ging1 zai3 gam2 caa1, keoi5 dou1 m4 daam1 sam1, waa6 "lou5 dau6 joeng5 zai2, zai2 joeng5 zai2".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在經濟這麼差，他也不擔心，說：「父母養子，孩子長大後會養自己的孩子。」
examples.english_sentence: With the economy so bad, he's not worried — he says, "Fathers raise sons, and sons will raise sons."

jyutping: lou5 dau6 sing3 mat1 dou1 m4 zi1
mandarin_meaning: 連自己爸爸姓什麼都不知道（形容人非常糊塗或毫無常識）
english_meaning: Literally 'doesn't even know his father's surname' — used to describe someone as completely clueless or ignorant
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語（貶義，形容詞性片語）
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俚語，字面意思是連父親的姓氏都不知道，用來形容一個人非常糊塗、缺乏基本常識或毫無頭緒，常帶有貶義或戲謔成分。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally meaning 'doesn't even know his father's surname.' It describes someone as extremely clueless, ignorant, or lacking basic common sense. Often used pejoratively or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢連老豆姓乜都唔知，點可以管理公司？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lin4 lou5 dau6 sing3 mat1 dou1 m4 zi1, dim2 ho2 ji5 gun2 lei5 gung1 si1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他連自己爸爸姓什麼都不知道，怎麼能管理公司？
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't even know his own father's surname — how could he possibly manage a company?

mandarin_meaning: 連爸爸都會想要更多（口語、誇張說法）
english_meaning: Even (my) dad would want more (colloquial/exaggerated expression)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某件事物、優惠或產品非常吸引或豐富，連父親（老豆）也會想要更多。通常是誇張或幽默的說法，帶有強調吸引力或份量多的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang phrase used to emphasize that something (a deal, product, portion, etc.) is so appealing or plentiful that even one's father ('old man') would want more. Often used humorously or exaggeratively to stress attractiveness or abundance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個優惠真係咁吸引，老豆都要多買幾件。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 jau1 wai6 zan1 hai6 gam2 kap1 jan5, lou5 dau6 dou1 jiu3 do1 maai5 gei2 gin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個優惠真的那麼吸引，連我爸爸都想多買幾件。
examples.english_sentence: This deal is so attractive that even my dad would want to buy more.

mandarin_meaning: 總是賺錢；一直獲利；（被）老是佔便宜
english_meaning: to always make a profit; consistently profitable; (of someone) to repeatedly take advantage of someone
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話詞語，表示經常賺錢或經常獲利；也可用於被他人反覆佔便宜（如“俾人老賺”）。可作謂語或描述狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to consistently make a profit or be reliably profitable. It can also be used to say someone keeps taking advantage of another (e.g., 'to be constantly taken advantage of').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做生意老賺，每次都有利潤。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 saang1 ji3 lou5 zaan6, mui5 ci3 dou1 jau5 lei6 jeon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做生意總是賺錢，每次都有利潤。
examples.english_sentence: He always makes money in his business; he profits every time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好俾人老賺，講清楚價錢先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 lou5 zaan6, gong2 cing1 co2 gaa3 cin2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要讓別人總是佔你的便宜，先把價格講清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let others keep taking advantage of you; make the price clear first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次投資好好，真係老賺啊！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 tau4 zi1 hou2 hou2, zan1 hai6 lou5 zaan6 aa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次投資很好，真是大賺了一筆！
examples.english_sentence: This investment went great — we really made a killing!

mandarin_meaning: 老派、守舊（口語、帶貶義）
english_meaning: old-fashioned; conservative; old fogey (slang, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「老階」是廣東話口語，用來形容一個人或行為思想很守舊、落伍、不合時宜，通常帶有輕微或明顯的貶義。
explanation_english: “老階” is Cantonese slang used to describe someone or something that is old-fashioned, conservative, or out of date. It usually carries a mildly or clearly derogatory tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好老階，成日話新嘢唔好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 lou5 gaai1, sing4 jat6 waa6 san1 je5 m4 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話很老派，總是說新東西不好。
examples.english_sentence: He talks very old-fashioned; always says new things are bad.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁老階，試下接受啲新潮嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 lou5 gaai1, si3 haa5 zip3 sau6 di1 san1 ciu4 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別那麼老派，試著接受一些新潮的東西。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so old-fashioned; try accepting some trendy things.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）年老體衰、行動遲緩；或形容物件非常破舊
english_meaning: (slang) very old and frail or creaky; also used for something extremely worn-out
explanation_mandarin: 「老革革」為廣東話口語/俚語，用來形容人年紀大、身體衰弱、動作遲緩，亦可用於形容物件破舊、老化。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe a person who is very old, frail, or moves slowly; it can also describe an object that is extremely worn-out or decrepit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家老革革，行唔到咁快。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 lou5 gaak3 gaak3, haang4 m4 dou2 gam2 faai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在老得走不動那麼快。
examples.english_sentence: He's so old and creaky now; he can't walk that fast.

jyutping: lou5 syu2 mei5 saang1 cong1, daai6 gik6 jau5 haan6
mandarin_meaning: 老鼠尾巴長了瘡，影響極為有限（用來淡化小問題的嚴重性）
english_meaning: A rat's tail getting sores — the damage/impact is very limited (used to downplay a minor problem)
explanation_mandarin: 此句為廣東話的口語表達（屬於俗語或方言用語，非標準成語），大意是即使出現微小的毛病或瑕疵（比喻為「老鼠尾生瘡」），其影響也極為有限，無需大驚小怪或過度擔心，常用來淡化或安撫小問題。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial expression (not a common standardized idiom) can be interpreted as: even if a tiny fault appears ('a rat's tail gets sores'), its effect is very limited. It is used to downplay minor problems and reassure people that there's no need to overreact.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔使太擔心，呢啲只係老鼠尾生疮，大极有限。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 sai2 taai3 daam1 sam1, ni1 di1 zi2 hai6 lou5 syu2 mei5 saang1 cong1, daai6 gik6 jau5 haan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不用太担心，這些只是老鼠尾巴長了瘡，影響極為有限。
examples.english_sentence: Don't worry too much; these are just minor issues and their impact is very limited.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 雖然機器有時會甩位，但通常係老鼠尾生疮，大极有限，唔使換新嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: seoi1 jin4 gei1 hei3 jau5 si4 wui5 lat1 wai6, daan6 tung1 soeng4 hai6 lou5 syu2 mei5 saang1 cong1, daai6 gik6 jau5 haan6, m4 sai2 wun6 san1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 雖然機器有時會出小問題，但通常只是小故障，影響非常有限，不需要換新的。
examples.english_sentence: Although the machine sometimes has small glitches, they're usually minor with very limited impact — no need to replace it.

cantonese: 老鼠拉鲇鱼，一命搏一命
jyutping: lou5 syu2 laai1 nim4 jyu4, jat1 ming6 bok3 jat1 ming6
mandarin_meaning: 形容在生死或絕境中拼命對抗，殊死一搏；雙方都不肯退讓的拼命搏鬥。
english_meaning: Describes a desperate, do-or-die struggle where both sides fight with everything they have; a life-or-death, all-or-nothing fight.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語比喻雙方在極端情況下拼命相斗、互不相讓，往往帶有冒險、殊死一搏的意思。
explanation_english: This proverb likens a situation to a desperate fight in which both parties risk everything and refuse to yield — an all-or-nothing, life-or-death struggle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單官司打到老鼠拉鲇鱼，一命搏一命，冇人肯退讓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dan1 gun1 si1 daa2 dou3 lou5 syu2 laai1 nim4 jyu4, jat1 ming6 bok3 jat1 ming6, mou5 jan4 hang2 teoi3 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這起官司打到老鼠拉鲇鱼，一命搏一命，沒有人肯退讓。
examples.english_sentence: This lawsuit has become a do-or-die fight — no one is willing to back down.

jyutping: lou5 syu2 laai1 gwai1, mou5 ding6 maai4 sau2
mandarin_meaning: 事情混亂、沒個定數或收場，難以收拾或了結的狀況（口語）
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese idiom describing a messy situation with no definite outcome or no way to finish/settle it; a hopeless/unfinished mess.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容事情混亂、收場無望或沒法妥善處理，類似「一團糟、沒著落」的意思。
explanation_english: Used to describe a chaotic situation that cannot be properly settled or finished — essentially a mess with no clear resolution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意咁亂，真係老鼠拉龜，冇定埋手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 gam2 lyun6, zan1 hai6 lou5 syu2 laai1 gwai1, mou5 ding6 maai4 sau2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這單生意這麼亂，真是沒法收場，沒有結果。
examples.english_sentence: This deal is such a mess — it's hopeless and there's no definite outcome.

jyutping: lou5 syu2 wan2 maau1, lo2 lei4 seoi1
mandarin_meaning: 自找麻烦 / 自討苦吃
english_meaning: to ask for trouble; to court disaster; to bring misfortune on oneself
explanation_mandarin: 比喻故意做或去招惹危險或不利的事，結果自招災禍、吃苦頭。
explanation_english: A proverb warning that someone who provokes danger or does risky things is asking for trouble and will suffer the consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁樣走去招惹啲危險嘅人，老鼠揾猫，攞嚟衰㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 joeng6 zau2 heoi3 ziu1 je5 di1 ngai4 him2 ge3 jan4, lou5 syu2 wan2 maau1, lo2 lei4 seoi1 ga3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要这样去招惹危险的人，自找麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: Don't go provoking dangerous people — you're asking for trouble.

jyutping: lou5 syu2 dit3 lok6 tin1 ping4, zi6 cing1 zi6
mandarin_meaning: 比喻微不足道的人却自夸重要；自以为是。
english_meaning: Literally: 'A mouse falls on the scale and proclaims itself heavy.' Figuratively: someone insignificant claiming to be important; boastful or pretentious.
explanation_mandarin: 用老鼠掉到天平上，自稱自己很重的比喻，形容人沒有本事或地位但卻自以為重要或自誇。
explanation_english: A metaphor comparing a mouse that falls onto a scale and claims to be heavy; used to describe someone insignificant who brags or pretends to be important.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇吓佢咁樣講嘢，真係老鼠跌落天平，自称自。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 keoi5 gam2 joeng6 gong2 je5, zan1 hai6 lou5 syu2 dit3 lok6 tin1 ping4, zi6 cing1 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看他那樣說話，真是老鼠掉到天平上，自稱自己很重（比喻自不量力）。
examples.english_sentence: Look at how he talks — like a mouse on a scale claiming it's heavy (i.e. someone insignificant who thinks they're important).

jyutping: lou5 syu2 tim2 dang1 zaan2, zi2 gu3 ngaan5 cin4 gwong1
mandarin_meaning: 形容目光短浅，只顾眼前利益或享受，不顾长远后果。
english_meaning: Describes short-sighted behavior: only caring about immediate gain or pleasure and ignoring long-term consequences.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻像老鼠去舔燈盞的光亮，只顧當前的好處或眼前的快樂，卻不顧以後會有壞結果，帶有貶義，常用以批評目光短淺或不顧後果的行為。
explanation_english: A metaphor meaning someone focuses on immediate benefits (like a mouse licking a lamp's light) without considering future repercussions. Used pejoratively to criticize short-sighted or reckless behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁做好似老鼠𫇘灯盏，只顾眼前光，無諗過後果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 zou6 hou2 ci5 lou5 syu2 tim2 dang1 zaan2, zi2 gu3 ngaan5 cin4 gwong1, mou5 lam2 gwo3 hau6 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样做像老鼠舔灯盏，只顾眼前的光，没考虑后果。
examples.english_sentence: Doing this is like a mouse licking the lamp — only caring about the immediate light and not thinking about the consequences.

mandarin_meaning: 如今；现在（书面/文言）
english_meaning: now; nowadays (literary/formal)
explanation_mandarin: 「而今」为书面或文言用语，意指現在、如今，多見於正式或文學語境，口語常用「現在/而家」替代。
explanation_english: A literary/formal adverb meaning 'now' or 'nowadays'. Common in written or literary contexts; colloquial Cantonese typically uses '而家' or equivalents.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而今社會變化好快。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gam1 se5 wui6 bin3 faa3 hou2 faai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如今社会变化很快。
examples.english_sentence: Nowadays society is changing very quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺文學裡，「而今」多用喺書面語。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 man4 hok6 leoi5, 「ji4 gam1」do1 jung6 hai2 syu1 min6 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在文学里，“而今”多用于书面语。
examples.english_sentence: In literature, '而今' is mostly used in written language.

mandarin_meaning: 耍太极（指拖延、推脱或敷衍）
english_meaning: to stall; to dodge; to use delaying or evasive tactics
explanation_mandarin: 指以拖延、推脱或敷衍的方式应付他人或回避正面回应，常用于形容人在谈判或问话时不直接回应。
explanation_english: To use delaying tactics, dodge responsibility, or give evasive answers; often used when someone avoids a direct response in negotiations or questioning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺會議上耍太極，唔肯直接答問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 wui6 ji5 soeng6 saa2 taai3 gik6, m4 hang2 zik6 zip3 daap3 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是在会议上耍太极，不肯直接回答问题。
examples.english_sentence: He always stalls in meetings and refuses to answer directly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想同佢傾呢單生意，驚佢會耍太極，拖長時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 seong2 tung4 keoi5 king1 ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3, geng1 keoi5 wui5 saa2 taai3 gik6, to1 coeng4 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想和他谈这笔生意，怕他会耍太极，拖延时间。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to negotiate this deal with him; I'm afraid he'll stall and drag out the time.

mandarin_meaning: 耍手兼拧头：形容人一邊耍弄、拖拉或耍滑，一邊又固執、不願配合或退讓
english_meaning: To stall and be uncooperative — acting cheeky or evasive while also being stubborn and refusing to comply
explanation_mandarin: 常用於粵語口語，描述某人在做事或被要求時耍滑、拖延或耍手段，同時又拧着头、不肯配合或退让，帶有不合作和固執的含義。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who stalls, plays tricks or shirks responsibility while simultaneously being stubborn and refusing to cooperate — conveys uncooperative, evasive behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要加班，佢就開始耍手兼拧头，話自己唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 gaa1 baan1, keoi5 zau6 hoi1 ci2 saa2 sau2 gim1 ning2 tau4, waa6 zi6 gei2 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要加班，他就耍手兼拧头，說自己不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: When the company asked for overtime, he started to stall and act stubborn, saying he wasn't feeling well.

mandarin_meaning: 耍花枪（shuǎ huā qiāng）：耍花招、耍手段、虚张声势或敷衍了事
english_meaning: to play tricks or use underhanded tactics; to bluff or go through the motions; to shirk responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 原指用花式招数变戏法，现常用来形容耍手段、弄虚作假、故意敷衍或虚张声势，不认真做事。
explanation_english: Originally referring to flashy spear play, now used to describe using tricks, deception, bluffing, or doing something perfunctorily rather than seriously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度耍花枪，講真啲啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 saa2 faa1 coeng1, gong2 zan1 di1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别在这里耍花枪，认真点说！
examples.english_sentence: Don't play tricks here — be serious!

mandarin_meaning: 農夫；以耕作為生的男子
english_meaning: farmer; a man who works the fields (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指以耕作為生的男子或農夫。有時帶有鄉下、樸實或戲謔的意味，也可用來描述返鄉務農的志向。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for a man who farms — a farmer. It can be a neutral occupational term or carry connotations of being rustic, simple, hardworking, or be used jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個耕田公，日日落田做工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 gang1 tin4 gung1, jat6 jat6 lok6 tin4 zou6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個農夫，每天下田幹活。
examples.english_sentence: He is a farmer, working in the fields every day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話想返鄉做耕田公，過簡單生活。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 soeng2 faan1 hoeng1 zou6 gang1 tin4 gung1, gwo3 gaan2 daan1 sang1 wut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說想回鄉當個農夫，過簡單的生活。
examples.english_sentence: He said he wanted to return to the countryside to be a farmer and live a simple life.

mandarin_meaning: （罕用廣東俚語）形容牙縫大或牙齒參差
english_meaning: A rare Cantonese slang used jokingly to describe someone with large tooth gaps or uneven teeth
explanation_mandarin: “耙齒蘿白”並非標準詞彙，多見於廣東地區的口語或俚語，用來戲稱或貶抑地形容牙縫大、門牙參差不齊的情況。較少正式使用，帶有戲謔或略微貶義的語感。
explanation_english: “耙齒蘿白” is an uncommon Cantonese colloquial/slang term. It’s used jokingly (often with a mildly derogatory tone) to describe someone whose teeth are gapped or uneven. It is not a standard term and is regionally informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲牙縫大到好似耙齒蘿白，成日俾人笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 ngaa4 fung3 daai6 dou3 hou2 ci5 paa4 ci2 lo4 baak6, sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的牙缝大得像耙齿萝白一样，总是被人取笑。
examples.english_sentence: His tooth gap is so big it's like '耙齒蘿白'—people often make fun of him.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳／罕見詞語（可能是錯別字或方言變體）
english_meaning: Unknown / very rare term (possibly a typo or a dialectal variant)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 未知（可能為名詞或片語）
explanation_mandarin: 「耳誖」一詞在現代粵語資料中罕見，未能在主要粵語詞典中找到可靠解釋。可能是拼寫錯誤、古字用法或某地區方言詞，故無法確定發音與確切含義。
explanation_english: The term "耳誖" is not attested in standard modern Cantonese references and lacks a reliable entry in major dictionaries. It may be a misspelling, an archaic character usage, or a regional dialectal variant, so its pronunciation and precise meaning cannot be confirmed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔識「耳誖」呢個字，可能係寫錯或者係好罕見嘅方言詞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik1 "耳誖" ni1 go3 zi6, ho2 nang4 hai6 se2 co3 waak6 ze2 hai6 hou2 hon2 gin3 ge3 fong1 jin4 ci4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不认识「耳誖」这个字，可能是写错或者是很罕见的方言词。
examples.english_sentence: I don't recognize the character "耳誖"; it might be a misspelling or a very rare dialectal word.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語口語）精神萎靡、懶散、偷懶、敷衍
english_meaning: (Cantonese slang) to be sluggish, listless, slack off or act perfunctorily
explanation_mandarin: 耷保為香港粵語口語，常用來形容一個人精神不振、懶散、做事敷衍或偷懶。有時也可指態度散漫、不認真。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who is listless, lazy, sluggish, or slacking off/being perfunctory. It often refers to a lack of energy or an indifferent attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好耷保啦，快啲做完啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 dap6 bou2 laa1, faai3 di1 zou6 jyun4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別耷保了，快點做完吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't slack off; finish it quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日耷保，做嘢提唔起精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 dap6 bou2, zou6 je5 tai4 m4 hei2 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近老是耷保，做事提不起精神。
examples.english_sentence: He's been sluggish lately and can't get motivated to work.

mandarin_meaning: 垂頭、垂頭喪氣、沮喪
english_meaning: to hang one's head; to look dejected; to droop
explanation_mandarin: 表示低垂著頭，情緒低落或無精打采，常用來形容沮喪或不開心的樣子。
explanation_english: Means to lower or hang one's head, showing dejection or lack of energy; commonly used to describe someone who looks downcast or dispirited.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試唔掂，佢耷頭返屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 m4 dim6, keoi5 daap3 tau4 faan1 uk1 kei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試沒考好，他垂頭回家了。
examples.english_sentence: He hung his head and went home after doing poorly on the exam.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 畀老細鬧完之後，佢成日耷頭，唔出聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 lou5 sai3 naau6 jyun4 zi1 hau6, keoi5 sing4 jat6 daap3 tau4, m4 ceot1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 被老闆責罵之後，他總是垂頭不語。
examples.english_sentence: After being scolded by his boss, he kept his head down and said nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 垂頭喪氣的人；鬱鬱寡歡的人
english_meaning: a gloomy, sulky or downcast person; someone who hangs their head
explanation_mandarin: 耷頭佬是廣東話口語，指經常低頭、顯得沮喪或悶悶不樂的人，用來描述情緒低落或鬱悶的人。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for a person who looks dejected, sulky, or downcast. Used as a noun to describe someone who keeps their head down or appears unhappy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日耷頭佬，唔知發生咩事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dap6 tau4 lou2, m4 zi1 faat3 sang1 me1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是垂頭喪氣，不知道發生了什麼事。
examples.english_sentence: He's always downcast; I don't know what's wrong.

mandarin_meaning: 垂下、耷拉；情緒低落
english_meaning: to droop or hang down; to be dejected
explanation_mandarin: 表示物體（如頭、眼皮等）下垂或形容人情緒低落、垂頭喪氣，常見於口語或書面描述。
explanation_english: Indicates that something (e.g. head, eyelids) is drooping or describes a person who is downcast or dejected; commonly used in spoken and written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢耷咗頭，望落好唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dap6 zo2 tau4, mong6 lok6 hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他垂下頭，看起來很不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He hung his head and looked very unhappy.

jyutping: lung4 lou2 baai3 nin4, daai6 gaa1 gam2 waa6
mandarin_meaning: 走過場式的拜年／敷衍的寒暄，大家都這麼說（用來形容形式化、沒有真心的問候）
english_meaning: A perfunctory/new-year greeting — going through the motions; everyone says so (used to describe formulaic, insincere greetings or comments).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容拜年或打招呼只是走形式、敷衍了事，沒有真心或實際內容。“大家噉话”帶有“大家都這麼說/都這樣認為”的語氣，常帶調侃或批評意味。
explanation_english: Used to describe greetings (especially New Year greetings) that are merely perfunctory and insincere. The latter part “everyone says so” implies a commonly held but dismissive view. Often used jokingly or critically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年佢啲拜年得個形式，真係聋佬拜年，大家噉话。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 keoi5 di1 baai3 nin4 dak1 go3 jing4 sik1, zan1 hai6 lung4 lou2 baai3 nin4, daai6 gaa1 gam2 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年他的拜年只是走走形式，真是走過場的拜年，大家都這麼說。
examples.english_sentence: This year his New Year greetings were just for show — a perfunctory greeting; everyone says so.

jyutping: lung4 lou2 tai2 hei3, m4 zi1 gong2 mat1
mandarin_meaning: 比喻完全听不懂别人说什么，对情况一头雾水。
english_meaning: Used to say someone is completely clueless about what's being said or what's going on (literally: a deaf man watching a play, not knowing what's being said).
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語用來形容對談話或情況毫無頭緒，聽不懂或不明白發生什麼事，常帶幽默或不滿的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial metaphor meaning someone doesn't understand what's being said or what's happening — used humorously or with mild criticism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽佢講嘅時候，真係聾佬睇戲，唔知講乜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 teng1 keoi5 gong2 ge3 si4 hau6, zan1 hai6 lung4 lou2 tai2 hei3, m4 zi1 gong2 mat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我听他讲的时候，真是一头雾水，完全听不懂他说什么。
examples.english_sentence: When I listened to him, I was completely clueless — I didn't understand what he was saying.

jyutping: seng1 daai6 daai6, mou5 je5 maai6
mandarin_meaning: 虛張聲勢；說得很厲害但沒有實質內容或東西可賣
english_meaning: All show and no substance; makes a big noise but has nothing to offer
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容聲勢很大、說得很厲害，但實際上沒有內容、沒有貨或沒有能力支撐這些說法。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone or something that makes a lot of noise or boasts but lacks real content, substance, or anything to deliver.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成日聲大大，冇嘢賣，連一啲證據都冇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 sing4 jat6 seng1 daai6 daai6, mou5 je5 maai6, jat1 di1 zing3 geoi3 dou1 mou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們老是聲勢很大，卻沒有東西可賣，連一點證據都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: They always make a big show but have nothing to sell — not even a shred of evidence.

mandarin_meaning: 鬧事、製造騷動或吵鬧（廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: to make a fuss / to make noise / to cause a disturbance (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「聲架」是香港廣東話的口語/俚語，常用來形容有人製造噪音、挑起爭端或刻意鬧事、搗亂。用法多為動詞，可與「搞」等動詞連用（如「搞聲架」）。
explanation_english: “聲架” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang meaning to make a fuss, create noise, or cause trouble/disturbance. It is commonly used as a verb and often appears with verbs like “搞” (e.g., “搞聲架”).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好搞聲架，我想訓覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gaau2 seng1 gaa3, ngo5 soeng2 fan3 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別鬧了，我想睡覺。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make a fuss/noise, I want to sleep.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺屋企搞聲架，搞到成間屋好吵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei5 gaau2 seng1 gaa3, gaau2 dou3 seng4 gaan1 uk1 hou2 caau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在家鬧事，弄得整間房子很吵。
examples.english_sentence: He is always making a fuss at home, making the whole house noisy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲學生喺課室度搞聲架，影響其他同學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 hok6 saang1 hai2 fo3 sat1 dou6 gaau2 seng1 gaa3, jing2 hoeng2 kei4 taa1 tung4 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些學生在課室裡鬧事，影響到其他同學。
examples.english_sentence: The students are making a fuss in the classroom, affecting the other classmates.

mandarin_meaning: 开始实行；使成为现实；落实（书面、古文用法）
english_meaning: to initiate/put into effect; to make something a reality; to implement (literary)
explanation_mandarin: 「肇實」為較書面或古文用詞，構成於「肇」（開始、造成）與「實」（成為真實、落實）之合用，表示開始使某事成為現實或落實執行。在現代口語粵語中較少使用，常以「落實」「實行」「推行」等替代。
explanation_english: “肇實” is a literary/formal term combining 肇 (to begin, to cause) and 實 (to make real, to realize). It means to initiate or put something into effect, to make it a reality. It is uncommon in everyday Cantonese speech and is typically replaced by words like “落實” (implement) or “實行” (carry out).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府今次宣佈嘅新政策要肇實，先至可以睇到成效。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gam1 ci3 syun1 bou3 ge3 san1 zing3 cak1 jiu3 ziu6 sat6, sin1 zi3 ho2 ji5 tai2 dou3 sing4 haau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府这次宣布的新政策要肇實（落实/實行），才能看到成效。
examples.english_sentence: The new policy announced by the government needs to be put into effect before any results can be seen.

jyutping: ziu6 hing3 ho4 baau1, to4 seoi1 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 會帶來厄運的人 / 帶衰的人
english_meaning: a person who brings bad luck; a jinx
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，用來形容某人會帶來霉運或不幸（即「帶衰」）。詞中「陀衰」相當於普通話的「帶衰」，整句帶有戲謔或輕蔑的語氣，屬地區性用法，來源與具體典故不一定明確。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe someone who brings bad luck (i.e. a jinx). The element “陀衰” corresponds to “bringing bad luck.” The phrase is regional, often jokingly or disparagingly used; exact origin is unclear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日同佢一齊，佢係個肇慶荷包，陀衰人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 tung4 keoi5 jat1 cai4, keoi5 hai6 go3 ziu6 hing3 ho4 baau1, to4 seoi1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別老是和他在一起，他是個會帶衰的人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't hang out with him all the time — he's a jinx; he brings bad luck.

mandarin_meaning: （1）皮膚上的小刺、倒刺（肉刺）；（2）（口語）感到尷尬、臉紅、羞愧（肉赤）
english_meaning: (1) a splinter / hangnail (literal); (2) (colloquial) to feel embarrassed, to blush, to be ashamed
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（字面義）；口語中可作形容詞/動詞（表尷尬）
explanation_mandarin: 「肉刺」可指卡在皮膚裡的小刺或倒刺，會痛；「肉赤」為粵語口語，表示因尷尬或羞愧而臉紅或覺得不好意思。
explanation_english: Literally, '肉刺' is a small splinter or hangnail in the skin that causes pain. Colloquially, '肉赤' describes feeling embarrassed or ashamed — literally 'flesh red' (blushing).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我指頭有肉刺，頂到好痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi2 tau4 jau5 juk6 ci3, deng2 dou3 hou2 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的手指出現了肉刺，壓到很痛。
examples.english_sentence: I have a splinter on my finger — it hurts when pressed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺眾人面前講起我嘅事，我聽到就肉赤。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zung3 jan4 min6 cin4 gong2 hei2 ngo5 ge3 si6, ngo5 teng1 dou3 zau6 juk6 cek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在眾人面前提起我的事，我聽了覺得很尷尬/臉紅。
examples.english_sentence: He brought up my matter in front of everyone — I felt really embarrassed.

mandarin_meaning: 肉屑、肉渣；（口語）比喻微不足道或價值低的東西/人
english_meaning: meat scraps or small bits of minced meat; (colloquial) something or someone of little value
explanation_mandarin: 指肉類經過切碎、剁碎或加工後產生的細小碎屑。在口語中有時也用作比喻，形容某物或某人微不足道、價值不高或無足輕重。
explanation_english: Refers to tiny pieces or scraps of meat produced after chopping or processing. Colloquially, it can be used metaphorically to describe something or someone insignificant or of low value.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚房度有啲肉糠，可能係剁牛肉嗰陣掉出嚟嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyu4 fong4 dou6 jau5 di1 juk6 kong1, ho2 nang4 hai6 deoi3 ngau4 juk6 go2 zan6 diu6 ceot1 lai4 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 廚房裡有些肉糠，可能是剁牛肉時掉出來的。
examples.english_sentence: There are some meat scraps in the kitchen; they might have fallen out when mincing the beef.

mandarin_meaning: 肚脐抽痛／肚脐附近的绞痛（口语）
english_meaning: a sudden twinge/cramp around the belly button (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，指肚臍或腹部附近突然出現的抽痛或悸動，常由胃痙攣、消化不良或飢餓引起，有時也用來形容短暫的不適感。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term describing a sudden twinge or cramp around the navel. Often caused by stomach cramps, indigestion, or hunger; sometimes used loosely for brief abdominal discomfort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近成日肚臍泵，好似胃痙攣，要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 tou5 kei4 bam1, hou2 ci5 wai6 ging3 lyun4, jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近老是肚脐那儿抽痛，好像胃痉挛，要去看医生。
examples.english_sentence: Lately I've been getting twinges in my belly button, like stomach cramps; I should see a doctor.

mandarin_meaning: （罕见）字面意思為「肚臍的鍋／煲」；並非常用成語或規範詞，可能為玩笑或自創俚語。
english_meaning: Literally "belly‑button pot"; not a standard Cantonese idiom. A rare or nonce slang term, typically used jokingly or as a coined expression.
explanation_mandarin: 「肚臍煲」並非廣泛認可的成語或常用詞，通常是字面玩笑或地區性、自創的俚語，用法有限且視語境而定。
explanation_english: Not a widely recognized idiom. "肚臍煲" is a literal, playful or coined expression in Cantonese; usage is rare and context-dependent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「肚臍煲」呢個詞好少人用，通常係玩笑式嘅自創詞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 「tou5 kei4 bou1」ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 siu2 jan4 jung6, tung1 soeng4 hai6 waan2 siu3 sik1 ge3 zi6 cong3 ci4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「肚臍煲」這個詞很少人用，通常是開玩笑或自創的詞語。
examples.english_sentence: "'Duqi bao' (lit. 'belly‑button pot') is rarely used; usually a joking or coined term."

mandarin_meaning: 口語稱呼短粒米（如壽司米），指粒形較短、煮熟後較黏的米
english_meaning: colloquial term for short, plump rice grains (e.g., sushi rice); rice that cooks up sticky
explanation_mandarin: 「肥仔米」是粵語口語用法，常用來形容粒形較短且煮熟時較黏的米（短粒米／壽司米）。屬於俗稱或市井說法，主要在香港或廣東地區口語中出現。
explanation_english: “Fei zai mai” is a Cantonese colloquial term used to describe short, plump rice grains that become sticky when cooked (short-grain or sushi rice). It's an informal/local name rather than a technical classification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢袋肥仔米煮出嚟好黏，啱整壽司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 doi2 fei4 zai2 mai5 zyu2 ceot1 lai4 hou2 nim1, aam1 zing2 sou3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這袋肥仔米煮出來很黏，適合做壽司。
examples.english_sentence: This bag of 'fei zai mai' cooks up sticky — it's suitable for making sushi.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我鍾意用肥仔米整白飯，食落好有嚼感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 ji3 jung6 fei4 zai2 mai5 zing2 baak6 faan6, sik6 lok6 hou2 jau5 zoek3 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我喜歡用肥仔米煮白飯，吃起來有嚼勁。
examples.english_sentence: I like using short, plump rice to cook plain rice — it has a nice chewy texture.

cantonese: 肥佬着喇叭裤，髀（比）上不足，髀（比）下有余
jyutping: fei4 lou2 zoek3 laa1 baa1 fu3, bei2 soeng6 bat1 zuk1, bei2 haa6 jau5 jyu4
mandarin_meaning: 肥胖的人穿喇叭褲，上大腿處太緊而下大腿處太鬆；引申為上下不協調或不合身、不對稱
english_meaning: Literally: 'A fat man wearing bell-bottoms — tight above the thigh, loose below.' Figuratively: describes something or someone ill-fitting, disproportionate, or mismatched (often used mockingly).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容衣服不合身或上下不協調的身形或事物，常帶有嘲諷或戲謔意味。
explanation_english: Used to describe clothing that doesn't fit or an object/person that's top‑heavy and bottom‑loose — i.e., disproportionate or mismatched. Often used jokingly or scornfully.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都亂配衫，睇落好似肥佬着喇叭裤，髀上不足，髀下有余。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 lyun6 pui3 saam1, tai2 lok6 hou2 ci5 fei4 lou2 zoek3 laa1 baa1 fu3, bei2 soeng6 bat1 zuk1, bei2 haa6 jau5 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是随便搭配衣服，看起来像“肥佬着喇叭裤，髀上不足，髀下有余”。
examples.english_sentence: He always mismatches his clothes; he looks like 'a fat guy in bell‑bottoms — tight above the thigh, loose below.'

cantonese: 肥佬着笠衫，几大就几大
jyutping: fei4 lou2 zoek3 lap1 saam1, gei2 daai6 zau6 gei2 daai6
mandarin_meaning: 胖子穿緊身衣，大小就是那樣；比喻不遮掩本來面目或按事實看待，不要作假或矯揉造作。
english_meaning: Literally: 'A fat man wears a tight shirt — as big as he is.' Used to say someone doesn't hide their true size or nature; take things as they are / don't pretend.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用來形容某人不隱藏自己的身形或本性，既然如此就按事實看待；也常用來勸人別做作、不要偽裝。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying describes someone who doesn't hide their true appearance or nature. It urges accepting facts as they are and can be used to tell someone not to pretend or put on airs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好扮高尚，做人實際啲——肥佬着笠衫，几大就几大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 baan6 gou1 soeng6, zou6 jan4 sat6 zai3 di1 —— fei4 lou2 zoek3 lap1 saam1, gei2 daai6 zau6 gei2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別裝得很高尚，做事實際一點——胖子穿緊身衣，大小就是那樣。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act so high-minded; be realistic — a fat man in a tight shirt is as big as he is.

mandarin_meaning: 肥头大耳（形容人肥胖、满足或懒散、得意忘形）
english_meaning: plump-looking and droopy-eared; complacent, smug, or lethargic in appearance
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容人显得肥胖、懒散或自满得意的样子，有时带贬义，指态度骄傲或无精打采。
explanation_english: An idiom used to describe someone who appears plump and droopy, often implying complacence, smugness, or lethargy; can be slightly derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近日日食太多野，成日肥頭耷耳，做嘢都冇精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 jat6 jat6 sik6 taai3 do1 je5, sing4 jat6 fei4 tau4 daa2 ji5, zou6 je5 dou1 mou5 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近每天吃太多了，整天肥头耷耳，做事也没有精神。
examples.english_sentence: He's been overeating lately; he's always looking plump and droopy (i.e. complacent and lethargic), and has no energy for work.

mandarin_meaning: 胖奶奶；指身形豐腴的（多為年長）女性，口語化稱呼，有時戲稱或帶貶義
english_meaning: literally 'fat granny' — a colloquial/slang label for a plump or chubby (often older) woman; can be affectionate, teasing, or insulting depending on context
explanation_mandarin: 「肥奶奶」為廣東話口語稱呼，常用來形容身形較豐腴的女性。語氣可親切、戲謔或帶貶義，視語境與說話人關係而定，在香港話語中較常見。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term literally meaning 'fat granny.' It describes a plump woman and can be used playfully, teasingly, or offensively depending on context and relationship between speakers. Commonly heard in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好笑佢，叫人『肥奶奶』會傷人㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 siu3 keoi5, giu3 jan4 'fei4 naai5 naai5' wui5 soeng1 jan4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要嘲笑她，叫人「肥奶奶」會傷人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't laugh at her; calling someone 'fei naai naai' can be hurtful.

jyutping: fei4 po4 co5 taap3, gaak3 gaak3 ham2
mandarin_meaning: 對胖女人的貶稱或口頭咒罵，帶有輕蔑和侮辱意味（俗語，帶粗俗成分）
english_meaning: A derogatory/vulgar Cantonese insult directed at an overweight woman; an expression of contempt (slang, coarse).
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱的廣東話罵語，結構上是以「肥婆」為目標的侮辱性表達，後半段為擬聲或強調性的粗口成分，常見於口語、非正式情境。語氣冒犯，請避免使用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese abusive expression targeting an overweight woman. The latter part functions as an emphatic/coarse expletive. It is offensive, informal slang and typically used in spoken contexts. Avoid using it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁樣講人啦，話人『肥婆坐塔，佮佮冚』，好傷人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 joeng6 gong2 jan4 laa3, waa6 jan4 'fei4 po4 co5 taap3, gaak3 gaak3 ham2', hou2 soeng1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那樣說人了，說人「肥婆坐塔，佮佮冚」，很傷人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't speak about people like that—calling someone 'fei po co taap, gaak gaak ham' is really hurtful.

mandarin_meaning: 又胖又大；又胖又壯（口語、貶義）
english_meaning: very fat and big; huge and bulky (colloquial, derogatory)
