examples.mandarin_sentence: 莊田附近突然有很多昆蟲飛，老人說螗𧋦滿天飛，風雨一齊來，收割要快一點。
examples.english_sentence: Many insects suddenly appeared near the fields; the elders said 'insects fill the sky, wind and rain come together,' so harvest quickly.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見或方言）對某種小蝦的稱呼，字面上由「螟」（幼蟲）和「蝦」組成，可能是地方俗稱
english_meaning: A rare or regional name for a kind of small shrimp; literally 'moth/larva shrimp' (obscure/local term)
explanation_mandarin: 螟蝦在粵語中為罕見或地區性詞彙，字面含義為「螟」（幼蟲）+「蝦」，多用作對某些小蝦的俗稱或方言名稱，在標準詞典中並不常見。
explanation_english: A rare or regional Cantonese term. Literally '螟' (larva/caterpillar) + '蝦' (shrimp). Likely used as a local name for certain small shrimp or as an obscure dialectal word; not common in standard dictionaries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 村入面有人叫嗰種細蝦做螟蝦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyun1 jap6 min6 jau5 jan4 giu3 go2 zung2 sai3 haa1 zou6 ming4 haa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 村里有人把那種小蝦稱為「螟蝦」。
examples.english_sentence: In the village, some people call that kind of small shrimp '螟蝦'.

mandarin_meaning: 狗（侮辱性稱呼，粗俗、帶有辱罵意味的字眼）
english_meaning: dog (derogatory insult; crude term used to disparage someone)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞 / 罵人用語（粗口）
explanation_mandarin: 「蟥䘆（犬）」為罕見或古老的書寫形式，用來表示以「狗」為侮辱對象的罵語。此寫法在現代粵語口語中極少見，且其確切讀音在可考資料中不明或已失傳。多見於欲以繁體異體字或委婉寫法代替粗口的情況下，表達貶低或侮辱的語氣。
explanation_english: "蟥䘆（犬）" is an obscure or archaic written form used to denote an insulting term meaning "dog." It is extremely rare in modern Cantonese usage and its exact pronunciation is not well-documented. The form appears in contexts where writers use uncommon characters or euphemistic orthography to represent coarse language; the sense is derogatory, aimed at belittling someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講嘢咁衰，成個蟥䘆（犬）嘅樣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 je5 gam2 seoi1, sing4 go3 蟳䘆（讀音不詳）ge3 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是講話那麼惡劣，整個人像個謬稱的狗似的。
examples.english_sentence: He always speaks so nastily; he acts like a real dog (used as an insult).

mandarin_meaning: 坐立不安；心裡發癢，急於做某事
english_meaning: feeling restless or antsy; eager/impatient to do something
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，用來形容人心情躁動、坐不住或急於行動，常帶有輕鬆或戲謔語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term describing someone who is restless, fidgety, or itching to do something. Often used informally with a playful tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等飛機嗰陣我一路蟲蟲蟻蟻，想快啲上機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 fei1 gei1 go2 zan6 ngo5 jat1 lou6 cung4 cung4 ngai5 ngai5, soeng2 faai3 di1 seong5 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在等飛機的時候我一直坐立不安，想快點上機。
examples.english_sentence: While waiting for the plane I was feeling restless and wanted to board quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 螞蟻多了也能咬死大象（強調人多力量大、團結能勝過強敵）
english_meaning: Many ants can kill an elephant — strength in numbers; small individuals united can overcome a much larger or stronger opponent.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用螞蟻和大象作比喻，說明即使是微小的個體，只要人多、團結起來，也能擊敗強大的對手。注意：常見的書寫形式是「蟻多咬死象」，字中的「褸」很可能是口語或書寫變體，實際發音為「咬」(ngaau5)。
explanation_english: The phrase uses ants and an elephant as a metaphor to show that many small individuals, when united, can defeat a powerful opponent. Note: the more common written form is "蟻多咬死象"; the character "褸" in the provided form is likely a variant/typo — the pronunciation corresponds to "咬" (ngaau5).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話一個人做唔成，但蟻多褸死象，一齊做就得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 jat1 go3 jan4 zou6 m4 sing4, daan6 ngai5 do1 ngaau5 sei2 zoeng6, jat1 cai4 zou6 zau6 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說一個人做不成，但蟻多咬死象，大家一起做就可以。
examples.english_sentence: He said one person can't do it, but many ants can kill an elephant — if we all work together it'll work.

mandarin_meaning: 蠔灰（蚝灰）：指焙烧或研磨自蠔壳（牡蛎壳）的粉末，主要成分为碳酸钙，常用于中药、补钙、土壤改良或建材原料。
english_meaning: oyster shell ash / calcined oyster-shell powder: powder made from burned or ground oyster shells, mainly calcium carbonate; used in traditional medicine, as a calcium supplement, soil amendment, or building material ingredient.
explanation_mandarin: 蠔灰是將蠔殼焙燒或碾磨後得到的粉末，含有豐富的碳酸鈣，民間用作補鈣、入藥或改善土壤和製磚等用途。
explanation_english: Oyster shell ash is a powder produced by calcining or grinding oyster shells, rich in calcium carbonate. It is traditionally used as a calcium supplement, in herbal medicine, for soil improvement, and in some construction materials.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽買咗包蠔灰，話可以用嚟落湯補鈣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 maai5 zo2 baau1 hou4fui1, waa6 ho2 ji5 jung6 lai4 lok6 tong1 bou2 goi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈买了一包蠔灰，说可以用来放到汤里补钙。
examples.english_sentence: Mom bought a pack of oyster shell ash, saying it can be added to soup to supplement calcium.

mandarin_meaning: 蠔田（指牡蛎养殖地或牡蛎床）
english_meaning: oyster bed; oyster farm (area where oysters are cultivated)
explanation_mandarin: 「蠔田」在粤语中用來指養殖蠔的區域或蠔床，即牡蛎養殖场或养殖区，為較具地方性或口語化的稱呼，在普通话中常用「蠔場」或「牡蛎养殖场」。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '蠔田' refers to an area where oysters are cultivated—an oyster bed or oyster farm. It's a noun, somewhat regional/colloquial; more commonly one might say '蠔場' or 'oyster farm' in Mandarin/English.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝我哋去咗蠔田巡查，見到啲蠔長得好大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 zo2 hou4 tin4 seon4 caa4, gin3 dou3 di1 hou4 zoeng2 dak1 hou2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上我们去蠔田巡查，看到很多牡蛎长得很大。
examples.english_sentence: This morning we went to the oyster beds to inspect and saw many oysters had grown very large.

mandarin_meaning: 蠖（huò）：指尺蠖等以弓形身體前後移動的毛毛蟲，亦可比喻蜿蜒、彎曲蠕動的狀態。
english_meaning: Inchworm (a looping caterpillar); figuratively, to writhe or move in a winding, looping manner.
explanation_mandarin: 「蠖」通常指尺蠖類的毛毛蟲，因其移動時身體呈弓形縮放，故常用來形容彎曲、蠕動的動作或狀態。
explanation_english: “蠖” usually refers to an inchworm (a caterpillar that moves by looping its body). It is also used metaphorically to describe winding or writhing movements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺花園見到一條尺蠖，佢慢慢爬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 faa1 jyun4 gin3 dou2 jat1 tiu4 cek3 wok6, keoi5 maan6 maan6 paa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在花園看到一條尺蠖，它慢慢爬行。
examples.english_sentence: I saw an inchworm in the garden; it was crawling slowly.

mandarin_meaning: 疑为古语中记载的一种小型昆虫名称，现代已罕见，确切所指物种不明
english_meaning: An obscure/archaic name for a small insect recorded in classical texts; rarely used in modern Cantonese and the exact species is uncertain
explanation_mandarin: 「蠗螘」一詞在現代粵語中極少見，主要見於古籍或文獻中，通常泛指小型昆蟲或某種蟲類，但文獻未能明確對應現代分類，屬於文言或方言中的罕用詞。
explanation_english: The term "蠗螘" is extremely rare in modern Cantonese and mainly appears in classical texts or old records. It generally refers to a small insect or some kind of bug, but sources do not clearly identify a corresponding modern species. It is an archaic/obscure lexical item.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字『蠗螘』好少見，多數只喺古書入面出現。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 '蠗螘' hou2 siu2 gin3, do1 sou3 zi2 hai6 gu2 syu1 jap6 min6 ceot1 jin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“蠗螘”很少见，多数只在古书里出现。
examples.english_sentence: The character "蠗螘" is very rare and mostly only appears in ancient books.

mandarin_meaning: 蠟質的綠色（或青色）包裝紙，常用來包燒味、點心等油膩食物
english_meaning: waxed green paper (a wax-coated green/blue wrapping paper commonly used to wrap roast meats, pastries and oily foods)
explanation_mandarin: 在香港常見的一種帶蠟或油性塗層的青色包裝紙，用來包燒味、蛋撻、月餅等，防油防滲但不太環保。
explanation_english: A type of waxed (or oil-coated) green/blue wrapping paper commonly seen in Hong Kong. It's used to wrap roast meats, egg tarts, mooncakes and other oily foods — oil-resistant but not very eco-friendly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 燒味舖會用蠟青紙包住燒鵝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu1 mei6 pou3 wui5 jung6 laap6 ceng1 zi2 baau1 zyu6 siu1 ngo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 燒味店會用蠟青紙包住燒鵝。
examples.english_sentence: The roast-meat shop wraps the roast goose in waxed green paper.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 買蛋撻嗰陣，店員用蠟青紙包好畀我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai5 daan6 taat1 go2 zan6, dim3 jyun4 jung6 laap6 ceng1 zi2 baau1 hou2 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 买蛋挞的时候，店员用蠟青纸包好给我。
examples.english_sentence: When I bought an egg tart, the shop assistant wrapped it in waxed green paper for me.

mandarin_meaning: 古文中指小蟲或幼蟲（少見字，現代漢語中罕用）
english_meaning: a rare/archaic character referring to a small insect or larva (rarely used in modern Chinese)
explanation_mandarin: 「蠯」為罕見漢字，多見於古籍，用來指稱某類小蟲或幼蟲。現代普通話與粵語中很少單獨使用，屬於文言或專名用字。
explanation_english: 蠯 is a rare/archaic character historically used in classical texts to denote a type of small insect or larva. It is seldom used in modern Mandarin or Cantonese outside of textual or scholarly contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本古書入面有寫到「蠯」，講緊一種細蟲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 gu2 syu1 jap6 min6 jau5 se2 dou3 "joek6", gong2 gan2 jat1 zung2 sai3 cung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这本古书里面写到“蠯”，说的是一种小虫。
examples.english_sentence: This ancient book mentions '蠯', referring to a kind of small insect.

mandarin_meaning: （非標準/口語或錯寫）芒果
english_meaning: mango (nonstandard/colloquial or mistaken writing)
explanation_mandarin: 「蠻果」並非標準漢字詞彙，常見作為網絡或口語中的非正式寫法或誤寫，用來表示「芒果」。在粵語中正規寫法為「芒果」（mong1 gwo2），但若按字面讀音「蠻果」可讀作maan4 gwo2，屬於俗寫或少見用法。
explanation_english: “蠻果” is not a standard lexical item; it appears as a nonstandard, colloquial or mistaken spelling used to refer to a mango. The correct/standard term is 芒果 (mong1 gwo2) in Cantonese. If read literally it would be pronounced maan4 gwo2, so this form is treated as an informal/rare variant.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想食蠻果，今日好熱，一啖冰凍蠻果好舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 maan4 gwo2, gam1 jat6 hou2 jit6, jat1 dam2 bing1 dung3 maan4 gwo2 hou2 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想吃蠻果，今天很熱，吃一口冰的蠻果很舒服。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat a mango; it's very hot today, and a bite of chilled mango would feel great.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 其實嗰間菜檔啲蠻果係指芒果，唔係新詞，係俗寫罷了。
examples.jyutping_sentence: kei4 sat6 go2 gaan1 coi3 dong3 di1 maan4 gwo2 hai6 zi2 mong1 gwo2, m4 hai6 san1 ci4, hai6 zuk6 se2 ba3 liu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 其實那間菜檔所說的蠻果是指芒果，並不是新詞，只是俗寫罷了。
examples.english_sentence: Actually, the greengrocer's '蠻果' refers to mango; it's not a new word, just an informal spelling.

jyutping: 不確定（可能讀作 maan4 cing4 coeng1，僅為推測）
mandarin_meaning: 此組合並非常見或被收錄的粵語詞語，可能為罕見寫法、網絡創詞或誤寫/打字錯誤，沒有公認的詞義。若根據字面猜測，可理解為「相當清澈/純粹」之類的意涵，但屬推測。
english_meaning: This combination is not an attested or common Cantonese term; it may be an obscure spelling, a coined internet slang, or a typo, and has no established meaning. Based on the characters alone, one could speculate a sense like "quite clear/pure," but this is conjectural.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 不定／非標準（無公認詞性）
partOfSpeech_english: Undetermined / nonstandard (no established part of speech)
explanation_mandarin: 「蠻澄鋹」不是常見的粵語詞彙或成語。單字分析：蠻（相當、粗野）、澄（清澈、澄清）、鋹（罕見字，可能與金屬或古字形有關）。三字合在一起沒有確定語義或用法，可能是網民創造、地區用語或打字錯誤。若需要準確使用，建議向來源查證或改用已確立的詞語。
explanation_english: "蠻澄鋹" is not a known Cantonese word, idiom, or slang with established usage. Character-wise: 蠻 (fairly, coarse), 澄 (clear, to clarify), 鋹 (a rare character, possibly metal-related or archaic). Together they have no confirmed meaning; this may be a nonce coinage, a regional/online invention, or a typo. For accurate use, verify the source or use a recognized term instead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔確定「蠻澄鋹」係咩意思，聽落好似唔係標準廣東話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 kok3 ding6 「maan4 ceng4 coeng1」 hai6 me1 ji3 si1, teng1 lok6 hou2 ci5 m4 hai6 biu1 zeon2 Gwong2 Dung1 Waa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不確定「蠻澄鋹」是什麼意思，聽起來好像不是標準廣東話。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not sure what "蠻澄鋹" means — it sounds like it's not standard Cantonese.

mandarin_meaning: 不常見粵語俚語（疑似）；可能用來形容草率、亂七八糟地辦事或敷衍了事
english_meaning: Uncommon/uncertain Cantonese slang; possibly describes handling something carelessly or messily—doing a poor, slapdash job.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞（非正式/俚語，待確認）
explanation_mandarin: 此詞在標準粵語辭典中罕見或未被收錄。根據字面與口語推測，可能作為動詞使用，表示以粗心、敷衍或混亂的方式處理事情。亦有可能是地區性變體或聽寫誤差，使用時應向當地說話者確認其準確含義與語境。
explanation_english: This term is rare or not recorded in standard Cantonese dictionaries. Based on literal reading and colloquial inference, it may be used as a verb meaning to handle things carelessly, sloppily, or half‑heartedly. It might also be a regional variant or a misheard form; verify with local speakers before using.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好似蠻班辦，成日整到東歪西倒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 ci5 maan4 baan1 baan6, sing4 jat6 zing2 dou3 dung1 waai1 sai1 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事好像很草率，常常弄得東倒西歪。
examples.english_sentence: He does things sloppily — he often makes a mess of them.

mandarin_meaning: 走過來；走過去方向的動作（口語）
english_meaning: to walk over (here); to come walking (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「行來」是廣東話口語用法，表示朝說話者或某方向走過來／走近，常見於日常會話（相當於普通話的「走過來／過來」）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to walk over or come walking toward someone or a place. It functions as a directional verb similar to Mandarin "走過來" or English "come over (walking)".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你行嚟做咩呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 haang4 lai4 zou6 me1 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你走過來做什麼？
examples.english_sentence: Why are you coming over? / What are you doing coming over here?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等陣你行嚟我哋一齊食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 zan6 nei5 haang4 lai4 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等一下你過來我們一起吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: Wait until you come over and we'll eat together.

mandarin_meaning: 上床；與某人發生性關係
english_meaning: to sleep with someone; to have sexual intercourse (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，通常指與某人發生性關係或上床。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang that usually means to have sexual intercourse with someone (to sleep with someone).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講佢同個同事行床咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 keoi5 tung4 go3 tung4 si6 hang4 cong4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽說他和那個同事上床了。
examples.english_sentence: I heard he slept with that colleague.

jyutping: haang4 wan6 haang4 dou3 goek3 zi2 gung1
mandarin_meaning: 運氣好到極點/好運延伸到腳趾
english_meaning: extremely lucky; luck has reached one's toes
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，用來形容運氣非常好，好運似乎延伸到身體最末端（腳趾），表示極其幸運。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone is extremely lucky — as if their good luck has reached their toes. Used to emphasize very fortunate circumstances.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日中咗頭獎，真係行運行到腳趾公！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 zung1 zo2 tau4 zoeng2, zan1 hai6 haang4 wan6 haang4 dou3 goek3 zi2 gung1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天中了頭獎，真是運氣好到極點！
examples.english_sentence: I won the jackpot today — I'm extremely lucky!

mandarin_meaning: 众所周知 / 家喻户晓
english_meaning: widely known; everyone has heard of it
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 片語 / 俗語（成語性用法）
explanation_mandarin: 表示某事或某人非常有名，人人聽聞、眾所周知。
explanation_english: Indicates something or someone is very well-known; everyone has heard about it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事已經係行雷都聽聞，冇人唔知道。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ji5 ging1 hai6 haang4 leoi4 dou1 ting1 man4, mou5 jan4 m4 zi1 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事已经众所周知，没人不知道。
examples.english_sentence: This matter is already well-known; everyone knows about it.

mandarin_meaning: 邻里大姐 / 街坊阿姨（指住在附近的年長女性，常指熱心或愛管閒事的鄰居）
english_meaning: neighborhood auntie / local auntie (an older woman in the neighborhood, often helpful or a bit of a busybody)
explanation_mandarin: 「街坊大姐」用來稱呼或形容住在同一社區、年紀較大的女性。語義可以偏向親切、熱心幫忙，也可帶有愛管閒事、八卦的意味，視語境而定。
explanation_english: “街坊大姐” refers to an older woman living in the neighborhood. The term can be affectionate—referring to a helpful local woman—or mildly pejorative, implying a nosy or gossipy neighbor, depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隔離街嗰位街坊大姐成日幫我哋買餸，真係好熱心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaak3 lei4 gaai1 go2 wai6 gaai1 fong1 daai6 ze2 sing4 jat6 bong1 ngo5 dei6 maai5 sung3, zan1 hai6 hou2 jit6 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 隔壁那條街的街坊大姐經常幫我們買菜，真的很熱心。
examples.english_sentence: The neighborhood auntie down the street often helps us buy groceries; she's really kind.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有時街坊大姐會八卦，乜嘢事都想知，大家要有心理準備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 si4 gaai1 fong1 daai6 ze2 wui5 baat3 gwaa3, mat1 je5 si6 dou1 soeng2 zi1, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 jau5 sam1 lei5 zeon2 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有時街坊大姐會愛八卦，什麼事都想知道，大家要有心理準備。
examples.english_sentence: Sometimes the neighborhood auntie is nosy and wants to know everything, so be prepared.

mandarin_meaning: 街巷；街道與巷弄
english_meaning: streets and alleys; lanes and byways
explanation_mandarin: 指城市或鄉鎮中的街道與巷弄，常用來描述一帶的街區或巷道聚集。
explanation_english: Refers to streets and alleys in a town or city; often used to describe a network or area of lanes and thoroughfares.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊區嘅街巷充滿歷史氣息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 keoi1 ge3 gaai1 hong6 cung1 mun5 lik6 si2 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 旧区的街巷充满历史气息。
examples.english_sentence: The streets and alleys of the old district are full of historical ambience.

mandarin_meaning: 趁天晴修補漏處；比喻趁有利時機處理問題
english_meaning: Fix leaks while the sky is clear; take advantage of favorable conditions to deal with problems
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是趁天氣晴朗的時候修補漏處，常用來比喻在有利時機時盡快解決問題或做好準備。
explanation_english: Literally 'repair leaks while the sky is clear.' Used figuratively to mean taking advantage of a favorable moment to fix problems or make preparations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋大廈個天台最近有啲漏水，補漏趁天晴，趁今日冇落雨快啲整好佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 daai6 haa6 go3 tin1 toi4 zeoi3 gan6 jau5 di1 lau6 seoi2, bou2 lau6 can3 tin1 cing4, can3 gam1 jat6 mou5 lok6 jyu5 faai3 di1 zing2 hou2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們大廈的天台最近有點漏水，趁天晴補漏，趁今天沒下雨趕快修好它。
examples.english_sentence: The rooftop of our building has been leaking recently. Fix leaks while the sky is clear — since it's not raining today, quickly get it repaired.

mandarin_meaning: 愛炫耀的人；愛出風頭的人（廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: a show-off; someone who likes to flaunt or boast (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「表士」是廣東話口語／俚語，用來形容愛炫耀、愛賣弄、喜歡出風頭的人。字面可聯想到「表」（名錶、展示）與「士」（人）結合，帶有貶義或戲謔意味，常用於香港日常對話中。
explanation_english: "表士" is Cantonese colloquial/slang for a person who shows off or likes to flaunt. Literally combining "表" (watch/display) and "士" (person), it carries a mildly pejorative or teasing tone and is commonly used in Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日戴名錶，好似個表士咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 daai3 ming4 biu2, hou2 ci5 go3 biu2 si6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是戴名表，好像個愛炫耀的人。
examples.english_sentence: He always wears designer watches, like a show-off.

mandarin_meaning: 误示好感；让别人误以为你对他/她有情感或暧昧
english_meaning: to give the wrong impression of affection; to make someone mistakenly think you have romantic interest
explanation_mandarin: 指不小心或故意的言行讓別人誤以為自己對對方有感情或有意思，造成誤會。
explanation_english: Refers to words or actions that accidentally or deliberately lead someone to believe you have romantic interest in them, causing a misunderstanding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好表錯情，佢已經有女朋友喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 biu2 co3 cing4, keoi5 ji5 ging1 jau5 neoi5 pang4 jau5 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要表错情，他/她已经有女朋友了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't give the wrong impression — he/she already has a girlfriend.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想畀人表錯情，所以我冇回覆佢啲訊息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 biu2 co3 cing4, so2 ji5 ngo5 mou5 wui4 fuk1 keoi5 di1 seon3 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想讓別人誤會我的感情，所以我沒有回覆他的訊息。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want people to misunderstand my feelings, so I didn't reply to his messages.

cantonese: 衫烂从小补，病从浅中医
jyutping: saam1 laan6 cung4 siu2 bou2, beng6 cung4 cin2 zung1 ji1
mandarin_meaning: 衣服破了要趁小補，生病不要隨便求助淺薄或不專業的中醫；強調小問題早處理、看病要謹慎選醫生。
english_meaning: A proverb advising to fix small problems early (mend clothes while the tear is small) and warning against relying on superficial or unqualified Chinese doctors when ill; in short, nip problems in the bud and be careful whom you consult for health issues.
explanation_mandarin: 前半句用修補衣物作比喻，說明小問題應及早處理；後半句提醒就醫要謹慎，不要因輕信不專業的人而造成更大問題。
explanation_english: The first half uses mending clothes as a metaphor for handling small problems early; the second half cautions about seeing superficial or unqualified practitioners for illness. Overall it advises early prevention and prudent choice of medical help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日話：『衫烂从小补，病从浅中医』，有事就應該早啲睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 waa6: 'saam1 laan6 cung4 siu2 bou2, beng6 cung4 cin2 zung1 ji1', jau5 si6 zau6 jing1 goi1 zou2 di1 tai2 ji1 saang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我媽媽常說：「衫烂从小补，病从浅中医」，有事應該及早看醫生。
examples.english_sentence: My mom always says, 'Mend clothes when the tear is small; don't rely on superficial Chinese doctors' — if something's wrong you should see a doctor early.

mandarin_meaning: 糟糕透顶 / 非常倒霉或很坏
english_meaning: extremely bad; terribly unlucky; awful
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俗语，用来形容某事或某人非常糟糕、倒霉或令人讨厌。用于强调负面程度，语气强烈，带有口语色彩，常见于香港日常用语。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang expression used to describe something or someone as extremely bad, unlucky, or detestable. It strongly emphasizes a negative degree and is informal, commonly heard in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試我衰到爆，連最簡單嗰題都答錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 ngo5 seoi1 dou3 baau3, lin4 zeoi3 gaan2 daan1 go2 tai4 dou1 daap3 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试我倒霉到爆，连最简单的题都答错。
examples.english_sentence: I was extremely unlucky in this exam; I even got the easiest questions wrong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係衰到爆，成日喺背後講我嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 seoi1 dou3 baau3, sing4 jat6 hai2 bui3 hau6 gong2 ngo5 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的是太坏了，总是在背后说我的坏话。
examples.english_sentence: He's really awful—always talking badly about me behind my back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝落雨又塞車，真係衰到爆！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 lok6 jyu5 jau6 sak1 ce1, zan1 hai6 seoi1 dou3 baau3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上下雨又塞车，真是倒霉透顶！
examples.english_sentence: It rained this morning and there were traffic jams—what a terrible day!

mandarin_meaning: 倒霉到极点 / 坏到极点（口语）
english_meaning: extremely unlucky; utterly pathetic/despicable (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，表示非常倒霉、非常糟糕或（形容人）非常惡劣、可恥。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning extremely unlucky or utterly pathetic; can also describe someone as exceptionally nasty or despicable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝遲到仲落大雨，真係衰到貼地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 ci4 dou3 zung6 lok6 daai6 jyu5, zan1 hai6 sui1 dou3 tip3 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上迟到又下大雨，真是倒霉到极点。
examples.english_sentence: I was late this morning and it poured — I'm really extremely unlucky.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁樣真係衰到貼地，唔值得信任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 joeng6 zan1 hai6 sui1 dou3 tip3 dei6, m4 zik1 dak1 seon3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这样真的衰到贴地，不值得信任。
examples.english_sentence: He's really despicable like that; not trustworthy.

mandarin_meaning: 嘴巴刻薄又多嘴（爱说别人坏话或爱插手别人的事）
english_meaning: spiteful and overly talkative; a person who gossips, badmouths others or sticks their nose into others' affairs
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人既愛多嘴又帶有刻薄、愛說閒話或在背後講別人壞話，常帶貶義且屬於廣東話口語用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who talks too much in a mean or meddlesome way — gossips, badmouths others, or constantly interferes. It's informal and usually negative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢衰多口，成日喺背後同人講人壞話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 do1 hau2, sing4 jat6 hai2 bui3 hau6 tung4 jan4 gong2 jan4 waai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他嘴巴不饶人，經常在背後說別人的壞話。
examples.english_sentence: He's mean-mouthed and talkative; he often badmouths others behind their backs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係唔鍾意同佢玩，衰多口，乜嘢都要插一腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 wun2, seoi1 do1 hau2, mat1 je5 dou1 jiu3 caap3 jat1 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真的不喜歡和他來往，他愛多嘴，什麼都要插一腳。
examples.english_sentence: I really don't like hanging out with him; he's always sticking his nose in and commenting on everything.

mandarin_meaning: 比偷猫还坏（形容人卑鄙、无良或非常可恶）
english_meaning: Literal: "worse than stealing cats." Idiomatic: despicable; very mean or unscrupulous.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，字面意思是「比偷猫还要坏」，用來形容一個人非常卑鄙、無良或做了很壞的事情。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "worse than stealing cats." It is used to describe someone as particularly nasty, mean, or morally unscrupulous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗自己利益騙晒人，真係衰过偷猫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 zi6 gei2 lei6 jik6 pin3 saai3 jan4, zan1 hai6 seoi1 gwo3 tau1 maau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了自己的利益欺騙了大家，真是比偷猫还坏。
examples.english_sentence: He cheated everyone for his own benefit — he's really despicable (worse than a cat thief).

jyutping: seoi1 hoi1 lai4 jau5 tau4 jau5 lou6
mandarin_meaning: 雖然一開始看起來倒楣或不順，但仍有出路或前途
english_meaning: Though it starts off badly or seems unlucky, there is still a way forward or prospects
explanation_mandarin: 「衰開嚟有頭有路」是廣東話口語，用來形容事情或人一開始看似倒楣、不順，但其實仍有出路或前途。語氣可帶安慰或諷刺，視語境而定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning that although something seems unlucky or starts off badly, it still has prospects or a viable way forward. The tone can be consoling or sarcastic depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份生意起初睇落衰開嚟有頭有路，點知半年之後已經賺到錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 saang1 ji3 hei2 co1 tai2 lok6 seoi1 hoi1 lai4 jau5 tau4 jau5 lou6, dim2 zi1 bun3 nin4 zi1 hau6 ji5 ging1 zaan6 dou3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這門生意一開始看起來很糟，但半年之後竟然已經賺到錢。
examples.english_sentence: This business looked bad at first, but six months later it was already making money.

mandarin_meaning: 用襪子、絲襪或其他布料臨時做成的胸罩／無肩帶上衣（俗稱、俚語）
english_meaning: A makeshift bra or tube-top made from socks, stockings, or other fabric; a slang term for a DIY/temporary chest covering
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱用絲襪、襪子或其他布料臨時製成，用來頂替胸罩或作無肩帶上衣的物品。常見於應急或非正式情況，有時帶有調侃意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang term for a makeshift bra or strapless top fashioned from socks, stockings, or other fabric to temporarily replace a bra. Often used in informal or emergency situations and sometimes said jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日冇帶胸圍，只係用條襪胸頂住出門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 mou5 daai3 hung1 wai4, zi2 hai6 jung6 tiu4 mat6 hung1 ding2 zyu6 ceot1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她今天沒帶胸罩，只好用襪子做成的臨時胸罩頂著出門。
examples.english_sentence: She didn't bring a bra today, so she had to use a sock-made makeshift bra to get by when going out.

mandarin_meaning: 被褥和蚊帐
english_meaning: bedding (quilt/bedclothes) and mosquito net
explanation_mandarin: 指睡覺時使用的被褥（被子、床單等）和蚊帳，通常在夏天或有蚊蟲的地方使用以防蚊咬。
explanation_english: Refers to bedding (quilt, bedclothes, etc.) and a mosquito net used while sleeping, typically used in summer or in mosquito-prone places to prevent bites.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天去鄉下，記得帶埋被铺蚊帐，夜晚先唔驚畀蚊咬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 heoi3 hoeng1 haa6, gei3 dak1 daai3 maai4 bei3 pou1 man4 zoeng3, je6 maan5 sin1 m4 geng1 bei2 man4 ngaau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天去乡下，记得把被褥和蚊帐带上，晚上就不怕被蚊子咬了。
examples.english_sentence: When you go to the countryside in summer, remember to bring your bedding and mosquito net so you're not afraid of being bitten by mosquitoes at night.

mandarin_meaning: 有裡襯的（衣物）；舊時用字，指衣服有內裡或夾層
english_meaning: lined (of clothing); a garment with an inner lining
explanation_mandarin: 「袷」通常用來形容衣物有裏襯或夾層，使衣服更保暖或更挺括。多見於複合詞或描述服裝結構的語境中。
explanation_english: Used to describe clothing that has an inner lining or layer, making it warmer or giving it structure. Commonly appears in compound terms or when describing garment construction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫係袷㗎，好舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 hai6 gaap3 gaa3, hou2 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件衣服有里衬，很舒服。
examples.english_sentence: This garment is lined and very comfortable.

jyutping: coi4 fung4 dou6 san1, jau5 fan1 cyun3
mandarin_meaning: 量身定做、恰到好处；形容做事或穿着合适、有分寸
english_meaning: Tailor-made; appropriate and well-proportioned — to act or dress with moderation and good judgment, or to make something to fit an individual's needs
explanation_mandarin: 比喻像裁缝为客人量身裁制衣服一样，根據實際需要斟酌拿捏，表示合適、有分寸或量身定做。
explanation_english: A figurative phrase meaning 'tailor-made' or 'to have a sense of proportion' — doing something appropriately and with good judgment, or creating something fitted to a person's needs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 設計師為客人度身訂造，真係裁缝度身，有分寸，件衫好啱身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sit3 gai3 si1 wai6 haak3 jan4 dou6 san1 deng6 zou6, zan1 hai6 coi4 fung4 dou6 san1, jau5 fan1 cyun3, gin6 saam1 hou2 aam1 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 设计师为顾客量身订做，真是裁缝度身、有分寸，衣服非常合身。
examples.english_sentence: The designer tailored the garment for the client — truly tailor-made and well-proportioned; the clothes fit perfectly.

mandarin_meaning: 装可怜／装弱／装无辜
english_meaning: to pretend to be pitiful/innocent/helpless to gain sympathy or avoid responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 表示故意裝作可憐、無辜或軟弱，以博取同情、逃避責任或達到某種目的的廣東話口語表達，帶貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression meaning to feign pity, innocence, or helplessness to win sympathy, shirk responsibility, or achieve some aim; generally derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再裝假狗啦，自己做錯嘢要負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 zong1 gaa2 gau2 laa1, zi6 gei2 zou6 co3 je5 jiu3 fu6 zaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再裝可憐了，自己做錯事要負責。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pretend to be pitiful anymore; take responsibility for your own mistakes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對上司裝假狗，就想攞多啲面子同升職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 deoi3 soeng6 si1 zong1 gaa2 gau2, zau6 soeng2 lo2 do1 di1 min6 zi2 tung4 sing1 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是對上司裝可憐，就是想多拿點面子和升職。
examples.english_sentence: He always acts pitiful in front of his boss; he's just trying to gain face and get promoted.

mandarin_meaning: 装上弹弓；（口语）比喻准备反击或报复、蓄势待发
english_meaning: Literally 'load a slingshot'; colloquially 'prepare to retaliate' or 'gear up for an attack/action'.
explanation_mandarin: 原指把彈弓裝好準備射擊，口語用法常比喻某人準備反擊、報復或蓄勢待發。
explanation_english: Originally means to load a slingshot ready to shoot. In colloquial Cantonese it often figuratively means someone is preparing to retaliate, strike back, or get ready for action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀人笑完之後就開始裝彈弓，話要報仇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 siu3 jyun4 zi1 hau6 zau6 hoi1 ci2 zong1 daan6 gung1, waa6 jiu3 bou3 cau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人嘲笑後就開始装弹弓，說要報仇。
examples.english_sentence: After being mocked, he started 'loading his slingshot', saying he would take revenge.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友喺度裝彈弓，準備射石仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 hai2 dou6 zong1 daan6 gung1, zeon2 bei6 se6 sek6 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友在那裡装弹弓，準備射石子。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are loading a slingshot, preparing to shoot pebbles.

mandarin_meaning: 衣衫不整；混亂、狼狽的樣子（俚語）
english_meaning: to be disheveled or in complete disarray (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，字面指裙子被拉、褲子掉落，用來形容人或場面非常凌亂、狼狽或失控。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression literally meaning 'skirt pulled, pants fallen.' It describes a person or situation that is very messy, disheveled, embarrassed, or out of control.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽搞到好亂，場面裙拉裤甩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 gaau2 dou3 hou2 lyun6, coeng4 min6 kwan4 laai1 fu3 lat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽搞得很亂，場面一片混亂。
examples.english_sentence: The competition turned into a mess; the scene was complete chaos.

mandarin_meaning: 裝傻、裝無辜、裝作不知情
english_meaning: to play dumb; to feign ignorance or innocence
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語/俚語，指故意裝作不知、不懂或無辜，以逃避責任或掩飾行為。常用於批評別人假裝無辜或躲避責任的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term meaning to deliberately pretend not to know, to play dumb or feign innocence—usually to avoid responsibility or hide one's actions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺老細面前裝假笱，話自己唔知犯咗錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 lou5 sai3 min6 cin4 zong1 gaa2 gau1, waa6 zi6 gei2 m4 zi1 faan6 zo2 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成日在老闆面前裝傻，說自己不知道犯了錯。
examples.english_sentence: He always plays dumb in front of the boss, saying he didn't know he made a mistake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再裝假笱啦，事實已經擺喺度，大家都見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 zong1 gaa2 gau1 laa3, si6 sat6 ji5 ging1 baai2 hai2 dou6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再裝假笱了，事實已經擺在那裡，大家都看到了。
examples.english_sentence: Stop pretending — the facts are already there and everyone has seen them.

mandarin_meaning: 裝腔作勢；擺架子
english_meaning: to put on airs; to act arrogantly or show off
explanation_mandarin: 「裝頂」是廣東話口語俚語，意思是故意擺出高人一等或裝腔作勢的態度，多帶貶義，用來形容某人愛顯擺或裝出高姿態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to put on airs or act superior. It describes behaving arrogantly or showing off and typically carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度裝頂，好討厭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 zong1 ding2, hou2 tou2 jim3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在那裡裝腔作勢，真討厭。
examples.english_sentence: He's always putting on airs; it's really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺我面前裝頂啦，我哋係朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: M4 hou2 hai2 ngo5 min6 cin4 zong1 ding2 laa1, ngo5 dei6 hai6 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在我面前擺架子，我們是朋友。
examples.english_sentence: Don't put on airs in front of me — we're friends.

mandarin_meaning: 包（裹）並蒸粽子；包粽子、做粽子
english_meaning: to wrap and steam zongzi (sticky rice dumplings); to make zongzi
explanation_mandarin: 指把糯米和餡料包在粽葉裡並蒸（或煮）成粽子，常見於端午節前後的傳統料理和家庭活動。在廣東話語境中也可稱為參與做粽子的動作。
explanation_english: Refers to wrapping glutinous rice and fillings in leaves and steaming (or cooking) zongzi. It is a common activity around the Dragon Boat Festival and can refer to taking part in making zongzi.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 下個禮拜我要返屋企幫阿媽裹蒸粽子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 ngo5 jiu3 faan1 uk1 kei2 bong1 aa3 maa1 gwo2 zing1 zung6 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 下个礼拜我要回家帮妈妈包粽子。
examples.english_sentence: Next week I'll go home to help my mother make (wrap and steam) zongzi.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 鄰居已經開始裹蒸粽子，屋企充滿糯米同肉嘅香味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: leon4 geoi1 ji5 ging1 hoi1 ci2 gwo2 zing1 zung6 zi2, uk1 kei2 cung1 mun5 no6 mai5 tung4 juk6 ge3 hoeng1 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 邻居已经开始裹蒸粽子了，家里充满了糯米和肉的香味。
examples.english_sentence: The neighbors have already started making zongzi; the house is filled with the aroma of glutinous rice and meat.

jyutping: lou4 so1 ji1 gau3 fo2, je5 fo2 soeng5 san1
mandarin_meaning: 好心救火卻招來麻煩／自找麻煩；想幫忙反而把自己捲入困境
english_meaning: To try to help but instead invite trouble for oneself; to get burned while trying to put out a fire (i.e. cause trouble for oneself by intervening).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容本意是幫忙或想解決問題，結果卻惹來更多麻煩或把自己捲入困境。
explanation_english: Used to describe a situation where someone's attempt to help or fix a problem results in more trouble or causes the helper to get into trouble themselves.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢本來想幫，但褛蓑衣救火，惹火上身，最後要自己負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bun2 loi4 soeng2 bong1, daan6 lou4 so1 ji1 gau3 fo2, je5 fo2 soeng5 san1, zeoi6 hau6 jiu3 zi6 gei2 fu6 zaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他本來想幫忙，但好心救火結果惹來麻煩，最後要自己負責。
examples.english_sentence: He originally wanted to help, but by trying to put out the fire he invited trouble and ended up having to take responsibility himself.

mandarin_meaning: 把手搭在別人肩上（表示親近或依靠）
english_meaning: to put one's arm around someone’s shoulder; to lean on/put an arm over someone (showing closeness or support)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指把手或手臂搭在別人肩膀上，常用以表示親近、安慰或倚靠。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to place one's arm over someone else's shoulder, often to show closeness, comfort, or to lean on them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到舊同學，就褡膊打招呼，好似好熟咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 gau6 tung4 hok6, zau6 daap3 bok3 daa2 ziu1 fu1, hou2 ci5 hou2 suk6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到舊同學，就把手搭在（對方）肩上打招呼，好像很熟悉。
examples.english_sentence: He saw an old classmate and put his arm around them to greet them, as if they were very close.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）裤子有洞；（口语）形容很穷或衣衫破旧
english_meaning: (literal) pants have a hole; (colloquial) to be very poor or wearing shabby clothes
explanation_mandarin: “褲穿窿”字面意思是褲子出現洞。有時用作口語說法，表示人很窮、衣服破爛。
explanation_english: Literally 'pants have a hole.' Used literally for torn pants and colloquially to describe being very poor or wearing shabby clothes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家窮到褲都穿窿，連飯都無錢買。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 kung4 dou3 fu3 dou1 cyun1 lung4, lin4 faan6 dou1 mou5 cin2 maai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我现在穷到裤子都有洞，连饭都没钱买。
examples.english_sentence: I'm so poor my pants have holes; I don't even have money to buy food.

mandarin_meaning: （不確定）疑為「褲襠／褲檔」，指褲子中間的檔位或褲子的下身、內褲部位
english_meaning: uncertain — likely refers to the crotch/crotch area of pants or underwear
explanation_mandarin: 詞中含罕見字「𧚅」，在可查資料中並不常見。根據用法推測，此寫法可能為口語或方言寫法，用來表示「褲襠／褲檔」（褲子的中間檔位）或泛指下身/內褲。由於資料有限，上述意義為推測，非權威定義。
explanation_english: The entry contains the rare character 𧚅 and is not commonly found in standard references. Based on usage patterns it appears to be a colloquial or dialectal spelling referring to the crotch area of trousers (the crotch/pant gusset) or more generally underwear/lower-body area. This is a tentative interpretation due to limited sources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢條褲𧚅裂咗，好尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tiu4 fu3 dong1 lit3 zo2, hou2 gam2 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的褲襠裂了，很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: His crotch split, very embarrassing.

mandarin_meaning: 甜言蜜语；花言巧语，用甜言来讨好或说服别人
english_meaning: sweet talk; flattering or seductive speech used to ingratiate or persuade someone
explanation_mandarin: “西施舌”是粤语俗语，形容用甜言或讨好话来哄骗、讨好或取得别人信任的说话方式，常带贬义。
explanation_english: “西施舌” is a Cantonese slang/idiom referring to honeyed or flattering speech used to cajole, ingratiate, or persuade others; often carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日用西施舌，想攞到老細信任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jung6 sai1 si1 sit3, soeng2 lok6 dou3 lou5 sai3 seon3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她总是用甜言蜜语，想取得老板的信任。
examples.english_sentence: He/She always uses sweet talk, trying to gain the boss's trust.

mandarin_meaning: 回扣；佣金；好處費（俗語）
english_meaning: kickback; rebate; commission (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「西水」是香港粵語俗語，常指供應商、經銷商或中介給予的暗中回扣或佣金。書寫上常見變體「洗水」（發音sai2 seoi2）。視語境可指合法的佣金或非法的回扣／賄賂。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese slang, "西水" refers to a hidden rebate, kickback, or commission paid to agents, middlemen, or staff. It is often written as "洗水" (pronounced sai2 seoi2). Depending on context it can mean a legitimate commission or an illicit kickback.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個供應商俾咗啲西水俾個業務員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 gung1 jing3 soeng1 bei2 zo2 di1 sai1 seoi2 bei2 go3 jip6 mou6 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 供應商給了業務員一些回扣。
examples.english_sentence: The supplier gave the salesperson some kickbacks.

mandarin_meaning: 回扣大；收取高額回扣或佣金
english_meaning: large kickback; receiving a big illicit commission
explanation_mandarin: 「西水」在廣東話俚語中指回扣、佣金或暗中收取的利益，「西水大」表示回扣或佣金數額很大，通常帶有貶義，暗示交易中有人牟取不當利益。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, "西水" refers to a kickback, commission, or secretly obtained payment. "西水大" means the kickback or commission is large. It often has a negative connotation, implying illicit or excessive profit from a deal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺呢單生意入面收咗好大嘅西水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ni1 daan1 sang1 ji3 jap6 min6 sau1 zo2 hou2 daai6 ge3 sai1 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在這宗生意中收了很大的回扣。
examples.english_sentence: He took a large kickback in this deal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個項目西水大，啲中間人賺到盡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hoeng6 muk6 sai1 seoi2 daai6, di1 zung1 gaan1 jan4 zaan6 dou3 zeon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個項目的回扣很大，中間人都賺翻了。
examples.english_sentence: The kickbacks on this project are huge; the middlemen are making a fortune.

mandarin_meaning: 马铃薯（洋芋、土豆）
english_meaning: potato (Solanum tuberosum)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语中对由西方引入的块茎作物的称呼，通常指马铃薯（即土豆）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term referring to the Western tuber crop, typically the potato (Solanum tuberosum).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚整咗西洋藷蓉配牛扒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 zing2 zo2 sai1 joeng4 syu4 jung4 pui3 ngau4 paa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我做了土豆泥配牛排。
examples.english_sentence: I made mashed potatoes to go with steak tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 市場啲西洋藷好新鮮，一斤幾蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si5 coeng4 di1 sai1 joeng4 syu4 hou2 san1 sin1, jat1 gan1 gei2 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市场上的土豆很新鲜，一斤几块钱。
examples.english_sentence: The potatoes at the market are very fresh; about a few dollars per catty.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）西綱魚；可能為錯別字，原意可能是「西貢魚」（西貢的魚）
english_meaning: Literal: "west-gang fish"; likely a misspelling of "西貢魚" (Sai Kung fish) — i.e., fish from Sai Kung
explanation_mandarin: 「西綱魚」並非常見的粵語詞彙。逐字義為「西」「綱」「魚」，但在香港語境中較可能是打錯字或筆誤，原本想寫的是「西貢魚」（指西貢出產或在西貢買到的魚）。若用作俗稱，沒有被廣泛確認的固定含義。
explanation_english: "西綱魚" is not a common Cantonese expression. Literally it reads as "west - gang/net - fish," but in Hong Kong context it is likely a typo for "西貢魚" (Sai Kung fish), meaning fish from Sai Kung. There is no well-established idiomatic or slang meaning for this exact spelling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頭先喺街市見到有人寫「西綱魚」，我估係打錯字，應該係「西貢魚」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4 sin1 hai2 gaai1 si5 gin3 dou3 jau5 jan4 se2 「sai1 gong1 jyu4」, ngo5 gu3 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6, jing1 goi1 hai6 「sai1 gung3 jyu4」.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我剛才在街市看到有人寫「西綱魚」，我猜是打錯字，應該是「西貢魚」。
examples.english_sentence: I just saw someone write "西綱魚" at the market; I think it's a typo — it should be "西貢魚" (fish from Sai Kung).

mandarin_meaning: 西关人；来自广州西关地区的人（含地域与文化身份的意味）
english_meaning: a person from Xiguan (the historic Xiguan district of Guangzhou); an Xiguan native
explanation_mandarin: 「西關地」是粤语俗称，用来指代来自广州西关一带的本地人或有西关背景的人，有时也带有地域、方言或传统文化身份的含义。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term referring to someone from Xiguan, the historic district in Guangzhou. It denotes local origin or cultural identity and can imply local accent or traditional background.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係西關地出身，好識講廣府話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 sai1 gwaan1 dei6 ceot1 san1, hou2 sik1 gong2 gwong2 fu2 waa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是西关人出身，很会讲广府话。
examples.english_sentence: He is from Xiguan and speaks Cantonese (Guangfu dialect) fluently.

cantonese: 西闪雨重重，南闪猛南风，北闪江水涨，东闪日头红
jyutping: sai1 sim2 jyu5 zung6 zung6, naam4 sim2 maang5 naam4 fung1, bak1 sim2 gong1 seoi2 zoeng3, dung1 sim2 jat6 tau4 hung4
mandarin_meaning: 根据闪电出现的方位来判断天气或水况：西闪意味着会下大雨，南闪意味着有强南风，北闪意味着江水上涨，东闪意味着太阳发红（与天气变化有关）。
english_meaning: A weather proverb: the direction of lightning predicts conditions — lightning in the west means heavy rain; in the south signals strong southerly winds; in the north indicates the river will rise; in the east the sun appears red.
explanation_mandarin: 这是粤语的俗谚，通过观察闪电出现的方向，判断接下来可能出现的降雨、风向或水位变化，多用于沿海或以航海、捕鱼为业的社群中作为经验性天气预报。
explanation_english: A Cantonese weather proverb that uses the direction of lightning as an omen: fishermen and coastal communities traditionally used it to anticipate rain, wind direction, or rising water levels as a practical, experience-based forecast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老一輩經常講：西閃雨重重，南閃猛南風，北閃江水漲，東閃日頭紅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jat1 bui3 ging1 soeng4 gong2: sai1 sim2 jyu5 zung6 zung6, naam4 sim2 maang5 naam4 fung1, bak1 sim2 gong1 seoi2 zoeng3, dung1 sim2 jat6 tau4 hung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老人常说：西闪（电）会下大雨，南闪表示有强南风，北闪说明江水会涨，东闪则太阳发红。
examples.english_sentence: The older generation often says: if lightning flashes in the west it means heavy rain; in the south it signals strong southerly wind; in the north the river will rise; in the east the sun turns red.

cantonese: 西风吹过昼，大水浸过灶
jyutping: sai1 fung1 ceoi1 gwo3 zau3, daai6 seoi2 zam3 gwo3 zou6
mandarin_meaning: 西风在白天吹过，洪水淹没灶台；指不祥的徵兆，预示将有灾祸或不幸到来
english_meaning: "When the west wind blows by day, a great flood will reach the stove." A Cantonese folk saying — an omen of disaster; used to warn of impending misfortune or household calamity.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的民間俗語，原本源於對天氣和水患的觀察。常用來形容形勢不妙或預示災禍將至，也可比喻一連串麻煩接踵而至。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk proverb originally linked to weather observations (west wind by day followed by flooding). It is used to indicate an ill omen or that trouble and misfortune are coming, and can be used metaphorically for a series of problems hitting at once.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆話：「西風吹過晝，大水浸過灶」，提醒我哋要做足防風同防洪嘅準備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 waa6: 'sai1 fung1 ceoi1 gwo3 zau3, daai6 seoi2 zam3 gwo3 zou6', tai4 sing2 ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zou6 zuk1 fong4 fung1 tung4 fong4 hung4 ge3 zeon2 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶說：「西風吹過晝，大水浸過灶」，提醒我們要做好防風防洪的準備。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma said, 'When the west wind blows by day, a great flood will reach the stove,' warning us to prepare for wind and flooding.

mandarin_meaning: 要漂亮不要命（图漂亮不顾性命）
english_meaning: Prioritize looking good over safety or life; willing to risk harm to appear attractive
explanation_mandarin: 形容為了追求外表或上鏡、好看，而不顧安全、健康，甚至可能危及生命。常用作批評或半開玩笑的說法。
explanation_english: Describes someone who values appearance so much that they ignore safety or health, even risking their life; often used critically or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日著高踭鞋落街，真係要靚唔要命。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zoek3 gou1 zaang1 haai4 lok6 gaai1, zan1 hai6 jiu3 leng3 m4 jiu3 ming6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她老是穿高跟鞋出門，真是圖漂亮不顧性命。
examples.english_sentence: She always wears high heels out; it's like she cares more about looking good than her safety.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗影張靚相佢爬上嗰座岩石，朋友話佢真係要靚唔要命。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 jing2 zoeng1 leng3 soeng2 keoi5 paa4 soeng5 go2 zo6 ngaam4 sek6, pang4 jau5 waa6 keoi5 zan1 hai6 jiu3 leng3 m4 jiu3 ming6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了拍張漂亮照片他爬上那塊岩石，朋友說他真是圖漂亮不顧性命。
examples.english_sentence: To get a nice photo he climbed onto that rock; his friends said he really values looking good more than his life.

mandarin_meaning: 為了面子或堅持己見、不顧後果（寧可拼命也要如此）
english_meaning: to be stubborn/obstinate to the point of risking everything; to insist on something regardless of the consequences
explanation_mandarin: 形容一個人為了堅持自己的面子或立場，不顧危險或後果，固執到底。
explanation_english: Describes someone who insists on keeping face or sticking to their position at all costs, ignoring danger or consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗面子要颈唔要命，點都唔肯認錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 min6 zi2 jiu3 geng2 m4 jiu3 ming6, dim2 dou1 m4 hang2 jing6 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了面子要頸唔要命，怎麼都不肯認錯。
examples.english_sentence: He's so fixated on saving face that he refuses to admit he's wrong, no matter what.

mandarin_meaning: 遇到很多倒霉事，看不到好事；形容運氣非常差
english_meaning: To encounter nothing but bad luck and no good fortune; extremely unlucky
explanation_mandarin: 此短語屬於香港粵語的俗語或俚語，書面記錄稀少，讀音和來源可能有地區差異。字面上可拆作「見到屎而（看）不見米白」，引申為只遇到壞事、看不到好事，用以抱怨運氣或處境非常不順利。
explanation_english: This phrase is an informal Hong Kong Cantonese saying; it is rare in written records and pronunciation/origin may vary by locality. Literally it reads like "see shit but not see white rice," and figuratively it means encountering only bad things and no good ones — used to complain about very bad luck or an unlucky situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 近排我真係見屎胐喐唔見米白，做乜嘢都唔順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 ngo5 zan1 hai6 gin3 si2 （讀音不詳） m4 gin3 mai5 baak6, zou6 mat1 je5 dou1 m4 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近我真是倒楣透顶，遇到的全是坏事，看不到好事，做什么都不顺。
examples.english_sentence: Lately I'm really unlucky — nothing but bad things happen and nothing goes right.

mandarin_meaning: 尋找；覓食（觅）
english_meaning: to look for; to seek (often used in compounds like '覓食' — to look for food)
explanation_mandarin: 表示尋找、覓取，常見於書面語或與「覓食」等詞語搭配，用於表示尋找人或物或覓求食物。
explanation_english: Means to search for or seek. It is often literary and appears in compounds such as '覓食' (to look for food).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街市覔新鮮蔬菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 si5 mik6 san1 sin1 so1 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在菜市場尋找新鮮蔬菜。
examples.english_sentence: He is looking for fresh vegetables at the market.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋去覔食，好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 mik6 sik6, hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我們去找東西吃，好嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Shall we go find something to eat tonight?

mandarin_meaning: 窺視；偷看（方言或罕用）
english_meaning: to peep; to spy on; to take a sneaky look (dialectal/rare)
explanation_mandarin: 覘（擔）為罕用或方言詞，表示偷偷張望、窺視別人的行為。現代書面語少見，多見於口語或方言用法。
explanation_english: A rare or dialectal verb meaning to peep or spy on someone. It denotes secretly looking or taking a sneaky glance; uncommon in standard written usage and mainly heard in colloquial/dialect contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺窗口覘（擔）隔離阿姨同人傾計，真係唔好意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 coeng1 hau2 caan1 (daam1) gaak3 lei4 aa3 ji4 tung4 jan4 king1 gai2, zan1 hai6 m4 hou2 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在窗邊偷看隔壁阿姨和別人聊天，真是不好意思。
examples.english_sentence: He was peeking out the window to watch the neighbour chatting with someone — it's really embarrassing.

mandarin_meaning: 覡公（方言）指民間的男巫或通靈者
english_meaning: a male shaman or spirit-medium (Cantonese dialect term)
explanation_mandarin: 指傳統民間信仰中負責與鬼神溝通、替人做法事或擺壇的男性巫師／通靈者，為粵語地區的方言稱呼。
explanation_english: Refers to a traditional male shaman or spirit-medium in Cantonese-speaking communities who communicates with spirits and performs rituals or ceremonies for people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日有人搵覡公擺壇求神保佑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 jau5 jan4 wun2 gik6 gung1 baai2 taan4 kau4 san4 bou2 jau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 經常有人找覡公擺壇求神保佑。
examples.english_sentence: People often go to the shaman to hold rituals and pray for protection.

mandarin_meaning: 女婿（指與自己女兒結婚的男子）
english_meaning: son-in-law (the man married to one's daughter)
explanation_mandarin: 「親家郎」是粵語用語，指與自己女兒結婚的男子，即女婿，通常在兩家成為姻親關係時使用的稱呼。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term referring to the man married to one's daughter — i.e., a son-in-law. Used between families connected by marriage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個女嫁咗，佢而家係我嘅親家郎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 neoi5 gaa3 zo2, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai6 ngo5 ge3 can1 gaa1 long4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的女兒嫁人了，他現在是我的女婿。
examples.english_sentence: My daughter got married; he is now my son-in-law.

mandarin_meaning: （願）觀音菩薩保佑年年十八歲——祝願某人永遠年輕
english_meaning: ‘May Guanyin bless you to be eighteen every year’ — a humorous/blessing expression wishing someone to stay forever young
explanation_mandarin: 這句話常見於廣東話口語，用來稱讚或祝福某人看起來年輕、保養得好。語氣帶有誇張和幽默成分，引用佛教慈悲象徵（觀音菩薩）來表達祝願。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to praise or bless someone who looks young or well preserved. It jokingly invokes Guanyin (a symbol of compassion) to wish the person remain eighteen every year; the tone is typically playful and exaggerated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢keep得咁好，年紀都幾大，但仲好似十八歲，真係「觀音菩薩，年年十八」！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 keep1 dak1 gam3 hou2, nin4gei3 dou1 gei2 daai6, daan6 zung6 hou2ci5 sap6baat3 seoi3, zan1hai6 "gun1jam1 pou4saat3, nin4nin4 sap6baat3"!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她保養得那麼好，年紀也不小，但還像十八歲一樣，真是「觀音菩薩，年年十八」！
examples.english_sentence: She takes such good care of herself; although she's older, she still looks eighteen — truly 'Guanyin Bodhisattva, eighteen every year'!

mandarin_meaning: 去世；死亡（委婉语）
english_meaning: to die; to pass away (euphemism)
explanation_mandarin: “见周公”是粤语/汉语中的委婉说法，用来表示某人去世或死亡。常用于非正式或婉转表达中。
explanation_english: “见周公” is a Cantonese/Chinese euphemism meaning to die or to pass away. It is used as a polite or indirect way to refer to someone's death.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢上個月已經見周公喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng6 go3 jyut6 ji5 ging1 gin3 zau1 gung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上个月已经去世了。
examples.english_sentence: He passed away last month.

mandarin_meaning: 见招拆招（jiàn zhāo chāi zhāo）：在对方出招或遇到变化时，灵活应对、逐一化解。
english_meaning: To respond flexibly to each move as it comes; to deal with situations one step at a time, reacting appropriately.
explanation_mandarin: 指在對方出招或遇到變化時，靈活應對、採取相應措施逐一應付。常用來形容遇事隨機應變，不採取固定方案。
explanation_english: Describes reacting flexibly to each action or change as it occurs, handling problems one by one. Often used to mean adapting to circumstances rather than following a fixed plan.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽入面，對手好勁，我哋只好見招拆招。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 jap6 min6, deoi3 sau2 hou2 ging6, ngo5 dei6 zi2 hou2 gin3 ziu1 caak3 ziu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比赛里面，对手很厉害，我们只好见招拆招。
examples.english_sentence: In the match, the opponent was very strong, so we had to respond move by move.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司政策經常轉變，我哋要見招拆招，保持靈活。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 zing3 caak3 ging1 soeng4 zyun2 bin3, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 gin3 ziu1 caak3 ziu1, bou2 ci4 ling4 wut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司政策经常转变，我们要见招拆招，保持灵活。
examples.english_sentence: Company policies keep changing; we must deal with things as they come and stay flexible.

mandarin_meaning: 走一步看一步；见机行事
english_meaning: to take things as they come; to play it by ear; to deal with matters step by step
explanation_mandarin: 表示在不確定或變動的情況下，不事先做長期打算，而是根據實際情況逐步應對，走一步看一步。
explanation_english: Used to describe handling uncertain or changing situations by not making long-term plans in advance but responding step by step as circumstances develop.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家情況咁樣，唔好諗太多，見步行步先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 cing4 fong3 gam2 joeng6, m4 hou2 lam2 taai3 do1, gin3 bou6 haang4 bou6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在情况这样，别想太多，走一步看一步吧。
examples.english_sentence: Given how things are now, don't overthink it — let's take it one step at a time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 疫情期間好多公司都係見步行步，唔敢輕易推新計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jik6 cing4 kei4 gaan1 hou2 do1 gung1 si1 dou1 hai6 gin3 bou6 haang4 bou6, m4 gam2 hing1 ji6 teoi1 san1 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在疫情期间，很多公司都是走一步看一步，不敢轻易推出新计划。
examples.english_sentence: During the pandemic, many companies were taking things as they came and didn't dare to roll out new plans.

mandarin_meaning: 只露表面、做表面功夫或遇事躲避不負責
english_meaning: to make only a token appearance; to be evasive or unreliable — show the surface but not true presence or responsibility
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語/成語（形容詞性用法，含貶義）
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人只是表面上出現或敷衍，遇到麻煩或需要負責任時就躲避或不見人，帶有批評意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom describing someone who only makes token or superficial appearances and disappears or avoids responsibility when needed; carries a critical tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日見牙唔見眼，約好咗又唔現身，真係唔可信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gin3 ngaa4 m4 gin3 ngaan5, joek3 hou2 zo2 jau6 m4 jin6 san1, zan1 hai6 m4 ho2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是見牙不見眼，約好了又不出現，真的不可信。
examples.english_sentence: He often makes only token appearances — he agrees to meet but doesn't show up; really untrustworthy.

jyutping: gin3 se4 m4 daa2 saam1 fan1 zeoi6
mandarin_meaning: 看到蛇不打要担三分罪（比喻看到明显的危险或错误却不制止，也要承担部分责任）
english_meaning: Literally 'if you see a snake and don't hit it, you're thirty percent guilty' — used to say one shares blame for failing to act when witnessing danger or wrongdoing.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻看到明顯的危險、錯誤或不當行為卻袖手旁觀、不出手阻止，自己也要承擔部分責任或過失。
explanation_english: A proverb used to warn that if you witness clear danger or wrongdoing and do nothing, you bear part of the blame.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你見到有人偷嘢唔出聲，真係見蛇唔打三分罪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gin3 dou3 jau5 jan4 tau1 je5 m4 ceot1 seng1, zan1 hai6 gin3 se4 m4 daa2 saam1 fan1 zeoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看到有人偷东西不出声，真是见蛇不打三分罪。
examples.english_sentence: If you see someone stealing and stay silent, it's really 'see a snake and don't hit it' — you're partly to blame.

mandarin_meaning: 見過驚嚇或不愉快的經歷後，對相關情況變得膽小或謹慎
english_meaning: Literally "having seen a ghost, afraid of the dark." Describes someone who becomes fearful or overly cautious about similar situations after a frightening or bad experience.
explanation_mandarin: 字面上是「見過鬼就怕黑」。比喻人經歷過一次驚嚇或不愉快的事情後，對相關情況變得害怕或格外小心。
explanation_english: The phrase literally means "having seen a ghost, afraid of the dark." It figuratively refers to someone who, after a frightening or unpleasant experience, becomes afraid or overly cautious in similar situations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿敏以前打夜班時遇過搶劫，依家唔敢夜晚出街，真係見過鬼怕黑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 man5 ji5 cin4 daa2 je6 baan1 si4 jyu6 gwo3 coeng2 gip6, ji1 gaa1 m4 gam2 je6 maan5 ceot1 gaai1, zan1 hai6 gin3 gwo3 gwai2 paa3 hak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿敏以前上夜班時遇到搶劫，現在不敢在晚上出門，真是見過鬼怕黑。
examples.english_sentence: Amin was robbed once while working the night shift; now she doesn't dare go out at night — truly, once you've seen a ghost you're afraid of the dark.

synonyms: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩

mandarin_meaning: 見風轉舵、趨炎附勢（機會主義）
english_meaning: to be opportunistic; to change one's stance or behaviour to suit circumstances; to curry favor with whoever is advantageous
explanation_mandarin: 口語、貶義。形容人根據情勢、利益變換立場或做法，迎合有利的一方以謀取私利或保全自己。
explanation_english: Colloquial, derogatory. Describes someone who changes position or behaviour according to circumstances or who flatters and sides with whoever is advantageous to gain personal benefit or save themselves.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日見風扯𢃇，冇主見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gin3 fung1 ce2 kei4, mou5 zyu2 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是見風轉舵，沒有主見。
examples.english_sentence: He's always being opportunistic and has no backbone.

mandarin_meaning: 见风使舵：根据形势改变立场或行为，趋利避害；机会主义的做法。
english_meaning: To change one's stance or behavior according to circumstances to gain advantage; to be opportunistic.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容人随环境或利益改变态度或立场，没有坚定原则，常带有贬义。
explanation_english: Describes someone who adjusts their stance or actions to suit changing circumstances or personal gain; often pejorative, implying lack of principles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日見風駛舵，冇主見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gin3 fung1 sai2 do6, mou5 zyu2 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常见风使舵，没主见。
examples.english_sentence: He often shifts his stance to suit the situation; he has no firm opinions.

jyutping: gin3 gou1 baai3, gin3 dai1 caai2
mandarin_meaning: 对有权势的人阿谀奉承，对地位低的人则欺压；趋炎附势。
english_meaning: To flatter those above and trample on those below; to be sycophantic to superiors and oppressive to inferiors.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容見風轉舵、没有原则、趋炎附势的人：對權勢者諂媚奉承，對弱勢者則欺壓或看不起。
explanation_english: Describes someone who shifts behavior to suit the powerful: flattering those of higher status while belittling or bullying those of lower status; opportunistic and sycophantic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日見高拜、見低踩，大家都唔鍾意佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gin3 gou1 baai3, gin3 dai1 caai2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是見高拜、見低踩，大家都不喜歡他。
examples.english_sentence: He is always flattering those above and trampling those below; nobody likes him.

mandarin_meaning: 解缆；起锚；起航
english_meaning: to cast off (a ship's cable); to weigh anchor; to set sail; to depart
explanation_mandarin: 指解开系缆使船只离岸或起航，也可引申为开始启程或出发。
explanation_english: To unfasten a ship's mooring cable and depart; to set sail. Can also be used figuratively to mean beginning a journey or setting off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 船長吩咐船員解纜出發。
examples.jyutping_sentence: syun4 zoeng2 fan1 fu6 syun4 jyun4 gaai2 laam5 ceot1 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 船长吩咐船员解缆出发。
examples.english_sentence: The captain told the crew to cast off and set sail.

mandarin_meaning: 推來推去；互相推諉
english_meaning: to pass responsibility around; to pass the buck
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容多人或不同部門之間互相推卸責任，將事情一再推來推去而不處理。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese phrase describing people or departments passing responsibility back and forth and avoiding dealing with an issue.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事唔好再託上託，邊個負責就講清楚啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 m4 hou2 zoi6 tok3 soeng5 tok3, bin1 go3 fu6 zaak3 zau6 gong2 cing1 co2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事不要再互相推來推去了，誰負責就說清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep passing this around — whoever's responsible should make it clear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部門之間唔停咁託上託，結果問題一直無人解決。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 mun4 zi1 gaan1 m4 ting4 gam2 tok3 soeng5 tok3, git3 gwo2 man6 tai4 jat1 zik6 mou5 jan4 gaai2 kyut3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 部門之間不停地互相推諉，結果問題一直沒有人解決。
examples.english_sentence: The departments keep passing the issue around, and as a result no one has resolved it.

mandarin_meaning: 訾（訿）讀作 zī，作動詞時有指責、責難的意思；亦可作姓氏。
english_meaning: To criticize or censure; also a Chinese surname (Zi).
explanation_mandarin: 「訾」較書面，常見於「訾議」等詞，表示對他人或事物加以指責、挑剔或責難；亦是少見的姓氏。
explanation_english: A literary/traditional character meaning to criticize or find fault (often seen in words like 訾議). It can also appear as a rare Chinese surname.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日訾議人哋嘅工作，大家都唔鍾意同佢共事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zi1 ji5 jan4 dei6 ge3 gung1 zok3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 gung6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天指責別人的工作，大家都不喜歡和他共事。
examples.english_sentence: He constantly criticizes other people's work; everyone dislikes working with him.

mandarin_meaning: 開玩笑；逗弄（口語、俗語）
english_meaning: to joke around; to tease or kid someone (colloquial Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「詏交」是廣東話的俗語/俚語，用來表示開玩笑、逗弄、鬧着玩。不一定帶惡意，常用於朋友間嬉鬧或不認真地說話。區域性較強，口語中較常見。
explanation_english: “詏交” is Cantonese slang meaning to joke around or tease someone. It's typically used in informal speech among friends to indicate playful teasing or not speaking seriously. It is colloquial and regionally used.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再詏交啦，我講真㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ngau1 gaau1 laa1, ngo5 gong2 zan1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別再開玩笑了，我是認真的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't joke around anymore; I'm being serious.

mandarin_meaning: 口頭上激烈責罵或爭吵
english_meaning: to verbally scold/argue; to have a heated quarrel
explanation_mandarin: 「詏數口」為粵語口語/俚語，用來形容以言語激烈責罵或互相爭吵。這個用法在香港口語圈較口語化，部分文獻中較少見，可能屬方言或俗語變體。
explanation_english: “詏數口” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase describing a heated verbal scolding or argument. It’s used to indicate someone verbally attacking or trading harsh words; the expression is informal and relatively localized.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢同你詏數口，唔好理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tung4 nei5 jeuk6 sou3 hau2, m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在和你口頭爭吵，別理他。
examples.english_sentence: He's verbally attacking/arguing with you — ignore him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到隔離鋪兩個人喺度詏數口，好嘈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 gaak3 lei4 pou3 loeng5 go3 jan4 hai2 dou6 jeuk6 sou3 hau2, hou2 cou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到隔壁店有兩個人在那裡吵架，很吵。
examples.english_sentence: I heard two people next door arguing loudly — it's noisy.

mandarin_meaning: 拍馬屁；諂媚
english_meaning: to flatter or butter someone up (to gain favor)
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，指為了獲取好處而刻意對人諂媚、拍馬屁。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang verb meaning to flatter or ingratiate oneself to someone, usually to gain favors or advantages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日詏頸個老闆，希望加人工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 waat3 geng2 go3 lou5 baan2, hei1 mong6 gaa1 jan4 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常拍老闆的馬屁，希望加薪。
examples.english_sentence: He always flatters the boss, hoping to get a raise.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係識詏頸，做嘢先要實力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 sik1 waat3 geng2, zou6 je5 sin1 jiu3 sat6 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只會拍馬屁，做事還是要有實力。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just know how to flatter; you need real ability to do the job.

mandarin_meaning: 装傻；故意装作不懂或不在意
english_meaning: to play dumb; to pretend to be ignorant or naive
explanation_mandarin: 表示故意裝作不懂、不知道或不在意，以躲避責任、逃避問題或取得某些利益。
explanation_english: To deliberately act as if one does not understand or notice something, often to avoid responsibility, evade a problem, or gain an advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日喺老闆面前詐傻，遲早會畀人識穿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 hai2 lou5 baan2 min6 cin4 zaa3 so4, ci4 zou2 wui5 bei2 jan4 sik1 cyun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別總是在老板面前装傻，早晚會被人识破。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep playing dumb in front of the boss — sooner or later someone will see through you.

mandarin_meaning: 诈和/诈糊：假装和解或假装胡牌（麻将术语）；比喻装作已经成功或达成一致以欺骗别人。
english_meaning: To fake a win (in mahjong) or to pretend reconciliation/success; to bluff by pretending you've won or settled something.
explanation_mandarin: 原本是麻将用語，指假装胡牌；引申為在社交或工作情境中假裝已和解或已完成以欺騙他人或掩飾失敗。
explanation_english: Originally a mahjong term meaning to fake a winning hand; extended to mean pretending to have reconciled, succeeded, or completed something to deceive others or hide failure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺麻雀度詐糊，結果俾人睇穿晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 maa4zoek3 dou6 zaa3 wu4, git3 gwo2 bei2 jan4 tai2 cyun1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在打麻将时诈胡，结果被人看穿了。
examples.english_sentence: He faked a win in mahjong and ended up being seen through.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩個人表面上詐和，其實心裡仲嬲緊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 go3 jan4 biu2 min6 soeng6 zaa3 wo4, kei4 sat6 sam1 leoi5 zung6 nau1 gan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 两个人表面上假装和好，其实心里还在生气。
examples.english_sentence: The two of them are pretending to be reconciled on the surface, but they're still angry inside.

mandarin_meaning: 裝聾作啞 / 裝聽不見
english_meaning: to pretend to be deaf; to feign not hearing (deliberately ignore someone)
explanation_mandarin: 指故意裝作聽不到別人說話或要求，故意不回應或迴避問題。
explanation_english: To deliberately pretend not to hear someone — intentionally not responding or avoiding addressing a question or request.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好詐耳聾，聽到就答聲啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zaa3 ji5 lung4, teng1 dou3 zau6 daap3 seng1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別裝聾，聽到了就回應一下吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pretend to be deaf — if you hear me, just respond.

mandarin_meaning: 裝聾作啞
english_meaning: to play deaf and dumb; to pretend not to hear or know (to avoid responsibility or confrontation)
explanation_mandarin: 故意裝作聽不到或不知道，以逃避責任或回答問題。
explanation_english: Deliberately pretending not to hear or know something in order to avoid responsibility, answering, or confrontation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺會議上明明知係佢嘅錯，仲詐聾扮啞唔肯承認。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 wui6 ji5 soeng6 ming4 ming4 zi1 hai6 keoi5 ge3 co3, zung6 zaa3 lung4 baan6 aa3 m4 hang2 sing4 jing6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在會議上明明知道是他的錯，還裝聾作啞不肯承認。
examples.english_sentence: He clearly knew in the meeting it was his mistake, yet he played deaf and dumb and refused to admit it.

mandarin_meaning: 告诉（某人）
english_meaning: to tell (someone); to let someone know
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的口語用法，表示把訊息或事情告訴某人，常見搭配如「話畀佢知」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to tell or inform someone. Commonly used in phrases like "話畀佢知" (tell him/her).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經話畀佢聽喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 waa6 bei2 keoi5 teng1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已经告诉他了。
examples.english_sentence: I've already told him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要話畀佢知你幾點會到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 waa6 bei2 keoi5 zi1 nei5 gei2 dim2 wui5 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要告诉他你几点会到。
examples.english_sentence: You need to tell him what time you'll arrive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 可唔可以話畀我知點樣做？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 waa6 bei2 ngo5 zi1 dim2 joeng6 zou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可以告诉我怎么做吗？
examples.english_sentence: Can you tell me how to do it?

jyutping: 無標準讀音（罕見／古字，現代廣東話一般無固定讀音）
mandarin_meaning: 罕見字、古字，現代漢語中無固定義項或用法（在古籍或字書中偶見）
english_meaning: A rare/archaic Chinese character; not commonly used in modern Cantonese and has no fixed modern meaning or pronunciation
explanation_mandarin: 「誁」為罕見或古文字，通常出現在古籍或專門字典中。現代廣東話和普通話中一般不使用，沒有廣泛接受的讀音或詞義，因此在日常語境中很少見。
explanation_english: “誁” is a rare or archaic character that appears mainly in classical texts or specialized dictionaries. It is not used in everyday Cantonese or Mandarin and lacks a commonly accepted modern pronunciation or meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「誁」好罕見，喺現代廣東話中冇固定讀音。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 '誁' hou2 ham2 gin3, hai2 jin6 doi6 gwong2 dung1 waa2 zung1 mou5 gu3 ding6 duk6 jam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“誁”很罕见，在现代广东话中没有固定读音。
examples.english_sentence: The character '誁' is very rare and has no fixed pronunciation in modern Cantonese.

cantonese: 認咗第二冇人敢認第一
jyutping: jing6 zo2 dai6 ji6 mou5 jan4 gam2 jing6 dai6 jat1
mandarin_meaning: 承認自己是第二，沒有人敢承認是第一（通常指沒人願意承擔第一名或最高責任）
english_meaning: Everyone admits to being second; no one dares to claim first (used when people avoid the top spot/responsibility because it's risky or blameworthy)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容在某種情況下，大家都甘願做第二，沒有人願意當第一（通常因為第一位風險大、責任重或容易被責備），帶有諷刺或批評意味。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where everyone is willing to be second and no one dares to be first — often because being first carries more responsibility, risk, or blame. Usually used sarcastically or critically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺呢個計劃入面，大家都認咗第二，冇人敢認第一。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 jap6 min6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 jing6 zo2 dai6 ji6, mou5 jan4 gam2 jing6 dai6 jat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在这个计划里，大家都承认自己是第二，没人敢承认是第一。
examples.english_sentence: In this project, everyone admits to being second; no one dares to claim first.

mandarin_meaning: 認輸／承認失敗
english_meaning: to admit defeat; to concede; to give up (often reluctantly)
explanation_mandarin: 「認掯」是香港粵語口語用語，表示承認失敗或讓步，通常帶有不情願或為了息事寧人的意味，相當於普通話的「認輸」或「認錯」。
explanation_english: "認掯" is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to admit defeat or concede. It often implies reluctance or doing so to stop an argument or preserve peace, similar to "admit defeat" or "give in."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最後都認掯，唔再同人鬥口。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 hau6 dou1 jing6 hon3 , m4 zoi6 tung4 jan4 dau3 hau2 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最後也認輸了，不再跟人爭辯。
examples.english_sentence: He finally admitted defeat and stopped arguing with people.

mandarin_meaning: 承認現實 / 認輸 / 暫時接受（通常帶無奈或自嘲）
english_meaning: to admit/accept the situation (often reluctantly) / to give up arguing or resistence
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話短語，用來表示接受現實、認輸或暫時放棄爭辯，語氣常帶無奈或自嘲。形字可有可無（認住/認形住）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to indicate accepting reality, admitting defeat, or temporarily giving up arguing. It often carries a sense of resignation or self-mockery. The character '形' is optional in casual use.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 算啦，你認（形）住啦，唔好再頂嘴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: syun3 laa1, nei5 jing6 (jing4) zyu6 laa1, m4 hou2 zoi3 deng2 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 算了，你认了吧，别再顶嘴了。
examples.english_sentence: Give it up — admit it already, don't argue anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要裁員，我都認（形）住先，之後再搵其他機會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 coi4 jyun4, ngo5 dou1 jing6 (jing4) zyu6 sin1, zi1 hau6 zoi3 wan2 kei4 taa1 gei1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要裁员，我先暂时接受，之后再找其他机会。
examples.english_sentence: The company is laying people off; I'll accept it for now and look for other opportunities later.

jyutping: sai3 jyun6 dong3 sik6 saang1 coi3
mandarin_meaning: 用誓言強調自己所說屬實，若不是就甘願吃生菜（作為誇張的懲罰或證明）
english_meaning: A colloquial vow meaning "I swear it's true — if not, I'll eat raw lettuce"; used to emphasize certainty with a joking/self‑punishing promise.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語式的誓言用語，多見於香港粵語網絡與口語，表示講者非常肯定某事；用「吃生菜」作為誇張的懲罰或證明，具有玩笑與誓言成分。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression used to emphasize certainty by making a playful yet emphatic promise — "I'll eat raw lettuce" if the statement is false. Commonly used online and in speech as a humorous oath.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同你講，呢單買賣冇問題，誓愿当食生菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 nei5 gong2, ni1 dun1 maai5 maai6 mou5 man6 tai4, sai3 jyun6 dong3 sik6 saang1 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我跟你說，這筆買賣沒問題，我發誓（若不是如此）就吃生菜。
examples.english_sentence: I'm telling you, this deal has no problem — I swear, I'll eat raw lettuce if it's not true.

mandarin_meaning: 请客吃糖果；在喜庆场合派发糖果或糖点作为庆祝或款待
english_meaning: to give out/hand out sweets (to guests); to treat people to candies at a celebratory occasion
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面意思「請人吃糖」，常用於婚禮、滿月、開張等喜慶場合，主辦方向來賓派發糖果或糖點以示慶祝或款待。有時也可泛指以小禮物或贈品招待或拉攏人心。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning 'invite (people) to eat candy.' It refers to hosts distributing candies or sweet treats at celebrations (weddings, a baby's one‑month event, shop openings) as a way to celebrate or treat guests. It can also be used more broadly to mean giving small freebies or gifts to attract or please people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺婚禮會請食糖畀賓客。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 fan1 lai5 wui5 cing2 sik6 tong4 bei2 ban1 haak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在婚禮會發糖給賓客。
examples.english_sentence: We'll hand out sweets to guests at our wedding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: BB滿月咗，阿媽話要請食糖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: B B mun5 jyut6 zo2, aa3 maa1 waa6 jiu3 cing2 sik6 tong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 寶寶滿月了，媽媽說要發放糖果。
examples.english_sentence: The baby is one month old; Mom says she'll distribute sweets.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新店開張，老闆會請食糖吸引街坊嚟光顧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 dim3 hoi1 zoeng1, lou5 baan2 wui5 cing2 sik6 tong4 kap1 jan5 gaai1 fong1 lai4 gwong1 gu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新店開張，老闆會發糖吸引街坊來光顧。
examples.english_sentence: For the new store opening, the owner will hand out sweets to attract locals to come.

mandarin_meaning: 想不到 / 想不出
english_meaning: can't think of; unable to come up with
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示無法想出某個點子、答案或無法想到某件事；有時也用來表示對某事感到意外、想不到會發生。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb phrase meaning 'cannot think of' or 'unable to come up with' something. It can indicate inability to produce an idea/answer or express surprise that something was unexpected.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係諗唔到佢會咁做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 lam2 m4 dou3 keoi5 wui5 gam2 zou6。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真的是想不到他會這樣做。
examples.english_sentence: I really couldn't imagine that he would do that.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試嗰條題我諗唔到答案。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 go2 tiu4 tai4 ngo5 lam2 m4 dou3 daap3 on3。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試那題我想不出答案。
examples.english_sentence: I couldn't come up with the answer to that exam question.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 要諗主意幫公司做宣傳，我諗唔到好嘅點子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 lam2 zyu2 ji3 bong1 gung1 si1 zou6 syun1 cyun4, ngo5 lam2 m4 dou3 hou2 ge3 dim2 zi2。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要想主意幫公司做宣傳，我想不出好的點子。
examples.english_sentence: I need to come up with ideas to promote the company, but I can't think of any good ones.

mandarin_meaning: 睡（睡覺）
english_meaning: to sleep; to take a nap
explanation_mandarin: 粵語常用字，表示入睡或小睡，與「瞓」同義，屬口語用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to sleep or take a nap. It is equivalent to 瞓 in Cantonese usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日好攰，想早啲謓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 hou2 gui6, soeng2 zou2 di1 fan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天很累，想早点睡。
examples.english_sentence: I'm very tired today and want to go to bed early.

mandarin_meaning: 告诉（某人）/让某人知道
english_meaning: to tell (someone) / to let someone know
explanation_mandarin: 表示把訊息告訴某人，常與人稱連用，例如「講畀佢知」（粵語用法）。
explanation_english: Used to indicate informing or telling someone; literally 'speak to give (to someone)'. Often followed by the person being told (e.g. '講畀佢知').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經講畀佢聽啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 gong2 bei2 keoi5 teng1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已經告诉他／她了。
examples.english_sentence: I've already told him/her.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要講畀老闆知，唔好遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 gong2 bei2 lou5 baan2 zi1, m4 hou2 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要告诉老板，不要迟到。
examples.english_sentence: You need to tell the boss — don't be late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 可唔可以講畀我聽點樣做？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 bei2 ngo5 teng1 dim2 joeng6 zou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可以告诉我怎样做吗？
examples.english_sentence: Can you tell me how to do it?

mandarin_meaning: 打电话
english_meaning: to talk on the phone; to make/receive a phone call
explanation_mandarin: 表示用電話與別人通話，包含撥打或接聽電話的行為。
explanation_english: Indicates speaking with someone by telephone; encompasses making or receiving a phone call.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好打擾我，我而家喺度講電話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 daa2 jiu2 ngo5, ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 dou6 gong2 din6 waa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别打扰我，我现在在打电话。
examples.english_sentence: Don't disturb me, I'm on the phone right now.

mandarin_meaning: （多見於詞語「謦欬」）清嗓、咳嗽；清喉嚨
english_meaning: to clear one's throat; cough (used especially in the compound 謦欬)
explanation_mandarin: 「謦」一字本身較少單獨使用，常見於「謦欬」，表示清嗓、咳嗽或喉嚨不適時的清喉動作或聲音，屬書面或古語用法。
explanation_english: The character is rarely used alone and commonly appears in the compound 謦欬, meaning to clear one's throat or to cough. It is a more literary/archaic term referring to the act or sound of throat-clearing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺講嘢之前謦咗一下，先開始講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gong2 je5 zi1 cin4 king4 zo2 jat1 haa6, sin1 hoi1 ci2 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在說話之前清了下嗓子，才開始說。
examples.english_sentence: He cleared his throat before speaking, then began.

mandarin_meaning: 荒谬、低俗
english_meaning: absurd and vulgar; ridiculous and crude
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容言論、想法或行為既荒謬又帶有低俗、不雅的成分，通常含有批評或貶義。
explanation_english: Describes speech, ideas, or behavior that are both absurd and vulgar; typically used critically to indicate something is illogical and crude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講嗰啲嘢好謬俚，聽落又荒謬又低俗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 go2 di1 je5 hou2 mau6 lei5, teng1 lok6 jau6 wong4 mau6 jau6 dai1 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說的那些話很謬俚，聽起來既荒謬又低俗。
examples.english_sentence: What you said is very absurd and vulgar; it sounds both ridiculous and crude.

mandarin_meaning: 谨防（小心防备，提防某种危险或问题）
english_meaning: beware of; take precautions against; be careful to guard against
explanation_mandarin: 用于提示或告诫，提醒人們小心防備某種危險、欺詐或不利情況，常見於警示語或提醒語境中。
explanation_english: Used to warn or advise caution; tells someone to guard against a danger, fraud, or unfavorable situation. Commonly used in warnings and notices.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門時謹防扒手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 si4 gan2 fong4 paa1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出門時謹防扒手。
examples.english_sentence: Take care to guard against pickpockets when you go out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 網上購物時謹防詐騙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mong5 soeng6 gau3 mat6 si4 gan2 fong4 zaa3 pin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 网上购物时谨防诈骗。
examples.english_sentence: Be cautious of scams when shopping online.

mandarin_meaning: 会弹（乐器）但不会唱（歌）；比喻只擅长某一方面而缺乏相配的技能
english_meaning: Can play (an instrument) but can't sing; figuratively, good at one thing but lacking a complementary skill
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是會彈奏樂器但不會唱歌，常用來形容某人只有一方面的本事，缺乏配套能力。
explanation_english: Literally 'can play but can't sing.' Used to describe someone who is skilled in one area but lacks the complementary ability; a colloquial idiom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢識彈唔識唱，所以喺樂隊入面主力做伴奏唔做主唱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sik1 daan6 m4 sik1 coeng3, so2 ji5 hai2 ngok6 deoi6 jap6 min6 zyu2 lik6 zou6 bun6 zau3 m4 zou6 zyu2 coeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他会弹（乐器）但不会唱，所以在乐队里主要做伴奏，不当主唱。
