examples.english_sentence: He can play an instrument but can't sing, so in the band he mainly provides accompaniment instead of being the lead singer.

mandarin_meaning: 變得耍小聰明/裝聰明（帶負面、狡猾或厚臉皮的意思）
english_meaning: to act smart/cheeky; to get sly or start showing off one's cleverness (usually negative)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容某人變得會耍小聰明、狡猾或在不適當場合裝懂、逞能，通常帶有批評或負面評價。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who becomes cheeky, sly, or starts showing off cleverness in a way that is inappropriate or annoying; often used critically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好識精，做返你份內嘅嘢就得啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sik1 zing1, zou6 faan1 nei5 fan6 noi6 ge3 je5 zau6 dak1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別耍小聰明，做好你本分就行。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act smart; just do your job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢識精咗，成日喺老闆面前扮識嘢，結果反而得罪咗啲人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sik1 zing1 zo2, sing4 jat6 hai2 lou5 baan2 min6 cin4 baan6 sik1 je5, git3 gwo2 faan2 ji5 dak1 zeoi6 zo2 di1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他變得愛裝懂，經常在老闆面前賣弄，結果反而得罪了人。
examples.english_sentence: He got cheeky and kept acting like he knew everything in front of the boss, and ended up alienating people.

mandarin_meaning: 懂得顧及面子／講究面子（注重在他人前保持體面）
english_meaning: to know how to keep up appearances; to be mindful of 'face' and act tactfully in front of others
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，指在他人面前懂得注意面子、保持體面或表現得有禮貌、合乎場合。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to be conscious of appearances or 'face' — to behave tactfully and maintain a proper impression in front of others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好識貌面，見到上司會好有禮貌咁講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 sik1 maau6 min6, gin3 dou2 soeng5 si1 wui5 hou2 jau5 lai5 maau6 gam2 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很會顧及面子，見到上司會很有禮貌地說話。
examples.english_sentence: He's good at keeping up appearances; when he sees his boss he speaks very politely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔使怕，喺客人面前要識貌面啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 sai2 paa3, hai2 haak3 jan4 min6 cin4 jiu3 sik1 maau6 min6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不用怕，在客人面前要注意顧及面子。
examples.english_sentence: Don't worry; in front of customers you should be mindful of maintaining appearances.

mandarin_meaning: 念稿子；照稿念（照本宣科）
english_meaning: to read from a script/teleprompter; to recite prewritten lines (sounding scripted, not spontaneous)
explanation_mandarin: 香港俗語，形容說話或發言像在念稿，缺乏即興或真誠感，常用來批評政治人物或公眾人物的發言方式。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to read from a script or teleprompter — speaking in prewritten lines with little spontaneity. Often used to criticize politicians or public figures who sound scripted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺台上講嘢完全係讀口簧，冇一啲即興感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 toi4 soeng5 gong2 je5 jyun4 cyun4 hai6 duk6 hau2 wong4, mou5 jat1 di1 zik1 hing3 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在台上說話完全是在念稿子，沒有一點即興感。
examples.english_sentence: He was reading scripted lines on stage with no sense of spontaneity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 記者話佢答問題好似讀口簧，唔係真心講嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gei3 ze2 waa6 keoi5 daap3 man6 tai4 hou2 ci5 duk6 hau2 wong4, m4 hai6 zan1 sam1 gong2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 記者說他回答問題好像在念稿子，不是發自內心的說法。
examples.english_sentence: Reporters said his answers sounded like he was reading from a script, not speaking from the heart.

mandarin_meaning: 书呆子；爱读书或只顾读书、不善交际的人
english_meaning: bookworm; nerd; a person who studies a lot (often to the exclusion of social activities)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容非常愛讀書或只顧讀書、不太參與社交的人。語氣可中性或帶輕微貶義，視語境而定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for someone who spends a lot of time studying or focuses on studying at the expense of social life. The tone can be neutral or mildly derogatory depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺屋企讀書，大家都會叫佢讀書佬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei2 duk6 syu1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 wui5 giu3 keoi5 duk6 syu1 lou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是在家读书，大家都叫他读书佬。
examples.english_sentence: He's always studying at home; everyone calls him a bookworm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做咁嘅讀書佬，出嚟玩下啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 gam2 ge3 duk6 syu1 lou2, ceot1 lai4 waan2 haa5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别做那种读书佬，出来玩一下吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be such a bookworm; come out and have some fun.

mandarin_meaning: 低声下气；示弱；认输
english_meaning: to grovel; to act humbly or submissively; to back down/admit defeat
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，表示在别人面前卑躬屈膝、示弱或为了某种利益而认输、低声下气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to abase oneself, act submissively or grovel in front of someone — often to avoid conflict or to keep a favor/job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗保住份工，佢喺老闆面前不斷認低威。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 bou2 zyu6 fan6 gung1, keoi5 hai2 lou5 baan2 min6 cin4 bat1 dyun6 jing6 dai1 wai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了保住工作，他在老板面前不断低声下气。
examples.english_sentence: To keep his job, he kept groveling in front of his boss.

mandarin_meaning: 承認自己認輸/示弱或裝可憐的人；承認認輸
english_meaning: Someone who admits defeat, gives up easily, or plays the victim; (verb phrase) to admit defeat or act like a loser
explanation_mandarin: 「认衰仔」為香港粵語俚語，字面上可理解為「承認自己衰（差、倒霉）的人」。常用來形容容易認輸、示弱或裝可憐以逃避責任的人；也可作動詞短語，表示認輸或放棄嘗試。
explanation_english: ‘認衰仔’ is Hong Kong Cantonese slang literally meaning 'admit-loser-guy.' It describes a person who readily admits defeat, gives up easily, or plays the victim; it can also be used as a verb phrase meaning to admit defeat or act like a loser.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做認衰仔，試下再努力一次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 jing6 seoi1 zai2, si3 haa5 zoi3 nou5 lik6 jat1 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別做總是認輸的人，試著再努力一次。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be such a quitter — try once more.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日認衰仔，咩事都話自己唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jing6 seoi1 zai2, me1 si6 dou1 waa6 zi6 gei2 m4 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是認輸，什麼事都說自己不行。
examples.english_sentence: He always plays the victim and says he can't do anything.

mandarin_meaning: 说三道四
english_meaning: to gossip / to criticize indiscriminately
explanation_mandarin: 指到处议论、乱批评或说长道短，带有贬义，形容对别人指指点点或搬弄是非。
explanation_english: To gossip or make indiscriminate, petty criticisms about others; usually derogatory and implies meddling or spreading rumours.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺街度同人講三講四，好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 dou6 tung4 jan4 gong2 saam1 gong2 sei3, hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天在街上和别人说三道四，真烦。
examples.english_sentence: He's always gossiping with others on the street; it's so annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 指懂得應酬、處理人際關係；有時帶貶義，指討好別人或拍馬屁。
english_meaning: To be good at socializing and handling interpersonal relations; sometimes used pejoratively to mean flattering or currying favor.
explanation_mandarin: 「講人事」是粵語俗語，常用來形容一個人善於應酬、處理人際關係；在某些語境下可用來批評有人只會討好上司或拍馬屁。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase describing someone who is good at social niceties and handling interpersonal matters; in some contexts it carries a negative sense of flattering others or currying favor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好識講人事，喺公司好受歡迎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 sik1 gong2 jan4 si6, hai2 gung1si1 hou2 sau6 fun1 jing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很會處理人際關係，在公司很受歡迎。
examples.english_sentence: He is good at handling interpersonal relations and is popular at the company.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係識講人事，要有真才實學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 sik1 gong2 jan4 si6, jiu3 jau5 zan1 coi4 sat6 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別只是會拍馬屁，要有真才實學。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just know how to flatter; have real skills.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺老闆面前講人事，其他同事唔鍾意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4jat6 hai2 lou5baan2 min6 cin4 gong2 jan4 si6, kei4taa1 tung4si6 m4 zung1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在老闆面前拍馬屁，其他同事不喜歡。
examples.english_sentence: He is always flattering the boss in front of him; the other colleagues don't like it.

mandarin_meaning: 说得容易（说起来容易，做起来难）
english_meaning: Easier said than done; it's easy to say that
explanation_mandarin: 用于回应别人把某事说得很简单，但实际上难做，表示‘说得容易，做起来难’的意思。
explanation_english: Used to respond when someone makes something sound simple but it's actually difficult — expresses 'easier said than done'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係講咁易，做到畀我睇先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 gong2 gam2 ji6, zou6 dou3 bei2 ngo5 tai2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只是说得容易，先做到给我看看。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just say it's easy; do it and show me first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話寫份報告好簡單？講咁易——你試下喺一個鐘內寫晒先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 se2 fan6 bou3 gou3 hou2 gaan2 daan1? gong2 gam2 ji6 -- nei5 si3 haa5 hai2 jat1 go3 zung1 noi6 se2 saai3 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说写份报告很简单？说得容易——你试着在一个小时内全部写完再说。
examples.english_sentence: You say writing the report is easy? Easier said than done—try finishing it within an hour.

jyutping: gong2 do1 mou4 wai6, sik6 do1 zai3 wai6
mandarin_meaning: 多说无益，吃多了会胃不舒服或消化不良。
english_meaning: No use talking too much; eating too much will upset your stomach.
explanation_mandarin: 这是一句粤语俗语，通常用来劝人别再多说无用的话，并提醒吃太多会导致胃部不适或消化不良。语气可严肃或半开玩笑。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying used to tell someone there's no point in talking more and to warn that overeating will upset the stomach. It can be used seriously or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再爭啦，讲多无谓，食多滞胃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 zang1 laa1, gong2 do1 mou4 wai6, sik6 do1 zai3 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再爭了，說再多也沒用，吃多了會胃不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: Don't argue anymore — talking more won't help, and eating too much will upset your stomach.

mandarin_meaning: 说得越多越容易出错（俗语）
english_meaning: The more you talk, the more likely you are to make mistakes.
explanation_mandarin: 意思是说话越多越有可能说错或暴露错误，常用来劝人少说多做或提醒别人谨言慎行。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb meaning that the more one talks, the more likely they are to make mistakes or reveal problems; often used to advise speaking less and being cautious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你少啲讲啦，讲多错多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 siu2 di1 gong2 laa3, gong2 do1 co3 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你少说点吧，话多错多。
examples.english_sentence: Say less, the more you talk the more you'll slip up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開會時唔好亂講數，講多錯多會丢臉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 wui2 si4 m4 hou2 lyun6 gong2 sou3, gong2 do1 co3 do1 wui5 diu1 lim5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开会时别随便乱说数字，说得越多越容易出错会丢脸。
examples.english_sentence: Don't blurt out numbers in the meeting; the more you say, the more mistakes you'll make and it will be embarrassing.

mandarin_meaning: 说大话；夸口、吹嘘
english_meaning: to boast; to tell lies or exaggerated stories; to brag
explanation_mandarin: 指说夸大或不真实的话，通常为了夸耀自己或欺骗他人，也可用于表示吹牛或夸张的言语。
explanation_english: To tell exaggerated or untrue statements, often to boast or deceive. Used for bragging or exaggeration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺朋友面前講大話，話自己乜都識做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 pang4 jau5 min6 cin4 gong2 daai6 waa6, waa6 zi6 gei2 mat1 dou1 sik1 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是在朋友面前说大话，说自己什么都会做。
examples.english_sentence: He always brags in front of his friends, saying he can do everything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好畀佢講大話呃到你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 keoi5 gong2 daai6 waa6 aak1 dou3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别让他说的大话骗到你。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let his bragging/lying fool you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話自己有好多錢，但我知佢係講大話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 jau5 hou2 do1 cin2, daan6 ngo5 zi1 dou6 keoi5 hai6 gong2 daai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说自己有很多钱，但我知道他在说大话。
examples.english_sentence: He says he has a lot of money, but I know he's lying.

mandarin_meaning: 說起來／一說到這件事
english_meaning: speaking of which; now that you mention it; once you start talking about it
explanation_mandarin: 「講開又講」是廣東話口語用語，用來引出與正在談話主題相關的話題或表示一說到某事就會繼續談下去，相當於普通話的「說起來／說到這兒」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to introduce a related topic or segue in conversation. It functions like "speaking of which" or "now that you mention it," implying that once the subject is raised more will be said.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講開又講，你仲記唔記得上次旅行嗰件事？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 hoi1 jau6 gong2, nei5 zung6 gei3 m4 gei3 dak1 soeng6 ci3 leoi5 hang4 go2 gin6 si6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說起來，你還記不記得上次旅行那件事？
examples.english_sentence: Speaking of which, do you still remember that thing from our last trip?

mandarin_meaning: 光说不练；夸夸其谈，说得好听但不付诸行动
english_meaning: All talk and no action; to boast or talk big without following through
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容某人只会夸夸其谈、说得很厉害或很有声势，但缺乏实际行动或能力，常带贬义。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who talks boastfully or loudly but fails to take concrete action; emphasizes empty talk or bragging.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講得口響，從來都唔肯幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 dak1 hau2 hoeng2, cung4 loi4 dou1 m4 hang2 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是光说不做，从来不肯帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks a big game but never helps.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講得口響有咩用？做啲嘢先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 dak1 hau2 hoeng2 jau5 me1 jung6? zou6 di1 je5 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你光说有什么用？先做点事情吧。
examples.english_sentence: What's the use of all your talk? Do something first.

mandarin_meaning: 說真心話 / 說實話（表示認真或誠懇）
english_meaning: to be honest; to speak from the heart; (used to ask/mark seriousness)
explanation_mandarin: 「講心嗰句」是廣東話口語，用來引出或強調一個真誠、認真的說法，類似「說真心話」「老實說」。有時也用來詢問對方是否認真（如「你講心嗰句定係講笑？」）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to preface or emphasize a sincere, earnest statement—similar to 'to be honest' or 'honestly speaking.' It can also be used to ask if someone is serious (e.g., 'Are you being serious or joking?').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講心嗰句，我真係唔想再見佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 sam1 go2 geoi3, ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 soeng2 zoi3 gin3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說真心話，我真的不想再見他/她。
examples.english_sentence: To be honest, I really don't want to see him/her again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講心嗰句定係講笑呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 sam1 go2 geoi3 ding6 hai6 gong2 siu3 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你是認真的還是在開玩笑？
examples.english_sentence: Are you being serious or joking?

mandarin_meaning: 口头约定；口头议价（粤语俚语）
english_meaning: to make an oral agreement / to agree verbally (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: “讲数口”是粤语俚语，指只是口头上讲好条件、议价或约定，通常强调没有书面记录，亦含有口头承诺可能不可靠的意味。
explanation_english: “讲数口” is Cantonese slang meaning to agree on terms or negotiate verbally. It usually implies an oral agreement without written records and can suggest the arrangement may be less reliable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係講數口，要寫低條款先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 gong2 sou3 hau2, jiu3 se2 dai1 tiu4 fun2 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别只口头说好，要先把条款写下来才行。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just agree verbally; write down the terms first.

cantonese: 讲来将去三幅被，量来量去二丈四
jyutping: gong2 loi4 zoeng1 heoi3 saam1 fuk1 bei3, loeng4 loi4 loeng4 heoi3 ji6 zoeng6 sei3
mandarin_meaning: 說來說去沒個着落、反覆衡量卻沒有結果（帶有誇張或戲謔意味）
english_meaning: Talking and measuring back and forth many times but reaching no useful or sensible conclusion; a humorous/cynical way to describe pointless back-and-forth that leads to absurd or exaggerated results.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用誇張的形象（「三幅被」、「二丈四」）來形容反覆說和反覆量但沒有實際結果或結論，常帶有嘲諷或戲謔意味，指浪費時間或空談。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial saying uses exaggerated images ("three quilts", "2 zhang 4") to mock pointless, repetitive talking or measuring that produces no concrete result. It's typically used wryly to criticize wasted time or empty talk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識講來将去三幅被，量來量去二丈四，最後乜都冇做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 gong2 loi4 zoeng1 heoi3 saam1 fuk1 bei3, loeng4 loi4 loeng4 heoi3 ji6 zoeng6 sei3, zeoi6 hau6 mat1 dou1 mou5 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會不停地說來說去、反覆衡量，最後什麼都沒做成。
examples.english_sentence: He only keeps talking and remeasuring over and over; in the end he accomplished nothing.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）开玩笑地找茬／找事、挑衅
english_meaning: jokingly looking for trouble / jokingly provoking someone
explanation_mandarin: “讲笑揾第样”是粤语口语说法，意思是以开玩笑的方式故意找茬或挑衅别人，或被用来警告对方别故意找事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to (jokingly) look for trouble or provoke someone. It can describe teasing that intentionally seeks a reaction or be used to warn someone not to stir up trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再讲笑揾第样，真係會惹事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 siu3 wan2 dai6 joeng6, zan1 hai6 wui5 je5 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再开玩笑找事，真的会惹麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep joking around looking for trouble; you'll really cause trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我只係讲笑，唔係想揾第样。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi2 hai6 gong2 siu3, m4 hai6 soeng2 wan2 dai6 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我只是开玩笑，不是想找事。
examples.english_sentence: I'm just joking — I don't mean to pick a fight.

mandarin_meaning: 传讲耶稣/传福音（传教）
english_meaning: to talk about Jesus; to preach/evangelize about Jesus
explanation_mandarin: 指向他人傳講耶穌基督和基督教教義，即傳福音或佈道。也可泛指以宗教或道德角度說教、勸人信教。
explanation_english: Refers to speaking to others about Jesus Christ and Christian teachings — i.e. to evangelize or preach. It can also be used more generally for moralizing or proselytizing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺街度向陌生人講耶穌，想傳福音。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 dou6 hoeng3 mak6 saang1 jan4 gong2 je4 sou1, soeng2 cyun4 fuk1 jam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在街上向陌生人講耶穌，希望傳福音。
examples.english_sentence: He often talks about Jesus to strangers on the street, hoping to evangelize.

mandarin_meaning: 說話有骨氣／說話有骨
english_meaning: to speak with backbone; to speak firmly, confidently, and with principle
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人說話有骨氣、立場堅定、直言不諱，不輕易妥協或屈服。
explanation_english: Describes someone who speaks with backbone—firm, principled, and unafraid to speak up; not easily compromised.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講話有骨，遇到唔公道嘅事都會出聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 waa6 jau5 gwat1, jyu6 dou3 m4 gung1 dou6 ge3 si6 dou1 wui5 ceot1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話有骨氣，遇到不公的事都會發聲。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks with backbone; when he encounters injustice he'll speak up.

mandarin_meaning: 識相／懂事／會分寸
english_meaning: be sensible/tactful; know how to act or what to do
explanation_mandarin: 「識做」是粵語口語，表示懂得分寸或識相，知道在不同情況下應該怎麼做或怎麼說以避免尷尬或取得好處。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to be sensible or tactful — to know how to behave or what to do in a situation so as to avoid awkwardness or gain advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要識做啲，唔好咁衝動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 sik1 zou6 di1, m4 hou2 gam2 cung1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要識相一點，不要這麼衝動。
examples.english_sentence: You should be more sensible; don't be so impulsive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係識做，見到客人即刻收起手機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 sik1 zou6, gin3 dou3 haak3 jan4 zik1 hak1 sau1 hei2 sau2 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很識相，看到客人就立刻把手機收起來。
examples.english_sentence: He's really tactful — he puts his phone away as soon as customers arrive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意要識做，先知道幾時讓步。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 sik1 zou6, sin1 zi1 dou3 gei2 si4 joeng6 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意要識相，才能知道何時讓步。
examples.english_sentence: In business you need to be tactful; only then do you know when to give way.

mandarin_meaning: 有分寸/有常識（別做沒分寸的事）
english_meaning: Show some sense / have some decency (don’t do something thoughtless)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語/祈使語氣（斥責或勸誡）
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來催促或責備對方要有分寸、要有常識或別做傻事，語氣可較直接或帶斥責。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese admonition telling someone to show some sense, common sense, or decency; often used reproachfully or as a warning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講嘢要識啲唔識啲，唔好講咁傷人嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 je5 jiu3 sik1 di1 m4 sik1 di1, m4 hou2 gong2 gam2 soeng1 jan4 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說話要有分寸，別說那麼傷人的話。
examples.english_sentence: When you speak, show some sense—don't say such hurtful things.

mandarin_meaning: 只会弹（乐器）不会唱歌；比喻只懂一部分本领或缺乏配套技能。
english_meaning: Literally 'can play (an instrument) but can't sing'; figuratively refers to someone who only knows part of a skill or lacks complementary abilities.
explanation_mandarin: 常用於粤语口語，原指會彈奏樂器卻不會唱歌，現多用來形容只掌握某項技藝的一部分或缺乏配套能力，不能獨當一面。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase. Originally refers to someone who can play an instrument but cannot sing. Figuratively used to describe a person who only has partial skills or lacks the complementary abilities needed to do the whole job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 雖然佢識彈唔識唱，但係做伴奏都幾有用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: seoi1 jin4 keoi5 sik1 daan6 m4 sik1 coeng3, daan6 hai6 zou6 bun6 zau3 dou1 gei2 jau5 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 雖然他會彈（樂器）但不會唱歌，但做伴奏還是很有幫助。
examples.english_sentence: Although he can play (an instrument) but can't sing, he's still quite useful as an accompanist.

jyutping: sik1 ze2 jyun1 joeng1, m4 sik1 ze2 loeng5 joeng6
mandarin_meaning: 有见识的人看成一对（鸳鸯），不懂的人看成两样；意思是同一件事/现象，懂的人和不懂的人会有不同的看法。
english_meaning: Those who understand see a matched pair (like mandarin ducks), those who don't see two separate things; meaning people with different knowledge or perspective interpret the same situation differently.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容同一情景会因见识或角度不同而产生不同的理解：有识之人能看出成双成对或内在联系，外行或不懂的人只看到表面的两个事物或两个人。
explanation_english: Used to describe situations that can be interpreted differently depending on one's knowledge or perspective: the perceptive see a pair/relationship, while the unknowing see merely two separate things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇吓佢哋咁黐埋一齊，识者鸳鸯，唔识者两样。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 keoi5 dei6 gam2 ci1 maai4 jat1 cai4, sik1 ze2 jyun1 joeng1, m4 sik1 ze2 loeng5 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看看他们那么黏在一起，识者看成鸳鸯，不识者看成两样。
examples.english_sentence: Look at them clinging together like that; the perceptive see a pair of lovers, the unknowing just see two separate people.

mandarin_meaning: 有本领却没有机会或资源施展（有才无用武之地）
english_meaning: Skilled or knowledgeable but lacking the opportunity or resources to use one's abilities
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面是「懂藥卻沒有柴火可燒」，用來形容人有本事或技術，但沒有機會、工作或資源可以發揮。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom literally meaning "knows medicine but has no firewood to burn". It describes someone who has skill or knowledge but lacks opportunities, work, or resources to apply it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢學咗醫學咁耐，技術好，但係識藥冇柴燒，幾年都搵唔到穩定份工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hok6 zo2 ji1 hok6 gam2 noi6, gei6 seot6 hou2, daan6 hai6 sik1 joek6 mou5 caai4 siu1, gei2 nin4 dou1 wan2 m4 dou2 wan2 ding6 fan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他學了醫學很久，技術很好，但有本領沒用武之地，幾年都找不到穩定的工作。
examples.english_sentence: He studied medicine for years and has excellent skills, but he's skilled with no opportunity — he hasn't been able to find steady work for years.

mandarin_meaning: 假意；假装有诚意或关心，实际并非如此
english_meaning: to feign sincerity or goodwill; to pretend interest or willingness while not meaning it
explanation_mandarin: “诈假意”指表面上装出有诚意、愿意或关心，但其实是假装的，常带有讨好或欺骗成分。
explanation_english: “Zaa3 gaa2 ji3” means to put on a show of sincerity, willingness, or concern while actually being insincere — often to flatter, manipulate, or deceive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺老細面前詐假意，實際上只係想討好老細。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 lou5 sai3 min6 cin4 zaa3 gaa2 ji3, sat6 zai3 seong6 zi2 hai6 soeng2 tou2 hou2 lou5 sai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在老板面前假装有诚意，实际上只是想讨好老板。
examples.english_sentence: He feigned sincerity in front of the boss, but in reality he was just trying to ingratiate himself.

mandarin_meaning: 装傻装蒙；假装不懂或不清楚以推脱责任或隐瞒真相
english_meaning: to play dumb; to feign ignorance or confusion to avoid responsibility or hide the truth
explanation_mandarin: 指故意裝作傻、裝作不明白或裝作糊塗，通常為了逃避責任、推脫或掩飾真正情況。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression meaning to deliberately act dumb or confused, usually to evade responsibility, avoid answering, or conceal the truth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺老闆面前诈傻扮懵，想逃避責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 lou5 baan2 min6 cin4 zaa3 so4 baan6 mung2, soeng2 tou4 bei6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在老闆面前裝傻裝蒙，想逃避責任。
examples.english_sentence: He always plays dumb in front of the boss to avoid responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你真係知，就唔好诈傻扮懵，老實啲講出嚟啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 zan1 hai6 zi1, zau6 m4 hou2 zaa3 so4 baan6 mung2, lou5 sat6 di1 gong2 ceot1 lai4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你真的知道，就別裝傻裝蒙，老實點說出來吧。
examples.english_sentence: If you really know, don't pretend to be ignorant—be honest and tell it.

mandarin_meaning: 装傻纳福（装傻以图好处/逃避责任）
english_meaning: play dumb to gain favor or avoid responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 指故意装傻、示弱或装无辜，以逃避责任或从中获得好处、照顾或宽待，常含讽刺意味，为口语/俗语用法。
explanation_english: To deliberately play dumb, appear innocent, or act foolish in order to avoid responsibility or obtain favors, leniency, or special treatment; colloquial and often pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺老闆面前詐傻納福，想唔使加班。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai6 lou5 baan2 min6 cin4 zaa3 so4 naap6 fuk1, soeng2 m4 sai2 gaa1 baan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常在老板面前装傻纳福，想不必加班。
examples.english_sentence: He often plays dumb in front of the boss to avoid having to work overtime.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 每逢見到親戚送禮佢就詐傻納福，等人多啲照顧佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mui5 fung4 gin3 dou3 can1 cik1 sung3 lai5 keoi5 zau6 zaa3 so4 naap6 fuk1 dang2 jan4 do1 di1 ziu3 gu3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 每逢见到亲戚送礼，他就装傻纳福，让人多照顾他。
examples.english_sentence: Whenever relatives give gifts, he plays dumb to get taken care of more.

mandarin_meaning: 装作不知道；假装不知道
english_meaning: pretend not to know; feign ignorance
explanation_mandarin: 指故意装作不知道或不明白某件事，常用来逃避责任或回避问题。
explanation_english: To deliberately pretend not to know or be aware of something, often to avoid responsibility or to evade a question.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢明明見到條單，但係佢就诈唔知。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ming4 ming4 gin3 dou2 tiu4 daan1, daan6 hai6 keoi5 zau6 zaa3 m4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他明明看到那张单，但他就装作不知道。
examples.english_sentence: He clearly saw the bill, but he pretended not to know.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老細問點解遲到，佢就诈唔知。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 sai3 man6 dim2 gaai2 ci4 dou3, keoi5 zau6 zaa3 m4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板问为什么迟到，他就装作不知道。
examples.english_sentence: When the boss asked why he was late, he pretended not to know.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好噉诈唔知，講清楚啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 zaa3 m4 zi1, gong2 cing1 co2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要这样装作不知道，把话说清楚吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pretend not to know like that; make it clear.

mandarin_meaning: 裝瘋賣傻（裝傻、裝瘋以逃避責任或責罰）
english_meaning: to pretend to be crazy or play dumb (to avoid responsibility or trouble)
explanation_mandarin: 指故意裝瘋或裝傻，以逃避責任、責罰或不想正面回答問題的行為。
explanation_english: Refers to deliberately pretending to be insane or acting dumb in order to avoid responsibility, punishment, or direct answers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 每次有事佢就诈癫扮傻，唔肯負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mui5 ci3 jau5 si6 keoi5 zau6 zaa3 din1 baan6 so4, m4 hang2 fu6 zaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 每次有事他就裝瘋賣傻，不肯負責。
examples.english_sentence: Every time there's a problem he just plays dumb and refuses to take responsibility.

mandarin_meaning: 告诉他 / 让他知道
english_meaning: tell him; let him know
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语表达，意为把某事告诉对方或让对方知道，常与「話畀佢知」「話佢知」通用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to tell someone or let them know about something. It is commonly used like '話畀佢知' or '話佢知'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好自己諗，話之佢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zi6 gei2 lam2, waa6 zi1 keoi5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要自己想，告诉他吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't decide on your own, tell him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等我哋決定咗先再話之佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 dei6 kyut3 ding6 zo2 sin1 zoi3 waa6 zi1 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等我们决定了再告诉他。
examples.english_sentence: Wait until we decide, then tell him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你已經幫到佢，就話之佢，叫佢準備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 ji5 ging1 bong1 dou3 keoi5, zau6 waa6 zi1 keoi5, giu3 keoi5 zyun2 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你已经帮到他，就告诉他，让他准备。
examples.english_sentence: If you've already helped him, tell him to get ready.

mandarin_meaning: 有決定權的人；說了算的人
english_meaning: a person who calls the shots; the decision-maker
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語或俗語，指在團體、家庭或場合中擁有最後決定權、說了算的人。語氣常帶口語或戲謔色彩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term referring to someone who has the final say or decision-making authority in a group, family, or situation. Often used in an informal or slightly teasing tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次就由佢話事偈，其他人唔好插手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 zau6 jau4 keoi5 waa6 si6 gai3, kei4 taa1 jan4 m4 hou2 caap3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次就由他做话事偈，其他人不要插手。
examples.english_sentence: This time he'll have the final say; others shouldn't interfere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司新政策由主管話事偈，大家要遵守。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 san1 zing3 caak3 jau4 zyu2 gun2 waa6 si6 gai3, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zeon1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的新政策由主管決定，大家要遵守。
examples.english_sentence: The company's new policy is decided by the manager; everyone must comply.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁樣講，好似以為自己係話事偈咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 joeng6 gong2, hou2 ci5 ji5 wai6 zi6 gei2 hai6 waa6 si6 gai3 gam3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这样说，好像以为自己是话事偈一样。
examples.english_sentence: What he said sounds like he thinks he's the one who calls the shots.

mandarin_meaning: 没那么快 / 别那么急 / 别下结论太早
english_meaning: Not so fast; don't be so hasty; hold on
explanation_mandarin: 口语用法，用来阻止对方过早行动或下结论，相当于“没那么快”“别急”“别下定论”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to stop someone from acting too quickly or drawing premature conclusions; equivalent to 'not so fast', 'hold on', or 'don't be so hasty'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好話冇咁快啦，等我諗清楚先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 waa6 mou5 gam2 faai3 laa1, dang2 ngo5 lam2 cing1 co2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别那么快，让我先想清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Not so fast — let me think it through first.

mandarin_meaning: 话还没说完 / 话未说完
english_meaning: I haven't finished speaking / before I finished my sentence
explanation_mandarin: 表示話還沒有說完，常用於被打斷或想接着說下去時提醒對方不要插嘴或表示自己還沒講完。
explanation_english: Indicates the speaker hasn't finished speaking; used to complain about being interrupted or to signal that one intends to continue talking. Equivalent to 'I wasn't finished' or 'before I finished my sentence.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等陣，話口未完，我仲有嘢要講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 zan6, waa6 hau2 mei6 jyun4, ngo5 zung6 jau5 je5 jiu3 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等等，話還沒說完，我還有話要說。
examples.english_sentence: Wait, I haven't finished speaking, I still have something to say.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱準備繼續講，話口未完就俾人插咗嘴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 zeon2 bei6 gai3 zuk6 gong2, waa6 hau2 mei6 jyun4 zau6 bei2 jan4 caap3 zo2 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛準備繼續說話，話還沒說完就被人插嘴了。
examples.english_sentence: He was just about to continue talking, but before he finished, someone interrupted him.

mandarin_meaning: （口语）没那么容易；说起来容易做起来难（常用来表示反驳或提醒）
english_meaning: Easier said than done; it's not that simple
explanation_mandarin: 用于表示某件事并不像说的那么简单，常用于反驳别人轻率的说法或提醒困难所在。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something is not as easy as it sounds; often used to rebut a casual claim or to point out practical difficulties.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話寫完呢份報告幾個鐘就得，話咁易？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 se2 jyun4 ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 gei2 go3 zung1 zau6 dak1, waa6 gam2 ji6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说几个小时就能写完这份报告，哪有那么容易？
examples.english_sentence: You say you can finish this report in a few hours — it's not that easy.

mandarin_meaning: 说不完 / 说不尽 / 没说完
english_meaning: can't say it all; unable to finish saying something or cover all points
explanation_mandarin: 表示话还没说完或说不完，无法在一次谈话中把所有内容讲清楚或讲完。
explanation_english: Indicates that one cannot finish saying something or cannot cover all points in a single conversation; there's not enough time/space to say everything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我有好多嘢想講，但時間太短，話唔埋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jau5 hou2 do1 je5 soeng2 gong2, daan6 si4 gaan3 taai3 dyun2, waa6 m4 maai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我有很多话想说，但时间太短，说不完。
examples.english_sentence: I had a lot to say, but time was too short — I couldn't say it all.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講到嗰度已經好複雜，話唔埋，要改日慢慢傾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 dou3 go2 dou6 ji5 ging1 hou2 fuk1 zaap6, waa6 m4 maai4, jiu3 goi2 jat6 maan6 maan6 king1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 讲到那裡已经很复杂，说不完，要改天慢慢谈。
examples.english_sentence: By the time we reached that point it was complicated; we couldn't finish talking about it — we'll have to discuss it another day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我仲有啲細節未講，唔想漏咗，話唔埋所以先寫低。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung6 jau5 di1 sai3 zit3 mei6 gong2, m4 soeng2 lau6 zo2, waa6 m4 maai4 so2 ji5 sin1 se2 dai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我还有些细节没说，不想漏掉，说不完所以先写下來。
examples.english_sentence: I still have some details unsaid and don't want to miss them — I can't say it all, so I'll write them down first.

mandarin_meaning: 说不定 / 可能
english_meaning: maybe; possibly; it might be the case
explanation_mandarin: 表示不确定，表示某事有可能发生或属实，常用于口语。
explanation_english: Expresses uncertainty; indicates that something might happen or might be true. Commonly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 話唔定聽日會落雨，記得帶把遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: waa6 m4 ding6 ting1 jat6 wui5 lok6 jyu5, gei3 dak1 daai3 baa2 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 说不定明天会下雨，记得带把伞。
examples.english_sentence: It might rain tomorrow; remember to bring an umbrella.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家唔喺度，話唔定已經走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 m4 hai2 dou6, waa6 m4 ding6 ji5 ging1 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在不在，说不定已经走了。
examples.english_sentence: He's not here now; he might have already left.

mandarin_meaning: 只是、而已、罷了
english_meaning: just; only; that's all; merely
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 語氣助詞 / 副詞性語助詞
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語常用句尾語氣詞，用來淡化語氣或表示僅此而已。常見寫法為「話啫」，「话嗻」可視為變體或非正字書寫。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese sentence-final particle meaning 'just', 'only', or 'that's all'. It downplays or minimizes a statement. Commonly written as 「話啫」; 「话嗻」 is a variant spelling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔使咁緊張，話啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 sai2 gam2 gan2 zoeng1, waa6 zek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不用那麼緊張，只是而已。
examples.english_sentence: You don't need to be so nervous, it's just that.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話唔係有心啫，唔好再鬧佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 m4 hai6 jau5 sam1 zek3, m4 hou2 zoi3 nau6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說不是有心的，只是而已，別再責怪他了。
examples.english_sentence: He said it wasn't on purpose, it's just that—don't scold him anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我只係開玩笑啫，唔使認真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi2 hai6 hoi1 waan2 siu3 zek3, m4 sai2 jing6 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我只是開玩笑而已，不用認真。
examples.english_sentence: I was just joking, no need to take it seriously.

mandarin_meaning: 欲言又止；开了头却没有说完/交代
english_meaning: to start to say something but stop; to leave a remark unfinished or leave something unsaid
explanation_mandarin: 形容說話時提到某件事或剛開始要說，但沒有把話說完或交代清楚，類似“欲言又止”或“說到一半就停住”。
explanation_english: Describes starting to mention something or beginning to speak but not finishing or making a clear conclusion—similar to 'starting to say something but stopping' or 'leaving a remark hanging.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話頭醒尾，好似有嘢想講但又講唔出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 waa6 tau4 sing2 mei5, hou2 ci5 jau5 je5 soeng2 gong2 daan6 jau6 gong2 m4 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常欲言又止，好像有事想说却又说不出来。
examples.english_sentence: He often starts to say something but stops; it seems like he wants to say something but can't get it out.

mandarin_meaning: 可以說是；可以算作
english_meaning: can be said to be; can be regarded as
explanation_mandarin: 表示某人或某事可以被這樣稱呼或歸入某個類別，相當於「可以說是」「說得上」。
explanation_english: Indicates that someone or something can be described or classified in a certain way; equivalent to "you could say" or "can be considered as."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔係正式員工，但可以話得埋係我哋一員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 hai6 zing3 sik1 jyun4 gung1, daan6 ho2 ji5 waa6 dak1 maai4 hai6 ngo5 dei6 jat1 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不是正式員工，但可以說得上是我們一員。
examples.english_sentence: He's not an official staff member, but you could say he's one of us.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件小事雖然唔大，但都可以話得埋係個問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 siu2 si6 seoi1 jin4 m4 daai6, daan6 dou1 ho2 ji5 waa6 dak1 maai4 hai6 go3 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件小事雖然不大，但也可以說是個問題。
examples.english_sentence: This minor matter may not be big, but you could still call it a problem.

mandarin_meaning: 明确告诉你／事先告诉你（我早就跟你说了）
english_meaning: to tell you clearly or explicitly; (often) 'I told you so' or 'I'll make it clear to you'
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语表达，表示把某事明确地告诉对方，常用来强调已告知或事先提醒对方可能后果。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to state something clearly to someone. Often used to emphasize that one has already informed someone or to warn them in advance of possible consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我早就話明你知，唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zou2 zau6 waa6 ming4 nei5 zi1, m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早就告诉你，不要相信他。
examples.english_sentence: I told you already — don't trust him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 話明你知，呢件事會有後果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: waa6 ming4 nei5 zi1, ni1 gin6 si6 wui5 jau5 hau6 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明确告诉你，这件事会有后果。
examples.english_sentence: I'm making it clear to you — this will have consequences.

mandarin_meaning: 毕竟还是 / 归根结底还是
english_meaning: after all; in the final analysis (it's still ...)
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語表達，用於總結或強調，表示在考慮所有情況後仍然是某種結果或理由，相當於“毕竟还是/归根结底还是”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to sum up or emphasize that, after considering everything, something is still the case — equivalent to 'after all' or 'in the final analysis'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 話晒都系你努力，先至有今日嘅成績。
examples.jyutping_sentence: waa6 saai3 dou1 hai6 nei5 nou5 lik6, sin1 zi3 jau5 gam1 jat6 ge3 sing4 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 毕竟还是你的努力，才有今天的成绩。
examples.english_sentence: After all, it's your hard work that led to today's results.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋未夠經驗，話晒都系細路，唔怪得人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 mei6 gau3 ging1 jim6, waa6 saai3 dou1 hai6 sai3 lou6, m4 gwaai3 dak1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们没有足够经验，毕竟还是孩子，不要怪他们。
examples.english_sentence: They lack experience — after all they're kids, so you can't blame them.

mandarin_meaning: 待會兒說／遲些再說
english_meaning: to tell/say (something) later; I'll tell you later
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示會在之後告訴或說明某事，相當於普通話的「待會兒說」或「遲些再說」。有時也作為填充語，表示暫緩回應。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to indicate that something will be said or explained later—equivalent to Mandarin "待會兒說" or English "I'll tell you later." It can also function as a filler to defer responding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等我話落畀你聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 waa6 lok6 bei2 nei5 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等我待會兒告訴你。
examples.english_sentence: I'll tell you later.

jyutping: cing2 san4 jung4 ji6 sung3 san4 naan4
mandarin_meaning: 请神容易送神难（qǐng shén róng yì sòng shén nán）：比喻做一件事容易开始，但要收回或结束却很困难。
english_meaning: Inviting the deity is easy but sending it away is hard — used metaphorically for situations that are easy to start but difficult to finish or to get someone/something to leave.
explanation_mandarin: 原指請神很容易，但送走神卻很困難。現多用來比喻開始一件事或引入某人很容易，收尾、撤回或讓對方離開卻很難處理。
explanation_english: Originally referring to how it's easy to invite a deity but hard to send it away; now used figuratively to mean something is easy to initiate (or bring someone in) but difficult to terminate or reverse.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 當初老闆請佢入嚟幫忙，依家想佢走就唔容易，真係請神容易送神難。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dong1 co1 lou5 baan2 cing2 keoi5 jap6 lei4 bong1 mong4, ji1 gaa1 soeng2 keoi5 zau2 zau6 m4 jung4 ji6, zan1 hai6 cing2 san4 jung4 ji6 sung3 san4 naan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 當初老板请他来帮忙，现在想让他走就不容易，真是请神容易送神难。
examples.english_sentence: The boss invited him in to help at first; now it's not easy to get him to leave — truly, inviting the god is easy but sending him off is hard.

synonyms: 請人入來容易，辭退卻難

mandarin_meaning: 把所有事情處理好；處理一切事務
english_meaning: to take care of / handle all matters; to manage everything
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指把各種大大小小的事情都處理妥當，常用於描述能夠打理家務或工作事務的人。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to handle or take care of all kinds of matters (big and small). Often used to describe someone who can manage household or work affairs effectively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一個人就可以諸事理晒屋企嘅大小事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4 zau6 ho2 ji5 zyu1 si6 lei5 saai3 uk1 kei5 ge3 daai6 siu2 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一個人就可以把家裡的大小事都處理好。
examples.english_sentence: He can handle all the big and small matters at home by himself.

mandarin_meaning: 想來想去；反覆思考
english_meaning: to keep thinking something over and over; to mull over; to go over and over in one's mind
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示對某事反覆思考、反覆琢磨、想來想去，常帶有猶豫或難以決定的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to repeatedly think about something or mull it over, often implying hesitation or difficulty deciding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我諗嚟度去都唔知道點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 nam2 lai4 dou6 heoi3 dou1 m4 zi1 dou6 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想來想去還是不知道怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: I've thought it over and over and still don't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 想认真一点 / 多考虑一下
english_meaning: think more carefully; be more serious/considerate
explanation_mandarin: 用于催促對方多想一想、认真考虑事情或别冲动行事，多见于粤语口语。
explanation_english: Used to urge someone to think more carefully or take something more seriously; colloquial Cantonese imperative often used to caution against impulsive actions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你谂真啲啦，呢單生意唔可以咁魯莽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 nam2 zan1 di1 laa1, ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 m4 ho2 ji5 gam2 lou5 mong5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你想认真一点，这笔生意不能这么鲁莽。
examples.english_sentence: Think more carefully — this deal can't be handled so recklessly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門前谂真啲，記得帶埋護照同錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 cin4 nam2 zan1 di1, gei3 dak1 daai3 maai4 wu6 ziu3 tung4 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出门之前想认真一点，记得把护照和钱都带好。
examples.english_sentence: Think more carefully before leaving — remember to bring your passport and money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你同佢分手前谂真啲，唔好衝動講出傷人嘅說話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tung4 keoi5 fan1 sau2 cin4 nam2 zan1 di1, m4 hou2 cung1 dung6 gong2 ceot1 soeng1 jan4 ge3 syut3 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在和他分手之前想认真一点，不要冲动说出伤人的话。
examples.english_sentence: Think carefully before breaking up with them — don't say hurtful things impulsively.

mandarin_meaning: 反悔、不履行诺言或在款项/数量上退缩、减少承诺
english_meaning: to renege on a promise (often by reducing the promised amount); to back out or shortchange someone
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语，通常指对已答应的事或金额反悔，临时缩减或不按原约定履行。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to go back on an agreement or promise—especially by reducing the promised amount or not honouring the original terms.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你答應畀我一千蚊，唔好谂缩数。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 daap3 jing3 bei2 ngo5 jat1 cin1 man1, m4 hou2 nam2 suk1 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你答应给我一千块钱，不要反悔缩数。
examples.english_sentence: You promised to give me $1,000—don't renege on that.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件事到最後佢又谂缩数，真係唔可靠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 si6 dou3 zeoi6 hau6 keoi5 jau6 nam2 suk1 sou3, zan1 hai6 m4 ho2 kaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 事情到最后他又反悔缩数，真不可靠。
examples.english_sentence: He backed out at the last minute again—really unreliable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意唔好谂缩数，會冇人信你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 m4 hou2 nam2 suk1 sou3, wui5 mou5 jan4 seon3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意不要反悔缩数，会没人相信你。
examples.english_sentence: Don't shortchange people in business—no one will trust you.

mandarin_meaning: 改变主意 / 重新考虑
english_meaning: to change one's mind; to rethink; to reconsider
explanation_mandarin: 口語粤语表达，表示原本的决定或想法被改变，重新考虑或改主意。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to change one's mind or to rethink/reconsider a decision.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我諗翻轉頭唔去旅行喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 nam2 faan1 zyun2 tau4 m4 heoi3 leoi5 hang4 laa3
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我改变主意了，不去旅行了。
examples.english_sentence: I changed my mind — I'm not going on the trip.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到價錢就諗翻轉頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 gaa3 cin2 zau6 nam2 faan1 zyun2 tau4
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一听到价钱就改变主意了。
examples.english_sentence: He changed his mind as soon as he heard the price.

mandarin_meaning: 靠爹／啃老（主要指靠父親提供金錢或資源）
english_meaning: to mooch off one's father; to rely on daddy (financially or for support)
explanation_mandarin: 「谷爹」為粵語俚語，通常用來形容某人依賴父親（多指父親提供金錢或資源），不願或不努力自立。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to rely on one's father (especially for money or resources), i.e., to mooch off dad instead of being independent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識谷爹，唔肯自己搵工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 guk1 de1, m4 hang2 zi6 gei2 wan2 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會靠爹，不肯自己找工作。
examples.english_sentence: He only knows how to mooch off his dad; he won't look for a job himself.

jyutping: si6 jau4 lou1 faan6, zing2 sik1 seoi2
mandarin_meaning: 豉油拌饭，做表面功夫；敷衍了事、弄虛作假
english_meaning: literally 'soy‑sauce rice; make it look nice' — colloquially to do a shabby/half‑hearted job and/or to make something look good only on the surface (for show)
explanation_mandarin: 兩個俗語合用。『豉油捞饭』原指簡單、隨便的一餐，引申為做事馬虎、敷衍；『整色水』指弄虛作樣、只做表面功夫。合起來用時，形容人做事既草率又愛作表面功夫，或把爛工夫包裝得好看。
explanation_english: A pairing of two Cantonese colloquialisms. '豉油捞饭' (soy‑sauce rice) originally refers to a plain, cheap meal and is extended to mean doing things carelessly or half‑heartedly. '整色水' means to prettify or make something look good only on the surface. Used together, the phrase criticizes work that is both sloppy and merely for show.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份報告你唔好豉油捞饭，整色水，老闆會睇出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 nei5 m4 hou2 si6 jau4 lou1 faan6, zing2 sik1 seoi2, lou5 baan2 wui5 tai2 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份報告你不要敷衍了事、裝樣子，老闆會看出來。
examples.english_sentence: Don't half‑ass this report or just make it look good on the surface; the boss will notice.

jyutping: si6 jau4 zyun1 zi2, haam4 sap1
mandarin_meaning: 好色、下流（帶有貶義的廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: lecherous; sexually suggestive or sleazy (Cantonese slang, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「豉油樽枳，咸湿」是廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人好色、言行帶有性暗示或令人覺得下流，帶有貶義和戲謔意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to describe someone who is lecherous or makes sexually suggestive/lewd remarks or actions. It is derogatory and often used humorously or disparagingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺巴士上望住啲女仔，仲講埋啲下流說話，真係豉油樽枳，咸湿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 baa1 si2 soeng5 mong6 zyu6 di1 neoi5 zai2, zung6 gong2 maai4 di1 haa6 lau4 syut3 waa6, zan1 hai6 si6 jau4 zyun1 zi2, haam4 sap1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在公車上盯著女生看，還說一些下流的話，真是好色又下流。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps staring at the girls on the bus and even makes lewd comments — he's really lecherous.

cantonese: 豉油辣椒酱，你想点就点
jyutping: si6 jau4 laat6 ziu1 zoeng3, nei5 soeng2 dim2 zau6 dim2
mandarin_meaning: （俚语）豉油辣椒酱，随你喜欢/你想怎样就怎样（表示随便、听你的）
english_meaning: A playful Cantonese slang phrase literally mentioning a soy‑sauce + chili mix and meaning "do as you like" / "suit yourself" (i.e., I'm leaving the choice to you).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語 / 俚語（句式）
explanation_mandarin: 這句話字面上提到一種調味醬（豉油加辣椒），實際用法是俚語或玩笑式地表示「隨便、你決定就好」，常用於不想多參與決定或把選擇權交給對方時。
explanation_english: Literally names a soy‑sauce + chili condiment, but used as a playful Cantonese slang line meaning "do as you like" or "whatever you want." It's often used to hand the decision to someone else or show indifference about the choice.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講：『豉油辣椒酱，你想点就点』，唔好煩我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2: 'si6 jau4 laat6 ziu1 zoeng3, nei5 soeng2 dim2 zau6 dim2', m4 hou2 faan4 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說：「豉油辣椒酱，你想点就点」，別煩我。
examples.english_sentence: He said, "豉油辣椒酱，你想点就点" — don't bother me.

mandarin_meaning: 耍脾气、发火、生气（口语）
english_meaning: to sulk, to get angry or huffy (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容因小事或不如意而耍脾气、发闷气或生气，类似“耍脾气/鬧彆扭”。通常用于描述人在情绪上表露不满或耍小性子。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to sulk, get huffy, or show annoyance—often over small matters. Used to describe someone displaying petulant or sullen behaviour.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日因為細微嘢就豎蔥，麻煩死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jan1 wai6 sai3 mei4 je5 zau6 syu6 cung1, maa4 faan4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常为了小事就耍脾气，真麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: He always sulks over small things; such a pain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好當住人面前豎蔥，會好尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 dong3 zyu6 jan4 min6 cin4 syu6 cung1, wui5 hou2 gaan1 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要当着别人面子耍脾气，会很尴尬。
examples.english_sentence: Don't sulk in front of others; it's embarrassing.

mandarin_meaning: 傲慢、擺架子（口語粵語俚語）
english_meaning: arrogant; stuck-up; to put on airs (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: “象拔（鼻）”是粵語口語俚語，用來形容一個人自以為是、傲慢、擺架子，看不起別人。語氣較口語且帶貶義。
explanation_english: “象拔 (bei)” is Cantonese colloquial slang used to describe someone who is arrogant, pretentious, or puts on airs. It's informal and carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁樣講嘢，真係好象拔鼻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 joeng6 gong2 je5, zan1 hai6 hou2 zoeng6 baat3 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那樣說話，真的很傲慢/很愛擺架子。
examples.english_sentence: He talks like that — he's really so arrogant.

mandarin_meaning: xiàngtián（常作人名或地名，字面為「象的田」）
english_meaning: Xiangtian (usually a personal or place name; literal meaning "elephant field")
explanation_mandarin: 「象田」並非常用的粵語詞彙，通常見於人名或地名。單字字面意思是「象的田」，但作為名稱時沒有特殊的慣用含義。
explanation_english: “象田” is not a common Cantonese lexical item; it is typically used as a personal name or place name. Literally it means “elephant field,” but as a name it carries no special idiomatic meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 象田先生聽日會嚟開會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng6 tin4 sin1 saang1 ting1 jat6 wui5 lai4 hoi1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 象田先生明天會來開會。
examples.english_sentence: Mr. Xiangtian will come to attend the meeting tomorrow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢屋企係象田村，喺鄉下好寧靜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 uk1 kei2 hai6 zoeng6 tin4 cyun1, hai2 hoeng1 haa6 hou2 ning4 zing6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他家在象田村，在鄉下很寧靜。
examples.english_sentence: His home is in Xiangtian Village, a quiet countryside place.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：大象的腳步或足跡；引申：笨重、踏實的步伐（此詞在現代粵語中極為罕見，主要為書面或文言用法）
english_meaning: Literal: an elephant's footstep/footprint; figurative: heavy, clumsy steps (this term is extremely rare in modern Cantonese and mainly literary/archaic)
explanation_mandarin: 「象跋」由「象」（大象）與「跋」（腳步、踏行、足跡）組成。現代口語粵語中幾乎不常見，通常可作字面意指大象留下的足印，或比喻步伐笨重、沉重。常見於書面或較文言的語境，而非日常口語。
explanation_english: Composed of '象' (elephant) and '跋' (step/footprint). In modern spoken Cantonese the term is extremely uncommon. It can be taken literally to mean an elephant's footprint, or used figuratively to describe heavy, clumsy steps. It is chiefly literary/archaic rather than colloquial.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢度嘅泥地留咗幾個好大嘅象跋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 ge3 nai4 dei6 lau4 zo2 gei2 go3 hou2 daai6 ge3 zoeng6 bat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这里的泥地留下了几处很大的象跋（象蹄印）。
examples.english_sentence: There are several large elephant footprints in the mud here.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢行路好似象跋咁笨重，步伐沉實。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haang4 lou6 hou2 ci5 zoeng6 bat6 gam2 ban6 zung6, bou6 faat3 cam4 sat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走路像象跋一样笨重，步伐沉稳。
examples.english_sentence: He walks with heavy, elephant-like steps; his gait is solid but clumsy.

mandarin_meaning: 豬仔薯：對小顆或作為零食的番薯的俗稱（廣東/香港口語）
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese term for small sweet potatoes or sweet-potato snacks (Hong Kong usage).
explanation_mandarin: 「豬仔藷」是廣東/香港地區口語用法，指較小顆或常作零食的番薯（甘薯、地瓜）。有時帶有親昵或兒時回憶的語感。
explanation_english: “豬仔藷” is a Cantonese colloquial term used in Guangdong/Hong Kong to refer to small sweet potatoes or sweet-potato snacks. It often carries a familiar or nostalgic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細個嗰陣，我成日食豬仔藷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 go3 go2 zan6, ngo5 seng4 jat6 sik6 zyu1 zai2 syu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小時候，我常常吃豬仔薯。
examples.english_sentence: When I was a child, I often ate piglet sweet potatoes (small sweet potatoes).

mandarin_meaning: （非標準詞）可能作為人名「朱莉」的音譯或作綽號使用，字面為「豬」+「利」，可帶親暱或戲謔意味
english_meaning: Not a standard lexical item; often appears as a personal name transliteration (e.g. 'Zhu Li') or a nickname literally 'pig-Li', used affectionately or teasingly
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（人名 / 綽號 / 俗稱）
explanation_mandarin: 「豬利」在粵語裡並非常見的固定詞彙，常見用法是作為綽號或人名的音譯。視語境可為親暱稱呼或帶有戲謔、貶義的語氣。
explanation_english: “豬利” is not a common standard Cantonese lexical item. It is commonly used as a nickname or a transliteration of a personal name (e.g. Zhu Li). Depending on context it can be affectionate or teasing/derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿豬利係我同學嘅綽號，大家都咁叫佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 zyu1 lei6 hai6 ngo5 tung4 hok6 ge3 coek3 hou6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 gam2 giu3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「阿豬利」是我同學的綽號，大家都這樣叫他／她。
examples.english_sentence: 'Ah Zyu Lei' is my classmate's nickname; everyone calls him/her that.

mandarin_meaning: 猪膀胱／猪尿囊（动物的膀胱），亦可作粗俗的贬义称呼（罕见）
english_meaning: pig bladder (the urinary bladder of a pig); occasionally a coarse derogatory term in Cantonese
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指豬的膀胱或尿囊，常見於烹飪或傳統藥膳的材料。於香港粵語裡也有少量俗用、帶貶義的情況，用來罵人沒用或可鄙，但此用法較粗俗且不常見。
explanation_english: Literally the pig's urinary bladder — an anatomical organ sometimes used as an ingredient in cooking or traditional remedies. In Hong Kong Cantonese it can also be used as a coarse, derogatory insult (rare), meaning a worthless or contemptible person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽話將豬尿胞洗淨再落去煲湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 waa6 zoeng1 zyu1 niu6 baau1 sai2 zing6 zoi3 lok6 heoi3 bou1 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽說把豬尿胞洗淨再放去煲湯。
examples.english_sentence: Mom said to clean the pig bladder before putting it in the soup.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 叫佢幫手佢就走，真係豬尿胞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: giu3 keoi5 bong1 sau2 keoi5 zau6 zau2, zan1 hai6 zyu1 niu6 baau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 叫他幫忙他就走，真是豬尿胞。
examples.english_sentence: When you asked him to help he just left — what a pig bladder (i.e., useless person).

mandarin_meaning: （俚語、貶義）形容無用或令人討厭的人
english_meaning: Cantonese slang insult for a worthless, contemptible, or lazy person
explanation_mandarin: 粵語粗俗俚語，用來罵人，意指一個無用、卑劣或討厭的人。帶有冒犯性，常於香港口語出現。字面為「豬屎鶫」，並非指真實的鳥。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang insult used to call someone worthless, contemptible, lazy, or annoying. It is offensive and common in Hong Kong colloquial speech. Literally "pig-shit thrush," not referring to an actual bird.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係豬屎鶫，做事又慢又懶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 zyu1 si2 dung1, zou6 si6 jau6 maan6 jau6 laan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個豬屎鶫，做事又慢又懶。
examples.english_sentence: He's a real '豬屎鶫' — slow and lazy when it comes to work.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語俚語）指心地軟、容易被人利用或上當的人
english_meaning: (Cantonese slang) a soft-hearted or easily gullible person; someone who gets taken advantage of
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 形容詞（口語用法）
explanation_mandarin: 「豬肚棉」是廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人心腸軟、易同情、容易被人利用或欺騙。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone soft-hearted, overly sympathetic, and easily used or deceived by others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到陌生人求助就幫，成日畀人利用，真係豬肚棉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 mak6 saang1 jan4 kau4 zo6 zau6 bong1, seng4 jat6 bei2 jan4 lei6 jung6, zan1 hai6 zyu1 tou5 min4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到陌生人求助就幫忙，經常被人利用，真是豬肚棉。
examples.english_sentence: He helps strangers who ask for help and often gets used — he's really a soft-hearted/gullible person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做豬肚棉，學識講唔得先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 zyu1 tou5 min4, hok6 sik1 gong2 m4 dak1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要做豬肚棉，先學會說不。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a pushover; learn to say no first.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）笨蛋、傻瓜
english_meaning: (slang) idiot; fool
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，用來戲稱或罵人笨拙、愚蠢，語氣通常為非正式且帶貶義或玩笑成分。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to mock or call someone foolish/stupid. It is informal and typically pejorative or joking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做，真係豬肝藷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 zou6, zan1 hai6 zyu1 gon1 syu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣做，真是個笨蛋。
examples.english_sentence: Doing this, you're really an idiot.

mandarin_meaning: 猪脚醋（猪脚姜）
english_meaning: pigs' trotters in vinegar (a Cantonese dish often served postpartum or at a baby's one-month celebration)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東傳統菜餚，將豬腳與薑和黑醋一同煮制，常在產後坐月或嬰兒滿月時用作補身和贈送的禮品。
explanation_english: A Cantonese traditional dish of pig's trotters cooked with ginger and black vinegar. It is commonly given to women after childbirth for recuperation and served or gifted at a baby's one-month celebration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿嫂坐完月，屋企人整咗豬腳醋嚟補身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 sou2 co5 jyut6, uk1 kei5 jan4 zing2 zo2 zyu1 goek3 cou3 lei4 bou2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 嫂子坐完月，家人煮了猪脚醋來補身。
examples.english_sentence: After my sister-in-law finished her confinement period, the family made pig's trotters in vinegar to help her recover.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺香港，滿月時通常會送豬腳醋畀親友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 hoeng1 gong2, mun5 jyut6 si4 tung1 soeng4 wui5 sung3 zyu1 goek3 cou3 bei2 can1 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在香港，滿月時通常會送豬腳醋給親友。
examples.english_sentence: In Hong Kong, it's common to give pig's trotters in vinegar to friends and relatives at a baby's one-month celebration.

mandarin_meaning: 猪踝、猪蹄的一部分（常指猪后腿靠近脚踝/猪肘一带，烹饪用材）
english_meaning: pork hock; pig's hock; pork knuckle (the joint/ankle area of a pig, commonly used as a cooking ingredient)
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语中指猪的踝部或猪蹄的一部分，常用來燉湯、紅燒或卤製，肉質帶筋膜和明膠，適合久燉或慢煮。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, it refers to the hock/ankle area of a pig (part of the pig's trotters or knuckle). It is commonly used in cooking (stews, braises, soups) and is valued for its gelatinous texture after long cooking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚煲豬踭湯，補返個身啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 bou1 zyu1 zaang1 tong1, bou2 faan1 go3 san1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚煲豬踝湯，補一補身體吧。
examples.english_sentence: I'm making pork hock soup tonight to help nourish the body.

mandarin_meaning: 豬舌；豬舌頭（食材）
english_meaning: pig tongue (food)
explanation_mandarin: 指豬的舌頭，常作食材使用，在粵菜或燒臘中較為常見，亦常見於街坊燒臘舖或小食店。
explanation_english: Refers to a pig's tongue, used as an ingredient or dish. Common in Cantonese cuisine and roast-meat shops.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食豬𧲡，去旺角嗰間燒臘舖有得買。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 zyu1 lei6, heoi3 wong6 gok3 go2 gaan1 siu1 laap6 pou3 jau5 dak1 maai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想吃豬舌，去旺角那間燒臘舖有得買。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat pig tongue tonight; the roast meat shop in Mong Kok sells it.

mandarin_meaning: 形容愚蠢的人（貶義），相當於「笨豬」「豬頭」
english_meaning: a derogatory slang term meaning a stupid person; idiot
explanation_mandarin: 「豬𧴪」是粵語口語罵人用語，帶貶義或戲謔意味。𧴪字屬罕用字，在這裡功能上相當於「笨」「傻」，用來形容人愚蠢或做事不理智。
explanation_english: “豬𧴪” is a Cantonese colloquial insult used derogatorily or jokingly. The rare character 𧴪 functions like “笨” or “stupid” here, so the phrase labels someone as foolish or acting idiotically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做乜咁豬𧴪㗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 mat1 gam2 zyu1 ban6 gaa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你为什么这么蠢？
examples.english_sentence: Why are you being so stupid?

mandarin_meaning: 未能確定；不是通行的粵語詞彙，可能為方言、地名、蔬菜俗稱或書寫錯誤。
english_meaning: Unclear/undetermined; not a recognized standard Cantonese term — possibly a dialectal/local name for a vegetable, a slang term, or a misspelling.
explanation_mandarin: 「豬𧴪菜」在常見粵語詞典與語料庫中查無明確條目。該詞可能是某地區對某種蔬菜的俗稱、口語化的稱呼或個別寫法錯誤。若需確切含義，建議向當地說粵語者或提供詞語出處以便核實。
explanation_english: The term '豬𧴪菜' does not appear in standard Cantonese dictionaries or corpora. It may be a local/common name for a vegetable, a colloquial/slang expression, or a misspelling. To determine its precise meaning, check with local Cantonese speakers or provide the source/context for verification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺街市聽到人叫嗰樣菜做「豬𧴪菜」，但我唔識，係乜嘢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 si5 teng1 dou3 jan4 giu3 go2 joeng6 coi3 zou6 '豬𧴪菜', daan6 ngo5 m4 sik1, hai6 mat1 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在街市聽到有人把那種菜稱作「豬𧴪菜」，但我不認識，那是什麼？
examples.english_sentence: I heard someone at the market call that vegetable '豬𧴪菜', but I don't recognize it — what is it?

mandarin_meaning: 粗俗的侮辱性稱呼（常用於罵人，類似「混蛋/王八蛋」）；此處的「𠺘」常用作避寫或代替廣東話粗口字「撚」。
english_meaning: A vulgar Cantonese insult (literally 'cat + [censored character]'); used to call someone a jerk/asshole. The second character 𠺘 is often used as a euphemistic/censored form of the swear character '撚'.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 粗口 / 侮辱性名詞或感嘆詞
explanation_mandarin: 「貓𠺘」是廣東話的粗俗罵人用語，讀作 maau1 lan2。字形中的「𠺘」多用來代替或避寫粗口字「撚」，整詞用以表示對人的輕蔑或憤怒，語氣較重，不宜在正式場合使用。
explanation_english: “貓𠺘” is Cantonese vulgar slang pronounced maau1 lan2. The character 𠺘 is often used as a censored or substitute form of the swear character '撚'. The term is an insulting, coarse way to call someone a jerk or bastard. Strongly informal and offensive; avoid in formal settings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你呢個貓𠺘，做嘢咁衰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ni1 go3 maau1 lan2, zou6 je5 gam2 seoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這個猫撚，做事這麼差。
examples.english_sentence: You damn jerk, you do such a terrible job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講大話，真係個貓𠺘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6, zan1 hai6 go3 maau1 lan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天說大話，真是個猫撚。
examples.english_sentence: He lies all the time — what a jerk.

mandarin_meaning: 猫腻
english_meaning: a shady trick; something suspicious; there’s something fishy
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，表示暗藏的問題、不光明的手段或可疑之處，常說「有貓腻」表示覺得事情不妥。
explanation_english: Colloquial slang meaning a hidden problem, dishonest trick, or something suspicious; commonly used as in “there’s something fishy.”

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單買賣有貓𧲕，我哋要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 maai5 maai6 jau5 maau1 nei6, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这笔买卖有猫腻，我们要小心。
examples.english_sentence: There's something fishy about this deal; we should be careful.

mandarin_meaning: 财神卡/财神咭（带来财运或提供优惠的卡片，常指商家发放的刮刮卡、优惠卡或戏称能“带来财运”的信用卡/储值卡）
english_meaning: “God of Wealth” card — a lucky/promo card (e.g. a scratch card, discount/membership card) or a joking term for a card that seems to bring money/fortune
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語口語用法。一般指商店或商场在节日或促销时发放、带有抽奖或折扣功能的卡片（如刮刮卡、會員卡），也可戏称某人常常帮人买单或运气特别好的信用卡为「財神咭」。属于口语/俚语用法。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang term. Usually refers to promotional cards given by shops or malls (scratch cards, discount or membership cards) that promise prizes or savings; it can also be a joking nickname for a credit/debit card that seems to bring luck or is frequently used to pay. Informal usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 商場送咗張財神咭，刮開可以抽獎同埋有折扣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng1 coeng4 sung3 zo2 zoeng1 coi4 san4 kaat1, gwaat3 hoi1 ho2 ji5 cau1 zoeng2 tung4 maai4 jau5 zit3 kau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 商场发了一张财神卡，刮开可以抽奖还有折扣。
examples.english_sentence: The mall handed out a 'God of Wealth' card — scratch it to enter a prize draw and get discounts.

mandarin_meaning: 小氣的女人；吝嗇的女人（貶義）
english_meaning: stingy woman; female cheapskate (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話的口語或俚語中，『貧婆』用來形容非常小氣、吝嗇或愛占便宜的女性，帶有貶義和責備意味，常用於非正式對話中。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, '貧婆' describes a woman who is stingy or miserly. It is pejorative and is commonly used in colloquial speech to scold or mock someone for being cheap.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你真係好貧婆，連請人飲杯嘢都唔肯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 hou2 pan4 po4, lin4 cing2 jan4 jam2 bui1 je5 dou1 m4 hang2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你真的是很小氣，連請人喝一杯都不願意。
examples.english_sentence: You're really stingy — you won't even buy someone a drink.

mandarin_meaning: 小販、小販子；在某些語境下可指販賣違法物品（如毒品、人）的人
english_meaning: a small-time vendor/peddler (colloquial); can also refer to a dealer/trafficker of illegal goods in some contexts
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，通常指在街頭擺賣或小規模做買賣的人（小販）。在某些語境下可擴展指販賣違法物品的人，通常帶有貶義或口語色彩。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term usually referring to a street vendor or small-scale seller (peddler). In some contexts it can be extended to mean someone who deals in illegal goods; the term is informal and can be pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市入面有好多販仔賣蔬菜同水果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 jap6 min6 jau5 hou2 do1 faan6 zai2 maai6 so1 coi3 tung4 seoi2 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 菜市場裡面有很多小販賣蔬菜和水果。
examples.english_sentence: There are many vendors selling vegetables and fruits in the market.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方話佢係毒品販仔，已經被捕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 duk6 ban2 faan6 zai2, ji5 ging1 bei6 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方說他是毒品販子，已經被捕。
examples.english_sentence: The police said he was a drug dealer and has been arrested.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語俚語）形容人擺架子、看起來高貴或某物價格昂貴，常帶諷刺或調侃意味。
english_meaning: Cantonese slang describing someone who is snobbish/pretentious or something that is expensive; often used sarcastically.
explanation_mandarin: 「貴木」字面上為「貴的木頭」，在粵語口語中作俚語使用，既可指人有高傲、擺架子的態度，也可指物品價格高昂。用法非正式，主要在香港粵語語境中出現，含有調侃或貶義色彩。
explanation_english: Literally 'expensive wood', this Cantonese slang is used informally to describe someone who acts posh/snobbish or something that is expensive. It is colloquial, mostly used in Hong Kong Cantonese, and often carries a sarcastic or mildly derogatory tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日咁貴木，冇人鍾意同佢做朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gam2 gwai3 muk6, mou5 jan4 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 zou6 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是如此擺架子，沒人喜歡和他做朋友。
examples.english_sentence: He's always so snobbish; nobody wants to be friends with him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間餐廳啲嘢真係好貴木，我哋平時唔會去嗰度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 je5 zan1 hai6 hou2 gwai3 muk6, ngo5 dei6 ping4 si4 m4 wui5 heoi3 go2 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間餐廳的東西真的很貴，我們平時不會去那裡。
examples.english_sentence: The food at that restaurant is really pricey; we usually don't go there.

mandarin_meaning: 拍馬屁；逢迎討好
english_meaning: to flatter; to suck up to someone; to curry favor
explanation_mandarin: 「貼沙」為香港廣東話口語俗語，通常用來形容對上司或有利可圖的人諂媚、討好，以圖獲取好處。語氣偏貶義，屬非正式用語。
explanation_english: “貼沙” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang meaning to flatter or ingratiate oneself with someone (often a boss or someone in a position of advantage) in order to gain favors. It is informal and usually has a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日向老闆貼沙，想升職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hoeng3 lou5 baan2 tip3 saa1, soeng2 sing1 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是向老板拍马屁，想升职。
examples.english_sentence: He constantly flatters the boss to try to get promoted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日貼沙，大家都睇得出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 tip3 saa1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 tai2 dak1 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别老是拍马屁，大家都看得出来。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep flattering people—everyone can tell.

mandarin_meaning: 傻瓜；笨蛋（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: a fool; a dummy (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「賀欄豆」是香港粵語中的俗語，通常用來戲稱或輕微貶低某人笨拙或做事愚蠢。語氣多為戲謔或非正式的貶稱，來源與構詞來歷不詳，屬口語用法。
explanation_english: “賀欄豆” is a colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to tease or mildly insult someone as being foolish or clumsy. It is informal and often used jokingly; the exact origin of the term is unclear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做啲蠢事，大家都笑佢係賀欄豆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zou6 di1 cyun2 si6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 siu3 keoi5 hai6 ho6 laan4 dau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是做傻事，大家都笑他是個賀欄豆。
examples.english_sentence: He always does stupid things; everyone teases him as a '賀欄豆' (a fool).

jyutping: bin1 go3 (likely a non-standard/archaic or dialectal variant of 邊個)
mandarin_meaning: 誰 / 哪個（可能為「邊個」的方言或誤寫）
english_meaning: who / which one (likely a dialectal or non-standard form of '邊個')
explanation_mandarin: 「賓箇」不是標準書面粵語寫法，常見解釋為方言或誤寫，對應標準粵語的「邊個」，用來詢問「誰/哪一個」。使用時應注意該詞較為罕見或口語化。
explanation_english: "賓箇" is not a standard written Cantonese form; it is likely a dialectal or non-standard/misspelled variant of "邊個" (bin1 go3), used to ask "who/which one." It is uncommon and chiefly colloquial or regional.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日用「賓箇」問人，意思係「邊個」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 jung6 'bin1 go3' man6 jan4, ji3 si6 hai6 'bin1 go3'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常用「賓箇」問人，意思是「誰」。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma often uses '賓箇' to ask who someone is; it means 'who'.

mandarin_meaning: 冷淡 / 故意冷落（某人）
english_meaning: to act cold or aloof; to give someone the cold shoulder
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語/俚語，指對人故意表現冷淡、冷落或擺冷臉，使對方感到被忽視或不受歡迎。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to deliberately act cold, aloof, or unfriendly toward someone — i.e., to give someone the cold shoulder.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家對我賣冷，唔肯同我講話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 deoi3 ngo5 maai6 laang5, m4 hang2 tung4 ngo5 gong2 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在對我很冷淡，不肯跟我說話。
examples.english_sentence: He's being cold toward me right now and won't talk to me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好賣冷啦，有事就直接講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 maai6 laang5 laa3, jau5 si6 zau6 zik6 zip3 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別擺冷，有事就直接說。
examples.english_sentence: Don't play cold — if something's up, just say it directly.

mandarin_meaning: 裝瘋/發瘋；誇張地表現得像瘋了一樣（常為吸引注意或發洩情緒）
english_meaning: to act crazy; behave wildly or over-the-top (often to attract attention or to lose control)
explanation_mandarin: 「賣瘋」是粵語口語，指故意或因情緒失控而表現得瘋狂、誇張或失常。可含貶義，既可指裝瘋賣傻吸引注意，也可指真正發瘋、失去理智。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquialism meaning to act crazily or like a maniac. It can imply deliberately putting on an exaggerated, attention-seeking display, or losing control and becoming furious; often carries a negative or informal tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺派對上賣瘋，成晚跳嚟跳去吸引晒人注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 paai3 deoi6 soeng6 maai6 fung1, sing4 maan5 tiu3 lai4 tiu3 heoi3 kap1 jan5 saai3 jan4 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在派對上賣瘋，整晚跳來跳去吸引大家注意。
examples.english_sentence: He was acting crazy at the party, jumping around all night to attract everyone's attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 一聽到佢咁講，我差啲賣瘋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat1 ting1 dou3 keoi5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 caa1 di1 maai6 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一聽到他這樣說，我差點發瘋。
examples.english_sentence: When I heard him say that, I almost went crazy.

mandarin_meaning: 裝瘋賣傻/裝瘋的女人
english_meaning: a woman who acts crazy or hysterical (usually to gain attention or sympathy)
explanation_mandarin: 貶義俗語，指故意裝瘋、賣弄瘋癲或誇張情緒以吸引注意或博取同情的女子。
explanation_english: Derogatory slang for a woman who deliberately acts crazy, hysterical, or overly dramatic to attract attention or gain sympathy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個賣瘋女，成日扮到好無辜，想攞人同情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 mai6 fung1 neoi5, seng4 jat6 baan6 dou3 hou2 mou4 gu1, soeng2 lo2 jan4 tung4 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她是個愛裝瘋的女人，常常裝得很無辜，想博取別人的同情。
examples.english_sentence: She's an attention-seeking woman; she often pretends to be innocent to get people's sympathy.

mandarin_meaning: 卖弄（风情）；卖弄、招摇以吸引注意
english_meaning: to show off; to flirt or act coquettishly to attract attention
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指故意擺出姿態、賣弄風情或誇張行為以吸引別人的注意或讚賞，帶有調情或賣弄的含義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term meaning to pose, show off, or act flirtatiously to attract attention or admiration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺派對度不停賣風，想吸引其他人注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 paai3 deoi3 dou6 bat1 ting4 maai6 fung1, soeng2 kap1 jan5 kei4 taa1 jan4 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在派對上不停賣弄風情，想吸引別人的注意。
examples.english_sentence: He kept showing off/flirting at the party, trying to attract people's attention.

cantonese: 賣魚佬洗身 - 冇腥（聲）氣
jyutping: maai6 jyu4 lou2 sai2 san1 - mou5 seng1 hei3
mandarin_meaning: 洗清嫌疑／沒有任何可疑跡象（字面：賣魚的人洗去腥味）
english_meaning: to be cleared of suspicion; to show no sign of being involved or 'fishy' (literally: a fish seller washes off the fishy smell)
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容某人或某事沒有留下可疑或不良的痕跡，已經洗脫嫌疑或看起來很乾淨、無牽連。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to say someone or something shows no trace of suspicion or wrongdoing — essentially 'cleared' or 'no fishy signs'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀人話偷咗啲錢，但最後證明係賣魚佬洗身，冇腥氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 waa6 tau1 zo2 di1 cin2, daan6 zeoi3 hau6 zing3 ming4 hai6 maai6 jyu4 lou2 sai2 san1, mou5 seng1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人說偷了錢，但最後證明洗清嫌疑，沒有任何可疑跡象。
examples.english_sentence: He was accused of stealing money, but in the end he was cleared — there was no hint of anything fishy.

mandarin_meaning: 随意打赌；胡乱赌注（俚语）
english_meaning: to gamble/take a reckless bet on a whim (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「賭𠵿」是香港粤语俚语，用来形容隨意、沖動或不負責任地下注或打賭，有時也泛指以碰運氣的方式冒險行事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used chiefly in Hong Kong meaning to place bets or take risks recklessly or on a whim; often implies impulsive, irresponsible gambling or taking a chance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日賭𠵿，結果輸晒所有錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dou2 dou2fei1, git3 gwo2 syu1 saai3 so2 jau5 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是隨意打賭，結果輸光了所有錢。
examples.english_sentence: He always gambles on a whim and ended up losing all his money.

mandarin_meaning: 佔便宜；撿便宜（口語）
english_meaning: to get a freebie / to benefit at someone's expense (informal slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「賺（盞）」是廣東話口語用法，指在某種情況下佔了便宜、撿到好處或獲得免費的東西或待遇。可用來形容短暫或小利益的獲得，有時帶有取巧或被動獲利的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to get a freebie or to come out ahead—i.e., to benefit or profit (often in a small or opportunistic way) at someone else's expense or by luck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚出街我賺盞，阿偉請咗我飲兩杯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ceot1 gaai1 ngo5 zaan6 zaan2, aa3 wai5 ceng2 zo2 ngo5 jam2 loeng5 bui1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚出去我佔了便宜，阿偉請我喝了兩杯。
examples.english_sentence: I got lucky tonight — Ah Wai bought me two drinks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日賺盞，唔好畀佢利用你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zaan6 zaan2, m4 hou2 bei2 keoi5 lei6 jung6 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常佔別人便宜，別讓他利用你。
examples.english_sentence: He always takes advantage of people; don't let him use you.

mandarin_meaning: 只賺到/只得到微小的收益或好處（帶有失望或輕視的語氣）
english_meaning: to only earn/get a very small gain or benefit (often said with disappointment or dismissiveness)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示所得很少、只得到一點點好處或錢，常帶不滿或輕視的語氣。括號內的「盞」是方言變體或強調用法，可有可無。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to say one only gets a very small amount (money or benefit). It often conveys disappointment or a dismissive attitude. The optional character 盞 is a dialectal/ emphatic variant and may be omitted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我做咗成日，淨係賺得個五十蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zou6 zo2 seng4 jat6, zing6 hai6 zaam6 dak1 go3 ng5 sap6 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我做了一整天，僅賺了五十元。
examples.english_sentence: I worked the whole day and only made fifty dollars.

mandarin_meaning: （舊譯）錫蘭（指錫蘭／錫蘭茶，今稱斯里蘭卡）
english_meaning: Ceylon (old transliteration; often used for Ceylon tea / Sri Lanka)
explanation_mandarin: 「賽蘭」是對英文 Ceylon 的字面音譯，常用於指錫蘭茶或舊時對錫蘭（即現今的斯里蘭卡）的稱呼。正式與常見寫法多為「錫蘭」或直接稱「斯里蘭卡」。
explanation_english: “賽蘭” is a literal Cantonese transliteration of Ceylon, often used to refer to Ceylon tea or the older name for Sri Lanka. The more common Chinese form is 錫蘭 or the modern name 斯里蘭卡.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢包賽蘭茶幾好味，唔苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 baau1 coi3 laan4 caa4 gei2 hou2 mei6, m4 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這包賽蘭茶挺好喝，不苦。
examples.english_sentence: This pack of Ceylon tea tastes pretty good; it's not bitter.

mandarin_meaning: 赑屃（bìxì），傳說中的龜形神獸，常作碑座；也可比喻背負重擔的人或物。
english_meaning: Bixi, a legendary turtle-like creature that carries a stele; also used metaphorically for something or someone that bears a heavy burden.
explanation_mandarin: 贔屭（俗寫為赑屃）為傳說中一種龜形神獸，常見於石碑下作為承座，象徵負重、支撐；在比喻用法中指承擔重任或負重的事物或人。
explanation_english: Bixi is a mythical turtle-like beast often depicted supporting a stele. It symbolizes bearing weight or support; metaphorically it refers to something or someone that bears heavy responsibilities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰座古碑擺喺一隻贔屭度，望落好有氣勢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zo6 gu2 bei1 baai2 hai2 jat1 zek3 bei6 sik1 dou6, mong6 lok6 hou2 jau5 hei3 sai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那座古碑擺在一隻贔屭上，看起來很有氣勢。
examples.english_sentence: The ancient stele sits on a bixi; it looks very imposing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個石座似贔屭，日日背住座碑，唔係咁易。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 sek6 zo6 ci5 bei6 sik1, jat6 jat6 bui3 zyu6 zo6 bei1, m4 hai6 gam2 ji6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個石座像贔屭，每天都在承擔著碑的重量，並不容易。
examples.english_sentence: This stone base is like a bixi, carrying the stele every day; it's not easy.

mandarin_meaning: 不炫耀財富；有錢也不張揚
english_meaning: Don't flaunt one's wealth; keep financial success low-profile
explanation_mandarin: 表示即使有錢也不張揚、不炫耀，保持低調。
explanation_english: An idiom advising not to show off wealth; to remain discreet about one's financial status.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家好有錢，但係一向好低調，真係財不露眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 jau5 cin2, daan6 hai6 jat1 hoeng3 hou2 dai1 diu6, zan1 hai6 coi4 bat1 lou6 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在很有钱，但一直很低调，真是财不露眼。
examples.english_sentence: He has a lot of money now, but he's always kept a low profile; he truly doesn't flaunt his wealth.

cantonese: 财多责死仔，粪多责死禾
jyutping: coi4 do1 zaak3 sei2 zai2, fan3 do1 zaak3 sei2 wo4
mandarin_meaning: 財多招惹麻煩，糞多會害死禾苗。比喻任何過多的東西反而會帶來麻煩或害處。
english_meaning: Too much wealth brings trouble; too much manure can kill the crop. A proverb warning that excess (even of something good) often causes problems — 'too much of a good thing.'
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東諺語字面意思是：財多會招惹禍事，糞多會害死禾苗。引申為提醒人們適可而止，過度往往會帶來不良後果或招致責難。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb literally contrasts excess money and excess manure to illustrate that too much of anything can be harmful. It warns that abundance can attract trouble or cause harm — essentially 'too much of a good thing.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意要小心，財多責死仔，唔好貪心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 siu2 sam1, coi4 do1 zaak3 sei2 zai2, m4 hou2 taam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意要小心，財多會招惹麻煩，不要貪心。
