examples.english_sentence: Be careful in business — too much wealth can bring trouble; don't be greedy.

cantonese: 财多身子弱，钱多瞓唔着
jyutping: coi4 do1 san1 zi2 joek6, cin2 do1 fan3 m4 zoek6
mandarin_meaning: 有錢但身體虛弱；有錢卻睡不著（暗示有錢反而帶來煩惱和健康問題）
english_meaning: Having lots of money but poor health; money brings worries — wealthy but sleepless (suggests wealth can cause stress and health issues)
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用來形容一方面有很多錢，但另一方面身體欠佳或因為擔心錢財而睡不着，帶出有錢未必帶來幸福的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying describing someone who has plenty of money but poor health or sleeplessness due to worry about money — highlighting that wealth doesn't necessarily bring well‑being.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯靠股票賺咗幾百萬，但佢成日瞓唔着，真係「財多身子弱，錢多瞓唔着」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 kaau3 gu2 piu3 zaan6 zo2 gei2 baak3 maan6, daan6 keoi5 sing4 jat6 fan3 m4 zoek6, zan1 hai6 「coi4 do1 san1 zi2 joek6, cin2 do1 fan3 m4 zoek6」。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿伯靠股票赚了几百万，但他经常睡不着，真是“财多身子弱，钱多睡不着”。
examples.english_sentence: Uncle made a few million from stocks, but he often can't sleep — truly, 'more wealth, weaker body; more money, sleepless nights.'

mandarin_meaning: 愛虛榮、好排場、講究享受
english_meaning: vain/status-seeking and pleasure-loving; likes to show off and enjoy luxuries
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人愛面子、講排場、貪享受，喜歡展示身份或物質享受，常帶貶義。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is vain and status-conscious, who likes to flaunt and enjoy luxuries (food, brands, experiences). Often negative or colloquial in tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日著名牌、去高級餐廳，真係贪威识食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zoek3 ming4 paai4, heoi3 gou1 kap1 caan1 teng1, zan1 hai6 taam1 wai1 sik1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天穿名牌、去高級餐廳，真是愛虛榮又愛享受。
examples.english_sentence: He always wears designer brands and eats at upscale restaurants—really vain and likes to indulge.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面對客人佢好識做，但背後其實贪威识食，淨係搵好處。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 deoi3 haak3 jan4 keoi5 hou2 sik1 zou6, daan6 bui3 hau6 kei4 sat6 taam1 wai1 sik1 sik6, zing6 hai6 wan2 hou2 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面對客人他很會做表面，但背地裡其實愛虛榮、愛享受，總是圖好處。
examples.english_sentence: In front of customers he's very professional, but behind the scenes he's actually vain and pleasure-seeking, only looking out for benefits.

mandarin_meaning: 自鳴得意 / 自滿
english_meaning: to be smug or self-satisfied; complacent
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容因為得到好處或小成就而自鳴得意、得意忘形，帶有輕微貶義，提醒對方不要太自滿或驕傲。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who becomes smug or overly pleased with themselves after a benefit or small success; mildly derogatory and often a warning not to be complacent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢攞咗個小獎就貪得意，開始擺架子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lo2 zo2 go3 siu2 zoeng2 zau6 taam1 dak1 ji3, hoi1 ci2 baai2 gaa3 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他拿了個小獎就自鳴得意，開始擺架子。
examples.english_sentence: He got a small prize and became smug, starting to put on airs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做得唔錯，但唔好貪得意，要繼續努力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 dak1 m4 co3, daan6 m4 hou2 taam1 dak1 ji3, jiu3 gai3 zuk6 nou5 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做得不錯，但不要自滿，要繼續努力。
examples.english_sentence: You did well, but don't get smug; keep working hard.

cantonese: 贱力得人敬，贱口得人憎
jyutping: zin6 lik6 dak1 jan4 ging3, zin6 hau2 dak1 jan4 zang1
mandarin_meaning: 肯吃苦的人會得到別人的尊重，嘴巴粗俗或愛說不中聽話的人會讓人討厭。
english_meaning: Those who humbly work hard earn others' respect; those with a cheap or rude mouth earn people's dislike.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語強調行為與言語對人際關係的影響：勤奮、肯吃苦、態度謙和會得到別人的敬重；說話粗俗、刻薄或輕率會招致反感。
explanation_english: This proverb emphasizes how actions and speech affect social standing: hardworking, humble behavior earns respect, while rude or cheap talk earns dislike.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強平時肯做嘢又有禮，大家都尊重佢，正所謂：贱力得人敬，贱口得人憎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 ping4 si4 hang2 zou6 je5 jau6 jau5 lai5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 zyun1 zung6 keoi5, zing3 so2 wai6 zin6 lik6 dak1 jan4 ging3, zin6 hau2 dak1 jan4 zang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿強平時肯做事又有禮，大家都尊重他，正所謂：肯吃苦的人得人尊敬，嘴賤的人讓人厭惡。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung usually works hard and is polite, so everyone respects him — as the saying goes: those who humbly work hard earn respect; those who are cheap-mouthed earn contempt.

mandarin_meaning: 贴身、缠得很紧的人；比喻像膏药一样紧跟在身边、难以摆脱的跟随者或纠缠者。
english_meaning: A clingy person or hanger-on who sticks to someone like a plaster; someone who follows closely and is hard to get rid of.
explanation_mandarin: 原指贴在身上的膏药，比喻形容人紧紧跟随、纠缠不放，常带贬义，用来形容黏人或难以摆脱的关系/人物。
explanation_english: Originally refers to a medicinal plaster stuck to the body; metaphorically used to describe someone who clings closely or pesters persistently — often pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日跟埋我，好似贴身膏药咁，真係煩死人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gan1 maai4 ngo5, hou2 ci5 tip3 san1 gou1 joek6 gam2, zan1 hai6 faan4 sei2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是跟着我，像贴身膏药一样，真让人烦。
examples.english_sentence: He always sticks to me like a clingy plaster — really annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 花钱买罪受
english_meaning: to pay money to suffer; to pay for misery / to ask for trouble (and pay for it)
explanation_mandarin: 口语俚语，意思是花錢做讓自己難受或受罪的事，相當於“花钱买罪受”。常用來批評某人自找苦吃或為無謂的東西付出金錢卻得到痛苦或不划算的結果。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase meaning 'to pay money to make oneself suffer.' It describes spending money that results in discomfort, trouble, or regret — equivalent to 'paying for misery' or 'asking for trouble.' Used to criticize someone who unnecessarily causes themselves pain or wastes money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰張票座位細又唔舒服，你仲要加錢換，真係貼錢買難受。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zoeng1 piu3 zo6 wai6 sai3 jau6 m4 syu1 fuk6, nei5 zung6 jiu3 gaa1 cin2 wun6, zan1 hai6 tit3 cin2 maai5 naan4 sau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那張票座位窄又不舒服，你還要加錢換，真是花钱买罪受。
examples.english_sentence: That ticket's seat is narrow and uncomfortable, and you still pay extra to change—you're really paying money to suffer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日俾人話嗰間美容院好，但療程又貴又痛，去到最後都係貼錢買難受。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 waa6 go2 gaan1 meng4 jung4 jyun6 hou2, daan6 liu4 cing4 jau6 gwai3 jau6 tung3, heoi3 dou3 zeoi3 hau6 dou1 hai6 tit3 cin2 maai5 naan4 sau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 總是有人說那間美容院好，但療程又貴又痛，去了最後也是花钱受罪。
examples.english_sentence: People keep saying that salon is good, but the treatments are expensive and painful — in the end you're just paying to suffer.

mandarin_meaning: 选错靠山 / 信错人
english_meaning: to back or trust the wrong person; to rely on the wrong protector
explanation_mandarin: 「贴错门神」原意来自春节贴门神以保平安的习俗，字面是把门神贴错了。引申为在现实中选错了靠山或信错了人，依赖的对象不能保护你甚至害你，常用于描述在感情、工作、政治或生意上依靠错误的人所导致的损失或被背叛的情况。
explanation_english: Literally 'pasted the wrong door god' (from the custom of putting door-god pictures for protection). Figuratively it means backing or trusting the wrong person — relying on someone who fails to protect you or even betrays you. Used colloquially in contexts like relationships, business, or politics to describe misplaced trust or support.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 原來我貼錯門神，佢只係想利用我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyun4 loi4 ngo5 tip3 co3 mun4 san4, keoi5 zi2 hai6 soeng2 lei6 juk6 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 原来我选错了靠山，他只是想利用我。
examples.english_sentence: It turned out I backed the wrong person — he only wanted to use me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次選舉我哋貼錯門神，支持嗰個議員最後反水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 syun2 geoi2 ngo5 dei6 tip3 co3 mun4 san4, zi1 ci4 go2 go3 ji5 jyun4 zeoi3 hau6 faan2 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次选举我们选错了靠山，支持的那位议员最后反水。
examples.english_sentence: In this election we backed the wrong candidate; the councilor we supported ultimately betrayed us.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我貼錯門神，畀佢經營間鋪，最後蝕晒本。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tip3 co3 mun4 san4, bei2 keoi5 ging1 jing4 gaan1 pou3, zeoi3 hau6 sik1 saai3 bun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我选错了靠山，让他经营那间铺子，最后赔了本。
examples.english_sentence: I backed the wrong person and let him run the shop; in the end I lost my investment.

jyutping: zeik6 gwo3 hing1 bing1, mou4 zai3 jyu1 si6
mandarin_meaning: 事后才采取行动，已来不及，补救无效（与“亡羊补牢，为时已晚”意义相近）
english_meaning: To take action after the damage is done; measures taken too late to be of any use.
explanation_mandarin: 形容在事情已经发生或损失已成之后才采取措施，无法挽回或不会产生实际效果。常用以批评行动迟缓或补救为时已晚。
explanation_english: Describes taking measures only after harm has occurred, when it's too late and those measures are ineffective. Often used to criticize slow reactions or belated fixes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 網站俾人入侵，等到資料已經俾人拎走先封鎖，真係贼过兴兵，无济于事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mong5 zaam6 bei2 jan4 jap6 cam1, dang2 dou3 zi1 liu2 ji5 ging1 bei2 jan4 ling1 zau2 sin1 fung1 so2, zan1 hai6 zeik6 gwo3 hing1 bing1, mou4 zai3 jyu1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 网站被入侵，等到资料已经被人拿走才封锁，真是贼过兴兵，无济于事。
examples.english_sentence: The website was hacked and they only blocked it after the data had already been taken — truly acting too late to be of any use.

mandarin_meaning: 賠償醫藥費
english_meaning: to pay for medical/medicine expenses; to compensate for medical treatment
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，指為對方受傷或生病負責而支付醫藥費，或買藥、煲湯等作為補償或照顧。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to cover or compensate for someone’s medical expenses (pay for medicine, treatment, or restorative soup as a form of making amends or care).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你係你嘅錯撞親佢，你要賠湯藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 hai6 nei5 ge3 co3 zong6 can1 keoi5, nei5 jiu3 pui4 tong1 joek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果是你的錯撞到她，你要賠償醫藥費。
examples.english_sentence: If it was your fault that you hit her, you have to pay for her medical expenses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要賠湯藥畀受傷嘅工人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 pui4 tong1 joek6 bei2 sau6 soeng1 ge3 gung1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要賠償受傷工人的醫藥費。
examples.english_sentence: The company has to cover the injured worker's medical expenses.

mandarin_meaning: 白白浪費口舌或精力；徒勞無功，不值得再爭辯或解釋
english_meaning: to waste one's breath; to argue or explain in vain; not worth the bother
explanation_mandarin: 指為了說服或爭論而白費口舌、耗費精力，但最終沒有結果或對方不會接受，表示徒勞。
explanation_english: Refers to spending words or energy trying to persuade or argue when it achieves nothing; emphasizes that the effort is futile.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再赚嘥气同佢解釋啦，佢唔會明嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 zaan6 saai1 hei3 tung4 keoi5 gaai2 sik1 laa1, keoi5 m4 wui5 ming4 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再白費口舌向他解釋了，他不會明白的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't waste your breath explaining it to him; he won't understand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 同啲人爭論冇意思，真係賺嘥气啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tung4 di1 jan4 zang1 leon6 mou5 ji3 si1, zan1 hai6 zaan6 saai1 hei3 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 跟那些人爭論沒意義，真的是在白費口舌。
examples.english_sentence: Arguing with those people is pointless — it's really just wasting your breath.

mandarin_meaning: 起初有赚头但最后亏本；开始有利可图却以亏损收场
english_meaning: To make a profit at the beginning but end up losing money; an initial gain that is wiped out by later losses
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容一项交易或计划开始时看似有利可图，但到最后反而亏本或没有收益。
explanation_english: Describes a deal or venture that appears profitable at first but ultimately results in a loss or no net gain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意頭時有賺頭，點知到尾反而蝕尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 tau4 si4 jau5 zyun3 tau4, dim2 zi1 dou3 mei5 faan2 ji4 sik1 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这笔生意起初有赚头，没想到最后却赔本。
examples.english_sentence: This deal looked profitable at first, but in the end it turned into a loss.

mandarin_meaning: 使（某人）倒霉 / 招来霉运（俚语）
english_meaning: to jinx someone; to bring bad luck to someone (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，指因言行或无意的举动而使别人或自己招惹不幸、倒霉，类似“给……招来霉运”或“说坏话把好运弄没”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to jinx someone or cause bad luck for someone through words or actions (i.e., to bring misfortune or spoil good luck).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁講，會賺衰佢㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 gong2, wui5 zaan6 seoi1 keoi5 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那樣說，會讓他倒霉的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say that, you'll jinx him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話自己好彩，點知最後賺衰咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 waa6 zi6 gei2 hou2 coi2, dim2 zi1 zeoi3 hau6 zaan6 seoi1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是說自己很走運，結果最後倒霉了。
examples.english_sentence: He kept saying he was lucky, but ended up being jinxed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心講咗啲嘢，結果賺衰咗，一出門就落雨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 gong2 zo2 di1 je5, git3 gwo2 zaan6 seoi1 zo2, jat1 ceot1 mun4 zau6 lok6 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不小心說了幾句，結果招來霉運，一出門就下雨。
examples.english_sentence: I accidentally said something and jinxed it — as soon as I went out it started raining.

mandarin_meaning: 红蟹；红色的螃蟹，通常指煮熟后呈红色的螃蟹或某些红色品种的螃蟹
english_meaning: red crab (a crab that is red in color; often refers to cooked crab or red-colored crab species)
explanation_mandarin: 指颜色为赤红的蟹类，常用于描述煮熟後变红的螃蟹或天然呈红色的蟹类品种。
explanation_english: Refers to crabs that are red in color; commonly used for crabs that turn red when cooked or for species that are naturally red.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 市場入面有新鮮嘅赤蟹賣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si5 coeng4 jap6 min6 jau5 san1 sin1 ge3 cek3 haai5 maai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市场里有新鲜的红蟹卖。
examples.english_sentence: There are fresh red crabs for sale at the market.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋食赤蟹，媽媽已經蒸好晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 sik6 cek3 haai5, maa4 maa1 ji5 ging1 zeng1 hou2 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我们吃红蟹，妈妈已经蒸好了。
examples.english_sentence: We're having red crab tonight; mum has already steamed it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢種赤蟹係潮間帶常見嘅物種。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zung2 cek3 haai5 hai6 ciu4 gaan1 daai3 soeng4 gin3 ge3 mat6 zung2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这种赤蟹是潮间带常见的物种。
examples.english_sentence: This kind of red crab is a common species in the intertidal zone.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）逃兵遇到强盗；（引申）本想躲避或逃离困境，结果却碰上更坏的祸患或麻烦。
english_meaning: Literally 'fleeing soldiers meet thieves'; figuratively, to try to escape one problem only to run into another — similar to 'out of the frying pan into the fire'.
explanation_mandarin: 形容本想避開或擺脫困境，結果遇上更壞的情況或新的災難，用來表示倒霉或禍不單行的情形。
explanation_english: Describes attempting to avoid or escape a difficulty only to encounter an even worse situation; used to express bad luck or cascading misfortunes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱想走佬，點知走兵遇着贼，俾人搶咗錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 soeng2 zau2 lou2, dim2 zi1 zau2 bing1 jyu6 zoek6 caak6, bei2 jan4 coeng2 zo2 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛想逃走，結果走兵遇着贼，被人搶了錢。
examples.english_sentence: He had just tried to run away, only to run into thieves and have his money stolen.

mandarin_meaning: 忙到連喘息或休息的時間都沒有（口語化）
english_meaning: so busy that one has no time to rest or catch a breath; running around non-stop
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語 / 動詞短語
explanation_mandarin: 「走夹唔唞」是廣東話口語，形容某人或大家因為事情繁忙而沒有時間休息，常用於抱怨工作或行程太緊湊。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone is so busy they have no time to rest or breathe. Commonly used to complain about heavy workloads or hectic schedules.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我呢排真係走夹唔唞，連瞓覺都冇時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ni1 paai4 zan1 hai6 zou2 gaap3 m4 tau2, lin4 fan3 gaau3 dou1 mou5 si4gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我最近真的忙到連睡覺的時間都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: I've been so busy lately that I don't even have time to sleep.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個項目搞到大家走夹唔唞，下星期先可以鬆一鬆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hong6 muk6 gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 zou2 gaap3 m4 tau2, haa6 sing1 kei4 sin1 ho2 ji5 sung1 jat1 sung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個項目把大家忙得不可開交，下星期才能稍微放鬆一下。
examples.english_sentence: This project has everyone running around non-stop; we can only relax a bit next week.

mandarin_meaning: 逃避責任；溜走、脫身
english_meaning: to escape or slip away from a responsibility or obligation; to shirk
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，指設法脫離某個責任或情況，逃避應負的責任或義務，常帶有消極逃避的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to get away from a responsibility or situation, to slip out or shirk obligations. It implies avoiding accountability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗唔想負責，成日都搵藉口走甩身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 m4 soeng2 fu6 zaak3, sing4 jat6 dou1 wan2 zek3 hau2 zau2-lat1-san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了不想負責，總是找藉口逃避責任。
examples.english_sentence: He always finds excuses to shirk responsibility because he doesn't want to be held accountable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開會嗰陣老闆問到敏感問題，佢就即刻走甩身唔答。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 wui6 go2 zan6 lou5 baan2 man6 dou3 man5 gam2 man6 tai4, keoi5 zau6 zik1 hak1 zau2-lat1-san1 m4 daap3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 開會時老闆問到敏感問題，他就立刻溜走不回答。
examples.english_sentence: When the boss raised a sensitive question in the meeting, he immediately slipped away and didn't answer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要熬夜趕報告，佢話有事走甩身，結果去飲茶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 ngou4 je6 gon2 bou3 gou3, keoi5 waa6 jau5 si6 zau2-lat1-san1, git3 gwo2 heoi3 jam2 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要熬夜趕報告，他說有事脫身，結果去喝茶了。
examples.english_sentence: The company had to stay late to finish the report; he said he had something to do and slipped away, ending up going for tea.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見/不確定）香港粵語俚語，常見解釋為「臨陣脫逃、推卸責任或退出某個角色/位置」，但詞源與確切用法在不同圈子可能有差異。
english_meaning: (rare/uncertain) Hong Kong Cantonese slang, commonly interpreted as "to bail out/abandon responsibility or withdraw from a role/position," though origin and exact usage vary by community.
explanation_mandarin: 「走第九」屬於香港口語俚語，使用範圍較狹窄且不一定被普遍理解。一般用來描述在需要負責或參與時，臨時撤出、逃避或放棄的人或行為。具體語感接近「走佬／跳船／失責」。由於沒有權威詞典條目，使用時應注意對象是否能理解。
explanation_english: "走第九" is a Hong Kong Cantonese slang term of limited and region-specific use. It generally describes someone who withdraws at the last moment, bails out, or shirks responsibility. The nuance is similar to "to run away/bail out/abandon ship." Because it is not widely documented, be cautious when using it—listeners may not always recognize the term.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次佢又走第九，乜都唔做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 keoi5 jau6 zou2 dai6 gau2, mat1 dou1 m4 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次他又走第九，什么都不做。
examples.english_sentence: This time he bailed again (走第九), doing nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 去世 / 死掉（俚語、委婉或粗俗說法）
english_meaning: to die; to pass away (slang/colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「走西水」是廣東話的俚語，用來指人去世或死掉，語氣非正式，有時帶有粗俗或幽默色彩，常見於香港口語中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression meaning to die or pass away. It is informal and can be coarse or euphemistic, commonly used in Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱啱聽到佢阿伯走西水喇，大家都好唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aam1 aam1 teng1 dou3 keoi5 aa3 baak3 zau2 sai1 seoi2 laa3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剛剛聽到他伯父去世了，大家都很難過。
examples.english_sentence: I just heard his uncle passed away; everyone is very sad.

jyutping: ziu6 kong1 jan3, daai6 sung3 (sung3) wong4
mandarin_meaning: 赵匡胤，大宋（餸）王（網絡俚語、綽號）：把人以趙匡胤（宋朝開國皇帝）作對比，並以「餸」與「宋」同音的粵語雙關，戲稱某人在煮食方面極為出色或自命不凡。
english_meaning: "Zhao Kuangyin, Great Song (Dish) King" — an internet slang/nickname that playfully compares someone to Emperor Zhao Kuangyin and, via a Cantonese homophone between '宋' (Song) and '餸' (dish), calls them the 'king of dishes'. Used to praise superb cooking or to tease someone being self-important in the kitchen.
explanation_mandarin: 此詞常見於香港網路和口語，用「趙匡胤」（宋朝開國者）作為梗，並以粵語「宋」和「餸」同音造成雙關。可用於誇讚某人廚藝高超（正面），亦可用作戲謔或諷刺（負面）。
explanation_english: This expression appears in Hong Kong online and spoken slang. It riffs on Zhao Kuangyin (founder of the Song dynasty) and exploits the Cantonese homophone between '宋' (Song) and '餸' (dish). It can be used to praise someone's excellent cooking or jokingly/sarcastically mock someone's self-importance in culinary matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿昌今晚煮嘢食煮得好掂，真係大宋（餸）王。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 coeng1 gam1 maan5 zyu2 je5 sik6 zyu2 dak1 hou2 dim6, zan1 hai6 daai6 sung3 (sung3) wong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿昌今晚做菜做得很棒，真是大宋（餸）王。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Cheung's cooking tonight was excellent — truly the 'Great Song (Dish) King'.

mandarin_meaning: 赶着去投胎
english_meaning: to hurry to be reborn; a slang insult telling someone to hurry up and die/reincarnate
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞短語（俚語／罵人用語）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的俚語，用來罵人或戲謔地說某人應該趕快死去並投胎，多用於生氣或嘲諷的語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used as an insult or joking remark meaning someone should hurry up and die/reincarnate; used in angry or teasing contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講嘅嘢完全冇道理，係咪趕住去投胎呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 ge3 je5 jyun4 cyun4 mou5 dou6 lei5, hai6 mai6 gon2 zyu6 heoi3 tau4 toi1 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說的完全沒有道理，是不是趕著去投胎啊？
examples.english_sentence: What you're saying makes no sense at all — are you rushing to be reincarnated?

mandarin_meaning: 来不及
english_meaning: can't make it in time; too late; unable to catch up
explanation_mandarin: 表示来不及做某事，无法在限定时间内完成或赶上（某事）。是粤语口语常用表达。
explanation_english: Indicates being unable to do something in time or to catch up; unable to meet a deadline or make it to an event. Commonly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日遲咗，趕唔切搭地鐵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 ci4 zo2, gon2 m4 cit3 daap3 dei6 tit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天迟到了，来不及赶上地铁。
examples.english_sentence: I'm late today; I can't make the subway.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遲咗半個鐘，趕唔切開會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci4 zo2 bun3 go3 zung1, gon2 m4 cit3 hoi1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他迟到半个小时，来不及参加会议。
examples.english_sentence: He was half an hour late and couldn't make the meeting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等車時太慢，結果趕唔切飛機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ce1 si4 taai3 maan6, git3 gwo2 gon2 m4 cit3 fei1 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等车的时候太慢，结果来不及赶飞机。
examples.english_sentence: We took too long waiting for the car and ended up missing the flight.

cantonese: 赶狗入穷巷，拧转头咬翻啖
jyutping: gon2 gau2 jap6 kung4 hong6, nau2 zyun2 tau4 ngaau5 faan1 daam6
mandarin_meaning: 把狗赶入穷巷，它会回头咬人。比喻把人逼到无路可走时，会反过来报复或反击。
english_meaning: Drive a dog into a dead-end alley and it will turn and bite. Metaphor: if you corner or push someone too far, they may fight back or retaliate.
explanation_mandarin: 此俗语用比喻手法说明不要把人逼到绝境，否则可能招致反抗或报复，常用于劝人行事谨慎或提醒不要过分逼迫他人。
explanation_english: This proverb warns that if you force someone into a corner, they may turn and retaliate. It's used to advise caution and not to push people too far.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做，等於趕狗入窮巷，扭轉頭就會咬翻啖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 zou6, dang2 jyu1 gon2 gau2 jap6 kung4 hong6, nau2 zyun2 tau4 zau6 wui5 ngaau5 faan1 daam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样做等于把狗赶入穷巷，转头就会咬你一口。
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing is like driving a dog into a dead-end alley; it will turn and bite you — don't push someone that far.

mandarin_meaning: 快点；加快速度；赶快
english_meaning: hurry up; speed up; accelerate (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，表示催促別人或事物加快速度或趕快行動。常見於香港日常對話中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to urge someone or something to go faster or to hurry. Common in everyday speech in Hong Kong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 起快啦，我哋要遲到喇！
examples.jyutping_sentence: hei2 faai3 laa1, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 ci4 dou3 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 快点，我们要迟到了！
examples.english_sentence: Hurry up, we're going to be late!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 師傅，起快啲啦，我哋等唔切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 fu6, hei2 faai3 di1 laa1, ngo5 dei6 dang2 m4 cit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 师傅，快点开/加速吧，我们来不及了。
examples.english_sentence: Driver, speed up a bit, we won't make it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日咁慢，起快啲啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 gam2 maan6, hei2 faai3 di1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你总是这么慢，快点吧！
examples.english_sentence: You're always so slow, hurry up!

mandarin_meaning: 承擔（責任、重任）
english_meaning: to shoulder a burden; to take on responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 表示接受或挑起某項責任或重擔，可以指實際搬運重物或比喻地承擔責任。
explanation_english: Means to accept or take up a responsibility or burden; can refer to physically carrying a load or metaphorically taking responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事要有人起擔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 jiu3 jau5 jan4 hei2 daam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事要有人承担责任。
examples.english_sentence: Someone has to take responsibility for this matter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老細叫佢起擔個項目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 sai3 giu3 keoi5 hei2 daam1 go3 hong6 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板叫他承担这个项目。
examples.english_sentence: The boss asked him to take on this project.

mandarin_meaning: 挑起爭端；挑事、惹事
english_meaning: to start a quarrel; to pick a fight; to stir up trouble
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語/俚語，指故意挑釁或製造事端，使人發生爭執或不愉快。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to deliberately provoke or create trouble, causing disputes or upsetting others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度起髮腳，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 hei2 faat3 goek3, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天在那裡挑事，搞得大家不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps stirring up trouble there, making everyone unhappy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再起髮腳啦，我哋傾下點樣解決問題好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 hei2 faat3 goek3 laa1, ngo5 dei6 king1 haa5 dim2 joeng6 gaai2 kyut3 man6 tai4 hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再挑事了，我們談談怎麼解決問題好不好？
examples.english_sentence: Stop picking fights. Let's talk about how to solve the problem, okay?

cantonese: 趁圩卖鱼尾，一定要搭嘴
jyutping: can3 wai1 maai6 jyu4 mei5, jat1 ding6 jiu3 daap3 zeoi2
mandarin_meaning: 趁著集市或熱鬧的時候賣剩下的東西要出聲吆喝；比喻遇到有利可圖或適當的場合就要抓住機會、發表意見或出面爭取。
english_meaning: When there's a busy market or a good opportunity, you must speak up (to attract attention or seize the chance); metaphorically, seize the opportunity and make your voice heard.
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指在集市（圩）賣魚剩尾時要大聲吆喝才能賣掉；引申為在有利或熱鬧的場合應該把握時機出聲、爭取利益或表達看法。
explanation_english: Literally refers to calling out when selling leftover fish at a busy market so customers notice you; figuratively it means taking advantage of a favorable or lively situation by speaking up to get attention, make a point, or seize an opportunity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日市集咁多人，你唔好冇反應，趁圩卖鱼尾，一定要搭嘴先有得賣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 si5 zaap6 gam2 do1 jan4, nei5 m4 hou2 mou5 faan2 jing3, can3 wai1 maai6 jyu4 mei5, jat1 ding6 jiu3 daap3 zeoi2 sin1 jau5 dak1 maai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天市集人這麼多，你不要沒反應，趁著熱鬧的時候要出聲，才有辦法賣掉。
examples.english_sentence: With so many people at the market today, don't stay silent — when there's a crowd you must speak up if you want to sell.

mandarin_meaning: 趁集市／墟日（去買東西）；趁機會做某事
english_meaning: to take advantage of a market day (to go shopping); more generally, to take advantage of an opportunity
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話裡的「趁墟／趁圩」原指在墟日或集市時趁機去買東西，延伸用法也可指利用某個時機或機會去做某事。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '趁墟' originally means going to the periodic market day to shop. By extension it can mean taking advantage of an occasion or opportunity to do something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日有墟，我想趁墟買餸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 jat6 jau5 heoi1, ngo5 soeng2 can3 heoi1 maai5 sung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天有集市，我想趁集市買菜。
examples.english_sentence: There's a market day tomorrow; I want to go to the market to buy groceries.

mandarin_meaning: 趁虛（趁虛而入、趁機）
english_meaning: to take advantage of an opening or weakness; seize the opportunity (often to exploit a gap)
explanation_mandarin: 表示在對方虛弱、放鬆或出現空檔時採取行動，通常含有利用機會或趁隙而入的意思，常見用法如「趁虛而入」。
explanation_english: Used to describe taking action when an opponent or situation is vulnerable, unguarded, or has an opening. Often implies exploiting a gap or seizing an opportunity (e.g., '趁虛而入').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到門冇鎖，就趁虛而入偷咗啲嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 mun4 mou5 so2, zau6 can3 heoi1 ji4 jap6, tau1 zo2 di1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到門沒鎖，就趁虛而入，偷了東西。
examples.english_sentence: He saw the door was unlocked and took advantage of the opening to break in and steal things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 對手出現漏洞，我哋要即刻趁虛而入，搶佔市場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: deoi3 sau2 ceot1 jin2 lau6 dung6, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zik1 hak1 can3 heoi1 ji4 jap6, coeng2 zim6 si5 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 對手出現漏洞，我們要立刻趁虛而入，搶佔市場。
examples.english_sentence: The competitor has a loophole; we must immediately seize the opportunity to capture the market.

mandarin_meaning: 趁勢而為；利用時機或隨勢行事，有時帶有投機、機會主義的含義
english_meaning: To seize the opportunity or act according to circumstances; to take advantage of a situation (can imply opportunism)
explanation_mandarin: 原指憑借風勢掌舵，比喻根據形勢變化採取行動或利用有利時機。有時含貶義，指見風使舵、投機取巧。
explanation_english: Originally meant steering by the wind; metaphorically it means to act according to changing circumstances or to take advantage of an opportunity. It can carry a negative sense of opportunism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見公司情況轉好，就趁风使𢃇，投靠有利嘅部門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 gung1si1 cing4fong3 zyun2 hou2, zau6 can3 fung1 si2 do6, tau4kau3 jau5lei6 ge3 bou6mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他見公司情況好轉，就趁勢而為，投靠有利的部門。
examples.english_sentence: He saw the company's situation improve, so he seized the opportunity and attached himself to a favorable department.

cantonese: 越穷越见鬼，肚饿倒泻米
jyutping: jyut6 hung4 jyut6 gin3 gwai2, tou5 ngo6 dou3 se3 mai5
mandarin_meaning: 越穷越倒霉，处境糟糕到连基本的东西也出问题
english_meaning: The poorer you are, the more misfortune you encounter; things go wrong even for the most basic needs
explanation_mandarin: 這句粤語俗語表示人越窮越容易遇到麻煩和不幸，“肚饿倒泻米”是比喻處境糟糕到連飯這類基本東西也出狀況。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb conveys that poverty tends to bring more troubles and misfortune; the phrase 'when you're hungry you even spill rice' is a metaphor for things going wrong even at the most basic level.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近啲嘢越嚟越差，真係越窮越見鬼，肚餓倒瀉米，點算好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 di1 je5 jyut6 lai4 jyut6 caa1, zan1 hai6 jyut6 hung4 jyut6 gin3 gwai2, tou5 ngo6 dou3 se3 mai5, dim2 syun3 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近事情越來越糟，真是越窮越見鬼，肚子餓到連米都會被打翻，怎麼辦？
examples.english_sentence: Things have been getting worse lately — it's really 'the poorer you are, the more misfortune you see; when you're hungry you even spill rice.' What should I do?

cantonese: 越穷越见鬼，越冷越翻风‍
jyutping: jyut6 hung4 jyut6 gin3 gwai2, jyut6 laang5 jyut6 faan1 fung1
mandarin_meaning: 祸不单行；越穷越倒霉，越冷越出乱子（形容坏事接连发生）
english_meaning: When misfortune strikes it often comes in succession — the poorer/unluckier you are, the more (strange/bad) things happen; when it's colder, problems multiply. (Equivalent: 'When it rains, it pours.' / 'Things go from bad to worse.')
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用来形容倒霉或问题接二连三发生，情况越糟糕似乎越容易冒出更多麻烦。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb used to describe how misfortunes or problems seem to come one after another — the worse the situation, the more complications arise.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近真係唔順，越穷越见鬼，越冷越翻风，愈嚟愈多麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 zan1 hai6 m4 seon6, jyut6 hung4 jyut6 gin3 gwai2, jyut6 laang5 jyut6 faan1 fung1, jyu6 loi4 jyu6 do1 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近真的很不顺，祸不单行，越穷越见鬼，越冷越翻风，麻烦越来越多。
examples.english_sentence: Things haven't been going well lately — misfortunes keep coming: the poorer/unluckier you are, the more problems show up; the colder it gets, the more trouble there is.

mandarin_meaning: 来不及
english_meaning: can't make it in time; too late; unable to catch up
explanation_mandarin: 表示時間不夠，無法在規定或預期的時間內完成某事，等同於「來不及」。常用於口語。
explanation_english: Indicates there isn't enough time to do something or to arrive on time; equivalent to 'too late' or 'can't make it'. Common colloquial Cantonese expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我趕唔得切，會遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gon2 m4 dak1 cit3, wui5 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我来不及了，会迟到。
examples.english_sentence: I can't make it in time; I'll be late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日太遲出門，可能趕唔得切返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 taai3 ci4 ceot1 mun4, ho2 nang4 gon2 m4 dak1 cit3 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天出门太晚，可能来不及上班。
examples.english_sentence: You left too late today; you might not make it to work on time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 班飛機已經起飛，我哋去到機場都趕唔得切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baan1 fei1 gei1 ji5 ging1 hei2 fei1, ngo5 dei6 heoi3 dou3 gei1 coeng4 dou1 gon2 m4 dak1 cit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 飞机已经起飞，我们到机场也来不及了。
examples.english_sentence: The plane has already taken off; even if we arrive at the airport now, it's too late.

mandarin_meaning: 赶得及；来得及
english_meaning: to be able to make it (in time); to be able to catch (a vehicle or meet a deadline)
explanation_mandarin: 表示有足够的时间赶上某件事或能够及时完成，例如赶上交通工具或赶及截止时间。
explanation_english: Indicates having enough time to catch or make something (e.g. a bus, train, or deadline); being able to do something in time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你而家出發，應該可以趕得起今晚八點嘅巴士。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 ji4 gaa1 ceot1 faat3, jing1 goi1 ho2 ji5 gon2 dak1 hei2 gam1 maan5 baat3 dim2 ge3 baa1 si2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你现在出发，应该可以赶得上今晚八点的公车。
examples.english_sentence: If you leave now, you should be able to make the 8pm bus tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 打發時間；閒聊、消磨時間（粵語口語）
english_meaning: to kill time; to chat casually to pass time (Cantonese colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「趕水」是粵語口語，用來描述透過閒聊或做些沒大事的事情來打發或消磨時間，也可指在等待或空檔時湊時間閒談。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to pass or kill time, often by chatting or doing light, unimportant activities while waiting or filling a gap.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋去商場行下，趕下水先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 soeng1 coeng4 haang4 haa5, gon2 haa5 seoi2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們去商場逛逛，打發一下時間。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the mall for a bit and kill some time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等巴士期間，我同朋友傾計，趕下水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 baa1 si2 kei4 gaan1, ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 king1 gai2, gon2 haa5 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等公交車的時候，我和朋友聊聊天打發時間。
examples.english_sentence: While waiting for the bus, I chatted with my friend to pass the time.

mandarin_meaning: 惹事、製造騷動或喧鬧
english_meaning: to cause trouble; to make a scene; to stir up a commotion
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指故意或無意中製造騷動、惹事或出醜，常用於抱怨某人惹麻煩或鬧事。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to cause a disturbance or trouble, often used to complain that someone is making a fuss or causing problems.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日趟聲，搞到鄰居好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 tong3 seng1, gaau2 dou3 leon4 geoi1 hou2 fan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是惹事，搞得鄰居很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always causes trouble, which really annoys the neighbors.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試嗰陣要穩陣，唔好趟聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si3 go2 zan6 jiu3 wan2 zan6, m4 hou2 tong3 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面試時要穩重，不要惹事。
examples.english_sentence: Be composed during the interview; don't cause any commotion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 酒後容易趟聲，大家要注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau2 hau6 jung4 ji6 tong3 seng1, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 喝酒後容易惹事，大家要注意。
examples.english_sentence: People tend to cause trouble after drinking; everyone should be careful.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見字，詞義不詳/不確定
english_meaning: Rare/obscure character; meaning and pronunciation uncertain
explanation_mandarin: 「趨𧺙」包含常見字「趨」與一個罕見漢字「𧺙」。這個組合在現代粵語詞典與常用語料中極少見或未被收錄，該字（𧺙）的讀音與確切詞義沒有公認記載。遇見時通常需要依上下文或古籍註釋判斷，並可能是筆誤、俗寫或地方用字。
explanation_english: The phrase contains the common character 趨 plus a rare/obscure character 𧺙. This combination is extremely rare or unrecorded in modern Cantonese dictionaries and corpora; the pronunciation and exact meaning of 𧺙 are not established. When encountered it usually requires context or historical notes to interpret and may be a scribal variant, colloquial form, or regional/archaic character.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺舊文獻入面見到「趨𧺙」，但呢個字好罕見，唔知點讀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gau6 man4 hyun6 jap6 min6 gin3 dou2 'ceoi1 [未知字]' , daan6 ni1 go3 zi6 hou2 hon2 gin3, m4 zi1 dim2 duk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在舊文獻中見到「趨𧺙」，但這個字很罕見，不知道怎麼讀。
examples.english_sentence: I saw "趨𧺙" in an old document, but the character is very rare and I don't know how to pronounce it.

mandarin_meaning: （古字）與「趨」義近，意為迅速前往、奔走、趕忙
english_meaning: An archaic/literary character meaning to hasten or run quickly; similar to 趨 (to hurry)
explanation_mandarin: 「趫」為古字，常與「趨」通用，表示迅速前往、奔走或趕忙的動作，現代書面語多用「趨」或「趕」替代。
explanation_english: 趫 is an archaic/literary character often used like 趨, meaning to hurry, hasten, or run quickly. In modern usage 趕 or 趨 are more common.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到消息後，佢即刻趫出街去幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 siu1si3 hau6, keoi5 zik1 hak1 ceoi1 ceot1 gaai1 heoi3 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到消息後，他立刻趕出去幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: After seeing the news, he immediately hurried out to help.

mandarin_meaning: 惨败；完蛋；被羞辱（粗俗俚语）
english_meaning: vulgar slang for suffering a crushing defeat, being humiliated, or being totally screwed/ruined
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話俚語，通常用來形容在比賽、考試或處境中遭遇慘敗、被狠狠羞辱或處於非常糟糕的狀態。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang term used to describe suffering a heavy defeat, being humiliated, or ending up in a very bad or ruined situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試我考到趴屎，完全唔及格。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 ngo5 haau2 dou3 paa1 si2, jyun4 cyun4 m4 kap6 gaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试我考得很差，完全不及格。
examples.english_sentence: I did terribly on this exam; I failed completely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺比賽度比人打到趴屎，面都冇得見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 bei2 coi3 dou6 bei2 jan4 daa2 dou3 paa1 si2, min6 dou1 mou5 dak1 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在比赛中被对手打得很惨，脸都没法见人。
examples.english_sentence: He got trounced in the match and was totally humiliated.

mandarin_meaning: 丟臉、出醜、失敗（口語）
english_meaning: to lose face; to be embarrassed/ humiliated; to fail or be exposed (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 「跌交」為廣東話口語用法，通常表示丟臉、出醜或在公眾面前被揭穿、失敗而失去面子。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to lose face, be embarrassed or humiliated; to be exposed or fail — often used when someone is caught out or makes a public mistake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺面試嗰日好緊張，結果跌交咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 min6 si3 go2 jat6 hou2 gan2 zoeng1, git3 gwo2 dit3 gaau1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在面試那天很緊張，結果表現失常，丟了面子。
examples.english_sentence: He was very nervous on the interview day and ended up messing up / losing face.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺公司面前講錯嘢，真係跌交。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gung1 si1 min6 cin4 gong2 co3 je5, zan1 hai6 dit3 gaau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在公司面前說錯話，真的很丟臉。
examples.english_sentence: He said the wrong thing in front of the company and really lost face.

jyutping: dit3 dai1 laa1 faan1 zaak3 saa1
mandarin_meaning: 跌得很慘／徹底失敗或丟臉、出糗
english_meaning: to fall flat or fail spectacularly; to be humiliated or make a fool of oneself
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，字面有跌倒、翻滾、弄得一身沙的意象，用來形容某人遭遇慘敗、出醜或被徹底打敗、丟臉。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally evoking falling, flipping and getting covered in sand; used to describe someone who fails miserably, is thoroughly humiliated, or makes a complete fool of themselves.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次面試搞到咁慘，真係跌低揦翻拃沙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 min6 si5 gaau2 dou3 gam2 caam2, zan1 hai6 dit3 dai1 laa1 faan1 zaak3 saa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次面试搞得这么惨，真是彻底失败/出丑。
examples.english_sentence: This interview went so badly — I totally bombed it and was humiliated.

mandarin_meaning: （可能是錯寫）應為「逮緝」，意思是逮捕、緝拿。
english_meaning: (likely a misspelling of "逮緝") to arrest; to capture; to nab
explanation_mandarin: 「跐緝」並非標準或常見的現代粵語詞彙，較多情況下是將「逮緝」錯寫為「跐緝」。「逮緝」指逮捕、緝拿罪犯或嫌疑人。
explanation_english: "跐緝" is not a standard or common modern Cantonese term; in most cases it appears to be a misspelling of "逮緝" (daai6 kap1), which means to arrest or capture someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有人喺論壇度打咗「跐緝」，其實應該寫「逮緝」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 jan4 hai2 leon6 taan4 dou6 daa2 zo2 'cit3 cap1', kei4 sat6 jing1 goi1 se2 'daai6 kap1'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人在論壇打了「跐緝」，其實應該寫成「逮緝」。
examples.english_sentence: Someone wrote "跐緝" on a forum; actually it should be written as "逮緝" (to arrest).

mandarin_meaning: 跑腿／跑手（幫人跑事、送件或在黑社會/非法活動中擔任收債、打手等跑腿角色）
english_meaning: runner; someone who runs errands or acts as a courier — can also mean a gofer/collector for criminal groups
explanation_mandarin: 「跑手」原意指替人跑腿、送文件或貨品的人，在廣東話口語裡也常用作俚語，指替黑社會或非法活動執行收債、恐嚇等任務的人。
explanation_english: Literally a person who runs errands or delivers items. In Cantonese slang it can also refer to a gofer or collector working for criminal organizations, e.g. someone who collects debts or does intimidation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日要做跑手，幫老闆送啲文件去對面公司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 zou6 paau2 sau2, bong1 lou5 baan2 sung3 di1 man4 gin2 heoi3 deoi3 min6 gung1 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天要當跑手，幫老闆把文件送到對面的公司。
examples.english_sentence: I have to be a runner today and deliver some documents for my boss to the company across the street.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講佢係黑社會嘅跑手，專門負責收債。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 gong2 keoi5 hai6 hak1 se5 wui6 ge3 paau2 sau2, zyun1 mun4 fu6 zak1 sau1 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽說他是黑社會的跑手，專門負責收債。
examples.english_sentence: I heard he's a runner for the triad, specializing in collecting debts.

mandarin_meaning: 比喻在不適合或極為困難的情況下去做精細的事，徒勞無功或不切實際。
english_meaning: Literally 'to shoot a mosquito's whisker while riding a galloping horse' — to attempt something delicate or precise under impossible or inappropriate conditions; a futile or impractical effort.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容做事方法、時機或情況不對，做再細緻也無用，常帶有徒勞或不切實際的含義。
explanation_english: Used to describe attempting a delicate task under the wrong conditions or in an impossible situation; implies the effort is futile or impractical.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家咁趕時間去整啲好細緻嘅嘢，等於跑马射蚊须，冇必要。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 gam2 gon2 si4 gaan3 heoi3 zing2 di1 hou2 sai3 zai3 ge3 je5, dang2 jyu4 paau2 maa5 se6 man1 syu1, mou5 bit1 jiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在這麼趕時間去做一些很細緻的事，相當於跑马射蚊须，沒必要。
examples.english_sentence: Rushing to do something delicate right now is like trying to shoot a mosquito's whisker from a galloping horse — pointless.

jyutping: bo2 sau2 taai3 gaan3, mou4 kyun4 mou4 sai3
mandarin_meaning: 沒權沒勢、無足輕重的人；無影響力、無權勢的人
english_meaning: a powerless, ineffectual person with no authority or influence
explanation_mandarin: 「跛手太监」字面上指行動或能力受限的太監，合起來比喻一個沒權沒勢、做事無影響力的人；「無拳（權）無勢」強調沒有權力與勢力。常用來貶低他人或形容無能無影響力的人。
explanation_english: Literally 'a lame-handed eunuch' and 'no fist (power) no influence' — used figuratively to describe someone who is powerless, ineffectual, or lacks authority and influence. Often used derogatorily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢根本係跛手太监，無拳無勢，講嘢冇人聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gan1 bun2 hai6 bo2 sau2 taai3 gaan3, mou4 kyun4 mou4 sai3, gong2 je5 mou5 jan4 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他根本就是個沒權沒勢的人，說話沒人聽。
examples.english_sentence: He's basically a powerless person with no influence; no one listens to him.

mandarin_meaning: 沒用的人；無能、懶惰或可靠性差的人（口語、貶義）
english_meaning: a useless or incompetent person (slang, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人無能、懶散或幫唔到手，帶有貶義和戲謔意味。字面上含「跛」（跛腳）的負面意象，但主要是比喻用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who is useless, incompetent, lazy, or unreliable. It's derogatory and often used jokingly or pejoratively. Literally invokes 'limping' imagery but is used metaphorically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日遲到又唔做嘢，佢真係個跛羅蓋子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3 jau6 m4 zou6 je5, keoi5 zan1 hai6 go3 bo2 lo4 goi3 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 經常遲到又不做事，他真是個沒用的人。
examples.english_sentence: He's always late and doesn't do any work — he's really a useless person.

mandarin_meaning: 形容只會說話、愛吹捧或裝可憐，但不願實際做事的人（貶義）
english_meaning: A derogatory Cantonese slang for someone who talks a lot or boasts but does not take real action — basically 'all talk, no action'.
explanation_mandarin: 「跛脚鹩哥」字面為「一隻跛腳的鹩哥」，引申用來形容那些只會說話、愛吹水或裝可憐以逃避責任，但實際上不做事或做事無力的人，帶有貶義與諷刺意味。
explanation_english: Literally 'a lame myna', used figuratively in Cantonese to describe someone who talks a lot, brags, or plays the victim to avoid responsibility but fails to act or perform — a derogatory label meaning 'all talk, no action'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日吹水，做嘢又唔落力，真係一個跛脚鹩哥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ceoi1 seoi2, zou6 je5 jau6 m4 lok6 lik6, zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 bo2 goek3 liu4 go1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是吹牛，做事又不認真，真是一個跛腳鹩哥。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks big and doesn't put effort into his work — he's really an 'all talk, no action' type.

jyutping: bo2 goek3 liu4 go1 zi6 jau5 fei1 loi4 maang2
mandarin_meaning: 即使有缺陷的人也會遇到合適的人或機會（每個人都有機緣）
english_meaning: Even someone with shortcomings will find a match or opportunity; everyone gets their chance.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用跛腳的鹩哥也能遇到飛來的蜢，形象地表達即使條件不完美的人，也會遇到合適的人或得到機會，不必過於自卑或灰心。
explanation_english: This proverb uses the image of a lame myna that nevertheless attracts a flying grasshopper to express that even imperfect people can find a suitable partner or opportunity — so don't be overly discouraged.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁灰心，跛脚鹩哥自有飞来蜢，總會有人鍾意你嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 fui1 sam1, bo2 goek3 liu4 go1 zi6 jau5 fei1 loi4 maang2, zung2 wui5 jau5 jan4 zung1 ji3 nei5 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別太灰心，跛腳的鹩哥自有飛來蜢，總會有人喜歡你的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so discouraged; even a lame myna will have a grasshopper come—someone will like you.

jyutping: bo2 goek3 ling4 go1 zi6 jau5 fei1 loi4 maang5
mandarin_meaning: 跛腳的鳥也會有飛來的蚱蜢（比喻即使不完美或處境不好，也會有意外的好運或機會）
english_meaning: Even a lame sparrow will have a grasshopper fly to it (i.e., everyone may get unexpected luck or a suitable match/opportunity despite imperfections or setbacks).
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用比喻說明：即使某人有缺陷或處境不佳，也有可能遇到意外的好機會或合適的對象，強調機會或運氣會降臨到每個人身上。
explanation_english: A proverbial saying meaning that even someone imperfect or unlucky can receive unexpected good fortune or find a fitting opportunity/partner; it stresses that everyone can get lucky eventually.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁灰心，跛腳鷯哥自有飛來蜢，遲啲你都會搵到好機會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 fui1 sam1, bo2 goek3 ling4 go1 zi6 jau5 fei1 loi4 maang5, ci4 di1 nei5 dou1 wui5 wan2 dou3 hou2 gei1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別灰心，跛腳鷯哥自有飛來蜢，遲些你也會找到好機會。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be discouraged; even a lame sparrow will have a grasshopper fly to it — you'll find a good opportunity eventually.

mandarin_meaning: 跟風傳播別人的閒言碎語；附和地重複或散播別人的八卦
english_meaning: to repeat or spread someone else's gossip; to follow along and pass on rumors without verifying
explanation_mandarin: 「跟人口水溦」是粵語口語用法，指不加求證地附和或傳播別人的閒言碎語、八卦。書寫上句中「溦」常見為「尾」的口語寫法，意思接近「尾隨、跟著」某人的說話尾部去散播或重複內容。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial phrase means to mindlessly echo or spread other people's gossip or rumors. The final character here is commonly written as 尾 (mei5) in related expressions; the phrase conveys piggybacking on someone else's remarks and passing them on without checking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂跟人口水溦，聽到啲八卦先查清楚再講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 gan1 jan4 hau2 seoi2 mei5, teng1 dou3 di1 baat3 gwaa3 sin1 caa4 cing1 co2 zoi3 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要随便跟风传播别人的闲言碎语，听到八卦要先查清楚再说。
examples.english_sentence: Don't blindly repeat other people's gossip; when you hear rumors, verify them before you repeat them.

mandarin_meaning: 跟屁虫（總是跟在別人後面的人；愛跟隨別人的人）
english_meaning: a tagalong; someone who constantly follows another person closely; a clingy follower
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，形容總是跟在別人身邊、不離不棄或盲目跟隨的人，有時帶貶義，表示依賴或諂媚。
explanation_english: A colloquial term for someone who always follows another person closely or clings to them; often used pejoratively to imply dependence, submissiveness, or sycophancy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日跟住我，好似個跟屁蟲咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gan1 zyu6 ngo5, hou2 ci5 go3 gan1 pei3 cung4 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是跟着我，好像个跟屁虫。
examples.english_sentence: He always follows me around, like a tagalong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日做人哋嘅跟屁蟲，要有自己嘅主見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 zou6 jan4 dei6 ge3 gan1 pei3 cung4, jiu3 jau5 zi6 gei2 ge3 zyu2 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要总是做别人的跟屁虫，要有自己的主见。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always be someone else's tagalong; have your own opinions.

mandarin_meaning: 跟斗（打跟斗、翻跟斗）
english_meaning: somersault; to do a somersault
explanation_mandarin: 表示翻跟斗或翻筋斗的動作，既可作名詞指一次翻轉，也可作動詞表示做這個動作。
explanation_english: Refers to a somersault (flipping the body over); can be used as a noun (a somersault) or a verb (to somersault).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺操場做體操，跳咗個跟斗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 cou1 coeng4 zou6 tai2 cou1, tiu3 zo2 go3 gan1 dau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在操场做体操，跳了一个跟斗。
examples.english_sentence: He was doing gymnastics on the playground and did a somersault.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細佬一個唔小心跌咗落地下，打咗個跟斗都冇事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou2 jat1 go3 m4 siu2 sam1 dit3 zo2 lok6 dei6 haa6, daa2 zo2 go3 gan1 dau2 dou1 mou5 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 弟弟不小心摔到地上，打了个跟斗也没事。
examples.english_sentence: My younger brother accidentally fell to the ground, did a somersault and was unhurt.

mandarin_meaning: 合眼緣；好看；令人滿意
english_meaning: pleasing to the eye; visually appealing; attractive
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示某人或某物在外觀上令人滿意、合眼緣或好看，常用於描述外表、衣着或擺盤等。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning visually pleasing or attractive; used to say someone or something is easy on the eyes (appearance, outfit, plating, etc.).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫好跟眼，著上身好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 hou2 gan1 ngaan5 zoek3 soeng6 san1 hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件衣服很合眼，穿上身很漂亮。
examples.english_sentence: This outfit is very pleasing to the eye; it looks great on.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個樣好跟眼，好多人鍾意睇佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 joeng6 hou2 gan1 ngaan5, hou2 do1 jan4 zung1 ji3 tai2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他長得很討人喜歡，很多人喜歡看他。
examples.english_sentence: He's quite easy on the eyes; many people like looking at him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢道菜擺盤好跟眼，令人好想試。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 coi3 baai2 pun4 hou2 gan1 ngaan5 ling6 jan4 hou2 soeng2 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這道菜擺盤很好看，讓人很想試吃。
examples.english_sentence: The dish's plating is very attractive; it makes people want to try it.

cantonese: 跟着好人学好人，跟着喃无学拜神
jyutping: gan1 zoek6 hou2 jan4 hok6 hou2 jan4, gan1 zoek6 naam4 mou5 hok6 baai3 san4
mandarin_meaning: 跟着好人会学好；跟着无知或不良的人会学迷信或不好的行为（俗语/谚语）
english_meaning: Follow good people and you'll learn to be good; follow ignorant or bad people and you'll pick up superstition or bad habits (proverb/saying).
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗語，強調交朋友或跟隨的對象會影響個人的行為與價值觀：跟好人會學好，跟不當的人或無知者可能會學到迷信或壞習慣。句中「喃无」為口語變體，常用於地方性說法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb stressing that the people you follow or associate with shape your behavior and values: following good people leads to good behavior, while following improper or ignorant people can lead to superstition or bad habits. The token “喃无” is a colloquial/local variant in speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺街市做生意嘅阿姨經常話：跟着好人学好人，跟着喃无学拜神，所以要揀啱朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gaai1 si5 zou6 saang1 ji3 ge3 aa3 ji4 ging1 soeng4 waa6: gan1 zoek6 hou2 jan4 hok6 hou2 jan4, gan1 zoek6 naam4 mou5 hok6 baai3 san4, so2 ji5 jiu3 gaan2 ngaam1 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在菜市場做生意的阿姨常說：跟着好人学好人，跟着喃无学拜神，所以要挑選合適的朋友。
examples.english_sentence: The auntie at the market often says: 'Follow good people and you'll learn to be good; follow the wrong/ignorant people and you'll learn superstition,' so choose your friends carefully.

mandarin_meaning: 見風轉舵；兩面討好；隨著形勢改變立場
english_meaning: to play both sides; to switch stance to suit the powerful; to pander to whoever is convenient
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容人沒有堅定立場，會隨着情勢或權勢改變自己的態度或表態，以討好不同一方。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquialism describing someone who has no firm stance and shifts position according to circumstances or powerful parties, courting whichever side is convenient.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日跟红顶白，老細一改口佢就轉晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gan1 hung4 ding2 baak6, lou5 sai3 jat1 goi2 hau2 keoi5 zau6 zyun3 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是見風轉舵，老闆一變口他就全部轉變。
examples.english_sentence: He always plays both sides — when the boss changes his tune, he immediately switches too.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺議會入面，有啲議員跟红顶白，令選民好失望。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 ji5 wui2 jap6 min6, jau5 di1 ji5 jyun4 gan1 hung4 ding2 baak6, ling6 syun2 man4 hou2 sat1 mong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在議會裡，有些議員兩面討好，讓選民很失望。
examples.english_sentence: In the council, some councillors pander to both sides, disappointing voters.

mandarin_meaning: 插队；抢在别人前面
english_meaning: to cut in line; to jump ahead of others
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指在排隊或行動中越過他人、從別人前面插入或搶先行動。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to cut in line or to jump ahead of others in a queue or situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 排隊唔好跨頭，大家有秩序啲啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: paai4 deoi6 m4 hou2 kwaa3 tau4, daai6 gaa1 jau5 zaap6 ceoi3 di1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 排队不要插队，大家要有秩序一點。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cut in line; everyone should be a bit more orderly.

jyutping: gwai3 cyu3 wai3 zyu1 naa5 tai2 cin2 fan6 soeng6
mandarin_meaning: 為了錢出賣尊嚴／為了錢卑躬屈膝
english_meaning: To sell one's dignity for money; to demean oneself or kowtow for the sake of money
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話俚語，用來形容為了獲取金錢而放下身段、出賣尊嚴或做卑微、屈辱的事。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who humiliates themselves or sells their dignity to obtain money — doing degrading acts for cash.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗錢，成日跪處喂豬乸睇錢份上，做啲好卑微嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 cin2, sing4 jat6 gwai3 cyu3 wai3 zyu1 naa5 tai2 cin2 fan6 soeng6, zou6 di1 hou2 bei1 mei4 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了錢，整天為了錢低聲下氣、出賣尊嚴，做些很卑微的事情。
examples.english_sentence: He, for the sake of money, is always kowtowing and selling his dignity, doing degrading things.

mandarin_meaning: 跳躍出水面的飛魚（字面意思）；並非常見的固定成語，主要為口語描述
english_meaning: literally 'jumping flying fish' — a flying fish leaping out of the water; primarily a literal/descriptive phrase rather than a fixed idiom
explanation_mandarin: 「跳天魚」照字面理解是指飛魚跳出水面的情況。該詞在廣東話中主要用作字面描述，並不是一個普遍使用的成語或固定俚語，但可用來形容海面上飛魚跳躍的景象或類似的跳躍動作。
explanation_english: Taken literally, "跳天魚" refers to flying fish leaping out of the water. It is mainly a descriptive phrase in Cantonese rather than a common fixed idiom or slang, used to describe the sight of flying fish or similar leaping movements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚喺海面見到幾隻跳天魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 hai2 hoi2 min6 gin3 dou2 gei2 zek3 tiu3 tin1 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚在海面上看到幾條跳躍的飛魚。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight I saw several flying fish leaping out of the sea.

mandarin_meaning: 大幅降价甩卖的商品；廉价货（常暗示质量差或为滞销品）
english_meaning: A fire-sale or clearance item sold at rock-bottom prices; a bargain item (often implying poor quality or unsold stock).
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容以極低價格出售的商品，通常指大甩賣或清貨品，有時帶有質量較差或滯銷的含義。
explanation_english: A colloquial term for goods sold at extremely low, clearance prices. It often refers to items on a deep discount and can imply poor quality or unsold stock.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部手機係跳楼货，價錢好平但質素差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 sau2 gei1 hai6 tiu3 lau4 fo3, gaa3 cin2 hou2 ping4 daan6 zat1 sou3 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那部手机是跳楼货，价格很便宜但质量差。
examples.english_sentence: That phone is a clearance item — very cheap but poor quality.

mandarin_meaning: 跳躍的魚；（罕見、口語或比喻用法）形容活潑、善於躲避或反覆無常的人
english_meaning: jumping fish; (rare/colloquial/figurative) someone lively, elusive, or fickle
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（口語時可作形容詞）
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指從水中跳出的魚。並非常見成語或廣泛俚語，但在口語或比喻情況下可用來形容人活潑、難以捉摸或容易放人鴿子（不守約）。
explanation_english: Literally 'jumping fish' — a fish leaping out of water. Not a common idiom; in colloquial/figurative use it can describe a person who is lively, elusive, or unreliable (e.g., stands people up).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 河面上有幾條跳魚，不停咁躍起，好壯觀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ho4 min6 seong6 jau5 gei2 tiu4 tiu3 jyu4, bat1 ting4 gam2 joek6 hei2, hou2 zong6 gun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 河面上有幾條跳出水面的魚，不停躍起，很壯觀。
examples.english_sentence: There were several fish jumping on the river surface, leaping continuously — very spectacular.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做人好跳魚，成日約人食飯又走數，唔可信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 jan4 hou2 tiu3 jyu4, sing4 jat6 joek3 jan4 sik6 faan6 jau6 zau2 sou3, m4 ho2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很『跳魚』（口語用法，意指善變或不可靠），常常約人吃飯又放鴿子，不可信。
examples.english_sentence: He's very 'jumping fish' — (colloquial: fickle/unreliable) — he often arranges to eat with people then stands them up; not trustworthy.

mandarin_meaning: 蹲著（久坐或蹲下的姿勢，常指盤腳或蹲伏在地上）
english_meaning: to squat/crouch on one's heels (a colloquial Cantonese posture of squatting close to the ground)
explanation_mandarin: 「踎格仔」是香港廣東話的口語說法，指的是以蹲伏或盤踞在地的姿勢長時間停留、坐着或作為休息、聊天的姿勢。常見於街市、街邊或社區的長者與小孩。
explanation_english: “踎格仔” is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquialism meaning to squat/crouch on one's heels (often for an extended time), typically used to describe people resting or chatting while squatting close to the ground—common among elders or children in markets and on sidewalks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲長者成日喺街市踎格仔傾偈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 coeng4 ze2 seng4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 si5 ngau1 gaak3 zai2 king1 gai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些老人經常在菜市場蹲着聊天。
examples.english_sentence: Those elders often squat and chat at the market.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路仔喺路邊踎格仔玩泥巴，好專心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 lou6 bin1 ngau1 gaak3 zai2 waan2 nai4 baa1, hou2 zyun1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子在路邊蹲着玩泥巴，很專心。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are squatting by the roadside playing with mud, very focused.

mandarin_meaning: 踢毽子（玩毽子）
english_meaning: to play shuttlecock (jianzi); to kick a shuttlecock
explanation_mandarin: 指用腳踢毽子（毽子是一種由羽毛或塑料等做成的小玩具），是一種傳統的運動或遊戲，要用腳等部位把毽子保持在空中。
explanation_english: Refers to playing the traditional shuttlecock game (jianzi), where players kick a weighted shuttlecock with their feet and other body parts (except hands) to keep it in the air.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路仔喺公園踢毽，好好玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 gung1 jyun4 tek3 zin3, hou2 hou2 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子在公园踢毽子，很好玩。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are playing shuttlecock in the park; it's a lot of fun.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）踩別人的地盤；爭奪或侵犯地盤
english_meaning: (slang) to encroach on or challenge someone else's turf/territory; to assert control over an area
explanation_mandarin: 『踩地盤』是廣東話口語，指侵入、挑戰或爭奪他人的地盤或勢力範圍，常用於商業競爭、幫派或社區衝突等情境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to trespass on or challenge someone else's territory or sphere of influence. Commonly used for business competition, gang turf disputes, or when one party intrudes on another's domain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好去踩人哋嘅地盤，會惹起衝突。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 heoi3 caai2 jan4 dei6 ge3 dei6 pun4, wui5 je5 hei2 cung1 dat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要去侵犯別人的地盤，會引起衝突。
examples.english_sentence: Don't trespass on other people's turf; it will cause conflict.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方話兩個幫派喺市中心踩地盤，已經拘捕咗幾個人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 waa6 loeng5 go3 bong1 paai3 hai2 si5 zung1 sam1 caai2 dei6 pun4, ji5 ging1 kau1 bou6 zo2 gei2 go3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方說兩個幫派在市中心爭地盤，已經拘捕了幾個人。
examples.english_sentence: The police said two gangs were fighting over turf in the city centre and have arrested several people.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）踩死蚂蚁；（口語）把某人徹底打敗或羞辱、欺負某人
english_meaning: (literal) to step on and kill an ant; (slang) to crush/defeat someone utterly or to humiliate/bully someone
explanation_mandarin: 「踩死蚁」是廣東話口語，用來形容把對方徹底打敗、羞辱或狠狠地批評、欺負對方。字面意思是踩死一隻螞蟻，延伸為比喻性的凌辱或壓倒性擊敗。
explanation_english: “踩死蚁” is Cantonese slang. Literally it means to step on (and kill) an ant; figuratively it describes crushing or utterly defeating someone, or humiliating/bullying them harshly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今場比賽佢哋畀對手踩死蚁，完全冇得還手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 coeng4 bei2 coi3 keoi5 dei6 bei2 deoi3 sau2 caai2 sei2 ngai5, jyun4 cyun4 mou5 dak1 waan4 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這場比賽他們被對手徹底打敗，完全沒有還手之力。
examples.english_sentence: They were totally crushed by the opponents in this match, with no chance to fight back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁踩死蚁人啦，大家都係朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 caai2 sei2 ngai5 jan4 laa1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hai6 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要這樣欺負別人啦，我們都是朋友。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so harsh on people; we're all friends.

mandarin_meaning: 踩（燈的）花/燈芯（字面意思）；粵語中並不常見的表達，通常為字面用法
english_meaning: Literally 'to step on the lamp's flower/wick/decoration'; a rare Cantonese expression, usually used literally
explanation_mandarin: 「踩灯花」在粵語中並非廣泛使用的慣用語，字面上指踩到燈上的花飾或燈芯，可能導致燈熄或破壞。並無普遍公認的隱喻或俗語性含義（可能有地區性或個別語境用法）。
explanation_english: This is not a widely used Cantonese idiom. Literally, it means stepping on a lamp's decorative part or wick, which could extinguish or damage the lamp. There is no widely recognized figurative meaning (regional or context-specific usages may exist).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲細路仔喺廟入面玩火，唔好去踩燈花，會危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 miu6 jap6 min6 waan2 fo2 , m4 hou2 heoi3 caai2 dang1 faa1 , wui5 ngai4 him2 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 孩子們在廟裡玩火，不要去踩燈花，會很危險。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are playing with fire in the temple; don't step on the lamp decoration/wick — it's dangerous.

jyutping: caai2 zoek3 wu6 gaap3 dong3 se4
mandarin_meaning: 把無害的東西當成危險或可怕的事物；小題大做、驚慌過度（相近於「草木皆兵 / 杯弓蛇影」）
english_meaning: To mistake something harmless for something dangerous; to overreact or make a fuss over nothing; to be jumpy or overly suspicious.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞短語（俚語/成語性用法）
explanation_mandarin: 比喻把無害或微不足道的東西誤認為有威脅，因而驚慌、過度反應或小題大做。
explanation_english: A metaphor for mistaking a harmless object for a threat, causing panic or an excessive reaction — making a mountain out of a molehill or being unduly jumpy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好踩着芋荚当蛇，佢只係遲到啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 caai2 zoek3 wu6 gaap3 dong3 se4, keoi5 zi2 hai6 ci4 dou3 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要小題大做，他只是遲到了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make a fuss — he's just late.

mandarin_meaning: 到場站台／到場助陣（為人助威或作公開支持）
english_meaning: to appear on stage or at an event to show support; to make a public appearance as a guest/supporter (esp. in entertainment or politics)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「踩上舞台」，口語上多指到別人的活動或演出現場出席以示支持或幫忙助陣；在娛樂圈或政治場合常見。
explanation_english: Literally 'step on the stage.' Colloquially it means to attend someone else's event or appearance to show support or lend backing; commonly used in entertainment and political contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次開騷，佢請咗好多圈中好友嚟踩臺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 hoi1 sou1, keoi5 ceng2 zo2 hou2 do1 hyun1 zung1 hou2 jau5 lai4 caai2 toi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次開演唱會，他請了很多圈內朋友來站台助陣。
examples.english_sentence: For this concert, he invited many industry friends to come and show their support.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政黨領袖嚟踩臺幫候選人拉票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 dong2 ling5 zau2 lai4 caai2 toi4 bong1 hau6 syun2 jan4 laai1 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政黨領袖來站台幫候選人拉票。
examples.english_sentence: A party leader came to lend support and help the candidate campaign.

mandarin_meaning: 在最后时刻把事情搞砸/毁掉
english_meaning: to ruin or spoil something at the last moment / to mess things up at the end
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容在事情快結束或關鍵時刻做了不當或冒失的行為，導致把整件事的結果弄砸或破壞了最後的氣氛。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing doing something inappropriate or clumsy at the final/critical moment that ruins the outcome or spoils the atmosphere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最後嗰句真係唔好，踩親條尾噉，搞到成場尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 hau6 go2 geoi3 zan1 hai6 m4 hou2, caai2 can1 tiu4 mei5 gam2, gaau2 dou3 seng4 coeng4 gon1 gaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最後說的那句真的不該說，這樣在最後把事情搞砸了，弄得全場尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: His last remark was really inappropriate — he ruined it at the end and made everyone feel awkward.

mandarin_meaning: （書面/罕用）踩、踱步、徘徊
english_meaning: archaic/rare verb meaning to step on, trample, or pace/pace back and forth
explanation_mandarin: 「蹅」為罕用或書面字，常見用法有表示用腳踩、踏或來回踱步、徘徊。現代口語中較少使用，部分方言或文言文中可見。
explanation_english: 蹅 is a rare/literary character used to mean to step on or trample, and in some contexts to pace or wander back and forth. It is uncommon in modern colloquial speech and mainly found in older or dialectal usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺街度蹅嚟蹅去，似乎諗緊嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 dou6 caat3 lei4 caat3 heoi3, ci5 fu4 lam2 gan2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天在街上蹅来蹅去，似乎在想事情。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps pacing up and down the street, as if he's thinking about something.

mandarin_meaning: 踩錯腳；犯錯、失足（常寫作「踩錯腳」）
english_meaning: to make a misstep; to blunder or put one's foot in it (often written as '踩錯腳')
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，指在行為或言語上犯錯、失當或踩到別人的地雷，導致尷尬或不利的結果。此詞常以『踩錯腳』的寫法出現。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to make a misstep — to commit a mistake in actions or words that causes embarrassment or trouble. Commonly written as '踩錯腳'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今次真係蹅錯腳，講嗰句令佢好尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 ci3 zan1 hai6 caai2 co3 goek3, gong2 go2 geoi3 ling6 keoi5 hou2 gaam1 go3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這次真是踩錯腳了，說那句話讓他很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: You really put your foot in it this time — that remark made him very embarrassed.

mandarin_meaning: 踩错脚；失足、出错；（也可比喻说话或做事失当）
english_meaning: to put one's foot wrong; to make a misstep or blunder; (figuratively) to put one's foot in one's mouth or offend someone
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，原指走路時踏錯步或失足，引申為在言行上犯錯、失禮或得罪別人。常見於廣東話口語中，有時寫作「踩錯腳」或「踏錯腳」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression originally meaning to take a wrong step or stumble; figuratively it means to make a mistake in words or actions or to offend someone. Often used interchangeably with 踩錯腳 or 踏錯腳.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我一路行落去，唔小心蹅錯腳跌咗一跤。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 lou6 haang4 lok6 heoi3 , m4 siu2 sam1 caai2 co3 goek3 dit3 zo2 jat1 goek3 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我一路走下去，不小心踏错脚摔了一跤。
examples.english_sentence: I was walking downhill and accidentally misstepped and fell.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講嘢要小心，唔好喺呢個時候蹅錯腳，會得罪人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 je5 jiu3 siu2 sam1 , m4 hou2 hai6 ni1 go3 si4 hau6 caai2 co3 goek3 , wui5 dak1 zeoi6 jan4 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 说话要小心，不要在这个时候踩错脚，会得罪人。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful what you say; don't put your foot in it now, you'll offend someone.

mandarin_meaning: 奇怪／古怪
english_meaning: strange; odd; peculiar
explanation_mandarin: 口語或方言用語，表示某人或某事有點怪異、不尋常。屬於非正式用法，常見於廣東地區的口語。若為罕見或拼寫變體，亦可能為「奇怪」的變體說法。
explanation_english: An informal Cantonese expression meaning someone or something is a bit odd or peculiar. It is nonstandard/slang and mainly used in spoken contexts in Cantonese-speaking areas; it can be treated as a colloquial variant of 'strange'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個人真係有啲蹺奇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 zan1 hai6 jau5 di1 kiu4 kei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這個人真的有點奇怪。
examples.english_sentence: He's really a bit strange.

mandarin_meaning: 急躁、容易發脾氣或焦躁不安的狀態
english_meaning: a state of irritability or restlessness; short-temperedness
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，主要在香港粵語中使用，形容一個人情緒急躁、容易發火或坐立不安的狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression (common in Hong Kong) describing someone who is irritable, short-tempered, or restless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁躁火，慢慢嚟啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 zou6 fo2, maan6 maan6 lai4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那麼急躁，慢慢來吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so irritable; take it slow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試壓力大，搞到我有啲躁火。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 aat3 lik6 daai6, gaau2 dou3 ngo5 jau5 di1 zou6 fo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試壓力很大，弄得我有點急躁。
examples.english_sentence: The pressure from exams is high, making me a bit irritable.

mandarin_meaning: （1）躉售、批發；（2）（與囤通用時）囤積、儲存
english_meaning: (1) to sell in bulk / wholesale; (2) to stockpile / hoard (depending on context)
explanation_mandarin: 「躉」在廣東話常見於詞語「躉售」，表示以一次大量出售、批發的方式；字形或在口語中與「囤」相近時，亦可表示囤積、儲存的意思，具體含義視語境而定。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 躉 commonly appears in 躉售 (dwan2 sau6) meaning to sell in bulk or wholesale. Depending on the character form and context (囤), it can also convey the idea of stockpiling or hoarding. The exact sense depends on usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲貨係躉售，買得越多，價錢越平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 fo3 hai6 dwan2 sau6, maai5 dak1 jyut6 do1, gaa3 cin2 jyut6 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些貨是躉售，買得越多，價錢越便宜。
examples.english_sentence: These goods are sold wholesale—the more you buy, the cheaper the price.

mandarin_meaning: （古）蹣跚、跛行、踉蹌
english_meaning: (archaic) to stumble, to limp, to walk unsteadily
explanation_mandarin: 躗是一個較罕見或古字，常用來形容行走不穩、蹣跚或跛行的狀態。現代漢語中此字少見，多以「蹣跚」「絆倒」等詞替代。
explanation_english: 躗 is a rare/archaic character used to describe unsteady walking—stumbling, limping, or staggering. It is seldom used in modern Chinese; contemporary synonyms include 'stumble' or 'limp'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢行路時突然躗咗一下，走唔穩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hang4 lou6 si4 dat6 jin4 wai1 zo2 jat1 haa6, zau2 m4 wan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走路時突然蹣跚了一下，走不穩。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly stumbled while walking and couldn't keep his balance.

mandarin_meaning: 快滚开；快走（粗俗俚语，用來叫人離開）
english_meaning: Scram; beat it; get lost (rude slang used to tell someone to go away)
explanation_mandarin: 「躝尸趷路」是香港粵語粗俗口語，通常用來粗魯地命令或催促對方離開、滾開。語氣強烈，帶有不禮貌或不耐煩的情緒。
explanation_english: A coarse Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase used to rudely tell someone to leave or get lost. It carries a strong, impolite, and impatient tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你無嘢做，唔好嚟打擾我，躝尸趷路啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 mou4 je5 zou6, m4 hou2 lai4 daa2 jiu2 ngo5, laan6 si1 hot3 lou6 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你沒事就不要來打擾我，快滾開！
examples.english_sentence: If you have nothing to do, don't bother me — get lost!

mandarin_meaning: 打扮整潔漂亮；外表光鮮亮麗
english_meaning: well-groomed; neatly and smartly dressed; looking clean and attractive
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，形容一個人穿戴整潔、打扮漂亮，外表看起來光鮮亮麗或很有精神。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is neatly dressed and well-groomed—appearing smart, clean, and attractive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日著得身光頸靚，好似去拍廣告咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 zoek3 dak1 san1 gwong1 geng2 leng3, hou2 ci5 heoi3 paak3 gwong2 gou3 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天打扮得很整潔漂亮，好像要拍廣告一樣。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is dressed so neatly and stylishly today, like they're going to film a commercial.

mandarin_meaning: 身体娇弱、被精心呵护或过于娇贵
english_meaning: physically delicate and pampered; treated as precious and not used to hard work
explanation_mandarin: 形容人身體嬌弱、受人細心照顧或生活嬌貴、不耐受粗重勞動。
explanation_english: Describes a person who is physically fragile or pampered, often treated as precious and not accustomed to hard or rough work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢身娇肉贵，连搬張椅都要人帮手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 san1 giu1 juk6 gwai3, lin4 baan1 zoeng1 ji2 dou1 jiu3 jan4 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她身体娇贵，连搬张椅子都要别人帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: She is delicate and pampered; she even needs someone to help move a chair.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）形容非常消瘦，瘦得像剝了皮的蘿蔔。
english_meaning: Colloquial slang meaning extremely thin; skin-and-bones (literally 'like the peel of a radish').
explanation_mandarin: 此詞為廣東話口語俚語，常用於香港地區，描述一個人瘦得很厲害、消瘦如柴。語氣偏口語、略帶貶義或打趣成分，並非書面常用詞。
explanation_english: This is a Cantonese colloquial/slang expression, commonly used in Hong Kong, to describe someone who is extremely thin. The tone is informal and can be teasing or derogatory; it is not a standard written term.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢病咗成個月，家陣瘦到身尸萝卜皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 beng6 zo2 seng4 go3 jyut6, gaa1 zan6 sou3 dou3 san1 si1 lo4 baak6 pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他病了整整一個月，現在瘦得像剝了皮的蘿蔔一樣。
examples.english_sentence: He was sick for a whole month; now he's so thin he's like a peeled radish.

mandarin_meaning: 聲音逼真、有臨場感（讓人有身臨其境的感覺）
english_meaning: immersive, lifelike sound; sound that makes one feel as if they are present
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，常用來形容錄音、音響或現場聲效非常逼真、有臨場感，使聽者彷彿置身現場。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression used to describe recordings, sound systems, or live audio that are highly realistic and immersive, making the listener feel as if they are actually there.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢隻耳機嘅聲好身歷聲，聽歌好有臨場感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 ji5 gei1 ge3 sing1 hou2 san1 lik6 sing1, teng1 go1 hou2 jau5 lam4 coeng4 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这副耳机的声音很身临其境，听歌很有临场感。
examples.english_sentence: The sound from these headphones is very immersive; listening to music feels like being there.

mandarin_meaning: 偃：本义为卧倒、俯伏；引申为停止、平息（多用于文言或成语，如“偃旗息鼓”）
english_meaning: A literary/classical verb meaning to lie down or prostrate; by extension, to stop or cease (especially hostilities) — used in idioms like '偃旗息鼓' (to cease fighting).
explanation_mandarin: 偃（躽為通用異體）在古漢語中常作動詞，原指臥倒、俯伏；在引申義上常表示停止、平息，常見於文言或成語中，如“偃旗息鼓”表示停止戰事。
explanation_english: The character is a literary/classical verb (躽 as a variant of 偃). Its original meaning is to lie down or prostrate; figuratively it means to stop or calm something (especially warfare). Commonly appears in literary contexts and idioms such as '偃旗息鼓' (to cease fighting).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢段歷史記載咗諸侯最終偃旗息鼓，結束咗多年戰爭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dyun6 lik6 si2 gei3 zoi6 zo2 zyu1 hau4 zeoi3 zung1 jin2 kei4 sik1 gu2, git3 suk1 zo2 do1 nin4 zin3 zang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这段历史记载诸侯最终偃旗息鼓，结束了多年战争。
examples.english_sentence: This historical account records that the lords eventually ceased hostilities, ending years of warfare.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見字，無標準現代漢語常用意義或讀音；可能為古字或異體字
english_meaning: A rare/obsolete character with no standard modern Cantonese pronunciation or common meaning; possibly an archaic or variant form
explanation_mandarin: 「軃」為罕見漢字，現代漢語與廣東話中無公認的常用讀音或固定詞義。常見於古籍、字書或作為異體字記錄，平常書寫與口語中很少使用。
explanation_english: This character is extremely rare and has no widely accepted modern Cantonese pronunciation or fixed meaning. It appears mainly in classical texts or character compendia as an archaic/variant form and is seldom used in everyday writing or speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「軃」呢個字好罕見，平時好少見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 『軃』 ni1 go3 zi6 hou2 hon2 gin3，ping4 si4 hou2 siu2 gin3 dou6。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「軃」这个字很罕见，平时很少见到。
examples.english_sentence: '軃' is a very rare character and is seldom seen in everyday use.

mandarin_meaning: 吹牛；夸大其词；说大话（口语）
english_meaning: to brag; to boast; to talk big; to bluster (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，常用於香港，指誇誇其談、吹噓或說不切實際的大話。可作動詞（車大炮）或作名詞（佢係個車大炮）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial slang (common in Hong Kong) meaning to boast, bluster, or talk big—often describing exaggerated or empty talk. It can be used as a verb or a noun.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日車大炮，講到好勁，其實做唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 seng4 jat6 ce1 daai6 paau3, gong2 dou3 hou2 ging6, kei4 sat6 zou6 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是吹牛，說得很厲害，其實做不到。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks big, saying he's great, but actually can't do it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好同佢計較，佢淨係識車大炮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: M4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 gai3 gaau3, keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 ce1 daai6 paau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要跟他計較，他只會吹牛。
examples.english_sentence: Don't argue with him; he only knows how to brag.

mandarin_meaning: 车道/马路
english_meaning: road; roadway; street (for vehicles)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語用詞，指車輛行駛的道路或路段。相當於普通話的「車道」或「馬路」，在香港口語中常用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term referring to a road or stretch of road used by vehicles. Equivalent to Mandarin '車道' or '馬路' and commonly used in Hong Kong spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條車路好窄，唔啱大車行。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 ce1 lou6 hou2 zaak3, m4 ngam1 daai6 ce1 haang4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条车路很窄，不适合大车通行。
examples.english_sentence: This road is very narrow; not suitable for large vehicles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚開車要小心，呢段車路有好多彎位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 hoi1 ce1 jiu3 siu2 sam1, ni1 dyun6 ce1 lou6 jau5 hou2 do1 waan1 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上开车要小心，这段车路有很多弯道。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful when driving at night; this stretch of road has many bends.

mandarin_meaning: （車輛）掉頭／調頭
english_meaning: to make a U-turn; to turn a vehicle around
explanation_mandarin: 指車輛在行駛途中改變行進方向，通常指掉頭或轉彎回頭的動作。
explanation_english: Refers to a vehicle changing its travelling direction, typically making a U-turn or turning around.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰架的士喺路口車轉，差啲撞到行人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaa3 dik1 si6 hai6 lou6 hau2 ce1 zyun2, caa1 di1 zong6 dou3 hang4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那輛的士在路口掉頭，差點撞到行人。
examples.english_sentence: That taxi made a U-turn at the junction and almost hit a pedestrian.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可以喺下一個路口車轉，跟住直行。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 ji5 hai6 haa6 jat1 go3 lou6 hau2 ce1 zyun2, gan1 zyu6 zik6 hang4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以在下一個路口掉頭，然後直行。
examples.english_sentence: You can make a U-turn at the next junction, then go straight.

mandarin_meaning: 樱桃（车厘子）
english_meaning: cherry (the fruit)
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話對英語“cherry”的音譯，指櫻桃（水果）。常見寫法有車厘子/車釐子，多指進口櫻桃，價格較高。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese transliteration of the English word 'cherry', referring to the fruit (Prunus avium / cherries). Often used for imported cherries and can imply they are relatively expensive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家市面嘅車釐子好貴，一盒要幾百蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 si5 min6 ge3 ce1 lei4 zi2 hou2 gwai3, jat1 hap6 jiu3 gei2 baak3 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在市场上的车厘子很贵，一盒要好几百块。
examples.english_sentence: Cherries are expensive in the market right now; a box costs several hundred dollars.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友好鍾意食車釐子，食一兩粒就好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 ce1 lei4 zi2, sik6 jat1 loeng5 liu2 zau6 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子很喜欢吃车厘子，吃一两颗就很开心。
examples.english_sentence: Kids love cherries; eating just one or two makes them very happy.

mandarin_meaning: 军人；当过兵的人；有时亦指穿军装或行为像军人的人（口语、俚语）
english_meaning: military person; ex-serviceman; someone who behaves or looks like a soldier (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「軍佬」是廣東話口語，通常指軍人或曾服兵役的人，也可泛指穿軍裝或舉止像軍人的人。根據語境可中性、戲稱或帶輕微貶義。
explanation_english: “軍佬” is a Cantonese colloquial term typically referring to a military person or someone who has served in the armed forces. It can also mean someone in uniform or who behaves like a soldier. Depending on context it can be neutral, jocular, or mildly derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢以前係軍佬，依家做保安。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5cin4 hai6 gwan1 lou2, ji1gaa1 zou6 bou2on1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他以前是军人，现在做保安。
