mandarin_meaning: 罕見詞彙或可能為書寫錯誤/方言變體，標準普通話中沒有固定對應。若在口語中出現，可能作為強調或形容某種程度的語氣詞或形容詞，具體意義需依語境確認。
english_meaning: An extremely rare or obscure term (possibly a misspelling or a dialectal variant). Not attested in standard references. If used colloquially, it may function as an emphatic particle or adjective to convey an intense or heightened state; exact meaning depends on context and needs confirmation.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 罕見/不詳（可能為形容詞或語氣詞）
explanation_mandarin: 「重屭屭」在常用字典與語料中極少見，可能是某地區口語、俚語或書寫失誤。遇到該詞，應向說話者或當地使用者求證，以了解具體語義與語用。此條目提供為釐清性說明，而非確定詞條。
explanation_english: The term '重屭屭' is extremely rare or possibly a misspelling; it is not recorded in standard dictionaries. It may be a local colloquialism whose function is emphatic or descriptive. Confirm the meaning with a native speaker in the specific context. This entry documents uncertainty rather than a definitive lexical analysis.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽到有人講「重屭屭」，但我唔知佢係咩意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 teng1 dou3 jau5 jan4 gong2 '重屭屭', daan6 ngo5 m4 zi1 keoi5 hai6 me1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我听到有人说“重屭屭”，但我不知道它是什么意思。
examples.english_sentence: I heard someone say '重屭屭', but I don't know what it means.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）顆粒感很重；有許多顆粒或渣，質地粗糙／不順滑
english_meaning: grainy; lumpy; full of bits — describes a texture that is coarse or has many particles
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容食物、飲品或化妝品等具有明顯顆粒感或渣，質地厚重或不順滑；屬口語用法。
explanation_english: Used to describe foods, drinks, cosmetics, etc. that have a pronounced grainy or pulpy texture — coarse, chunky, or not smooth. Colloquial usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碗湯好重粒粒，飲落口感唔太順滑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wun2 tong1 hou2 zung6 lap1 lap1, jam2 lok6 hau2 gam2 m4 taai3 seon6 waat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這碗湯顆粒很多，入口口感不太順滑。
examples.english_sentence: This bowl of soup is very grainy; the mouthfeel isn't very smooth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔鍾意呢款果汁，好重粒粒，有好多果渣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 ni1 kwan2 gwo2 zap1, hou2 zung6 lap1 lap1, jau5 hou2 do1 gwo2 zaa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不喜歡這款果汁，很顆粒，有很多果渣。
examples.english_sentence: I don't like this juice — it's very pulpy and has lots of fruit bits.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢支粉底上妝之後好重粒粒，唔貼面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 fan2 dai2 soeng5 zong1 zi1 hau6 hou2 zung6 lap1 lap1, m4 tip3 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這款粉底上妝後顆粒感很重，不服帖。
examples.english_sentence: This foundation looks grainy after application and doesn't sit smoothly on the skin.

mandarin_meaning: 垂頭喪氣／無精打采
english_meaning: downcast; droopy; listless; dejected
explanation_mandarin: 口語詞，形容人精神萎靡、垂頭或沒有幹勁，顯得很沮喪或沒精神。
explanation_english: Colloquial term describing someone who looks droopy or listless—downcast, lacking energy or spirit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試失敗後，佢成個人重耷耷，好似冇晒心機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 sat1 baai6 hau6, keoi5 sing4 go3 jan4 zung6 dap6 dap6, hou2 ci5 mou5 saai3 sam1 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考试失败后，他整个人垂头丧气，好像没有了干劲。
examples.english_sentence: After failing the exam, he was completely downcast, as if he had no energy left.

mandarin_meaning: 體重增加；變得較壯實（口語）
english_meaning: to gain weight; to become heavier or more solid in build (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「重身」是香港廣東話中的口語用法，常用來形容一個人變得較為壯實或體重增加。此詞較口語化，使用頻率不如「肥」或「發福」普遍，視語境可作動詞或形容詞使用。
explanation_english: “重身” is a colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese expression typically used to describe someone who has become heavier or more solid in build (i.e., gained weight). It is informal and less common than words like “fat” or “put on weight,” and can function as a verb or adjective depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近佢好似重身咗，冇以前咁瘦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 keoi5 hou2 ci5 zung6 san1 zo2, mou5 ji5 cin4 gam2 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近他好像胖了，不像以前那麼瘦。
examples.english_sentence: Lately he seems to have gained weight; he's not as slim as before.

cantonese: 重阳有雷声，瓜菜唔得平
jyutping: cung4 joeng4 jau5 leoi4 sing1, gwaa1 coi3 m4 dak1 ping4
mandarin_meaning: 重阳节若有雷声，瓜果蔬菜不会便宜（民间以天象预示农产品供需和价格变化）
english_meaning: If there's thunder on the Double Ninth (Chongyang) Festival, melons and vegetables won't be cheap (folk weather lore predicting produce shortages or higher prices).
explanation_mandarin: 这是一句粤语民间谚语，通过观察重阳（农历九月九日）当天出现的雷声来预测后期瓜果蔬菜的供需和价格变化，表示可能会出现短缺或价格上涨。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk proverb that uses the occurrence of thunder on the Double Ninth festival as a weather omen to predict later shortages or rising prices of melons and vegetables; i.e., a sign of likely higher produce prices.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽話：「重阳有雷声，瓜菜唔得平」，你睇吓市場啲菜價已經開始升晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 waa6: "cung4 joeng4 jau5 leoi4 sing1, gwaa1 coi3 m4 dak1 ping4", nei5 tai2 haa5 si5 coeng4 di1 coi3 gaa3 ji5 ging1 hoi1 ci2 sing1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈说：“重阳如果有雷声，瓜菜就不会便宜。”你看市场上的菜价已经开始上涨了。
examples.english_sentence: Mom said, "If there's thunder on Chongyang, melons and vegetables won't be cheap." Look, vegetable prices at the market have already started rising.

cantonese: 重阳水浸基，饿死冇人知
jyutping: cung4 joeng4 seoi2 zam3 gei1, ngo6 sei2 mou5 jan4 zi1
mandarin_meaning: 形容極度貧困、受苦卻無人知曉或無人關心
english_meaning: A proverb describing extreme poverty or suffering that goes unnoticed and uncared for
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗語。字面提到重陽節與「水浸基（墓地被水淹）」的景象，用來比喻處境孤苦無助、貧困或受苦卻沒有人知道或理會。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb. Literally referring to the Double Ninth Festival and flooded graves, it metaphorically describes being in extreme poverty or suffering and being completely neglected or unnoticed by others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢屋企窮到冇人理，真係重阳水浸基，饿死冇人知。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 uk1 kei2 kung4 dou3 mou5 jan4 lei5, zan1 hai6 cung4 joeng4 seoi2 zam3 gei1, ngo6 sei2 mou5 jan4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他家窮到沒人理會，真是「重陽水浸基，餓死沒人知」。
examples.english_sentence: His family is so poor and neglected — it's like 'on Double Ninth the graves are flooded; if someone starves to death no one would know.'

mandarin_meaning: 野芋（野生的芋類，塊莖可食）
english_meaning: wild taro (a wild species of taro; edible tuber)
explanation_mandarin: 野芋是指野生的芋類植物，其塊莖可食，但通常需要充分烹煮以去除刺激性的草酸晶體或其他有害物質。
explanation_english: Wild taro refers to wild species of taro whose tubers are edible; they usually require thorough cooking to remove irritating calcium oxalate crystals and make them safe to eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢度有啲野芋，可以煮嚟食，但記住要煮熟先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 jau5 di1 je5 wu6, ho2 ji5 zyu2 lai4 sik6, daan6 gei3 zyu6 jiu3 zyu2 suk6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這裡有一些野芋，可以煮來吃，但記得要煮熟。
examples.english_sentence: There are some wild taro here; you can cook and eat them, but remember to cook them thoroughly.

mandarin_meaning: 野姜花（Alpinia zerumbet），俗稱貝殼薑或海芋薑，為一種有香味的薑科植物，花朵常呈白色或帶粉紅，有時用於泡茶或作為香料、觀賞植物。
english_meaning: Wild ginger flower (Alpinia zerumbet), also called shell ginger; a fragrant ginger-family plant with white/pink flowers, used ornamentally, in teas, or as a flavoring.
explanation_mandarin: 野薑花是薑科的一種植物，花朵有清香，常見於亞熱帶地區。花葉可做觀賞或入藥、入茶和調味。
explanation_english: A species in the ginger family with fragrant flowers and leaves. Common in subtropical areas; used ornamentally, in teas, traditional remedies, and sometimes as a flavoring.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隔離屋企種咗好多野薑花，夏天聞落好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaak3 lei4 uk1 kei5 zung6 zo2 hou2 do1 je5 goeng1 faa1, haa6 tin1 man4 lok6 hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 隔壁家种了很多野姜花，夏天闻起来很香。
examples.english_sentence: The neighbors planted many wild ginger flowers; they smell very fragrant in summer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽用野薑花泡咗杯茶，味道好清香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 jung6 je5 goeng1 faa1 paau4 zo2 bui1 caa4, mei6 dou6 hou2 cing1 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈用野姜花泡了杯茶，味道很清香。
examples.english_sentence: Mom brewed a cup of tea with wild ginger flowers; it tastes very fragrant.

mandarin_meaning: 野餐 / 在户外吃东西
english_meaning: to eat outdoors; picnic; outdoor meal
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指在戶外（如海邊、郊外、屋頂等）吃東西或野餐，通常較隨意、非正式。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to eat outdoors or have a picnic (e.g., at the beach, countryside, or rooftop); an informal, casual outdoor meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋星期日去大浪灣野食，好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sing1 kei4 jat6 heoi3 daai6 long6 waan1 je5 sik6, hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们星期日去大浪湾野餐，好吗？
examples.english_sentence: Shall we go have a picnic at Tai Long Wan on Sunday?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成班朋友成日去屋頂野食，邊度都可以。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 seng4 baan1 pang4 jau5 sing4 jat6 heoi3 nguk1 deng2 je5 sik6, bin1 dou6 dou1 ho2 ji5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们一群朋友经常去屋顶吃东西，哪里都可以。
examples.english_sentence: They and their friends often eat on the rooftop; anywhere works.

mandarin_meaning: 非常罕見或非標準詞彙，可能為錯別字或音譯
english_meaning: Not a standard Cantonese term; possibly a typo, rare/local usage, or a transliteration
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 非標準／未知（疑似音譯或錯寫，詞性不明）
partOfSpeech_english: non-standard term (part of speech unknown; possibly transliteration or typo)
explanation_mandarin: 「釐士」在常見粵語辭典與語料中罕見，沒有固定或廣泛接受的意義。常見可能性包括：打字錯誤、地方用語、或從外語音譯而來。若有具體上下文，才可進一步釐清含義。
explanation_english: The term "釐士" is rare in standard Cantonese references and has no widely accepted meaning. Likely explanations include a typo, local/rare usage, or a loanword/transliteration from another language. Additional context is needed to determine a precise meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「釐士」唔係一個常用詞，可能係打錯或者音譯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 「lei4 si6」 m4 hai6 jat1 go3 soeng4 jung6 ci4, ho2 nang4 hai6 daa2 co3 waak6 ze2 jam1 jik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「釐士」不是常用词，可能是打错或音译。
examples.english_sentence: "釐士" is not a commonly used word; it may be a typo or a transliteration.

mandarin_meaning: 為微不足道的小錢或小事斤斤計較
english_meaning: to quibble over trivial amounts or petty matters (literally fuss over minute sums)
explanation_mandarin: 口語、廣東話俗語，指為很小的錢或瑣碎的事情過分計較或爭執，帶有貶義。常用於日常對話中批評愛計較的人或行為。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to haggle over or make an issue of very small amounts of money or trivial matters. It carries a mildly negative sense of being petty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好為嗰幾蚊釐戥咁嘈啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 wai6 go2 gei2 man1 lei4 dang1 gam3 cou3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別為那幾塊小錢吵來吵去了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't argue over those few dollars.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日為啲小事釐戥，同人講唔停。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 wai6 di1 siu2 si6 lei4 dang1, tung4 jan4 gong2 m4 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常為小事斤斤計較，跟人說個不停。
examples.english_sentence: He always quibbles over trivial matters and keeps complaining to people.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見或古文字形，無在現代粵語中廣泛記錄的固定詞義
english_meaning: Rare/obscure written form with no widely attested meaning or pronunciation in modern Cantonese
explanation_mandarin: 「金䍇」所用的字形（尤其是第二字「䍇」）屬於罕見或古字，沒有在現代粵語詞典或語料中找到一致、常見的讀音或固定詞義。遇到此寫法時，通常需查考古籍或原文語境，或以常用字（例如「金龜」）替代。此條目旨在說明其罕見性，而非給出確定釋義。
explanation_english: The form "金䍇" uses a rare/archaic character (particularly the second character "䍇") and does not have an established pronunciation or fixed meaning in modern Cantonese reference sources. When encountered, one should consult historical sources or the original context, or consider substituting a common form (for example "金龜"). This entry documents its rarity rather than providing a definitive sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「金䍇」呢個寫法好罕見，好多時候唔會用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 「金䍇」ni1 go3 se2faat3 hou2 hon2gin3, hou2 do1 si4hou6 m4 wui5 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「金䍇」這個寫法很罕見，很多時候不會使用。
examples.english_sentence: The writing "金䍇" is very rare and often not used.

mandarin_meaning: 金山芋（芋頭的一種俗稱）
english_meaning: Jinshan taro (a colloquial name for a type of taro/yam)
explanation_mandarin: 「金山芋」是對某些品種的芋頭或俗稱，通常指質地細膩、偏甜、適合用來煮糖水、甜品或入菜的芋頭品種。在廣東話語境中常用來稱呼這類芋頭。
explanation_english: "金山芋" is a colloquial/local name for certain varieties of taro (yams), typically those with a fine texture and slightly sweet taste, often used in sweet soups, desserts, or cooking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚煲咗金山芋糖水，好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 bou1 zo2 gam1 saan1 wu6 tong4 seoi2, hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚煮了金山芋糖水，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: We made Jinshan taro sweet soup tonight — it's delicious.

mandarin_meaning: 金带蛇（指有金色或黄色带纹的蛇，常用于描述华南及东南亚分布的某些带状蛇类）
english_meaning: golden-banded snake (a snake with golden or yellow bands; a common name for certain banded snakes)
explanation_mandarin: 指具有金色或黄色带状体纹的蛇类的通称，通常用于描述分布于华南、东南亚等地的带纹蛇。主要是动物学或日常称呼，非广泛的习语。
explanation_english: A common name for snakes that have golden or yellow banded markings. Typically used to describe certain banded snake species found in South China and Southeast Asia. Primarily a zoological or descriptive term rather than a widely used idiom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日喺公園見到一條金帶蛇，嚇死我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 hai2 gung1 jyun4 gin3 dou3 jat1 tiu4 gam1 daai3 se4, haak3 sei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天在公园看到一条金带蛇，吓死我了。
examples.english_sentence: I saw a golden-banded snake in the park today — it scared me to death.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 山裏成日有金帶蛇出沒，行山要著長褲同留意腳下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: saan1 leoi5 sing4 jat6 jau5 gam1 daai3 se4 ceot1 mut6, haang4 saan1 jiu3 zoek3 coeng4 fu3 tung4 lau4 ji3 goek3 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 山里经常有金带蛇出没，爬山要穿长裤并注意脚下。
examples.english_sentence: There are often golden-banded snakes in the hills; when hiking, wear long pants and watch your step.

mandarin_meaning: 金桔（小型柑橘類水果）
english_meaning: kumquat (a small citrus fruit)
explanation_mandarin: 金橘是一種小型的柑橘類水果，果皮薄且可食，常用來直接食用、做蜜餞或泡茶。外形多為橢圓或圓形，味道酸甜兼具。
explanation_english: Kumquat is a small citrus fruit with an edible thin rind. It is often eaten whole, candied, or used in teas. The fruit is typically oval or round and has a sweet-tart flavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗啲金橘，打算整金橘蜜餞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 di1 gam1 gat1, daa2 syun3 zing2 gam1 gat1 mat6 zin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我买了些金桔，打算做成金桔蜜饯。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some kumquats and plan to make candied kumquats.

mandarin_meaning: 金瓜（指一種皮色偏金黃的南瓜/瓜類，有時指日式南瓜 kabocha）
english_meaning: kabocha / pumpkin (a type of squash, literally 'golden gourd')
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，金瓜通常指一種可食用的瓜類，皮色偏金黃，常用來煲湯或做甜品。有時也用來指日式南瓜（kabocha）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 金瓜 refers to a type of edible squash/pumpkin with a golden-hued skin. It is commonly used in soups and desserts and can also refer to kabocha (Japanese pumpkin).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽整咗碗金瓜湯俾我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 zing2 zo2 wun2 gam1 gwaa1 tong1 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽給我煲了一碗金瓜湯。
examples.english_sentence: My mom made me a bowl of pumpkin (kabocha) soup.

mandarin_meaning: 金条；金砖（字面意思）；引申为非常值钱或能带来高额收益的事物；在政治语境中也可作为“金砖国家”（BRICS）的简称
english_meaning: gold bar (literal); figuratively a very valuable asset or money-making opportunity; can also abbreviate BRICS in political contexts
explanation_mandarin: “金磚”本义指以砖块形状铸成的黄金条块（即金条、金块）。延伸义可用来形容某事物非常有价值或能带来大量收益（如“是个金磚生意”）。在讨论国际事务时，有时也用作“金砖国家”（BRICS）的简称。
explanation_english: Literally a gold bar (a bar of gold). Figuratively used to describe something extremely valuable or highly profitable (e.g., "a goldmine of a deal"). In political contexts it can also be shorthand for the BRICS countries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗幾塊金磚做投資。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 gei2 faai3 gam1 zyun1 zou6 tau4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他买了几块金条作为投资。
examples.english_sentence: He bought several gold bars as an investment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意係金磚，賺好多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 sang1 ji3 hai6 gam1 zyun1, zaan6 hou2 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这笔生意是个金矿，赚了很多钱。
examples.english_sentence: This deal is a goldmine; it makes a lot of money.

mandarin_meaning: 金竹（指具金黃色莖幹的竹子，常見的觀賞植物）
english_meaning: golden bamboo (a bamboo species or cultivar with yellow/golden culms; an ornamental plant)
explanation_mandarin: 指莖幹呈金黃色或淡黃色的竹類品種（如某些觀賞竹），常用於園藝佈置或作為景觀植物，有時也象徵吉祥、繁榮。
explanation_english: Refers to bamboo varieties with yellow or golden culms (stems), often used as ornamental plants in gardens and landscapes; sometimes symbolizes good fortune and prosperity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺屋企後院種咗幾棵金竹，成個庭院睇落好有生氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 uk1 kei5 hau6 jyun2 zung6 zo2 gei2 fo2 gam1 zuk1, sing4 go3 ting4 jyun2 tai2 lok6 hou2 jau5 sang1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在家後院種了幾棵金竹，整個庭院看起來很有生氣。
examples.english_sentence: He planted several golden bamboo in his backyard; the whole garden looks very lively.

mandarin_meaning: 金丝划（字面）：金色的细线、划痕；引申为细长的金色装饰或细痕（该词在粤语中较少见，可能为方言、口语或笔误）
english_meaning: Golden streak/line (literal): a fine gold-colored thread-like line or scratch; can mean a delicate gold decorative line or hairline mark (this term is uncommon in Cantonese and may be dialectal or a misspelling)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（可作名詞短語，偶爾用作形容詞性描述）
explanation_mandarin: 由「金絲」＋「劃」組成，字面上指像金色絲線般的痕跡或線條。實際口語使用較罕見，常見於描述陶瓷、金屬或布料上的細金色裝飾線或細小划痕。有時可能是方言用法或筆誤。
explanation_english: Composed of "golden thread" (金絲) + "stroke/mark" (劃), literally referring to a thin gold-colored thread-like mark or line. The term is uncommon in everyday Cantonese; it would be used to describe delicate gold decoration lines or hairline scratches on ceramics, metal, or fabric. It may also be dialectal or a misspelling in some contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個碟上有條金絲劃，好似係裝飾嚟㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 dip6 soeng6 jau5 tiu4 gam1 si1 waak6, hou2 ci5 hai6 zong1 sik1 lai4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 盘子上有一条金丝划，好像是装饰。
examples.english_sentence: There is a golden streak on the plate; it looks like a decoration.

mandarin_meaning: 外表華麗但缺乏內涵（華而不實）
english_meaning: To adorn or dress ostentatiously; showy and superficially attractive but lacking real substance.
explanation_mandarin: 原指用金線裝飾芙蓉，現用來形容外表華美或裝飾得很漂亮，但實質內容空洞、虛浮不實。
explanation_english: Originally referring to decorating a hibiscus with gold thread, it is now used to describe something or someone that is lavishly or ostentatiously decorated — attractive in appearance but superficial and lacking real content.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日著到金線吊芙蓉，實際上冇乜內涵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zoek3 dou3 gam1 sin3 diu3 fu4 jung4, sat6 zai3 soeng6 mou5 mat1 noi6 ham4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她總是打扮得金線吊芙蓉，實際上沒什麼內涵。
examples.english_sentence: She always dresses in a flashy, over-embellished way — beautiful on the outside but actually lacking substance.

mandarin_meaning: 相當於「金蟬脫殼」或「全身而退」，指巧妙或暗中撤退以免牽連或避嫌。
english_meaning: To withdraw discreetly or make a graceful escape/retreat to avoid trouble or implication.
explanation_mandarin: 「金蟬退」常用於廣東話語境，形容某人為免牽連或維持體面，悄悄撤退或退出某事，帶有巧妙、保全自身的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese expression meaning to quietly withdraw or bow out of a situation to avoid being implicated or to save face, often implying a clever or discreet escape.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到事情會牽連太多人，於是決定金蟬退，唔再出聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 si6 cing4 wui5 hin1 lin4 taai3 do1 jan4, jyu1 si6 kyut3 ding6 gam1 sim4 teoi3, m4 zoi3 ceot1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到事情會牽連太多人，於是決定金蟬退，不再出聲。
examples.english_sentence: He saw the matter would implicate too many people, so he decided to withdraw quietly and stopped speaking up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗保護公司聲譽，經理選擇金蟬退，默默辭職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 bou2 wu6 gung1 si1 sing1 jyu6, ging1 lei5 syun2 zaak6 gam1 sim4 teoi3, mak6 mak6 ci4 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了保護公司聲譽，經理選擇金蟬退，默默辭職。
examples.english_sentence: To protect the company's reputation, the manager chose to bow out discreetly and quietly resign.

mandarin_meaning: 金腰带；（口语）指佩戴金饰、爱炫富的人或事物
english_meaning: literally 'golden-corner belt'; colloquially a flashy gold belt or, figuratively, someone or something that shows off wealth
explanation_mandarin: 「金角帶」字面上指金屬或金色的腰帶；在口語或俚語中可用來形容穿戴金飾、喜歡炫耀財富或打扮非常招搖的人／物。
explanation_english: Literally refers to a gold (ornamental) belt. Colloquially or slangily, it describes a flashy gold accessory or is used figuratively for a person/thing that ostentatiously shows off wealth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日戴住金角帶去派對，成日畀人話佢鐘意炫富。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 daai3 zyu6 gam1 gok3 daai3 heoi3 paai3 deoi6, sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 waa6 keoi5 zung1 ji3 syun6 fu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是戴着金角带去派对，总被人说他爱炫富。
examples.english_sentence: He always wears a 'golden-corner belt' to parties; people always say he likes to show off his wealth.

mandarin_meaning: 紙錢，燒給祖先或神明的金銀紙
english_meaning: joss paper; spirit money (paper offerings burned for ancestors or deities)
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱為燒給祖先或神明的紙錢，用於祭祀、祭祖或超渡，象徵供奉金銀財寶給陰間的親人或神靈。
explanation_english: Paper offerings (joss paper or spirit money) that are burned during rituals, funerals, or ancestor worship to symbolically provide wealth and offerings to deceased relatives or deities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 清明嗰陣，記得買啲金銀紙去燒畀祖先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cing1 ming4 go2 zan6, gei3 dak1 maai5 di1 gam1 ngan4 zi2 heoi3 siu1 bei2 zou2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 清明的時候，記得買一些金銀紙去燒給祖先。
examples.english_sentence: During Qingming, remember to buy some joss paper to burn for your ancestors.

mandarin_meaning: 金錢龜（可指一種小型淡水龜或某些地區的傳統糕點）
english_meaning: gold-coin turtle (can refer to a small freshwater turtle species or a traditional pastry shaped/named like a turtle)
explanation_mandarin: 「金錢龜」字面上是指帶有「金錢」花紋或外型的小型龜類；在一些華南地區和香港，「金錢龜」亦是傳統糕點的名稱，因外形或寓意與錢幣、吉利有關。
explanation_english: Literally 'gold-coin turtle.' It can denote a small freshwater turtle (named for coin-like markings or shell appearance). In some southern Chinese regions, including Hong Kong, it is also the name of a traditional pastry/snack shaped or named after a turtle, with auspicious associations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餅舖嘅金錢龜好受歡迎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 beng2 pou3 ge3 gam1 cin2 gwai1 hou2 sau6 fun1 jing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間餅店的金錢龜很受歡迎。
examples.english_sentence: The bakery's 'gold-coin turtles' are very popular.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢屋企養咗隻金錢龜，嗰隻好可愛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 uk1 kei2 joeng5 zo2 zek3 gam1 cin2 gwai1, go2 zek3 hou2 ho2 oi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他家裡養了一隻金錢龜，那隻很可愛。
examples.english_sentence: They keep a 'gold-coin turtle' at home; it's very cute.

mandarin_meaning: 金鲤（指金色的鲤鱼，常作观赏鱼或象征吉祥）
english_meaning: golden carp (a gold-colored carp, often an ornamental koi or symbol of good fortune)
explanation_mandarin: “金鯉”字面上指金色的鲤鱼，在园林池塘或观赏鱼中常见。金色鲤鱼在华人文化里常被视为吉祥、招财的象征，也常被用作店名或品牌名。
explanation_english: Literally 'golden carp.' Refers to a gold-colored carp (koi) commonly kept as an ornamental fish. In Chinese culture the golden carp is often associated with good luck and prosperity and may be used as a poetic name or business name.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺池塘入面有隻金鯉，好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 ci4 tong4 jap6 min6 jau5 zek3 gam1 lei5, hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 池塘里有一条金鲤，很漂亮。
examples.english_sentence: There is a golden carp in the pond; it's very beautiful.

mandarin_meaning: 金色的鯽魚；金鯽魚（魚名）
english_meaning: golden crucian carp (a crucian carp with golden coloration)
explanation_mandarin: 指一種體色偏金黃的鯽魚，常作食用魚或觀賞魚。有時也稱為金鯽魚。
explanation_english: Refers to a crucian carp that has a golden coloration. It can be used as a food fish or kept as an ornamental fish; also called golden crucian carp.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢去魚市場買咗條金鯽，打算燒嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 heoi3 jyu4 si5 coeng4 maai5 zo2 tiu4 gam1 zik6, daa2 syun3 siu1 lai4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他去魚市買了一條金鯽，打算燒來吃。
examples.english_sentence: He went to the fish market and bought a golden crucian carp, intending to roast and eat it.

mandarin_meaning: 弹珠台；弹球机（pinball）
english_meaning: pinball (arcade game / pinball machine)
explanation_mandarin: 「針球」在廣東話中常用來指彈珠台或彈球機，即投幣後用彈簧發射鋼珠，操控彈珠避開針狀障礙並得分的機動遊戲。有時也可口語化說去「打針球」指去玩彈珠機或pinball。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "針球" commonly refers to a pinball machine (pinball). It denotes the arcade game where steel balls are launched and bounced off pins and bumpers to score points. Colloquially, people may say "go play 針球" to mean going to play pinball.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細個成日去機鋪打針球。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 sing4 jat6 heoi3 gei1 pou3 daa2 zam1 kau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小时候经常去游戏厅打弹珠机。
examples.english_sentence: When I was a kid I often went to the arcade to play pinball.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部針球機幾好玩，彈到分好快。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 zam1 kau4 gei2 hou2 waan2, daan6 dou3 fan1 hou2 faai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这台弹珠机很好玩，分数上升得很快。
examples.english_sentence: This pinball machine is really fun — the scores climb quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 周末去商場玩針球啦，打多幾局。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau1 mut6 heoi3 soeng1 coeng4 waan2 zam1 kau4 laa1, daa2 do1 gei2 guk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 周末去商场玩弹珠机吧，再打几局。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the mall this weekend to play pinball, and play a few rounds.

mandarin_meaning: 针鱼（長嘴狀的細長魚類），常見於沿海，亦可食用
english_meaning: needlefish — a long, slender fish with an elongated beak, common in coastal waters and used as food
explanation_mandarin: 針魚指一類體型細長、嘴部伸長如針的魚，常見於沿海地區，常用作食材或釣獵目標。
explanation_english: Refers to a group of slender, long-bodied fish with needle-like beaks (needlefish). They are common in coastal waters and are often caught for food or sport fishing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 漁夫喺碼頭釣到幾條針魚，今晚可以煎嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 fu1 hai2 maa5 tau4 diu3 dou2 gei2 tiu4 zam1 jyu4, gam1 maan5 ho2 ji5 zin1 lai4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 渔夫在码头钓到几条针鱼，今晚可以煎来吃。
examples.english_sentence: The fisherman caught several needlefish at the pier; we can pan-fry them for dinner tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗啲新鮮針魚，肉質細嫩，好啱快炒或者煎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 di1 san1 sin1 zam1 jyu4, juk6 zat1 sai3 jan6, hou2 aam1 faai3 caau2 waak6 ze2 zin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我买了些新鲜的针鱼，肉质细嫩，很适合快炒或者煎。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some fresh needlefish; the flesh is tender and suits quick stir-frying or pan-frying.

mandarin_meaning: 花花公子／愛在酒吧等場合搭訕、追求異性的男子（貶義）
english_meaning: a womanizer / a man who cruises bars or social venues to pick up women (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 口語、偏貶義的稱呼，指常常在酒吧、夜店或社交場合主動搭訕、追求女性，帶有輕佻或玩弄感情的意味。
explanation_english: Colloquial, pejorative term for a man who frequently hangs around bars or social venues to hit on or pick up women, implying flirtatious or manipulative behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個釣魚公，經常喺酒吧追女仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 diu3 jyu4 gung1, ging1 soeng4 hai2 zau2 baa1 zeoi1 neoi5 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個釣魚公，經常在酒吧追女孩。
examples.english_sentence: He's a womanizer; he often chases girls at bars.

mandarin_meaning: 钓鱼人；渔夫（以钓鱼为业或嗜好的人）
english_meaning: angler; fisherman (someone who fishes as an occupation or hobby)
explanation_mandarin: 指以釣魚為生或以釣魚為嗜好的人。可用於口語或書面，語氣中性，帶有職業或愛好描述的意味。
explanation_english: Refers to a person who fishes, either as a profession or as a hobby. Can be used in casual or literary contexts; neutral in tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個釣魚郎成日喺海邊坐到日落先返屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 diu3 jyu4 long4 sing4 jat6 hai2 hoi2 bin1 co5 dou3 jat6 lok6 sin1 faan1 uk1 kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个钓鱼郎每天都在海边坐到日落才回家。
examples.english_sentence: The fisherman sits by the sea every day until sunset before going home.

mandarin_meaning: 斧；斧頭（古字或異體字）
english_meaning: axe; hatchet (archaic/variant character for 斧)
explanation_mandarin: 鈇為較少見或古體漢字，常作「斧」的異體，指用於砍伐或作為武器的金屬製工具。
explanation_english: A rare or archaic character used as a variant of 斧 (axe). Refers to a metal tool used for chopping or as a weapon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用一把鈇劈柴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 jat1 baa2 fu2 pik1 caai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他用一把斧头劈柴。
examples.english_sentence: He uses an axe to chop firewood.

mandarin_meaning: 可能為誤寫，正確或常見寫法為「瓣蕊」，指花瓣與花蕊（花的構造）
english_meaning: Likely a misspelling of 瓣蕊 (bànruǐ) — petals and the flower's reproductive parts (flower parts)
explanation_mandarin: 「鈑蕊」並非常見詞彙。根據字形推測，可能是誤用「鈑」字，常見且正確的寫法應為「瓣蕊」，為植物學或日常描述中指花瓣與花蕊（花的構造）。
explanation_english: “鈑蕊” is not a common or standard term. Based on the characters, it is likely a misspelling of 瓣蕊 (petals and the flower's reproductive parts). The correct form 瓣蕊 is used in botanical contexts to refer to parts of a flower.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字好少見，可能係寫錯，應該係「瓣蕊」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 hou2 siu2 gin3, ho2 nang4 hai6 se2 co3, jing1 goi1 hai6 "bun6 seoi2".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字很少见，可能是写错了，应该是「瓣蕊」。
examples.english_sentence: This character is rare and may be a misspelling; it should be "瓣蕊" (petals and the flower's reproductive parts).

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）形容笨重、複雜或經常出故障、無用的機器；亦可戲稱某人行為古怪或效率低下。
english_meaning: (slang) A pejorative term for a clunky, overly complicated, or frequently malfunctioning machine; also used jokingly about a person who behaves oddly or is inefficient.
explanation_mandarin: 鈒骨機是香港口語中的俚語，通常用來形容某個裝置又舊又常壞、運作怪異或完全無用；在日常對話中也可用來半開玩笑地形容某人做事笨拙或反應奇怪。
explanation_english: 鈒骨機 is a Hong Kong Cantonese slang term. It typically describes a device that is old, frequently breaks down, or behaves strangely — essentially a useless or troublesome machine. It can also be used jokingly to describe a person who is clumsy, inefficient, or acts oddly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部舊洗碗機已經壞晒，成日發出奇怪聲，好似鈒骨機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 gau6 sai2 wun2 gei1 ji5 ging1 waai6 saai3, sing4 jat6 faat3 ceot1 kei4 gwaai3 seng1, hou2 ci5 faan4 gwat1 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這台舊洗碗機已經壞得一塌糊塗，常常發出奇怪的聲音，好像鈒骨機。
examples.english_sentence: This old dishwasher is completely broken and often makes strange noises — like a 'faan4 gwat1 gei1'.

mandarin_meaning: 模仿小鈴、鑰匙等輕微金屬敲擊或搖動時發出的叮噹聲（擬聲詞）
english_meaning: An onomatopoeic word imitating the light jingling or tinkling sound of small bells, keys, or metal objects being struck or shaken
explanation_mandarin: 「鈴啷」常用作擬聲語，形容細小金屬物件（如手鐲、風鈴、鑰匙）輕微碰撞或搖晃時發出的叮叮噹噹聲，有時重複使用以增強語氣（如「鈴啷鈴啷」）。
explanation_english: Used as an onomatopoeic expression to describe the light jingling or tinkling noise made by small metal objects (e.g., bracelets, wind chimes, keys) when they strike or are shaken. It is often repeated (e.g., "鈴啷鈴啷") for emphasis.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢戴住個手鐲，行嘅時候就鈴啷鈴啷咁响。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daai3 zyu6 go3 sau2 zoek3, haang4 ge3 si4 hau6 zau6 ling4 long4 ling4 long4 gam2 hoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她戴著手鐲，走路的時候就叮噹叮噹地響。
examples.english_sentence: She wore a bracelet that jangled as she walked.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 門口掛住啲風鈴，微風一吹就鈴啷鈴啷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mun4 hau2 gwaa3 zyu6 di1 fung1 ling4, mei4 fung1 jat1 ceoi1 zau6 ling4 long4 ling4 long4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 門口掛著風鈴，微風一吹就叮噹叮噹。
examples.english_sentence: Wind chimes hung at the door jingled as the breeze blew.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）全部垮掉／全都完了
english_meaning: colloquial: everything has fallen apart / it's all gone to pieces
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語／口語片語（感嘆或描述）
explanation_mandarin: 「鈴鈴都掉埋」屬於廣東話口語俚語，用來誇張地形容事情完全失控、全部散掉或完蛋了。較口語化，有時帶幽默或諷刺意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to exaggerate that everything has collapsed, fallen apart, or is completely ruined. Informal and often used with humor or irony.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次個計劃搞到一鑊粥，真係鈴鈴都掉埋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 go3 gai3 waak6 gaau2 dou3 jat1 wok6 zuk1, zan1 hai6 ling4 ling4 dou1 diu6 maai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次计划弄得一团糟，真是全部都完了。
examples.english_sentence: This plan turned into a total mess — it's like everything's gone to pieces.

mandarin_meaning: （用鉋子）刨、鉋平（木材或金屬表面）；鉋子（工具名）
english_meaning: to plane/pare/plane smooth (a surface); a plane (carpenter's/tool)
explanation_mandarin: 指用鉋子將木材或其他材料的表面刨平，也可指用於刨平表面的工具（鉋子）。
explanation_english: Refers to using a plane to shave or smooth the surface of wood or other materials; can also mean the tool (a plane) used for that purpose.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 師傅用鉋將木板鉋平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 fu1 jung6 bou6 zoeng1 muk6 baan2 bou6 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 師傅用鉋子把木板鉋平。
examples.english_sentence: The craftsman used a plane to smooth the wooden board.

mandarin_meaning: 刨木头；用刨子把木材刨平、修整
english_meaning: to plane wood; to shave/trim wood with a plane (tool)
explanation_mandarin: 口語或書面用語，指用刨子（鉋）把木材表面刨平或修整，以便做家具或其他工藝用途。
explanation_english: Refers to using a plane (tool) to shave or trim wood, smoothing or shaping the surface for furniture or carpentry work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 師傅喺度鉋柴整櫃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 fu1 hai2 dou6 paau4 caai4 zing2 gwai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 师傅在刨木头做柜子。
examples.english_sentence: The carpenter is planing wood to make a cabinet.

mandarin_meaning: 小銅鑼、小鉦（敲擊發聲的金屬器）
english_meaning: a small gong or metal bell used as a percussion instrument; the sound produced by such an instrument
explanation_mandarin: 「鉎」字在粵語中常用來指小型的金屬敲擊樂器（如鉦、小鑼）或其發出的聲音。此字較少見，常與儀式或傳統音樂場景相關，也可用作擬聲詞。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 鉎 typically refers to a small metal percussion instrument (a small gong or bell) or the sound it makes. The character is relatively rare and is often associated with ritual or traditional musical contexts; it can also be used onomatopoeically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用鉎敲咗一下，提醒大家開始。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 zaang1 haau1 zo2 jat1 haa6, tai4 sing4 daai6 gaa1 hoi1 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他敲了一下鉦，提醒大家開始。
examples.english_sentence: He struck the small gong once to signal everyone to start.

mandarin_meaning: 擬聲詞，形容金屬或硬物相互撞擊、叩擊所發出的清脆或刺耳的聲音（相當於「叮叮聲／當啷聲」）
english_meaning: An onomatopoeic Cantonese term for a light, metallic clinking/clicking sound — 'clink-clink' or 'cling-cling'.
partOfSpeech_english: onomatopoeia (noun; can be used verb-like in colloquial speech)
explanation_mandarin: 「鉗鉗聲」是粵語口語中的擬聲詞，用來描述金屬或硬物互相碰撞、敲擊時發出的短促、清脆或略帶刺耳的聲響。常用於口語描寫環境聲或物件碰撞的聲音。
explanation_english: “鉗鉗聲” is a Cantonese onomatopoeia describing the short, crisp (often metallic) clinking or clicking noise produced when hard objects strike each other. It is used colloquially to depict environmental or object-collision sounds.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 鎖匙同金屬碰到，發出鉗鉗聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: so2 si4 tung4 gam1 suk6 pung3 dou3, faat3 ceot1 kim4 kim4 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 钥匙和金属碰撞，发出叮叮的声音。
examples.english_sentence: The keys hit the metal and made a clink-clink sound.

mandarin_meaning: 乞討用的碗；指乞討或化緣（口語）
english_meaning: begging bowl; (colloquially) to beg/collect alms
partOfSpeech_english: noun (slang); can be used as a verbal phrase in context (‘to beg’)
explanation_mandarin: 「鉢頭」原指乞討或化緣用的碗，口語中也常用來指乞討這個行為（如「打鉢頭」）。
explanation_english: Originally refers to the bowl used for begging or collecting alms; colloquially it can also refer to the act of begging (e.g. 'to go beg').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好笑佢，佢真係要出去打鉢頭搵食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 siu3 keoi5, keoi5 zan1 hai6 jiu3 ceot1 heoi3 daa2 but6 tau4 wan2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別笑他，他真的必須出去乞討謀生。
examples.english_sentence: Don't laugh at him; he really has to go out and beg to make a living.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細個嗰陣，爺爺話佢哋餓嘅時候會用鉢頭去化緣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 go3 go2 zan6, je4 je5 waa6 keoi5 dei6 ngo6 ge3 si4 hau6 wui5 jung6 but6 tau4 heoi3 faa3 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小的時候，爺爺說他們餓的時候會用乞討的碗去化緣。
examples.english_sentence: When we were kids, Grandpa said that when they're hungry they use a begging bowl to collect alms.

mandarin_meaning: 剪、剪開；（亦有指鉸鏈、鉸刀等）
english_meaning: to cut or snip (with scissors); to trim; (can also refer to a hinge or shears in some contexts)
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話口語中，「鉸」常用作動詞，表示用剪刀或利器把東西剪開、剪短或修剪。字形有時見作「骹」，用法上與「鉸」相近。也可在特定語境指鉸鏈或鉸刀等工具。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 「鉸」 (gaau2) is commonly used as a verb meaning to cut, snip, or trim with scissors or a cutting tool. The character can also appear as 「骹」 in informal writing. In some contexts it may refer to a hinge or cutting tool.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可唔可以幫我鉸開條布？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 gaau2 hoi1 tiu4 bou3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以幫我把布剪開嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Can you help me cut open the cloth?

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）敲詐、抽取錢財 / 占取別人錢財
english_meaning: (slang) to take a cut / to extort or skim money from others
explanation_mandarin: 「銀占」為香港粵語俚語，通常用來形容以不正當或占便宜的方式獲取他人金錢，類似「抽水」或「敲詐」。用法偏口語化且帶貶義。
explanation_english: "銀占" is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to describe taking money from others, often unfairly or by skimming/extorting. It is colloquial and carries a negative connotation, similar to "taking a cut" or "ripping people off."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲騙子專門銀占人哋嘅錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 pin3 zi2 zyun1 mun4 ngan4 zim1 jan4 dei6 ge3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些騙子專門從別人那裡攫取錢財。
examples.english_sentence: Those scammers specialize in taking people's money.

mandarin_meaning: 银带蛇 (yín dài shé)
english_meaning: silver-banded snake
explanation_mandarin: “银带蛇”是对一些体表具有银白色或淡色带状花纹的蛇类的通称。不同地区、不同物种的银带蛇在体色、习性和是否有毒方面可能有所不同，遇到野外蛇类应保持距离并谨慎处理。
explanation_english: “Silver-banded snake” is a common name for snakes that have silvery or pale banded patterns on their bodies. Different species and regional populations may vary in appearance, behavior, and venomousness. In the wild, keep a safe distance and treat any snake with caution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你喺山上見到一條銀帶蛇，唔好郁佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai2 saan1 soeng6 gin3 dou3 jat1 tiu4 ngan4 daai3 se4, m4 hou2 juk6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在山上看到一条银带蛇，别碰它。
examples.english_sentence: You saw a silver-banded snake on the mountain; don't touch it.

mandarin_meaning: 零錢 / 小額現金（口語、方言用法，較少見）
english_meaning: small change; loose coins (colloquial/archaic)
explanation_mandarin: 「銀稔」是粵語中較少見或方言色彩的說法，通常指零錢、散錢或小額現金。現代口語中常用「零錢」「散紙」替代。
explanation_english: A relatively rare/colloquial Cantonese expression meaning small change or loose coins. In modern speech speakers more commonly use words like "ling4 cin2" (零钱) or "saan2 si2" (散紙).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我袋入面冇乜銀稔，買嘢唔夠錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 doi6 jap6 min6 mou5 mat1 ngan4 jan5, maai5 je5 m4 gau3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我口袋裡沒有多少零錢，買東西不夠錢。
examples.english_sentence: I don't have much change in my pocket; I don't have enough money to buy it.

mandarin_meaning: 字面上指「銀角形的腰帶」，即以銀飾或銀片裝飾的腰帶；多見於傳統服飾或戲服（如粵劇）中，現代口語較少使用。
english_meaning: Literally 'silver-horn belt' — a belt decorated with silver ornaments (often shaped like small horns or curved pieces); typically seen in traditional dress or Cantonese opera costumes and uncommon in everyday modern speech.
explanation_mandarin: 銀角帶是一種腰飾，通常由銀製飾件串連或鑲嵌而成，常見於粵劇服飾、傳統婚俗或民間服飾的裝飾配件。屬於傳統服飾詞彙，現代生活中較少見。
explanation_english: A waist accessory made from silver ornaments, often strung or attached to form a decorative belt. It appears in Cantonese opera costumes, traditional wedding attire, or folk dress. It is a traditional term and is uncommon in contemporary daily use.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 演出嗰晚，佢着住粵劇服，腰間繫住條銀角帶，好搶眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jin2 ceot1 go2 maan5, keoi5 zoek3 zyu6 jyut6 kek6 fuk6, jiu1 gaan1 gai3 zyu6 tiu4 ngan4 gok3 daai3, hou2 coeng2 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 演出當晚，他穿著粵劇服，腰間繫著一條銀角帶，很搶眼。
examples.english_sentence: On the night of the performance, he was wearing Cantonese opera costume with a silver-horn belt around his waist — very eye-catching.

mandarin_meaning: 钱；银（指金钱）；（口语/俚语）指有钱人
english_meaning: money; cash; (colloquial/slang) a wealthy person
explanation_mandarin: 「銀」在香港廣東話口語中常用作“钱、现金”的意思，可單獨使用或出現在複合詞中（如「銀紙」、「銀包」）。括號內的「仁」常用來指人，合起來非正式地用以稱呼有錢人或形容某人闊綽。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, '銀' (ngan4) is a colloquial term for money or cash and appears in compounds like 銀紙 (banknotes) and 銀包 (wallet). The parenthesized '仁' (jan4) indicates the character used when referring to a person; together it can be used informally to call someone a rich/wealthy person or to describe generosity with money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家冇銀，買唔到嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 mou5 ngan4, maai5 m4 dou2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在沒有錢，買不到東西。
examples.english_sentence: I don't have any money right now; I can't buy anything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢出名有銀，成日請人食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ceot1 ming4 jau5 ngan4, seng4 jat6 ceng2 jan4 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很有錢，經常請人吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: He's known to be wealthy and often treats people to meals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老細係個銀仁，出手好闊綽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 sai3 hai6 go3 ngan4 jan4, ceot1 sau2 hou2 fut3 coek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老闆是個有錢人，出手很闊綽。
examples.english_sentence: The boss is a rich man and very generous with money.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見漢字，現代中文中無固定含義，常見於人名或古文典籍中作字形或人名用字
english_meaning: a rare/archaic Chinese character with no fixed modern meaning; sometimes seen in personal names or old texts
explanation_mandarin: 「銒」為帶金字旁的罕見漢字，現代漢語中不常使用，通常作人名、地名或古籍中的字形出現，無通用的現代詞義。
explanation_english: The character '銒' is a rare Chinese character (with the metal radical). It is not commonly used in modern Chinese and typically appears in personal names, place names, or classical texts; it does not have a widely used modern lexical meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「銒」好罕見，通常只喺人名或者古書見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 'jung4' hou2 hon2 gin3, tung1 soeng4 zi2 hai6 jan4 ming4 waak6 ze2 gu2 syu1 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字「銒」很罕见，通常只在姓名或者古书中见到。
examples.english_sentence: The character '銒' is very rare and usually only seen in personal names or ancient books.

mandarin_meaning: 铝砖
english_meaning: aluminum brick / aluminum ingot / aluminum block
explanation_mandarin: 由鋁熔化澆鑄或壓製成的長方形或塊狀金屬，常用於工業加工、儲運或回收。
explanation_english: A bar or block of aluminum produced by casting or pressing; used in industry, transport/storage, or metal recycling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢幾塊鋁磚好重，要兩個人先搬得動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gei2 faai3 leoi5 zyun1 hou2 zung6, jiu3 loeng5 go3 jan4 sin1 baan1 dak1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這幾塊鋁磚很重，要兩個人才能搬動。
examples.english_sentence: These aluminum bricks are very heavy; it takes two people to move them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 鋁磚通常喺煉鋁廠或金屬回收場見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: leoi5 zyun1 tung1 soeng4 hai2 lin6 leoi5 cong3 waak6 gam1 seot6 wui4 sau1 coeng4 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 鋁磚通常在煉鋁廠或金屬回收場看到。
examples.english_sentence: Aluminum bricks are usually seen at aluminum smelters or metal recycling yards.

mandarin_meaning: 店铺；铺设、铺排（动词用法）
english_meaning: shop/store; to lay out or set up; to arrange
explanation_mandarin: 「鋪」常用作名词（舖、鋪頭，粤语读作 pou3），表示店铺或铺面；亦可作动词（粤语读作 pou1），表示铺设、铺排或安排。括号中的「甫」有时在古籍或人名中见到，但现代粤语日常用字通常为「鋪／舖」。
explanation_english: 「鋪」 has two common uses in Cantonese: as a noun (pou3) meaning a shop or store, and as a verb (pou1) meaning to lay out, set up, or arrange. The character 甫 appears historically or in names but is not the usual modern form for everyday Cantonese usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間鋪頭生意好好，日日都多人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 tau4 saang1 ji3 hou2 hou2, jat6 jat6 dou1 hou2 do1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间店铺生意很好，每天都有很多人。
examples.english_sentence: This shop does great business; it's busy with people every day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經鋪排好明日嘅行程。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 pou1 paai4 hou2 ming4 jat6 ge3 hang4 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已经铺排好明天的行程。
examples.english_sentence: I've already arranged tomorrow's itinerary.

mandarin_meaning: 錐子（小型尖頭手工工具）
english_meaning: awl (a small pointed hand tool used to pierce holes)
explanation_mandarin: 指一種有尖頭、用來在木材、皮革等材料上刺孔或劃線的小型手工工具，也可泛指小錐子。
explanation_english: Refers to a small pointed hand tool (awl) used to pierce holes or scribe materials like wood or leather; can also mean a small awl in general.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用錐仔喺木頭度鑽咗一個洞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 zeoi1 zai2 hai2 muk6 tau4 dou6 zyun3 zo2 jat1 go3 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他用錐子在木头上钻了一个洞。
examples.english_sentence: He used an awl to make a hole in the wood.

mandarin_meaning: 錐子（zhuīzi）— 一種尖頭工具，用來刺、鑽孔或劃線；也可作比喻，形容刺痛或刺入的感覺。
english_meaning: awl — a small pointed tool used for piercing, making holes, or scribing; metaphorically, a sharp, piercing pain or sensation.
explanation_mandarin: 指一種小而尖的手工具，常用於木工或手作中刺、鑽孔、劃線；在口語或書面語中也常用來比喻刺痛或刺入的感覺。
explanation_english: Refers to a small pointed hand tool commonly used in carpentry or crafting to pierce, make holes, or scribe lines; also used metaphorically to describe a piercing pain or sensation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我攞住錐子鑽個洞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lo2 zyu6 zeoi1 zi2 zyun3 go3 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我拿著錐子鑽一個洞。
examples.english_sentence: I'm holding an awl and drilling a hole.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰句話刺到我心，好似畀錐子插到咁痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 ge3 waa6 ci3 dou3 ngo5 sam1, hou2 ci5 bei2 zeoi1 zi2 caap3 dou3 gam2 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那句話刺痛了我的心，好像被錐子刺了一樣痛。
examples.english_sentence: His words pierced my heart; it felt like being stabbed with an awl.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做細木工要用錐子畫線同鑽孔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 sai3 muk6 gung1 jiu3 jung6 zeoi1 zi2 waa6 sin3 tung4 zyun3 hung2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做細木工要用錐子畫線和鑽孔。
examples.english_sentence: A carpenter needs to use an awl to scribe lines and drill holes.

mandarin_meaning: 零錢；小額錢（俚語，用於貶或輕視小額錢財）
english_meaning: loose change; petty cash (slang, often dismissive of small sums)
explanation_mandarin: 「錢鱗」是廣東話俚語，指零錢或小額錢，常帶有輕視或貶低的語氣，用來形容不值錢或不重要的錢財。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term referring to small amounts of money or loose change. Often used dismissively to indicate trivial or insignificant sums.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好為咗啲錢鱗搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 wai6 zo2 di1 cin2 leon4 gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要為了這點小錢讓大家不高興。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let a bit of loose change make everyone unhappy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆唔肯俾我加人工，只係因為啲錢鱗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 m4 hang2 bei2 ngo5 gaa1 jan4 gung1, zi2 hai6 jan1 wai6 di1 cin2 leon4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老闆不肯給我加薪，只因為是小錢。
examples.english_sentence: The boss refused to give me a raise just because it's petty cash.

mandarin_meaning: 表链（手表的金属链式表带）
english_meaning: watch bracelet; metal watch band; watch chain
explanation_mandarin: 指手表上的金属链或链式表带，用來固定手表在手腕上，也具有裝飾作用。
explanation_english: Refers to the metal chain or bracelet attached to a watch used to secure it on the wrist; also serves a decorative purpose.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我新買咗一條錶鏈，好襯我隻錶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 san1 maai5 zo2 jat1 tiu4 biu1 lin4, hou2 can3 ngo5 zek3 biu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我新买了一条表链，很配我的手表。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a new watch bracelet; it matches my watch well.

mandarin_meaning: 金屬鉤子；（引申）比喻為人設下的圈套或陷阱（詞彙較少見、偏方言或古老用法）
english_meaning: a metal hook; (figuratively) a trap or snare set by someone (rare/archaic usage)
explanation_mandarin: 「鎉鉤」原指金屬製的鉤子或掛鉤，用於掛、勾、固定物件。此詞在現代廣東話中較為罕見，有時也可作比喻用，指人設下的圈套或陷阱。
explanation_english: Originally refers to a metal hook or hanger used to hook, hang, or secure objects. The term is relatively rare in modern Cantonese and can sometimes be used figuratively to mean a trap or snare set by someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊工廠用緊啲鎉鉤嚟掛重物。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 gung1 cong2 jung6 gan2 di1 dap6-gau1 lai4 gwaa3 zung6 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 舊工廠正在用那些鎉鉤來掛重物。
examples.english_sentence: The old factory is using those metal hooks to hang heavy objects.

mandarin_meaning: 锁镣（指用于束缚犯人手脚的铁制器具，也可引申为限制、束缚）
english_meaning: shackles; fetters (iron restraints used to bind a prisoner's hands or feet); figuratively, constraints or restrictions
explanation_mandarin: 鎖鐐（繁體：鎖鐐，簡體：锁镣）是用來束縛犯人手腳的鐵製器具。口語或書面語中亦可用作比喻，表示對人或事的限制、束縛。
explanation_english: Refers to iron restraints (shackles/fetters) used to bind a prisoner's hands or feet. It can also be used metaphorically to describe something that restricts or confines freedom or action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 囚犯腳上戴住鎖鐐，行路好唔方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cau4 faan6 gok3 soeng6 daai3 zyu6 so2 liu4, haang4 lou6 hou2 m4 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 囚犯脚上戴着锁镣，走路很不方便。
examples.english_sentence: The prisoner's feet were shackled, so it's very difficult for him to walk.

mandarin_meaning: 夷平地皮 / 清拆（以便重建）
english_meaning: to clear/level a site (by demolishing existing buildings), to raze land for redevelopment
explanation_mandarin: 俚語或口語用法，指把地皮或上面的舊建築物夷平、清拆，通常是為了重建或發展用途。有時含有強制、收地或大規模拆除的含意。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression meaning to clear or level a plot of land by demolishing existing buildings, usually for redevelopment. It can imply forceful clearance or large-scale demolition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 發展商買咗嗰塊地皮，鏟咗啲舊樓準備起新樓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 zin2 soeng1 maai5 zo2 go2 faai3 dei6 pei4, caan2 zo2 di1 gau6 lau4 zeon2 bei6 hei2 san1 lau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 發展商買下了那塊地皮，拆掉了舊樓準備起新樓。
examples.english_sentence: The developer bought that plot of land and demolished the old buildings to prepare for new construction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府計劃鏟走嗰個舊街市嘅地皮，改建成商場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gai3 waak6 caan2 zau2 go2 go3 gau6 gaai1 si5 ge3 dei6 pei4, goi2 gin3 sing4 soeng1 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府計劃拆走那個舊街市的地皮，改建成商場。
examples.english_sentence: The government plans to clear that old market site and redevelop it into a shopping mall.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個工程要先鏟平塊地皮，先可以打樁做地基。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gung1 cing4 jiu3 sin1 caan2 ping4 faai3 dei6 pei4, sin1 ho2 ji5 daa2 zong1 zou6 dei6 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個工程要先把地皮夷平，才能打樁做地基。
examples.english_sentence: This project needs to level the site first before piling the foundations.

mandarin_meaning: 鏟子；鏟除、清除（動作）
english_meaning: shovel, spade; to shovel/scoop; to remove or eliminate
explanation_mandarin: 表示一種用來挖掘或鏟起物料的工具（鏟子），也可作動詞，表示用鏟子鏟、清除或剷除某物。
explanation_english: Refers to a tool used for digging or scooping (a shovel); also used as a verb meaning to shovel, scoop up, or remove something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗把鏟，準備整理花園。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 baa2 caan2, zeon2 bei6 zing2 lei5 faa1 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我買了一把鏟，準備整理花園。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a shovel to tidy the garden.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢將窗台上嘅塵鏟走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoeng1 coeng1 toi4 soeng6 ge3 can4 caan2 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他把窗台上的灰塵鏟走了。
examples.english_sentence: He shoveled away the dust on the windowsill.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）指喜歡指手畫腳、愛出主意或批評別人的中年／老年男子，帶貶義。
english_meaning: Colloquial term for an older man who meddles, gives unsolicited advice or criticizes others — a know-it-all 'uncle' (pejorative).
explanation_mandarin: 「鐸叔／度叔」是香港粵語的俗稱，通常用來稱呼那些喜歡對別人指指點點、插手瑣事或愛發表負面意見的中年或老年男子。語氣多為貶義或帶調侃。
explanation_english: “鐸叔/度叔” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang for an older man who habitually meddles, offers unsolicited advice or criticizes others. The term is usually pejorative or teasing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度做鐸叔，對啲細事都要插手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 zou6 doek3 suk1, deoi3 di1 sai3 si6 dou1 jiu3 caap3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在那裡當“鐸叔”，對小事都要插手。
examples.english_sentence: He's always acting like a meddling 'uncle', sticking his nose into trivial matters.

mandarin_meaning: 金屬被敲打或碰撞時發出的短促響聲（擬聲詞）
english_meaning: a short, sharp metallic clang; onomatopoeic word representing a metallic striking sound
explanation_mandarin: 「鐺」常作擬聲詞，用來模仿鐘、鍋、門鉸等金屬物件被敲擊或碰撞時發出的清脆或沉響。也可寫作鏜（作音近義替代）。
explanation_english: “鐺” is an onomatopoeic word imitating the short metallic sound produced when metal objects (bells, pans, hinges, etc.) are struck or collide. It conveys a sharp or resonant clang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢推門，門鉸鐺一聲就合埋咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teoi1 mun4, mun4 gaau2 dong1 jat1 seng1 zau6 hap6 maai4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他推门，门铰“鐺”一声就合上了。
examples.english_sentence: He pushed the door; the hinge went 'clang' as it shut.

mandarin_meaning: 完蛋；出大問題；麻煩
english_meaning: screwed; in big trouble; things have gone badly wrong
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語 / 感嘆詞（或形容詞短語）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，通常用作感嘆或描述情況非常糟糕、出大問題，類似「完蛋了」的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to exclaim or describe that something has gone very wrong or someone is in serious trouble—similar to 'we're screwed' or 'it's all over'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果嗰份文件遺失咗，真係鑊黸喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 go2 fan6 man4 gin6 wai4 sat1 zo2, zan1 hai6 wok6 lau4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果那份文件丟失了，真是完蛋了。
examples.english_sentence: If that document is lost, we're really screwed.

mandarin_meaning: 擬聲詞：模仿金屬撞擊或鏗鏘的聲音；引申可用來形容聲音大、敲鑼打鼓般的浮誇場面，或口語上用以嘲諷/形容某事荒謬、胡說。
english_meaning: An onomatopoeic expression imitating a metallic clanging or clattering sound; figuratively used to describe something loud, ostentatious, or to dismiss something as nonsense/exaggeration.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 擬聲詞 / 感嘆詞（口語）
explanation_mandarin: 「鑔督錚」屬於廣東話的口語擬聲詞，模仿金屬撞擊或鏗鏘作響的聲音。使用上既可直接表示聽到類似的聲音，也可延伸用作比喻，形容某些場面或言行浮誇、噪雜，或帶有嘲諷、不屑的語氣。此詞較口語化、使用頻率不高，主要見於香港或廣東的俗語與網絡用語中。
explanation_english: “鑔督錚” is a Cantonese colloquial onomatopoeia that imitates a metallic clang or clatter. It can be used literally for such sounds, or figuratively to describe scenes or behavior that are loud, showy, or ostentatious. It may also be used sarcastically to dismiss something as ridiculous or nonsensical. The term is colloquial and relatively informal, chiefly found in Hong Kong/Cantonese speech and online contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱啱聽到樓下有陣鑔督錚，嚇親我一跳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngaam1 ngaam1 teng1 dou3 lau4 haa6 jau5 zan6 caap3 duk1 zeng1, haak3 can1 ngo5 jat1 tiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剛剛聽到樓下有一陣叮噹聲，嚇了我一跳。
examples.english_sentence: I just heard a clanging noise downstairs and it startled me.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見或古老詞彙，現代漢語和廣東話中無通行的固定義；字面可拆為「熔化／消融」(鑠) 與「馬」，但並非實際用法。
english_meaning: A rare or archaic term with no standard meaning in modern Cantonese; literally the characters read 'melt/melted horse' but it has no established usage.
explanation_mandarin: 「鑠馬」並非現代粵語常用詞彙，文獻與口語中極少見到。單字意義可推為「鑠＝熔化／消減、馬＝馬」，但沒有可靠的慣用或比喻義。
explanation_english: Not attested as a common Cantonese word or idiom. The characters individually mean 'melt/reduce' (鑠) and 'horse' (馬), but there is no established or commonly understood compound meaning in contemporary usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「鑠馬」呢個詞好罕見，喺現代廣東話入面幾乎唔會見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soek3 maa5 ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 hon2 gin3, hai2 jin6 doi6 gwong2 dung1 waa2 jap6 min6 gei2 fu1 m4 wui5 gin3 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「鑠馬」这个词很罕见，在现代广东话中几乎看不到。
examples.english_sentence: '鑠馬' is a very rare term and is almost never seen in modern Cantonese.

mandarin_meaning: 爐（lú）：用來生火、熔煉或烹飪的器具、熔爐或火爐
english_meaning: furnace; stove; kiln; brazier (a device used for heating, smelting, or cooking)
explanation_mandarin: 「鑪」為「爐」的異體字或古字，指用來生火、燒煉、熔化金屬或烹煮食物的器具或設備。
explanation_english: The character '鑪' is a variant/archaic form of '爐' and denotes a stove, furnace, or kiln used for heating, smelting, or cooking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個鑪用嚟煲水同煮嘢食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 lou4 jung6 lai4 bou1 seoi2 tung4 zyu2 je5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個爐用來燒水和煮東西吃。
examples.english_sentence: This stove is used to boil water and cook food.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見/不確定（可能為古字或方言用語，現代普通話無明確對應）
english_meaning: Extremely rare/uncertain (possibly an archaic or dialectal term; no clear modern equivalent)
explanation_mandarin: 「鑪𨱋」為罕見字形組合，現代粵語與普通話主要詞典中少有或無收錄。字首「鑪」與「爐/炉」相關（爐、火爐），但後一字𨱋為罕用字，讀音與詞義在現代語境下不穩定、難以確定。以下解釋屬推測性質：可能為地方用字或古字，現代用法極少，若遇到此字通常須依上下文或古籍考證。
explanation_english: “鑪𨱋” is an extremely rare character combination with little or no presence in major modern Cantonese or Mandarin dictionaries. The first character 鑪 relates to 'stove/furnace' (爐/炉), while the second character 𨱋 is an uncommon glyph; its pronunciation and meaning in contemporary usage are uncertain. The entry below is cautious and speculative: it may be an archaic or dialectal term and is rarely used today; determining its meaning typically requires contextual or historical research.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「鑪𨱋」好罕見，唔知點讀同埋乜意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 'lou4 bok3' hou2 hon2 gin3, m4 zi1 dim2 duk6 tung4 maai4 mat1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個字「鑪𨱋」很罕見，不知道怎麼讀和什麼意思。
examples.english_sentence: The character '鑪𨱋' is very rare; I don't know how to read it or what it means.

mandarin_meaning: 鏨子、鑿子；用於刻、鑿、修整金屬或石材的工具
english_meaning: chisel; a chisel-like tool used for carving, cutting, or trimming metal or stone
explanation_mandarin: 鑱通常指一種金屬製的鏨或鑿，用來在石材、金屬等材料上鑿刻、修整或去除多餘部分，常見於石匠或鐵匠工作中。
explanation_english: A chisel-like hand tool, typically metal, used to carve, chip, or trim material such as stone or metal. Commonly used by stonemasons and metalworkers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 匠人用鑱修整石材嘅邊緣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng6 jan4 jung6 caan4 sau1 zing2 sek6 coi4 ge3 bin1 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 匠人用鑱修整石材的邊緣。
examples.english_sentence: The craftsman used a chisel to trim the edge of the stone.

mandarin_meaning: 罐；金屬製的鍋或罐（書面或古字）
english_meaning: a metal pot or jar (archaic/literary)
explanation_mandarin: 「鑵」多為書面或古字，用來指金屬製的容器，如鍋、罐，與「罐」「鍋」意義接近。
explanation_english: An archaic or literary character referring to a metal container such as a pot or jar, similar in meaning to '罐' or '鍋'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚房入面有個鑵，係用嚟煲湯嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyu4 fong4 jap6 min6 jau5 go3 gun3, hai6 jung6 lei4 bou1 tong1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 厨房里有一个鑵（鐵鍋），用来熬汤。
examples.english_sentence: There's a metal pot in the kitchen used for simmering soup.

mandarin_meaning: 愛挑毛病、愛管閒事的人（俚語）
english_meaning: a nitpicker / busybody; someone who fusses over trivial things or meddles in others' affairs
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來形容喜歡挑剔、對小事過份計較或愛管別人閒事的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe a person who nitpicks, is overly fussy about minor issues, or meddles in others' business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做鑽屎蟲，啲小事唔使咁計較。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 zyun3 si2 cung4, di1 siu2 si6 m4 sai2 gam2 gai3 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別做鑽屎蟲，別為小事斤斤計較。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a nitpicker; don't fuss over small things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係個鑽屎蟲，對同事成日話長短。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 go3 zyun3 si2 cung4, deoi3 tung4 si6 sing4 jat6 waa6 coeng4 dyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個愛挑剔的人，總是對同事挑三揀四。
examples.english_sentence: He's really a nitpicker; always criticizing his coworkers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你老豆係鑽屎蟲，你要學識點樣應付佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 laau5 dou6 hai6 zyun3 si2 cung4, nei5 jiu3 hok6 sik1 dim2 joeng6 jing3 fu6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你爸爸很愛挑剔，你要學會如何應對他。
examples.english_sentence: If your dad is a nitpicker, you need to learn how to deal with him.

mandarin_meaning: 目瞪口呆；呆住、驚呆
english_meaning: to be dumbfounded; to gape in shock or astonishment
explanation_mandarin: 粵語粗俗口語，形容因驚訝或震驚而瞪大眼、呆住說不出話來，類似「目瞪口呆」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar slang phrase describing being stunned or shocked, staring wide-eyed and speechless. Similar in meaning to "dumbfounded" or "gaping in astonishment."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到呢件事，鑿大屎眼，一句都講唔出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou3 ni1 gin6 si6, zaak3 daai6 si2 ngaan5, jat1 ge3 dou1 gong2 m4 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽到這件事，目瞪口呆，一句話也說不出來。
examples.english_sentence: When he heard about it, he was dumbfounded and couldn't say a word.

mandarin_meaning: 針尖般鋒利，能削鐵；形容非常鋒利或說話刻薄
english_meaning: As sharp as a needle (can shave iron); extremely sharp — can describe a physical edge or cutting, incisive remarks
explanation_mandarin: 比喻物件非常鋒利或言語尖刻。字面上是針尖能削鐵，用來強調鋒利程度或批評話語的刻薄。
explanation_english: A figurative expression meaning extremely sharp (literally a needle point that can shave iron). Used for very sharp objects or for cutting, caustic remarks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰把菜刀針鼻削鐵，斬菜切肉好輕鬆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 baa2 coi3 dou1 zam1 bei6 zoek3 tit3, zaam2 coi3 cit3 juk6 hou2 hing1 sung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的菜刀鋒利無比，切菜切肉都很輕鬆。
examples.english_sentence: His kitchen knife is extremely sharp; it's easy to chop vegetables and meat.

mandarin_meaning: 用手指勾動招呼或召喚（亦可指勾小拇指作為承諾）
english_meaning: To beckon/call someone by curling a finger; (also) to hook little fingers as a pinky promise
explanation_mandarin: 指用手指彎勾的動作向人示意、召喚（有時被視為不禮貌的招呼方式）。另有時用於指勾小拇指互勾表示承諾或約定。
explanation_english: Refers to the action of curling a finger to signal or call someone over (sometimes considered impolite). It can also refer to hooking little fingers together as a pinky-swear or promise.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街度用手指勾我過嚟，真係好無禮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 dou6 jung6 sau2 zi2 gau1 ngo5 gwo3 lai4, zan1 hai6 hou2 mou4 lai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街上用手指把我招過來，真的很沒禮貌。
examples.english_sentence: He beckoned me over with his finger on the street; it was really rude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋會用小指勾手指做承諾，答應下次一齊去旅行。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 wui5 jung6 siu2 zi2 gau1 sau2 zi2 zou6 sing4 nok6, daap3 jing3 haa6 ci3 jat1 cai4 heoi3 leoi5 hang4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們會用小指勾手指做承諾，答應下次一起去旅行。
examples.english_sentence: We hook our little fingers as a promise (pinky-swear), agreeing to go on a trip together next time.

jyutping: tit3 zeoi2 gai1, ngaa4 zim1 zeoi2 lei6
mandarin_meaning: 嘴巴尖刻、毒舌；说话刻薄或口齿伶俐、善于反驳
english_meaning: sharp-tongued; biting or quick-witted with words—ready with sarcastic or cutting remarks
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容說話尖刻、善於反駁或愛抬槓的人。"铁嘴鸡"偏向口不服輸、不肯認錯；"牙尖嘴利"強調言語尖刻、反應快。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is sharp-tongued or quick with biting remarks. "Tit3 zeoi2 gai1" (iron-mouthed) implies someone who rarely admits defeat or refuses to back down; "ngaa4 zim1 zeoi2 lei6" emphasizes a sarcastic, cutting, and quick-witted way of speaking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個鐵嘴雞，牙尖嘴利，成日同人抬槓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 tit3 zeoi2 gai1, ngaa4 zim1 zeoi2 lei6, seng4 jat6 tung4 jan4 taai4 gong3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是个铁嘴鸡，牙尖嘴利，经常和别人抬杠。
examples.english_sentence: He's an iron-mouthed, sharp-tongued person who is always arguing with others.

mandarin_meaning: 比喻做事笨拙、只會用一招或只會用單一方法，不能圓滿完成
english_meaning: An idiomatic/slang expression meaning to be clumsy or inept, to tackle something with only one (ineffective) method or a lame attempt
explanation_mandarin: 此句字面是說鐵拐李（一位拐杖仙人）踢足球只能用一隻腳，常用來形容做事笨拙、手段單一或徒勞無功。有時帶戲謔或嘲諷意味。
explanation_english: Literally 'Tieguai Li playing soccer, kicking with one leg.' Used to describe someone who is clumsy, has only one (ineffective) approach, or makes a lame/ineffective attempt. Often humorous or mildly mocking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁做，好似鐵拐李打足球，一腳踢，點都搞唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 zou6, hou2 ci5 tit3-gwaai2-lei5-daa2-zuk1-kau4, jat1-goek3-tek3, dim2-dou1 gaau2 m4-dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣做，像鐵拐李踢足球，只能用一隻腳踢，怎麼都弄不成。
examples.english_sentence: Doing it like this is like Tieguai Li playing soccer—kicking with one leg—you won't get it done.

jyutping: tit3 muk6 zan1 daa2 zai2, daai6 hon6 lam4 sai3 hon6
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）形容因緊張、害怕或極度勞累而全身大汗小汗不停、汗流浹背
english_meaning: (colloquial) to be drenched in sweat; to sweat profusely — often from fear, nervousness, or heavy exertion
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語把歷史人物「鐵木真」（成吉思汗）的名字放入語句，以誇張手法形容一個人因為驚慌、緊張或勞累而汗流不止。語氣多半帶幽默或誇張色彩，屬口語用法。
explanation_english: This colloquial expression inserts the name 'Temüjin' (Genghis Khan) for emphasis and uses hyperbole to describe someone sweating uncontrollably from fear, nervousness, or physical exertion. It's informal and often used humorously or exaggeratively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱跑完步，成個人鐵木真打仔，大汗𢱕細汗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aam1 aam1 paau2 jyun4 bou6, sing4 go3 jan4 tit3 muk6 zan1 daa2 zai2, daai6 hon6 lam4 sai3 hon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我剛跑完步，整個人像鐵木真打仔一樣，滿身大汗淋漓。
examples.english_sentence: I just finished running and I'm soaked — I'm sweating profusely (like the phrase 'Temüjin beats kids' — used humorously).

jyutping: tit3 saa1 lei4, ngaau5 m4 jap6
mandarin_meaning: 字面：像鐵一樣硬的梨，咬不動；引申：非常硬頸、難以說服或難以應付
english_meaning: Literal: a pear as hard as iron — can't bite into it; Figurative: extremely stubborn or very hard to deal with; a tough nut to crack
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，原指食物非常硬，咬不動；引申用來形容人或事情難以對付、頑固或難以改變。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase. Literally refers to food so hard you can't bite it; figuratively used to describe a person or situation that is stubborn, unyielding, or very difficult to handle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好鐵沙梨，咬唔入，乜都唔肯讓步。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 tit3 saa1 lei4, ngaau5 m4 jap6, mat1 dou1 m4 hang2 joeng6 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這個人很鐵沙梨，咬不動，什麼都不肯讓步。
examples.english_sentence: He's really 'iron-pear' — impossible to get along with; he refuses to give ground on anything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個梨硬到似鐵沙梨，真係咬唔入，唔好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 lei4 ngaang6 dou3 ci5 tit3 saa1 lei4, zan1 hai6 ngaau5 m4 jap6, m4 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個梨硬得像鐵沙梨，真的咬不動，別吃了。
examples.english_sentence: This pear is as hard as 'iron-pear' — you really can't bite into it. Don't eat it.

mandarin_meaning: （小物件）全部掉落／都掉光了；也可比喻事情全部出了問題或崩盘
english_meaning: All the little bells (or small items) have fallen off; used literally for small objects falling off or figuratively to mean everything has gone wrong / everything collapsed
explanation_mandarin: 「铃铃都掉埋」是廣東話口語說法，字面指細小有鈴聲的物件（如耳環、小飾物）全部掉落。也可用作比喻，表示事情全部出亂子、完蛋或完全失敗。常見於香港口語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase. Literally it refers to small bell-like items (e.g. earrings) all falling off. Figuratively it can mean that everything has gone wrong or fallen apart. Commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個耳環鬆咗，啲铃铃都掉埋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 ji5 waan4 sung1 zo2, di1 ling4 ling4 dou1 diu6 maai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 耳环松了，铃铛都掉了。
examples.english_sentence: My earring came loose and the little bells all fell off.

jyutping: tung4 baan2 cit3 dau6 fu6, loeng5 min6 gwong1
mandarin_meaning: 两面讨好 / 两面派（表里不一、讨好双方）
english_meaning: To try to please both sides; be two-faced or play both sides; avoid taking a stand (often negative, implying hypocrisy or opportunism).
explanation_mandarin: 比喻為迎合双方、兩面討好或表裡不一，帶有貶義，表示沒有原則或投機取巧。
explanation_english: An idiom meaning to curry favor with both sides or be two-faced — to play both sides or avoid taking a stand. Often used negatively to imply hypocrisy or opportunism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日銅板切豆腐，兩面光，唔可信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 tung4 baan2 cit3 dau6 fu6, loeng5 min6 gwong1, m4 ho2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天两面讨好，两面派，不可信。
examples.english_sentence: He's always trying to please both sides — two-faced and untrustworthy.

cantonese: 铜银买病猪，两家偷欢喜
jyutping: tung4 ngan4 maai5 beng6 zyu1, loeng5 gaa1 tau1 fun1 hei2
mandarin_meaning: 買賣不光彩的交易，雙方暗自得利或因他人不幸而同時受益的情況
english_meaning: A saying for a shady deal where both parties quietly benefit (often at someone else's expense); both sides secretly happy about the arrangement.
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語比喻在不太光彩或有利害關係的情況下，交易或安排使雙方暗自得利，通常帶有利用或牽涉第三者不利處境的含意。
explanation_english: This proverb metaphorically describes a situation where a deal or arrangement — often morally questionable — results in both parties quietly benefiting, typically by taking advantage of a third party's misfortune or through collusion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺度做嗰筆交易，好似銅銀買病豬，兩家偷歡喜，外人就唔知道真相。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 dou6 zou6 go2 bat1 gaau1 jik6, hou2 ci5 tung4 ngan4 maai5 beng6 zyu1, loeng5 gaa1 tau1 fun1 hei2, ngoi6 jan4 zau6 m4 zi1 zan1 soeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们做那笔交易，好像铜银买病猪，两家偷欢喜，外人就不知道真相。
examples.english_sentence: Their deal looked like 'buying a sick pig for money' — both parties secretly happy — outsiders don't know the truth.

mandarin_meaning: 錯也有錯著 / 錯裡有對（口語）
english_meaning: There is some truth or a redeeming point even in a mistake; wrong but with something right about it (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 表示某件事雖然有錯，但當中仍有值得肯定或有道理的地方。常用於口語，帶有讓步或折衷的語氣。
explanation_english: Indicates that although something is mistaken or wrong, there is still something valid or worthwhile in it. Commonly used colloquially to concede a point while acknowledging merit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嗰啲嘢雖然唔啱，但錯有錯着，佢都有啲觀點值得諗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 go2 di1 je5 seoi1 jin4 m4 ngaam1, daan6 co3 jau5 co3 zoek3, keoi5 dou1 jau5 di1 gun1 dim2 zik1 dak1 lam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說的那些話雖然不對，但錯有錯着，他也有一些觀點值得思考。
examples.english_sentence: What he said isn't entirely right, but there's some truth in it; he has points worth considering.

cantonese: 锦上添花易，雪中送炭难
jyutping: gam2 soeng5 tim1 faa1 ji6, syut3 zung1 sung3 taan3 naan4
mandarin_meaning: 锦上添花容易，雪中送炭困难；在别人顺利时帮忙容易，在别人困难时给予实质帮助却很难。
english_meaning: It's easier to add decorations when things are already going well than to provide real help when someone is in dire need — i.e., flattering or helping in good times is easy, but offering practical help in hard times is difficult.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用“锦上添花”与“雪中送炭”对比，指出在顺境中做些附加的好事很容易，但在别人处于困境时给予实质性帮助更难，强调真正的帮助和真朋友的价值。
explanation_english: The proverb contrasts 'adding flowers to brocade' with 'sending charcoal in snowy weather' to show that it's easy to do pleasant or flattering things when someone is already successful, but much harder to offer substantial help when someone is in real need; it highlights the value of timely, practical support and true friendship.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 錦上添花易，雪中送炭難；真正嘅朋友會喺你最需要嘅時候幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2 soeng5 tim1 faa1 ji6, syut3 zung1 sung3 taan3 naan4; zan1 zing3 ge3 pang4 jau5 wui5 hai2 nei5 zeoi3 seoi1 jiu3 ge3 si4 hau6 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 锦上添花容易，雪中送炭困难；真正的朋友会在你最需要的时候帮助你。
examples.english_sentence: It's easy to add flowers to brocade but hard to send charcoal in snowy weather; a true friend helps you when you need it most.

mandarin_meaning: 颜面尽失；非常丢脸
english_meaning: to lose face completely; to be utterly humiliated
explanation_mandarin: “镬底噉面”是粤语俗语，字面意为“像锅底一样的脸”，用于形容在公众场合被彻底打败或受到严重羞辱，丢尽颜面。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning 'face like the bottom of a wok.' It describes being thoroughly humiliated or losing face completely, especially in public.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次輸到镬底噉面，成班人都笑死佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 syu1 dou3 wok6 dai2 gam2 min6, sing4 baan1 jan4 dou1 siu3 sei2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次他输得颜面尽失，整班人都笑死他。
examples.english_sentence: He lost so badly this time that he was utterly humiliated; the whole group laughed at him.

mandarin_meaning: 椭圆形 / 长圆形（指形状像被拉长的圆）
english_meaning: oval; elliptical shape (an elongated circle)
explanation_mandarin: 指形狀像被拉長的圓，常用來描述橢圓或長圓的幾何形狀，例如某些桌面、蛋糕或鏡子的外形。
explanation_english: Refers to a shape like an elongated circle—an oval or ellipse. Used to describe objects (tables, cakes, mirrors, etc.) with an elongated circular outline.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個蛋糕係長圓形，切片好方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 daan2 gou1 hai6 coeng4 jyun4 jing4, cit3 pin2 hou2 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个蛋糕是长圆形的，切片很方便。
examples.english_sentence: This cake is oval, so it's easy to slice.

mandarin_meaning: 长毛贼
english_meaning: literally "long-haired thief"; a colloquial derogatory term for a thief or used to insult hippies/activists/protesters
explanation_mandarin: 口語貶義稱呼，字面指留長髮的賊，亦常被用來貶低示威者、嬉皮或激進分子，帶有侮辱性。
explanation_english: A colloquial, derogatory term literally meaning "long-haired thief." It can refer to a thief with long hair or be used as an insulting label for hippies, activists, or protesters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 巴士上有個長毛賊偷咗佢個袋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baa1 si2 soeng6 jau5 go3 coeng4 mou4 caak6 tau1 zo2 keoi5 go3 doi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公車上有個長毛賊偷了他的包。
examples.english_sentence: There was a long-haired thief on the bus who stole his bag.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲人將示威者罵做長毛賊，帶有貶義。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 jan4 zoeng1 si6 wai1 ze2 maa6 zou6 coeng4 mou4 caak6, daai3 jau5 bin2 ji6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些人把示威者罵作長毛賊，含有貶義。
examples.english_sentence: Some people call protesters 'long-haired thieves', which is derogatory.

mandarin_meaning: 长寿；长命（表示寿命长，常用于祝愿或成语中）
english_meaning: long life; longevity (often used as a wish or in idioms)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词/形容词（常作为祝愿或成语的一部分）
partOfSpeech_english: noun/adjective (often used as a wish or in compounds/idioms)
explanation_mandarin: 表示寿命长、长久生活，常见于祝福语或成语，如“長生不老”或与“長命”互用。
explanation_english: Indicates living a long life or longevity. Commonly used in blessings or idioms (e.g., "長生不老") and often interchangeable with terms like "long-lived."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 祝你長命百歲，身體健康，長生不老！
examples.jyutping_sentence: zuk1 nei5 coeng4 ming6 baak3 seoi3, san1 tai2 gin6 hong1, coeng4 saang1 bat1 lou5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 祝你长命百岁，身体健康，长生不老！
examples.english_sentence: Wishing you many years, good health, and perpetual youth!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺生日宴上，親戚輪流祝你長生、長命百歲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 sang1 jat6 jin6 soeng6, can1 cik1 leon4 lau4 zuk1 nei5 coeng4 saang1, coeng4 ming6 baak3 seoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在生日宴会上，亲戚轮流祝你长生、长命百岁。
examples.english_sentence: At the birthday banquet, relatives took turns wishing you a long life and many years.

mandarin_meaning: 比喻到處跑、常常換地方或換工作的人；愛流動、難以定居或長期留職的人
english_meaning: Literally 'long-legged grasshopper'; slang for a person who is always on the move — a wanderer, drifter, or job-hopper who doesn't stay long in one place
explanation_mandarin: 「長腳蜢」是廣東話俚語，字面是長腿的蚱蜢，用來形容那些喜歡到處跑動、經常換地方或工作，難以長期停留的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term literally meaning 'long-legged grasshopper'. It describes someone who constantly moves around — frequently changing jobs or locations, unable or unwilling to settle down.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個長腳蜢，成日周圍走，唔會喺一間公司做得耐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 coeng4 goek3 maang2, sing4 jat6 zau1 wai4 zau2, m4 wui5 hai6 jat1 gaan1 gung1 si1 zou6 dak1 noi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個到處跑的人，總是在外面流動，無法在一家公司做久。
examples.english_sentence: He's a 'long-legged grasshopper' — always moving around and can't stay long at one company.

mandarin_meaning: 長期依賴；老是賴著別人（不肯自立）
english_meaning: to keep relying on someone for a long time; to cling to others; to freeload
explanation_mandarin: 「長賴」是廣東話口語，表示長期依賴別人、不肯自立或常常賴著別人不走，多帶有貶義或不滿語氣。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to rely on someone for an extended period, to cling to or freeload off others; often used with a critical or disapproving tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好長賴住我，自己搵工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 coeng4 laai6 zyu6 ngo5, zi6 gei2 wan2 gung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要一直賴著我，自己找工作吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep relying on me — find a job yourself.

mandarin_meaning: 人名，無特殊成語義。普通話讀音可標為 Zhǎng Chénshēng；按粵語姓氏羅馬化可寫作 Cheung Chan-sing。
english_meaning: A personal name (proper noun). Cantonese romanization: Cheung Chan-sing; Mandarin pinyin: Zhang/Chang Chensheng.
explanation_mandarin: 「長陳陞」通常作為人名使用，並非成語或常見片語。單字分別為「長」、「陳」、「陞」，在粵語中讀作 coeng4 can4 sing1。
explanation_english: Usually used as a personal name rather than an idiom or common phrase. The characters are read in Cantonese as coeng4 can4 sing1.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢叫長陳陞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 giu3 coeng4 can4 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他叫長陳陞。
examples.english_sentence: His name is Cheung Chan-sing.

mandarin_meaning: 長頸瓶／長頸罐（指頸部較長的瓶罐，常用來指啤酒等長頸瓶）；也可比喻脖子很長的人
english_meaning: literally 'long-necked jar/bottle' — a long-necked bottle (e.g. beer bottle); colloquially used to describe someone with a long neck
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指頸部較長的罐或瓶，粵語口語中常用來指長頸的酒瓶（例如啤酒），有時也用作比喻，形容人脖子長。
explanation_english: Literally refers to a jar or bottle with a long neck. In Cantonese slang it commonly denotes a long-necked bottle (for example a beer bottle) and can be used metaphorically to describe a person with a long neck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰支長頸罌啤酒幾好飲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zi1 coeng4 geng2 jeng1 be1 zau2 gei2 hou2 jam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那支長頸瓶啤酒挺好喝的。
examples.english_sentence: That long-necked beer bottle tastes pretty good.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個脖子長到好似長頸罌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 bot6 zi2 coeng4 dou3 hou2 ci5 coeng4 geng2 jeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的脖子長得像長頸瓶。
examples.english_sentence: His neck is so long, like a long-necked bottle.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）長條的魚；（俗）形容人瘦長
english_meaning: literally 'long fish'; colloquially used to describe a person who is very tall and thin
explanation_mandarin: 「長魚」字面意思是長條的魚，在粵語口語中可用作俚語，非正式地形容一個人瘦長、身形像條長魚。此用法較為口語化，並非標準書面語，地域使用上以香港或廣東地區口語為主，亦可能較少見或因人而異。
explanation_english: Literally 'long fish'. In Cantonese colloquial speech it can be used as slang to describe someone who is very tall and thin — their body shape being likened to a long fish. This is informal and regional usage, not standard written language, and may be uncommon depending on speaker.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個仔成日俾人講係條長魚，件衫成日唔啱身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 zai2 seng4 jat6 bei2 jan4 gong2 hai6 tiu4 coeng4 jyu4, gin6 saam1 seng4 jat6 m4 aap3 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他兒子常被人說是條長魚，衣服經常不合身。
examples.english_sentence: People often call his son a 'long fish' — his clothes never fit him.

jyutping: coeng4 ming6 zai3 coeng4 ming6 waan4
mandarin_meaning: 长命债长命还（俗语/谚语），表示对救命或重大恩情会在有生之年或长久地报答；也可引申为欠下的债或人情终会偿还。
english_meaning: A Cantonese proverb meaning 'a long-life debt is repaid with a long life' — used to say a debt of gratitude (especially for saving someone's life) will be repaid over time; more generally, debts or favors will eventually be returned.
explanation_mandarin: 此語常用於表示對救命或重大恩情的回報，帶有'必定會還'或'在有生之年慢慢償還'的意思，也常用來形容人情債會在未來還清。
explanation_english: Used to express that a debt of gratitude (often for saving a life) will be repaid in due course or over a long time. It can also imply that any debt or obligation will eventually be settled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 多謝你救咗我一命，呢份長命債我會長命還。
examples.jyutping_sentence: do1 ze6 nei5 gau3 zo2 ngo5 jat1 ming6, ni1 fan6 coeng4 ming6 zai3 ngo5 wui5 coeng4 ming6 waan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 谢谢你救了我一命，这份长命债我会在有生之年偿还。
examples.english_sentence: Thanks for saving my life — I'll repay this life-debt during my lifetime.

synonyms: 滴水之恩，當以湧泉相報

mandarin_meaning: 持久、耐用；能維持很長一段時間
english_meaning: long-lasting; durable; lasting for a long time
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，用來形容某物或某種狀態可以持續很長時間、耐用或不易壞，也可泛指長時間的功夫或耐性。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to describe something that lasts a long time or is durable; can also refer more generally to a long period of effort or patience.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫唔係長命工夫，洗幾次就爛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 m4 hai6 coeng4 ming6 gung1 fu1, sai2 gei2 ci3 zau6 laan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件衣服不耐穿，洗几次就破了。
examples.english_sentence: This shirt isn't durable — it rips after a few washes.

jyutping: coeng4 ming6 gung1 fu1 coeng4 ming6 zou6
mandarin_meaning: 活着就得一直工作（活到老、干到老）；表示长期劳动或无奈地持续干活。
english_meaning: As long as one lives, one must keep working; a resigned saying about lifelong or continuous labor.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容只要活着就要继续做事或干活，常带有对长期劳作的无奈或习以为常的意味。
