explanation_english: An idiom describing that things proceed very smoothly and without obstacles; often used to wish someone success or smooth progress.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 希望你新嘅生意順風順水，越做越好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hei1 mong6 nei5 san1 ge3 saang1 ji3 seon6 fung1 seon6 seoi2, jyut6 zou6 jyut6 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 希望你的生意顺风顺水，越做越好。
examples.english_sentence: I hope your business goes smoothly and becomes more and more successful.

jyutping: gu3 dak1 jau1 fu3 jau6 lat1 gat1
mandarin_meaning: 顾此失彼；只顾小节而忽略重要的事
english_meaning: To fuss over trivial matters or appearances and thereby neglect important things; to attend to the wrong things
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俚語，形容只顧着處理一些瑣碎或表面的事情，而忽略了更重要或關鍵的事；通常帶批評或嘲諷的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase describing someone who fusses over trivial or superficial matters and neglects more important issues; usually used with a critical or ironic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你淨係顧得优裤又甩髻，重要嘅嘢都唔理，遲啲就會出事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zing6 hai6 gu3 dak1 jau1 fu3 jau6 lat1 gat1, zung6 jiu3 ge3 je5 dou1 m4 lei5, ci4 di1 zau6 wui5 ceot1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你只顾着小节而忽略了重要的事情，迟早会出事。
examples.english_sentence: You're only fussing over trivial matters and neglecting important ones — something will go wrong sooner or later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做報告嗰陣佢成日顧得优裤又甩髻，完全跟唔到重點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 bou3 gou3 go2 zan6 keoi5 sing4 jat6 gu3 dak1 jau1 fu3 jau6 lat1 gat1, jyun4 cyun4 gan1 m4 dou3 zung6 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做报告的时候，他总是只顾着小事，完全抓不到重点。
examples.english_sentence: During the presentation he kept getting hung up on trivial things and completely missed the main points.

mandarin_meaning: 领取 / 領取（東西、款項等）
english_meaning: to receive; to collect; to pick up (items, payments, benefits)
explanation_mandarin: 「领嘢」是廣東話口語，意思是去領取或收取某樣東西或款項。通常用於領工資、獎金、包裹或福利等。與「拎嘢/攞嘢」相比，「領嘢」較偏向正式或由機構發放的領取行為。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to receive or collect something (items, payments, benefits). Commonly used for collecting salary, bonuses, parcels, or welfare. Compared with verbs like 'ling1/lo2 je5' meaning to take/carry, 'ling5 je5' often implies an official or issued collection.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日要去公司領嘢，聽講有獎金。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 gung1 si1 ling5 je5, teng1 gong2 jau5 zoeng2 gam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天要去公司領取東西，聽說有獎金。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to the company today to collect something; I heard there's a bonus.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我去郵局領嘢，拎包裹返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 heoi3 jau4 guk6 ling5 je5, ling1 baau1 gwo2 faan1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我去郵局領取包裹，拿回來。
examples.english_sentence: I went to the post office to pick up my parcel and brought it back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你記唔記得去福利署領嘢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gei3 m4 gei3 dak1 heoi3 fu6 lei6 cyu3 ling5 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你記得去社會福利署領取東西嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Did you remember to go to the Social Welfare Department to collect the items?

mandarin_meaning: 迷信風水或從事風水行業的人（俗稱）
english_meaning: a person who practices or is obsessive about feng shui; (colloquial) someone who relies on feng shui for decisions
explanation_mandarin: 「風水生」是香港廣東話中的俗稱，用來形容經常相信風水、會替人看風水或以風水為業的人。語氣可中性亦可帶貶義，視語境而定。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "風水生" is a colloquial term for someone who frequently believes in feng shui, consults or practices feng shui. The term can be neutral or mildly derogatory depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁迷信風水生講嘅嘢，實際情況都要考慮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 mai4 seon3 fung1 seoi2 saang1 gong2 ge3 je5, sat6 zai3 cing4 fong3 dou1 jiu3 haau2 leoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別那麼迷信風水生說的話，實際情況也要考慮。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so superstitious about what feng shui people say; you still need to consider the real situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 搬屋之前佢去搵咗個風水生擺位，話咁做對屋企運勢有幫助。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bun1 uk1 zi1 cin4 keoi5 heoi3 wan2 zo2 go3 fung1 seoi2 saang1 baai2 wai6, waa6 gam2 zou6 deoi3 uk1 kei2 wan6 se3 jau5 bong1 zo6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 搬家之前他去找了一個風水生擺位，說這樣做對家裡運勢有幫助。
examples.english_sentence: Before moving house he consulted a feng shui person to arrange the layout, saying it would help the household's luck.

mandarin_meaning: 過時、不再流行
english_meaning: out of fashion; outdated; unfashionable
explanation_mandarin: 表示某物或某事已經過時、不再受歡迎或不符合當前潮流。常用來形容款式、潮流、想法等。
explanation_english: Indicates that something has become outdated or is no longer in fashion or popular. Commonly used to describe styles, trends, or ideas.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫而家有啲風舊，年輕人唔會著。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 ji4 gaa1 jau5 di1 fung1 gau6, nin4 hing1 jan4 m4 wui5 zoek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件衣服現在有點過時，年輕人不會穿。
examples.english_sentence: This piece of clothing is a bit out of fashion now; young people won't wear it.

mandarin_meaning: （非正式）愛說風涼話或愛誇耀、愛出風頭的人（地區性、俚語用法）
english_meaning: (colloquial) a person who makes sarcastic/judgemental remarks, shows off, or brags (regional slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「風鱓」屬於廣東話的非正式俚語或地方用語，用來貶義地形容喜歡講風涼話、愛出風頭或愛誇耀、唔實在的人。此詞使用並不普遍，具地區性或口語化特徵。
explanation_english: “風鱓” is an informal Cantonese slang term, used pejoratively to describe someone who makes sarcastic/judgemental remarks, shows off, or brags. It is regional and colloquial rather than standard vocabulary.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度講大話，真係個風鱓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 gong2 daai6 waa6, zan1 hai6 go3 fung1 saan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在那裡說大話，真的是個風鱓。
examples.english_sentence: He’s always lying and bragging — he really is a 'fungsaan'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽佢嗰啲評論，幾風鱓，好傷人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 keoi5 go2 di1 ping4 leon6, gei2 fung1 saan3, hou2 soeng1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽他那些評論，挺冷嘲熱諷的，很傷人。
examples.english_sentence: Listening to his comments — quite snide and hurtful.

mandarin_meaning: 油腔滑調、愛出風頭或善於花言巧語的人
english_meaning: a slick, slippery person; a smooth talker or show-off
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語 / 俚語（名詞，貶義）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面為「風」與「鱔（鰻魚）」，比喻人說話油滑、善用花言巧語或愛出風頭，難以捉摸且常帶貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term literally combining 'wind' and 'eel' to describe someone slippery and slick — a smooth talker or attention-seeker who is hard to pin down. Usually pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺派對度扮晒大嘢，真係個風鱔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 paai3 deoi6 dou6 baan6 saai3 daai6 je5, zan1 hai6 go3 fung1 sin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在派對上裝腔作勢，真是個愛出風頭的人。
examples.english_sentence: He always acts like a big shot at parties — such a show-off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好畀佢呃，佢係個風鱔，聽落幾好都唔好信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 keoi5 aak1, keoi5 hai6 go3 fung1 sin6, teng1 lok6 gei2 hou2 dou1 m4 hou2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別讓他騙了，他是個花言巧語的人，聽起來再好也別相信。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be fooled by him — he's a smooth talker; don't trust him even if he sounds convincing.

mandarin_meaning: （速度）非常快；（時間）過得很快
english_meaning: so fast; extremely quick (also used to say time flies)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容速度很快，或感嘆時間流逝得很快。屬於口語/廣東話俗語表達。
explanation_english: Used to describe something happening very quickly or to express that time passes quickly. It's a Cantonese colloquial/slang expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 時間飛咁快，轉眼間已經十年喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si4 gaan1 fei1 gam2 faai3, zyun2 ngaan5 gaan1 ji5 ging1 sap6 nin4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 時間過得真快，轉眼已經十年了。
examples.english_sentence: Time flies so fast — in the blink of an eye it's already been ten years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢跑得飛咁快，追都追唔到佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 paau2 dak1 fei1 gam2 faai3, zeoi1 dou1 zeoi1 m4 dou2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他跑得非常快，追都追不到他。
examples.english_sentence: He runs so fast that you can't catch him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲貨車開得飛咁快，好危險喎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 fo3 ce1 hoi1 dak1 fei1 gam2 faai3, hou2 ngai4 him2 wo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些貨車開得非常快，很危險。
examples.english_sentence: Those trucks were going so fast — very dangerous.

mandarin_meaning: 放飛機；爽約；無故不出席（翹班、放人鸽子）
english_meaning: to stand someone up; to flake on plans; to skip work or an appointment
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語（俚語）用法，通常指答應會出現或參加但最後無故缺席或爽約，相當於「放飛機」或「翹班」。此詞區域性強，使用頻率較口語化。
explanation_english: Cantonese colloquial slang meaning to fail to show up for an agreed meeting or duty — i.e., to stand someone up, flake on plans, or skip work. It is informal and regionally used, similar to 'to flake' or 'to stand someone up'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話會嚟，但最後又飛宮咗我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 wui5 lai4, daan6 zeoi6 hau6 jau6 fei1 gung1 zo2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说会来，但最后又放了我鸽子。
examples.english_sentence: He said he'd come, but in the end he stood me up.

mandarin_meaning: 飛機恤（非正式用語）
english_meaning: literally "airplane shirt"; colloquial/rare term for a T‑shirt (often one with an airplane print)
explanation_mandarin: 「飛機裇」為廣東話的非正式說法，字面上是「飛機」加上「恤（衫）」，可用來指T恤，尤其是印有飛機圖案或趣味圖案的T恤。此用法較口語化且不算普遍，部分情況可視為「飛機恤」的寫法變體。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning "airplane shirt" (飛機 + 恤). It is used informally to refer to a T‑shirt, especially novelty T‑shirts printed with airplane motifs. The term is informal and relatively uncommon, a variant spelling of 飛機恤.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢著住件飛機裇，好得意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoek3 zyu6 gin6 fei1 gei1 seot1, hou2 dak1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他穿著那件飛機裇，很可愛。
examples.english_sentence: He's wearing that "fei gei seot" (airplane shirt) — it's cute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間舖頭賣緊好多飛機裇，上面印咗飛機圖案。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 pou3 tau4 maai6 gan2 hou2 do1 fei1 gei1 seot1, soeng6 min6 jan3 zo2 fei1 gei1 tou4 ngon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間店在賣很多飛機裇，上面印有飛機圖案。
examples.english_sentence: That shop is selling lots of "fei gei seot" with airplane prints on them.

mandarin_meaning: 俚語：手淫（即“打飛機”）；也可指經常手淫的人
english_meaning: Slang for masturbation (to 'jerk off'); can also refer to a person who masturbates frequently
explanation_mandarin: 「飛機銻」是香港粵語俚語，與「打飛機」意思相近，用來描述手淫這一行為，或稱呼經常手淫的人。屬非正式、口語用法。
explanation_english: “飛機銻” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang similar to “打飛機”, referring to the act of masturbation or to someone who regularly masturbates. It is informal and colloquial.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做啲唔好意思講嘅嘢，啲人叫佢係飛機銻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zou6 di1 m4 hou2 ji3 si1 gong2 ge3 je5, di1 jan4 giu3 keoi5 hai6 fei1 gei1 tai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常做一些不好意思說的事，大家都說他是個飛機銻。
examples.english_sentence: He often does things people are embarrassed to talk about; people call him a 'fei1 gei1 tai1' (masturbator).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講到性話題時，佢有時會用「飛機銻」嚟開玩笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 dou3 sing3 waa6 tai4 si4, keoi5 jau5 si4 wui5 jung6 “fei1 gei1 tai1” lai4 hoi1 waan2 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 談到性話題時，他有時會用「飛機銻」來開玩笑。
examples.english_sentence: When sex topics come up, he sometimes jokes by saying 'fei1 gei1 tai1'.

mandarin_meaning: 飞翼；翅膀；（航空）飞翼式飞机设计
english_meaning: wing; wing (of a bird or aircraft); flying-wing (aircraft design)
explanation_mandarin: 可指生物的翅膀或飛行器的翼；在航空學上也指「飛翼式」的機體設計，即沒有明顯機身與機翼分界的整體翼面構型。
explanation_english: Refers to a wing (of a bird or aircraft). In aeronautics it also denotes the 'flying-wing' configuration — an aircraft design where the wing and fuselage are integrated into a single lifting surface.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰款飛翼無人機嘅設計好新穎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 fun2 fei1 jik6 mou4 jan4 gei1 ge3 cit3 gai3 hou2 san1 wing5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那款飞翼无人机的设计很新颖。
examples.english_sentence: That flying-wing drone's design is very novel.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 飛翼嘅形狀會影響飛機嘅空氣動力學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fei1 jik6 ge3 jing4 zong6 wui5 jing2 hoeng2 fei1 gei1 ge3 hung1 hei3 dung6 lik6 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 飞翼的形状会影响飞机的空气动力学。
examples.english_sentence: The shape of a flying wing affects an aircraft's aerodynamics.

mandarin_meaning: 再度引起關注／再次掀起風波；重新流行或重新成為話題
english_meaning: to flare up again; to resurface in public attention or controversy; to regain popularity
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指某件事、舊案或舊物再次成為公眾關注的話題或重新流行起來，常用於新聞或談論熱點時。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning that an issue, old case, or item has become a topic of public attention again or has regained popularity; often used when something resurfaces in the news or social discussion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊案又飜風，記者又問番一次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 on3 jau6 faan1 fung1, gei3 ze2 jau6 man6 faan1 jat1 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 舊案又翻起風波，記者再問了一次。
examples.english_sentence: The old case has flared up again; reporters asked about it once more.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰首舊歌突然又飜風，成班年輕人開始翻唱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 sau2 gau6 go1 dat6 syun4 jau6 faan1 fung1, sing4 baan1 nin4 heng1 jan4 hoi1 ci2 faan1 coeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那首舊歌突然又重新流行，很多年輕人開始翻唱。
examples.english_sentence: That old song suddenly became popular again; many young people started covering it.

mandarin_meaning: 了不起的本領 / 誇張、不切實際的本事
english_meaning: an incredible or fanciful skill/ability; a tall tale or exaggerated claim
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，常用來形容某人自稱有很厲害或超乎常理的本領，通常帶有誇張、不太可信或戲謔的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to describe someone claiming an extraordinary or supernatural ability. Often carries a sense of exaggeration, incredulity, or playful mockery.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日自稱有飛天本事，實際只係吹牛罷了。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zi6 cing1 jau5 fei1 tin1 bun2 si6, sat6 zai3 zi2 hai6 ceoi1 ngau4 baa6 liu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是自稱有飛天本領，實際上只是吹牛而已。
examples.english_sentence: He always claims to have amazing abilities, but actually he's just bragging.

jyutping: 未知（查無可靠拼音記錄）
mandarin_meaning: 不詳（疑為罕見字詞或造字，未有可靠定義）
english_meaning: Unknown/obscure Cantonese term — no reliable definition found
explanation_mandarin: 在常用字典和語料庫中查無此詞的可靠解釋。可能屬於罕見字、方言變體、筆誤或新造詞。若需確切含義，建議向熟悉當地方言的長者或專家查詢原始語境資料。
explanation_english: No reliable explanation is found in available dictionaries or corpora. The term may be a rare character sequence, a regional variant, a typo, or a newly coined word. For a definitive meaning, consult local speakers or specialists and check original contextual sources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺舊書入面見到「飞天蠄𮔚」，但唔知係乜意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gau6 syu1 jap6 min6 gin3 dou2 '飞天蠄𮔚', daan6 m4 zi1 hai6 mat1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在舊書裡見到「飞天蠄𮔚」，但不知道是什麼意思。
examples.english_sentence: I found '飞天蠄𮔚' in an old book, but I don't know what it means.

mandarin_meaning: 猛然出手攻擊、抓住機會狠狠打擊（口語／俚語）
english_meaning: To pounce on and bite; to launch a sudden, fierce attack. Figuratively, to seize an opportunity and strike hard (colloquial/slang).
explanation_mandarin: 「飞擒大咬」是廣東話口語或俚語，字面意思為迅速擒拿並咬住；引申指突然出手、猛攻或抓住對方失誤猛然抨擊，常用於形容言語或行動上的猛烈反擊或揭短。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase literally meaning 'pounce, grab and bite.' Figuratively used to describe making a sudden, aggressive attack—physical, verbal, or opportunistic—or pouncing on a mistake/opportunity to strike hard.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見對方分心，立刻飛擒大咬，奪返個位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 deoi3 fong1 fan1 sam1, lap6 hak1 fei1 cam4 daai6 ngaau5, doek6 faan1 go3 wai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到對方分心，立刻出手猛攻，奪回那個位置。
examples.english_sentence: He saw his opponent was distracted, immediately pounced and retook the position.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新聞一爆出差錯，網民即刻飛擒大咬，公司高層都唔敢出聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 man4 jat1 baau3 ceot1 caa1 co3, mong5 man4 zik1 hak1 fei1 cam4 daai6 ngaau5, gung1 si1 gou1 cang4 dou1 m4 gam2 ceot1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新聞一爆出差錯，網民立刻猛烈抨擊，公司高層都不敢出聲。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as the mistake in the news broke, netizens pounced mercilessly, and the company's executives didn't dare respond.

jyutping: fei1 gei1 daa2 gaau1, gou1 dau2
mandarin_meaning: 大吵大闹、打架；制造骚动（口语、方言用法）
english_meaning: to quarrel/brawl noisily; to make a commotion (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 此短語為廣東話口語，常用以描述多人在公共場所大聲爭吵或打鬥、製造騷亂。文字有不同寫法（如「高斗」「高窦」），屬方言或俚語用法，語氣可帶貶義或戲謔。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe people making a loud quarrel or brawl and causing a commotion in public. The written form varies (e.g. 高斗 / 高窦). It is regional/slang and can sound derogatory or humorous depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲人喺酒樓門口飛機打交，高斗起晒，唔知點算。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 jan4 hai2 zau2 lau4 mun4 hau2 fei1 gei1 daa2 gaau1, gou1 dau2 hei2 saai3, m4 zi1 dim2 syun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人在酒樓門口大吵大鬧、打架，鬧得不可收拾，真不知道怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: People were brawling noisily at the restaurant entrance, causing a big scene — nobody knew what to do.

jyutping: fei1 gei1 fo2 zuk1, siu1 wan4
mandarin_meaning: 火烧云／晚霞（形容天空被夕阳照得像着了火似的）
english_meaning: fiery clouds; a sky ablaze at sunset (describes red/orange sunset clouds)
explanation_mandarin: 这是一个形象的描写性短语，字面指“飞机火烛、烧云”，常用来描述傍晚或朝霞时天边呈现出灿烂的红色、橙色云彩（即火烧云、晚霞）。在口语或文学中也可作比喻，用来形容场面或气氛热烈、壮丽。
explanation_english: A figurative, descriptive phrase literally meaning "airplane candle, burning clouds." It commonly refers to fiery clouds at sunrise or sunset (red/orange sky), i.e. spectacular evening/morning sky. It can also be used metaphorically to describe an intense or dramatic atmosphere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚個天空成晒飛機火燭、燒雲，好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 go3 tin1 hung1 seng4 saai3 fei1 gei1 fo2 zuk1, siu1 wan4, hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚的天空完全被火烧云染红，很漂亮。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight the sky is filled with fiery clouds at sunset — it's very beautiful.

mandarin_meaning: 不速之客；突如其來的訪客
english_meaning: an unexpected visitor; someone who shows up out of the blue
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，用來形容沒經通知、突然出現的訪客或插入者，帶有非正式或略帶輕微批評的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for a person who appears suddenly or without notice (an unexpected guest or someone who 'crashes' in); informal and slightly pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個飛來蜢，成日無預告就飛來我哋屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 fei1 loi4 maang5, seng4 jat6 mou4 jyu6 gou3 zau6 fei1 loi4 ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個不速之客，經常沒預告就來我們家。
examples.english_sentence: He's an unexpected guest — he often shows up at our place without warning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚唔好邀請佢，唔想有飛來蜢亂入派對。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 m4 hou2 jiu1 cing2 keoi5, m4 soeng2 jau5 fei1 loi4 maang5 lyun6 jap6 paai3 deoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚別邀請他，不想有不速之客闖入派對。
examples.english_sentence: Don't invite him tonight; we don't want any unexpected guests crashing the party.

mandarin_meaning: 飞象过河（比喻做不可能或突破常规的事）
english_meaning: literally 'a flying elephant crossing the river'; metaphor for attempting the impossible or making a bold/unconventional breakthrough
explanation_mandarin: 来源可追溯到象棋与比喻用法：象通常不能过河，‘飞象过河’用来形容做不可能的事、突破常规或冒险的举动。
explanation_english: Originating from the imagery of an elephant crossing a river (in xiangqi an elephant normally cannot cross the river), 'flying elephant across the river' is used figuratively to describe attempting the impossible, taking a bold risk, or breaking conventions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話要喺一個月內完成嗰份計劃，簡直係飛象過河。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 jiu3 hai6 jat1 go3 jyut6 noi6 jyun4 sing4 go2 fan6 gai3 waak6, gaan2 zik6 hai6 fei1 zoeng6 gwo3 ho4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说要在一个月内完成那份计划，简直是飞象过河。
examples.english_sentence: He says he'll finish that project within a month — it's practically impossible.

mandarin_meaning: 收賄 / 吃回扣
english_meaning: to take a bribe; to pocket a kickback or illicit cut
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，字面為「吃三兩銀」，指收受賄賂、拿回扣或暗中取得不當利益，通常帶貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression literally 'to eat three taels (of silver)'; it means to accept bribes, take kickbacks, or secretly pocket illicit gains; usually derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個官員成日食三兩，案件就查唔清。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 gun1 jyun4 sing4 jat6 sik6 saam1 loeng5, on3 gin6 zau6 caa4 m4 cing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個官員經常收賄，案件就查不清楚。
examples.english_sentence: That official often takes bribes, so the cases can't be properly investigated.

mandarin_meaning: 大吃一顿；盛宴
english_meaning: to have a huge meal; to feast; to hold a lavish banquet
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，字面是“吃九大簋”（簋为大食器），用来形容大吃一顿或举行盛大的宴席，常用于庆祝或聚会场合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "eat nine big food vessels" (簋 refers to a large food container). It describes having a huge meal or holding a lavish banquet, often used for celebrations or big gatherings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去酒樓食九大簋，齊齊慶祝阿媽生日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 zau2 lau4 sik6 gau2 daai6 gwai2, cai4 cai4 hing3 zuk1 aa3 maa1 saang1 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去酒楼大吃一顿，一起庆祝妈妈生日。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight we're going to the restaurant to have a big feast to celebrate Mom's birthday together.

mandarin_meaning: 手淫；自慰（粗俗俚語）
english_meaning: to masturbate (vulgar slang, manual self-stimulation)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語粗俗俚語，字面上是「吃五指果」，實際上指以手進行性自我刺激（自慰）。屬於非正式及粗俗用語，常用於口語或粗鄙語境中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar slang expression literally meaning "eat five-finger fruit." It refers to manual masturbation (self-stimulation with the hand). It is informal and coarse, used in colloquial or crude contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一個人喺房度食五指果，唔好入嚟打擾佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4 hai2 fong2 dou6 sik6 ng5 zi2 gwo2, m4 hou2 jap6 lei4 daa2 jiu6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一個人在房間裡自慰，別進來打擾他。
examples.english_sentence: He was masturbating alone in his room; don't come in and disturb him.

cantonese: 食人一碗饭，做到头都烂；食人一碗粥，做到头都秃
jyutping: sik6 jan4 jat1 wun2 faan6, zou6 dou3 tau4 dou1 laan6; sik6 jan4 jat1 wun2 zuk1, zou6 dou3 tau4 dou1 duk1
mandarin_meaning: 吃別人給的飯（或粥）就得對供養自己的人完全忠心服從，形容依附他人、阿諛奉承或賣命效力。
english_meaning: If you eat someone's rice (or porridge), you must serve them to the end — used to describe being beholden, totally submissive, or sycophantic toward the one who provides for you.
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語用飯與粥做比喻，說明依靠別人生活就要對供養者無條件效忠或服從，常用以批評逢迎拍馬、失去自主的人際關係行為。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb uses 'rice' and 'porridge' as metaphors: if you rely on someone for sustenance, you're expected to be totally loyal or obedient to them. It's often used to criticize sycophancy, servility, or loss of independence due to dependence on others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日拍老闆馬屁，真係食人一碗饭，做到头都烂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 paak3 maa5 pei3, zan1 hai6 sik6 jan4 jat1 wun2 faan6, zou6 dou3 tau4 dou1 laan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天拍老板馬屁，真是吃別人的一碗飯，做到頭都爛。
examples.english_sentence: He flatters the boss all the time; he's really someone who eats off others and will serve them to the bitter end.

synonyms: 吃人嘴短 (吃人嘴短，拿人手短)

mandarin_meaning: 宰客／剝削人（以不合理方式收取費用或占人便宜）
english_meaning: to rip people off; to exploit or overcharge someone
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容商家、機構或個人以不合理或掠奪性的方式向顧客或他人索取金錢、收取額外費用或占便宜，相當於「宰客」或「剝削」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to describe businesses, organizations, or people who exploit others by overcharging, charging unreasonable extra fees, or otherwise ripping people off. Equivalent to 'to rip off' or 'to exploit'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間旅館真係食人只车，房租又貴，仲成日收奇怪嘅費用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 leoi5 gun2 zan1 hai6 sik6 jan4 zek3 ce1, fong4 zou1 jau6 gwai3, zung6 sing4 jat6 sau1 kei4 gwaai3 ge3 fai3 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間旅館真是宰客，房租又貴，還經常收一些奇怪的費用。
examples.english_sentence: That hotel really rips people off; the room rates are expensive and they keep charging strange fees.

mandarin_meaning: 被騙、吃虧或落空
english_meaning: to be cheated, take a loss, or have one's expectations dashed
explanation_mandarin: 「食冻柑」是香港廣東話的俚語，常用來形容原本有期望、計劃或交易卻落空、被耍或吃了虧。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression used to describe having one's expectations dashed, being tricked/cheated, or suffering a loss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我以為嗰筆生意有得賺，點知最後食冻柑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 wai6 go2 bat1 saang1 ji3 jau5 dak1 zaan6, dim2 zi1 zeoi6 hau6 sik6 dung3 gam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我以為那筆生意可以賺錢，結果最後被騙/吃虧了。
examples.english_sentence: I thought that deal would make money, but in the end I got cheated/took a loss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢約我出嚟，臨時走數，我真係食冻柑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 joek3 ngo5 ceot1 lai4, lam4 si4 zau2 sou3, ngo5 zan1 hai6 sik6 dung3 gam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他約我出來，臨時放我鴿子，我真的很失望／被耍了。
examples.english_sentence: He stood me up at the last minute; I was really left hanging.

mandarin_meaning: 吃北风（挨饿、失业、没钱或没收入而生活困窘）
english_meaning: To go hungry; to be penniless or unemployed (literally 'eat the north wind')
explanation_mandarin: 「食北风」原指挨饿，現常用來形容失業、沒錢或沒有收入而生活困窘，屬於俗語/俚語。
explanation_english: Originally 'to eat the north wind' meaning to starve; now commonly used to describe being unemployed, penniless, or having no income. It's a colloquial idiom/slang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢公司裁員之後，依家成日都係屋企食北风。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gung1si1 coi4jyun4 zi1hau6, ji1gaa1 sing4 jat6 dou1 hai6 uk1kei2 sik6 bak1 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他公司裁員之後，現在常常在家裡吃北风。
examples.english_sentence: After his company laid off employees, he's been at home unemployed and going hungry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年完咗，仲未搵到工，唔想再食北风啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 wan4 zo2, zung6 mei6 wan2 dou3 gung1, m4 soeng2 zoi3 sik6 bak1 fung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年已經過了，還沒找到工作，不想再挨餓了。
examples.english_sentence: The New Year has passed and I still haven't found a job—I don't want to go hungry anymore.

mandarin_meaning: （1）打成和局、两边平手；（2）（牌类）胡牌，通常指吃別人打出的牌而胡
english_meaning: (1) to end in a draw / to come out even; (2) (in mahjong) to win by claiming another player's discard (to 'hu')
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法：1) 指比賽、賭局等沒有分出勝負，雙方打成平手，互不輸贏；2) 在麻將等牌局中，指吃別人打出的牌而胡牌（也寫作「食糊／食胡」）。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese: 1) to finish a contest or bet with no winner — a draw or breaking even; 2) in mahjong/gaming contexts, to win by claiming another player's discard (often written/said as 'sik6 wu4' / '食糊').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今場波兩隊踢成和，賽果係食和。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 coeng4 bo1 loeng5 deoi6 tek3 seng4 wo4, saai3 gwo2 hai6 sik6 wo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这场比赛两队打成平局，结果是和局。
examples.english_sentence: The match ended in a draw — it's a tie.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱食糊，贏咗一把。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ngaam1 ngaam1 sik6 wu4, jing4 zo2 jat1 baa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我刚刚胡牌了，赢了一局。
examples.english_sentence: I just won a hand (I claimed a discard and hu'd).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次賭局大家唔想硬拗，最後決定食和。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 dou2 guk6 daai6 gaa1 m4 soeng2 ngaang6 aau3, zeoi3 hau6 kyut3 ding6 sik6 wo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次赌局大家不想再硬拼，最后决定打成和局。
examples.english_sentence: In this bet nobody wanted to keep fighting, so they agreed to call it a draw.

mandarin_meaning: 上當／被騙、被耍
english_meaning: to be duped/cheated; to be made a fool of
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，表示被人欺騙或耍弄，上當受騙。通常用來形容買到假貨或被人佈局吃虧。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression meaning to be deceived, tricked, or made a fool of. Often used when someone is cheated (for example, buying a fake item) or otherwise taken advantage of.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我以為件衫係真，點知買咗先發現係假，真係食咗草龙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5wai6 gin6 saam1 hai6 zan1, dim2 zi1 maai5 zo2 sin1 faat3jin4 hai6 gaa2, zan1 hai6 sik6 zo2 cou2 lung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我以為那件襯衫是真的，結果買了才發現是假的，真是上當了。
examples.english_sentence: I thought that shirt was genuine, but after buying it I found out it was fake — I really got duped.

mandarin_meaning: 吃醋；嫉妒
english_meaning: to be jealous; to feel envious or resentful
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語/俗語，表示對別人（如對方的關係或待遇）感到嫉妒、不服或吃味，類似普通話的「吃醋」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to feel jealous or envious of someone (often over relationships or preferential treatment). It corresponds to Mandarin '吃醋' and English 'to be jealous'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好食咸水啦，佢只係講笑啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sik6 haam4 seoi2 laa1, keoi5 zi2 hai6 gong2 siu3 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要吃醋了，他只是開玩笑而已。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be jealous — he was only joking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 睇住佢成日同女同事傾偈，你就開始食咸水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tai2 zyu6 keoi5 sing4 jat6 tung4 neoi5 tung4 si6 king1 gai2, nei5 zau6 hoi1 ci2 sik6 haam4 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到他經常和女同事聊天，你就開始吃醋了。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing him always chatting with a female colleague, you started to get jealous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路見到人哋有玩具就會食咸水，好快又會忘記。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 gin3 dou3 jan4 dei6 jau5 waan2 geoi6 zau6 wui5 sik6 haam4 seoi2, hou2 faai3 jau6 wui5 mong4 gei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子看到別人有玩具就會吃醋，很快又會忘記。
examples.english_sentence: Kids will get jealous when they see others have toys, but they'll forget quickly.

cantonese: 食嘢唔做嘢，做嘢打烂嘢
jyutping: sik6 je5 m4 zou6 je5, zou6 je5 daa2 laan6 je5
mandarin_meaning: 只會吃不做事，做事還把東西弄壞
english_meaning: Only takes advantage (eats) without working; when they try to work they mess things up or break them
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人只會享受或占便宜、不願意做事；即使開始做事，通常也做得很差、把事情弄壞。帶有批評或嘲諷意味，常見於香港口語。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying used to criticize someone who takes advantage or shirks work; if they do try to work, they bunglingly ruin things. It has a critical/derogatory tone and is common in Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿John淨係食嘢唔做嘢，做嘢打烂嘢，點樣可以信佢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 John zing6 hai6 sik6 je5 m4 zou6 je5, zou6 je5 daa2 laan6 je5, dim2 joeng6 ho2 ji5 seon3 keoi5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: John 只會吃不做事，做事還把東西弄壞，怎麼能信他？
examples.english_sentence: John only eats and doesn't work; when he works he breaks things. How can we trust him?

jyutping: sik6 je5 daa2 bui3 zek3 lok6
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）吃東西時嗆到，需要拍背幫助把食物排出／咳出
english_meaning: Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to choke on food while eating and need someone to pat the back to help dislodge it
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，字面為「吃東西時拍（打）背脊把東西弄落（排出）」，通常指吃東西嗆到或噎到，需要拍背協助咳出或排出異物。多在家庭或照顧嬰幼兒時使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning 'eat and pat the back down.' It normally describes someone choking or being momentarily blocked when eating and needing another person to pat their back to help dislodge the food. Commonly used in family/care contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢食嘢打背脊落，差啲窒息，嚇死我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sik6 je5 daa2 bui3 zek3 lok6, caa1 di1 zat6 sik1, haak3 sei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他吃東西嗆到差點窒息，嚇死我了。
examples.english_sentence: He choked on his food and almost suffocated — it really scared me.

cantonese: 食嘢食味道，睇戏睇全套
jyutping: sik6 je5 sik6 mei6 dou6, tai2 hei3 tai2 cyun4 tou3
mandarin_meaning: 既然要做某件事，就要徹底享受或做好，不要半途而廢
english_meaning: If you're going to do something, do it fully — savor the food and experience the whole thing; don't do it half-heartedly.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話多用於勸人盡情投入或徹底去做某事。字面上指吃東西要吃出味道、看戲要看完整套，實際是「既然做就做足」的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to urge someone to fully enjoy or complete an activity. Literally 'when eating, taste it; when watching a movie, watch the whole set' — meaning 'if you're going to do it, do it properly.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 既然今次嚟香港玩，唔好留手，食嘢食味道，睇戏睇全套，盡情享受啲體驗啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gei3 jin4 gam1 ci3 lai4 hoeng1 gong2 waan2, m4 hou2 lau4 sau2, sik6 je5 sik6 mei6 dou6, tai2 hei3 tai2 cyun4 tou3, zeon6 cing4 hoeng2 sau6 di1 tai2 jim6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 既然这次来香港玩，就不要客氣，吃東西要吃出味道，看電影就看完整，盡情享受這些體驗吧。
examples.english_sentence: Since you're visiting Hong Kong this time, don't hold back — savor the food and watch the whole movie; fully enjoy the experience.

jyutping: sik6 do1 di1 daai6 tau4 coi3
mandarin_meaning: 多吃大头菜（字面意思：多吃萝卜/根菜）；口语上也可用来打趣地劝人多吃东西以增重或保健。
english_meaning: Eat more turnips (literal). Colloquially/jokingly: telling someone to eat more (to gain weight or for health).
explanation_mandarin: 「食多啲大头菜」是粤语口语短语，字面意思为“多吃大头菜/萝卜”。常用于字面劝人多吃蔬菜或作为打趣性的劝说，叫瘦或没胃口的人多吃东西以增重或保健。在年轻人和网络语境中，也有时被用作玩笑或引用与“大头菜”（例如电子游戏中的道具）相关的梗。
explanation_english: “食多啲大头菜” is a Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning “eat more turnips.” It’s commonly used literally to urge someone to eat more vegetables, or jokingly to tell someone who is thin or has no appetite to eat more to gain weight or stay healthy. In youth or online contexts it can also be used playfully or as a reference to cultural/gaming jokes involving “turnips.”

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你最近瘦咗，好似冇胃口，食多啲大頭菜啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zeoi3 gan6 sou3 zo2, hou2 ci5 mou5 wai6 hau2, sik6 do1 di1 daai6 tau4 coi3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你最近瘦了，好像没胃口，多吃点大头菜吧。
examples.english_sentence: You've lost weight recently and seem to have no appetite — eat more turnips.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽煲咗大頭菜湯，食多啲大頭菜，會暖啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa1 bou1 zo2 daai6 tau4 coi3 tong1, sik6 do1 di1 daai6 tau4 coi3, wui5 nyun5 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈煲了大头菜汤，多吃点大头菜，会暖和一些。
examples.english_sentence: Mom's made turnip soup — eat more turnips, it'll warm you up.

mandarin_meaning: 吃夜宵
english_meaning: eat a late-night snack / have supper
explanation_mandarin: 指在深夜或晚飯後吃輕便的食物，常見於香港的夜生活文化，可以是外出或在家吃。
explanation_english: Refers to eating snacks or a small meal late at night, usually after dinner; common in Hong Kong nightlife culture, whether eaten out or at home.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去旺角食夜宵啦？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 wong6 gok3 sik6 je6 siu1 laa1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去旺角吃夜宵吧？
examples.english_sentence: Shall we go to Mong Kok for late-night snacks tonight?

mandarin_meaning: 吃宵夜 / 吃夜粥
english_meaning: to have a late-night meal (literally 'eat night congee')
explanation_mandarin: 指在深夜吃東西，字面是吃粥，但在香港口語中常泛指吃宵夜或在晚上聚餐、夜間小吃。
explanation_english: Refers to eating a late-night meal or snack. Literally 'eat night congee', but in Hong Kong Cantonese it generally means having supper/late-night food or socializing over a late meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚加班到好夜，我哋去食夜粥慰勞一下自己。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 gaa1 baan1 dou3 hou2 je6, ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 je6 zuk1 wai6 lou4 jat1 haa6 zi6 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚加班到很晚，我們去吃宵夜慰勞一下自己。
examples.english_sentence: We worked late tonight — let's go have a late-night meal to treat ourselves.

mandarin_meaning: 惹上大麻烦；遭到严重的后果
english_meaning: to get into big trouble; to face severe consequences
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面意為「吃大茶飯」，用來表示會遭受嚴重後果或惹上大麻煩、被處罰或受責備。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally meaning "eat a big tea meal." It is used to say someone will get into serious trouble, face severe consequences, or be punished.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做，小心要食大茶飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 zou6, siu2 sam1 jiu3 sik6 daai6 caa4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样做，小心会惹上大麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: If you do that, be careful—you could get into big trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你偷公司錢，你肯定會食大茶飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 tau1 gung1 si1 cin2, nei5 hang2 ding6 wui5 sik6 daai6 caa4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你偷公司钱，你肯定会惹上大麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: If you steal from the company, you'll definitely be in big trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 吃大餐；大吃一顿
english_meaning: to eat a big/feast meal; to have a lavish meal; to treat someone
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，指吃豐富或奢華的一餐，或由別人請客大吃一頓，常用於慶祝或款待場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to have a sumptuous or lavish meal, often used for celebrations or when someone is treating others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去食大餐，慶祝你升職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 sik6 daai6 caan1, hing3 zuk1 nei5 sing1 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去吃大餐，庆祝你升职。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go have a big meal tonight to celebrate your promotion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話請我哋食大餐，大家好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 cing2 ngo5 dei6 sik6 daai6 caan1, daai6 gaa1 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说请我们吃大餐，大家很开心。
examples.english_sentence: He said he'll treat us to a big meal; everyone was happy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 年尾公司請客，我哋可以食大餐去慶祝一年辛苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nin4 mei5 gung1 si1 cing2 haak3, ngo5 dei6 ho2 ji5 sik6 daai6 caan1 heoi3 hing3 zuk1 jat1 nin4 san1 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 年底公司请客，我们可以吃大餐去庆祝一年的辛苦。
examples.english_sentence: The company is treating at year-end; we can have a big meal to celebrate a year's hard work.

mandarin_meaning: 夹在中间受气；两面受责备
english_meaning: to be caught in the middle and take the blame or suffer from both sides
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，形容某人夾在兩方之間，承受雙方指責或不公平待遇，處境尷尬或吃虧。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to be stuck between two parties and suffer or be blamed by both sides — to be caught in the middle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你兩邊都唔講清楚，搞到我要食夹棍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 loeng5 bin1 dou1 m4 gong2 cing1 co2, gaau2 dou3 ngo5 jiu3 sik6 gaap3 gwan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你兩邊都不说清楚，弄得我要夹在中间受气。
examples.english_sentence: Both sides aren't being clear, and it's making me get caught in the middle and take the blame.

cantonese: 食完五月粽，过咗百日又系冬
jyutping: sik6 jyun4 ng5 jyut6 zung2, gwo3 zo2 baak3 jat6 jau6 hai6 dung1
mandarin_meaning: 吃完五月的粽子，過了一百天又是冬天（諺語）
english_meaning: After eating the zongzi of the fifth lunar month, a hundred days later it's winter again (proverb)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗諺，原指天氣反常或變化無常——剛過端午不久竟又轉冷；也可比喻事物迅速回復原狀或變化反覆。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb describing sudden or unusual changes (especially in weather) — soon after Dragon Boat Festival it can feel like winter again; it can also metaphorically mean something quickly reverts to an earlier state or is changeable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝落雨又凍，老細笑住同我講：『食完五月粽，過咗百日又系冬。』
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 lok6 jyu5 jau6 dung3, lou5 sai3 siu3 zyu6 tung4 ngo5 gong2: 'sik6 jyun4 ng5 jyut6 zung2, gwo3 zo2 baak3 jat6 jau6 hai6 dung1.'
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上下雨又冷，老闆笑著對我說：「吃完五月粽，過了百日又是冬天。」
examples.english_sentence: It rained and was cold this morning; my boss laughed and said, 'After eating the zongzi in May, a hundred days later it's winter again.'

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）遭受屈辱、吃虧或落得很慘的下場（字面：吃屎、拉飯）
english_meaning: Vulgar slang for ending up humiliated, cheated, or in a miserable situation (literally "eat shit, shit rice").
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話粗俗俚語，用來形容某人最後遭受羞辱、吃虧或落得很差的下場。字面意思荒誕，通常帶貶義或警告意味。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang phrase used to describe someone ending up humiliated, cheated, or suffering a bad outcome. The literal image is crude and it is typically derogatory or used as a warning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂投資，冇做功課嘅話遲啲會食屎屙饭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 tau4zi1, mou5 zou6 gung1fo3 ge3 waa6 ci4di1 wui5 sik6 si2 o1 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要隨便投資，不做功課的話遲早會吃屎拉飯（比喻遭受慘敗或羞辱）。
examples.english_sentence: Don't invest recklessly; if you don't do your homework you'll end up eating shit and shitting rice (i.e., suffer a humiliating loss).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日畀人呃，仲唔醒目，大家都話佢以後會食屎屙饭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 bei2 jan4 ngaa6, zung6 m4 sing2 muk6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 keoi5 ji5 hau6 wui5 sik6 si2 o1 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是被人欺騙，又不長進，大家都說他以後會吃屎拉飯（比喻會遭遇慘況）。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps getting fooled and never learns; everyone says he'll end up eating shit and shitting rice (i.e., facing a miserable fate).

mandarin_meaning: 倒霉透顶；一连串很不顺利的事
english_meaning: extremely unlucky; experiencing a run of misfortunes
explanation_mandarin: 「食屎食着豆」是廣東話口語俚語，用來形容某人非常倒楣、接二連三出了不好的事，類似「倒霉透顶」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to describe someone who is extremely unlucky or has a streak of misfortunes — akin to 'having the worst luck' or 'things go from bad to worse.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今朝又遲到，仲畀老細鬧，真係食屎食着豆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ziu1 jau6 ci4 dou3, zung6 bei2 lou5 sai3 nau6, zan1 hai6 sik6 si2 sik6 zoek3 dau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天早上又迟到，還被老板骂，真是倒霉透顶。
examples.english_sentence: He was late again this morning and got scolded by the boss — he really had the worst luck.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語粗俗說法）倒霉透顶，遇到一连串不顺或麻烦
english_meaning: A vulgar Cantonese slang expression meaning to be extremely unlucky or to suffer a run of bad luck
explanation_mandarin: 「食屎食著豆」是粵語的粗俗俚語，字面為「吃屎還吃到豆」，用來形容非常倒霉或連續遇到不幸，語氣多帶幽默或貶損。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "eat shit and also eat beans." It is used to describe being extremely unlucky or having a streak of misfortunes; often used colloquially with humorous or derogatory tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日真係食屎食著豆，約錯咗時間仲俾人鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 sik6 si2 sik6 zoek3 dau6, joek3 co3 zo2 si4 gaan3 zung6 bei2 jan4 nau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天真倒楣，約錯了時間還被人罵。
examples.english_sentence: He's really unlucky today — he got the appointment time wrong and still got yelled at.

jyutping: sik6 dak1 haam4 jyu4 dai2 dak1 hot3
mandarin_meaning: 吃了咸魚要忍渴；自作自受，承擔後果
english_meaning: You must accept the consequences of your actions (literally: if you eat salted fish you must endure thirst).
explanation_mandarin: 表示做了某事就要承擔相應的後果。字面意思是吃了鹹魚就得忍渴，用來比喻自作自受或自負其果。
explanation_english: Expresses that one must bear the consequences of one's actions. Literally 'if you eat salted fish you must endure thirst' — used to mean 'you reap what you sow' or 'you made your bed, now lie in it.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你當初唔諗後果，依家要負責，食得咸魚抵得渴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dong1 co1 m4 lam2 hau6 gwo2, ji1 gaa1 jiu3 fu6 zaak3, sik6 dak1 haam4 jyu4 dai2 dak1 hot3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你當初不考慮後果，現在要負責，吃了鹹魚就得忍渴。
examples.english_sentence: You didn't think about the consequences before; now you must take responsibility — you've eaten salted fish, so you must endure the thirst.

mandarin_meaning: 能吃能睡 / 吃得睡得
english_meaning: not picky about food or sleeping arrangements; able to live simply and adapt easily
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人適應力強、不挑剔，能在簡單或不理想的環境下吃得好、睡得著。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who is adaptable and not fussy—can eat and sleep comfortably in simple or less-than-ideal conditions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好食得瞓得，旅行時住咩地方都唔介意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 sik6 dak1 fan3 dak1, leoi5 haang4 si4 zyu6 me1 dei6 fong1 dou1 m4 gaai3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很能吃能睡，旅行時住什麼地方都不介意。
examples.english_sentence: He's really easy-going about food and sleep; he doesn't mind where he stays when traveling.

cantonese: 食得系福，着得系禄，瞓得就生肉
jyutping: sik6 dak1 hai6 fuk1, zoek3 dak1 hai6 luk6, fan3 dak1 zau6 saang1 juk6
mandarin_meaning: 能吃是福，能穿是禄，能睡就会长肉（能吃能穿能睡就是福气）
english_meaning: Being able to eat is a blessing, being able to dress is prosperity, being able to sleep leads to gaining flesh — having these basic comforts is a sign of good fortune.
explanation_mandarin: 这是粤语俗语，用来表达有基本的吃、穿、睡三样生活需求就是福气，劝人知足、珍惜眼前的生活。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb expressing that having the basics — food, clothing and rest — is a blessing; it encourages contentment and appreciation of simple comforts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日講：食得系福，着得系禄，瞓得就生肉，知足啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 gong2: sik6 dak1 hai6 fuk1, zoek3 dak1 hai6 luk6, fan3 dak1 zau6 saang1 juk6, zi1 zuk1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈常说：能吃是福，能穿是禄，能睡就会长肉，知足吧。
examples.english_sentence: My mother always says: being able to eat is a blessing, being able to dress is prosperity, being able to sleep means you'll get plump — be content.

mandarin_meaning: 遭受侮辱、受氣或被人欺負
english_meaning: to be humiliated, to endure mistreatment or be treated poorly
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面為「吃拖鞋的飯」，用來形容在生活或工作中長期被人欺負、受氣、受屈或處於卑微、受辱的狀態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally meaning "to eat slipper rice." It describes being humiliated, mistreated, or constantly having to endure abuse or indignity in daily life or at work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱失業，成日要向人借錢，真係要食拖鞋飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 sat1 jip6, sing4 jat6 jiu3 hoeng3 jan4 ze3 cin2, zan1 hai6 jiu3 sik6 to1 haai4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛失業，經常要向別人借錢，真是要受氣／受窮。
examples.english_sentence: He just lost his job and often has to borrow money from others; he's really having to endure humiliation/hardship.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺公司度成日俾人欺負，日日都好似喺食拖鞋飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gung1 si1 dou6 sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 hei1 fu2, jat6 jat6 dou1 hou2 ci5 hai6 sik6 to1 haai4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在公司裡經常被人欺負，每天都像在受氣一樣。
examples.english_sentence: He is frequently bullied at the company and seems to be enduring humiliation every day.

cantonese: 食斋都会升仙，牛马早就上西天
jyutping: sik6 zaa1 dou1 wui5 sing1 sin1, ngau4 maa5 zou2 zau6 soeng5 sai1 tin1
mandarin_meaning: 如果吃斋就能成仙，那牛和马早就上西天了。
english_meaning: If eating vegetarian could make you immortal, then cows and horses would already have gone to heaven. (A sarcastic remark mocking the idea that a simple ritual or act guarantees salvation or miraculous results.)
explanation_mandarin: 一句帶有諷刺意味的廣東話俗語。用來嘲諷那些認為只靠表面或簡單的宗教/道德行為就能獲得神奇回報或成就的人，意指若真有此理，牛馬早就上西天了。
explanation_english: A Cantonese sarcastic saying used to mock the belief that performing a simple act (e.g. going vegetarian) will bring miraculous rewards or salvation. It points out the absurdity by saying that if it were true, cows and horses would already have ascended to heaven.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好以為食斋都会升仙，牛马早就上西天，唔係咁容易。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ji5 wai6 sik6 zaa1 dou1 wui5 sing1 sin1, ngau4 maa5 zou2 zau6 soeng5 sai1 tin1, m4 hai6 gam2 jung4 ji6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別以為吃斋就能成仙，牛馬早就上西天，沒那麼簡單。
examples.english_sentence: Don't think that eating vegetarian will make you immortal — if that were true, cows and horses would already have gone to heaven. It's not that simple.

synonyms: 若吃素就成仙，牛馬早就上西天

mandarin_meaning: 吃早饭 / 吃早餐
english_meaning: to have breakfast; to eat breakfast
explanation_mandarin: 口語的廣東話說法，指在早上吃早餐（吃東西以作早晨的正餐或簡單餐點）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to eat breakfast or have a morning meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食咗早未啊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 zo2 zou2 mei6 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你吃早饭了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you had breakfast?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝我冇時間食早，淨係飲杯咖啡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 ngo5 mou5 si4 gaan3 sik6 zou2, zing6 hai6 jam2 bui1 gaa3 fe1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上我沒時間吃早饭，只喝了一杯咖啡。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't have time for breakfast this morning; I only had a cup of coffee.

mandarin_meaning: 吃晚饭
english_meaning: have dinner; eat the evening meal
explanation_mandarin: 「食晚」是廣東話口語用法，等同「食晚飯」，表示吃晚餐、用晚餐的動作。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression equivalent to "食晚飯", meaning to have or eat dinner (the evening meal).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋去食晚，好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 maan5, hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我们去吃晚饭，好吗？
examples.english_sentence: Shall we go have dinner tonight?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經食過晚啦，唔使等我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 sik6 gwo3 maan5 laa1, m4 sai2 dang2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已经吃过晚饭了，不用等我。
examples.english_sentence: I've already had dinner, don't wait for me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你幾點會去食晚？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gei2 dim2 wui5 heoi3 sik6 maan5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你几点会去吃晚饭？
examples.english_sentence: What time will you go have dinner?

synonyms: 食晏（注意：部分地區用法不同，通常指午餐）

mandarin_meaning: 顶罪；代人承受责任（背黑锅）
english_meaning: to take the blame; to be made a scapegoat; to take the fall for someone else
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，指替别人承担责任或罪名，做替罪羊，通常含有被动或不公平被利用的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/idiom meaning to take the blame or be made a scapegoat for someone else; often implies being unfairly blamed or used.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好叫我去食死猫，呢件事係佢搞嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 giu3 ngo5 heoi3 sik6 sei2 maau1, ni1 gin6 si6 hai6 keoi5 gaau2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别叫我去顶罪，这件事是他做的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't ask me to take the blame; this was his doing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司遇到問題後，經理竟然將責任推畀下屬去食死猫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jyu6 dou3 man6 tai4 hau6, ging1 lei5 ging2 jin4 zoeng1 zaak3 jam6 teoi1 bei2 haa6 suk6 heoi3 sik6 sei2 maau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司遇到问题后，经理竟然把责任推给下属让他们顶罪。
examples.english_sentence: After the company ran into trouble, the manager actually pushed the responsibility onto subordinates to take the fall.

mandarin_meaning: 被騙；吃虧（粵語俚語）
english_meaning: to be cheated or to suffer a loss (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「食波饼」是香港粵語俚語，通常用來形容在賭博、買賣或人際互動中被人欺騙或佔便宜、吃虧。詞源不明，多為口語用法。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to be cheated, ripped off, or otherwise suffer a loss—commonly used in contexts like gambling, transactions, or being taken advantage of. Colloquial; origin unclear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢去賭場，結果食波饼，蝕咗成萬元。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 heoi3 dou2 coeng4, git3 gwo2 sik6 bo1 beng2, sik1 zo2 seng4 maan6 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他去賭場，結果被騙/輸錢，虧了一萬元。
examples.english_sentence: He went to the casino and got ripped off, losing ten thousand dollars.

cantonese: 食猪红屙黑屎，马上见功
jyutping: sik6 zyu1 hung4 o1 hak1 si2, maa5 soeng6 gin3 gung1
mandarin_meaning: （粗俗俚语）很快见效 / 立刻起作用（讽刺或夸张地说法）
english_meaning: Vulgar slang meaning 'to take effect immediately' or 'see instant results' (used sarcastically or hyperbolically)
explanation_mandarin: 这是一句粤语粗俗俚语，字面为“吃猪红屙黑屎，马上见功”，用来形容期望某事马上见效或立刻有结果，常带讽刺或夸张意味，不适合正式场合。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang phrase literally saying 'eat pig's blood, shit black feces, immediately see effect.' It means expecting instant results; typically used sarcastically or hyperbolically and unsuitable for formal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好諗住食猪红屙黑屎，马上见功，學嘢係要花時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lam2 zy6 sik6 zyu1 hung4 o1 hak1 si2, maa5 soeng6 gin3 gung1, hok6 je5 hai6 jiu3 faa1 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别指望吃了猪红就会马上见效，学习是需要时间的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't expect instant results; you can't expect miracles right away—learning takes time.

mandarin_meaning: 上當；被騙（被別人的外表或花言巧語所迷惑）
english_meaning: to be fooled/taken in (by someone's appearance or sweet talk); literally 'eat cat face'
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面為「吃貓面」，用來形容因對方裝可愛或說話甜言蜜語而輕信、上當被騙。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb literally meaning 'eat cat face'. It describes being fooled or taken in—usually by someone's cute/innocent look or flattering talk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁易食猫面啦，佢其實唔係咁好人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 ji6 sik6 maau1 min6 laa1, keoi5 kei4 sat6 m4 hai6 gam2 hou2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那么容易上当，她其實不是那么好的人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so easily fooled — she's not such a good person.

jyutping: sik6 pei1 soeng1 o1 si2 duk6 gau2
mandarin_meaning: 詛咒或辱罵對方，字面為「吃砒霜、拉屎，毒狗」，相當於罵對方去死或希望對方受苦
english_meaning: A harsh Cantonese curse meaning literally 'eat arsenic, shit, poisonous dog' — an insult wishing harm or death on someone
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的罵人用語，將多個強烈詞彙結合成一句詛咒語，通常用來表達極度憤怒或仇恨。有時朋友間以玩笑方式使用，但一般屬於冒犯性語句，應避免正式場合使用。
explanation_english: A vulgar curse phrase combining strong insults to express extreme anger or hatred. It can be used jokingly among close friends but is generally offensive and inappropriate in formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢背叛我，我真係想同佢講：食砒霜屙屎毒狗！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bui3 pun6 ngo5, ngo5 zan1 hai6 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 gong2: sik6 pei1 soeng1 o1 si2 duk6 gau2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他背叛了我，我真的想對他說：去死吧，你這毒狗！
examples.english_sentence: He betrayed me; I really wanted to tell him: eat arsenic and die, you poisonous dog!

mandarin_meaning: 享福；享受福分（多指被動或不需太努力就能得到好處）
english_meaning: to enjoy good fortune/comfort; to reap benefits (often passively or without much effort)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面是“吃福”，用來表示享受福氣或好處，常含有被動獲益或不需太多努力就能享受的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally 'eat fortune' used to mean enjoying blessings or comforts, often implying benefiting passively or without much effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家攞咗遺產，可以成世食福。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 lo2 zo2 wai4 caan2, ho2 ji5 sing4 sai3 sik6 fuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在拿了遺產，可以一輩子享福。
examples.english_sentence: He inherited an estate; he can enjoy a comfortable life for the rest of his life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係想食福，要學識獨立。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 soeng2 sik6 fuk1, jiu3 hok6 sik1 duk6 laap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要只想着享福，要學會獨立。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just think about enjoying the good life; learn to be independent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司最近加咗人工，同事都有bonus，大家可以一齊食福。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 zeoi3 gan6 gaa1 zo2 jan4 gung1, tung4 si6 dou1 jau5 bonus, daai6 gaa1 ho2 ji5 jat1 cai4 sik6 fuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司最近加薪了，同事也都有獎金，大家可以一起享福。
examples.english_sentence: The company recently raised salaries and colleagues got bonuses; everyone can enjoy the good life together.

mandarin_meaning: 被篩掉 / 被淘汰 / 被拒絕（口語）
english_meaning: to be filtered out / rejected / snubbed (slang); can also mean being stood up or ghosted
explanation_mandarin: 「食篩」是香港廣東話的口語說法，字面是「吃篩子」，引申指被篩選掉、被淘汰或被人拒絕。常用於求職、報名、約會等情境，表示申請未獲選、被甩／被放飛機或被排除在外。
explanation_english: “食篩” (sik6 sai1) is Hong Kong Cantonese slang literally meaning “eat a sieve.” It figuratively means to be filtered out, rejected, or snubbed. It’s used in contexts like job applications, competitions, or dating to say an application was discarded, one was stood up/ghosted, or otherwise excluded.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我投咗好多間公司，全部都食篩，冇人約我面試。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4 zo2 hou2 do1 gaan1 gung1si1, cyun4 bou6 dou1 sik6 sai1, mou5 jan4 joek3 ngo5 min6 si5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我投了很多間公司的履歷，全都被篩掉了，沒有人約我面試。
examples.english_sentence: I applied to many companies, but all my applications were filtered out and nobody invited me for an interview.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢約咗個女仔食飯，點知對方唔覆訊息，佢話自己食篩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 joek3 zo2 go3 neoi5zai2 sik6 faan6, dim2 zi1 deoi3fong1 m4 fuk1 seon3sik1, keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 sik6 sai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他約了一個女生吃飯，結果對方不回訊息，他說自己被篩掉了。
examples.english_sentence: He asked a girl out to dinner, but she didn't reply; he says he got snubbed/stood up.

mandarin_meaning: 吃莲子羹（吃一种由莲子炖成的甜汤或甜品）
english_meaning: to eat lotus-seed soup (a sweet dessert soup made from lotus seeds)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是吃莲子羹（一种用莲子煮成的甜汤或甜品）。在粤语中通常为字面用法，并非常见成语或普遍俚语；若被比喻使用，通常仍指享受简单的美味或惬意的时刻。
explanation_english: Literally 'to eat lotus-seed soup', a sweet dessert soup made from lotus seeds. Primarily used in the literal sense in Cantonese and is not a widely established idiom or slang. If used figuratively, it usually conveys enjoying a simple treat or a moment of comfort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冬天食碗熱嘅莲子羹好舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dung1 tin1 sik6 wun2 jit6 ge3 lin4 zi2 gung1 hou2 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 冬天吃一碗热的莲子羹很舒服。
examples.english_sentence: Eating a hot bowl of lotus-seed soup in winter feels very comforting.

mandarin_meaning: 吃藥；（俚語）精神失常、發瘋
english_meaning: to take medicine; (slang) to act crazy or be mentally unwell
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「服用藥物」。口語或俚語中可用來形容一個人言行反常、像發瘋或不理智（如「食錯藥」）。
explanation_english: Literally 'to take medicine.' In colloquial/slang use it can describe someone acting irrationally or 'crazy' (e.g. the expression '食錯藥' — 'took the wrong medicine').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話我要開始食藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 ngo5 jiu3 hoi1 ci2 sik6 joek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 医生说我要开始吃药。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said I need to start taking medicine.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講咁嘅嘢，係咪食錯藥呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 gam2 ge3 je5, hai6 mai6 sik6 co3 joek6 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说这种话，是不是吃错药了？
examples.english_sentence: Saying things like that — are you out of your mind?

mandarin_meaning: 接受封口费/贿赂，以金钱了结纠纷或不再追究
english_meaning: to accept hush money/a payoff or bribe to settle a dispute or to drop charges
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，指接受对方给的钱（如和解金或封口费），以金钱了结纠纷或不再追究对方的行为，常含贬义（收受不当利益或被收买）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to accept a payoff (hush money or settlement) to end a dispute or refrain from pursuing a complaint; often pejorative, implying bribery or being bought off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 律師為咗息事寧人竟然食诈和，收咗對方嘅和解金就唔再追究。
examples.jyutping_sentence: leot6 si1 wai6 zo2 sik1 si6 ning4 jan4 ging2 jin4 sik6 zaak3 wo4 sau1 zo2 deoi3 fong1 ge3 wo4 gaai2 gam1 zau6 m4 zoi6 zeoi1 gau3
examples.mandarin_sentence: 律師為了息事寧人竟然收取封口費（食诈和），收了對方的和解金就不再追究。
examples.english_sentence: The lawyer, to keep the matter quiet, actually accepted a payoff (ate the settlement), took the other's settlement money and didn't pursue the case further.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講嗰個官員收人錢食诈和，依家有人調查佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 go2 go3 gun1 jyun4 sau1 jan4 cin2 sik6 zaak3 wo4 ji1 gaa1 jau5 jan4 diu6 caa4 keoi5
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽說那個官員收了人的錢來食诈和，現在有人正在調查他。
examples.english_sentence: I heard that the official accepted money to settle quietly (ate the payoff), and now someone is investigating him.

mandarin_meaning: 被騙、上當
english_meaning: to be tricked / to fall for a scam
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話俚語，指被人欺騙或上當受騙，通常用於口語場景。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to be deceived or to fall for a scam; commonly used in spoken contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你又食谷種喇，俾人呃咗三百蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau6 sik6 guk1 zung2 laa3, bei2 jan4 aak1 zo2 saam1 baak3 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你又上當了，被人骗了300港币。
examples.english_sentence: You fell for it again — you got scammed out of HK$300.

cantonese: 食豬紅屙黑屎 - 即刻見功
jyutping: sik6 zyu1 hung4 o1 hak1 si2 - zik1 hak1 gin3 gung1
mandarin_meaning: 馬上見效／立刻見效（俗語、俚語）
english_meaning: to take effect immediately; to show instant results (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 一個廣東話粗俗的俗語，字面上形容吃豬紅會立即排出黑便，用來誇張地表示某事或某藥馬上見效、立刻有明顯效果。語氣口語、粗獷，多用於日常對話或打趣。
explanation_english: A coarse Cantonese slang phrase. Literally it describes eating pig's blood and immediately passing black stool; used hyperbolically to say something (e.g. a remedy or measure) produces instant, visible effects. It is colloquial and vulgar, often used jokingly or emphatically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個偏方真係食豬紅屙黑屎，即刻見功，痛症即刻輕咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 pin1 fong1 zan1 hai6 sik6 zyu1 hung4 o1 hak1 si2, zik1 hak1 gin3 gung1, tung3 zang3 zik1 hak1 hing1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個偏方真的像「食豬紅屙黑屎」，立刻見效，疼痛馬上減輕。
examples.english_sentence: This folk remedy really works instantly — it's like '食豬紅屙黑屎', the pain eased immediately.

mandarin_meaning: 吃软饭
english_meaning: to live off a woman; to be a kept man; to freeload
explanation_mandarin: 带有贬义，通常指成年男子依靠女性（如女朋友或妻子）提供经济支持而不自己谋生，也可泛指依赖他人养活的行为。
explanation_english: A derogatory slang phrase for a man who relies on a woman (e.g., girlfriend or wife) for financial support and does not support himself; more generally, to freeload or live off someone else.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日唔做嘢，淨係食軟飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5, zing6 hai6 sik6 jyun5 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天不工作，只会吃软饭。
examples.english_sentence: He never works and just lives off a woman.

mandarin_meaning: 吃过还想再吃 / 回味无穷
english_meaning: To find something (usually food) so delicious that one wants to eat it again; to be left savoring or reminiscing about the taste
explanation_mandarin: （口语）形容食物好吃到一吃过就会想再吃，或对某种经历回味不已。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing food (or an experience) so good that you want to have it again or keep savoring/reminiscing about it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間茶餐廳嘅蛋撻真係食過返尋味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 daan6 tat1 zan1 hai6 sik6 gwo3 faan1 cam4 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家茶餐厅的蛋挞真是吃过还想再吃。
examples.english_sentence: The egg tart at this cha chaan teng is truly something you'll want to eat again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上次去日本嗰啲美食真係食過返尋味，我而家仲諗住再去一次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 ci3 heoi3 jat6 bun2 go2 di1 mei5 sik6 zan1 hai6 sik6 gwo3 faan1 cam4 mei6, ngo5 ji4 gaa1 zung6 lam2 zyu6 zoi3 heoi3 jat1 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上次去日本的那些美食真是吃过还想再吃，我现在还打算再去一次。
examples.english_sentence: The food we had in Japan last time was really something I wanted to eat again; I'm now planning to go back.

jyutping: sik6 faan6 faai3, o1 si2 cou1
mandarin_meaning: 做事急躁會導致粗糙或出錯（相當於「欲速則不達」）
english_meaning: Rushing leads to sloppy or poor work (equivalent to "haste makes waste").
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語用粗俗的比喻提醒人們不要太急躁，匆忙做事往往會導致品質差或犯錯。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying uses a coarse metaphor to warn that being too hasty often produces low-quality or sloppy results. It conveys the same idea as "haste makes waste."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份報告唔好趕住交，記住「食飯快，屙屎粗」，慢啲做好啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 m4 hou2 gon2 zyu6 gaau1, gei3 zyu6 sik6 faan6 faai3, o1 si2 cou1, maan6 di1 zou6 hou2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这份报告不要赶着交，记住“做事急会粗糙”，慢一点做好一点。
examples.english_sentence: Don't rush to hand in this report. Remember 'haste makes waste' — take your time and do it properly.

mandarin_meaning: 把吃饭看得比天还重要 / 以吃饭为最重要的事
english_meaning: to regard eating as the most important thing; to prioritize food above everything else
explanation_mandarin: 形容把吃饭看得極其重要，甚至凌駕於其他事物之上，常用來評論某人重視食物或生活享受而不顧其他。
explanation_english: An idiomatic expression describing someone who treats eating (or food/enjoyment) as the most important thing, often implying they neglect other responsibilities or priorities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話食飯大過天，唔理其他嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4jat6 waa6 sik6faan6 daai6gwo3 tin1, m4 lei5 kei4taa1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總說吃飯比什麼都重要，不管其他事情。
examples.english_sentence: He always says eating is more important than anything else and ignores other matters.

mandarin_meaning: 不用为温饱担心；生活有保障，有足够的食物或钱
english_meaning: to have enough to eat / enough money for basic needs; no worries about making ends meet
explanation_mandarin: 「食饱无忧米」是廣東話俗語，字面指吃飽不用擔心米（食物／錢），引申為生活基本所需有保障，不用為溫飽煩惱。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquialism meaning literally 'eat until full, no worries about rice' — figuratively, having enough food or money to meet basic needs and thus no worries about subsistence.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家有份穩定嘅工，唔使為生計擔心，算係食饱无忧米啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 jau5 fan6 wan2 ding6 ge3 gung1, m4 sai2 wai6 saang1 gai3 daam1 sam1, syun3 hai6 sik6 baau2 mou4 jau1 mai5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在有一份稳定的工作，不用为生计担心，可以说是吃饱无忧米了。
examples.english_sentence: He now has a steady job and doesn't have to worry about making ends meet — you could say he has enough to eat and no worries.

cantonese: 食饽睡一睡，好过做元帥
jyutping: sik6 baau2 seoi6 jat1 seoi6, hou2 gwo3 zou6 jyun4 seoi3
mandarin_meaning: 吃饱睡一觉，比起当元帅更好
english_meaning: Better to eat and sleep than to be a marshal — preferring a comfortable, peaceful life over pursuing high rank or heavy responsibility.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語表示寧可選擇簡單安穩的生活（吃飽、睡覺），也不願追求高位或承擔重大責任，語氣常帶有調侃或自嘲意味。
explanation_english: This saying expresses a preference for a simple, comfortable life (eat and sleep) over seeking high rank or taking on heavy responsibilities. It is often used jokingly or self-deprecatingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有時我寧願食饽睡一睡，好過做元帥，唔想應酬同處理咁多嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 si4 ngo5 ning4 jyun6 sik6 baau2 seoi6 jat1 seoi6, hou2 gwo3 zou6 jyun4 seoi3, m4 soeng2 jing3 cau1 tung4 cyu2 lei5 gam2 do1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有時我寧願吃飽睡一覺，也不想當元帥，不想應酬和處理那麼多事情。
examples.english_sentence: Sometimes I'd rather eat and sleep than be a marshal; I don't want to deal with socializing and so many responsibilities.

jyutping: sik6 jyu4 sik6 juk6, m4 ci5 faan6 co1 suk6
mandarin_meaning: 吃了鱼肉，不再满足于粗茶淡饭（形容习惯了优渥生活后不再满足于简单生活）
english_meaning: Having eaten fish and meat, no longer satisfied with plain rice (i.e., once accustomed to luxury, one won't be content with simple living)
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語用魚肉對比簡單的飯，意思是習慣了較好的生活或待遇之後，就不會再滿足於簡單或樸素的生活，帶有被寵壞或難以回復從前的含義。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb contrasts fish and meat with plain rice: once someone becomes used to better food or a more comfortable lifestyle, they are no longer satisfied with simple or modest living. It implies being spoiled by abundance and unable to return to previous simplicity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家成日食魚食肉，唔似飯初熟，一啲簡單嘢佢都唔肯食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 seng4 jat6 sik6 jyu4 sik6 juk6, m4 ci5 faan6 co1 suk6, jat1 di1 gaan2 daan1 je5 keoi5 dou1 m4 hang2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在常常吃魚吃肉，不再像以前那樣滿足於簡單的飯食。
examples.english_sentence: He now often eats fish and meat; he's no longer content with simple meals as before.

jyutping: sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6
mandarin_meaning: 对某事完全提不起兴趣；连再好的东西也觉得没意思（字面：连吃龙肉都觉得没味道）
english_meaning: Completely unimpressed or indifferent; nothing excites someone anymore (literally: even eating dragon meat would taste bland)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容對某些事物完全失去興趣或覺得索然無味，即使是極好的或罕見的事物也喚不起興趣。
explanation_english: Used to describe being completely uninterested or unimpressed by something — even an extraordinary thing would fail to excite the person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家啲嘢對佢嚟講，食龍肉都冇味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 di1 je5 deoi3 keoi5 lai4 gong2, sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 对他来说，什么都提不起兴趣，连吃龙肉都觉得没味道。
examples.english_sentence: For him, nothing excites him anymore — even eating dragon meat would taste bland.

mandarin_meaning: 吃白食的人；依靠別人供養、愛佔便宜的人（貶義）
english_meaning: freeloader; someone who lives off others or mooches meals/support (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 「飯匙頭」是廣東話俗語，用來形容經常靠別人吃飯或依賴他人供養、佔便宜的人，帶有貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for a person who habitually sponges off others for meals or support — someone who freeloads; derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做飯匙頭，自己搵食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 faan6 ci4 tau4, zi6 gei2 wan2 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要當飯匙頭，自己謀生吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a freeloader; earn your own living.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日靠女朋友俾錢，真係個飯匙頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 kaau3 neoi5 pang4 jau5 bei2 cin2, zan1 hai6 go3 faan6 ci4 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常靠女朋友給錢，真是個飯匙頭。
examples.english_sentence: He always depends on his girlfriend's money — he's really a freeloader.

mandarin_meaning: 吃白饭的人；靠别人养活的寄生者（俚语）
english_meaning: a freeloader; someone who lives off others' food/support (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「飯杓頭」是香港粵語俚語，用來形容成天不工作、靠別人供養或占便宜的人，帶貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who never works and relies on others for food or support; derogatory term for a freeloader.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個飯杓頭，成日唔做嘢，靠人供養。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 faan6 biu1 tau4, sing4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5, kaau3 jan4 gung1 joeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個飯杓頭，整天不工作，靠別人供養。
examples.english_sentence: He's a freeloader — never works and lives off others.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）肚子飽了、吃飽
english_meaning: full; satiated (after eating) — Cantonese colloquial
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，形容吃飽、肚子感到滿足。通常用於非正式場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe being full or satiated after eating. Common in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我食咗好多，已經飽腸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik6 zo2 hou2 do1, ji5 ging1 baau2 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我吃了很多，肚子已經飽了。
examples.english_sentence: I ate a lot; I'm already full.

mandarin_meaning: 養育孩子／撫養（子女）
english_meaning: to raise/bring up children (literally: raise a son)
explanation_mandarin: 指照顧、供養並教育子女，使其成長。粤語口語常用，既可指養兒也可泛指養育子女。
explanation_english: Refers to taking care of, supporting, and educating one's children as they grow up. Common colloquial Cantonese term; literally 'raise a son' but often used for raising children in general.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做父母唔容易，養仔養女都要好多心機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 fu6 mou5 m4 jung4 ji6, joeng5 zai2 joeng5 neoi5 dou1 jiu3 hou2 do1 sam1 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做父母不容易，養兒養女都需要很多心力。
examples.english_sentence: Being parents isn't easy; raising sons and daughters both takes a lot of effort.

mandarin_meaning: 飯卡／食堂卡（用於食堂或餐廳付款的卡）
english_meaning: meal card; canteen/dining card (used to pay for meals)
explanation_mandarin: 指在學校、公司或機構的食堂或餐廳用來支付餐費的儲值卡或識別卡，通常需預先充值或由單位發放。
explanation_english: A stored-value or ID card used at a school, company, or institution cafeteria to pay for meals; typically preloaded with credit or issued by the organization.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔記得帶餐卡，午餐點算？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 caan1 kaat1, ng5 caan1 dim2 syun3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我忘記帶飯卡，午餐怎麼辦？
examples.english_sentence: I forgot to bring my meal card — what should I do about lunch?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司餐廳可以用餐卡付款。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 caan1 teng1 ho2 ji5 jung6 caan1 kaat1 fu6 fun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司食堂可以用餐卡付款。
examples.english_sentence: The company canteen accepts meal cards for payment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐卡冇錢，要上網充值先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 kaat1 mou5 cin2, jiu3 soeng5 mong5 cung1 zik6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐卡沒錢了，要上網充值才行。
examples.english_sentence: My meal card has no money; I need to top it up online first.

mandarin_meaning: 經歷過饑餓；比喻吃過苦、經歷過困難
english_meaning: to have experienced hunger; figuratively, to have gone through hardship or privation
explanation_mandarin: 表示曾經遭受饑餓或艱苦生活，亦可引申為經歷過困難，因此更懂得珍惜或謹慎。
explanation_english: Indicates having gone through hunger or hard times; can be used figuratively to mean having experienced difficulties and therefore being more appreciative or cautious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細個餓過饑，所以好珍惜每一餐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 go3 ngo6 gwo3 gei1, so2 ji5 hou2 zan1 sik6 mui5 jat1 caan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他小時候經歷過饑餓，所以很珍惜每一餐。
examples.english_sentence: He experienced hunger when he was young, so he treasures every meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋嗰陣餓過饑，先學識點樣省錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 go2 zan6 ngo6 gwo3 gei1, sin1 hok6 sik1 dim2 joeng6 saang2 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們那時曾經挨餓，才學會如何省錢。
examples.english_sentence: We once went hungry; that's when we learned to save money.

mandarin_meaning: （古字/方言）与糖、糖漿有關；表黏稠、甜膩的狀態或糖果類（如餳糖）
english_meaning: a rare/archaic Cantonese character referring to sugar/syrup or a sticky, syrupy quality; also used for toffee/candy in colloquial usage
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词 / 形容词（方言用法）
explanation_mandarin: 餳為罕用字，常出現在方言或口語中，表示含糖、黏稠或甜膩的質地；也可指某類黏牙的糖果（如餳糖）。現代漢語中較少使用，屬地域性或俗語用法。
explanation_english: 餳 is a rare/archaic character used in Cantonese dialect to denote sugar, syrup, or a sticky/syrupy quality. It can also refer colloquially to sticky candies (toffees). It is uncommon in standard modern Chinese and appears mainly in regional or colloquial speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路最鍾意食餳糖，食完成日會黐牙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 sik6 tong4 tong4, sik6 jyun4 seng4 jat6 wui5 ci1 ngaa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 孩子最喜欢吃餳糖，吃完常常会黏牙。
examples.english_sentence: Kids love eating toffee; it often sticks to their teeth afterwards.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語方言、罕見）碎屑、剩菜剩飯或零碎食物
english_meaning: scraps; leftover food; bits and pieces of food
explanation_mandarin: 「餺餦」為粵語中較罕見或方言性的詞彙，常用來指稱食物的碎屑、剩菜剩飯或零碎的小塊食物。語感偏口語或地區性用語，文獻記載較少。
explanation_english: A rare/regionally used Cantonese term referring to food scraps, leftovers, or tiny bits of food. It is colloquial and dialectal, not common in formal written Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企啲餺餦唔好即刻倒咗，留返畀街貓食下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei5 di1 bou2 ngaat6 m4 hou2 zik1 hak1 dou3 zo2, lau4 faan1 bei2 gaai1 maau1 sik6 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡的餺餦不要馬上倒掉，留給街貓吃。
examples.english_sentence: Don't throw away the scraps at home right away; leave them for the stray cats.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 煮飯時少啲餺餦，唔好浪費食物。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zyu2 faan6 si4 siu2 di1 bou2 ngaat6, m4 hou2 long6 fai3 sik6 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 煮飯時要減少餺餦，不要浪費食物。
examples.english_sentence: When cooking, produce fewer scraps; don't waste food.

jyutping: faan6 nim1 di1 sik6 dak1 jan4 fei4
mandarin_meaning: （字面）米饭黏一点容易让人发胖；（引申）有时用来比喻某物有“黏性”或吸引力，能留住人或让人上瘾。
english_meaning: Literally: if the rice is stickier, it can make people fat; figuratively: something sticky/attractive that keeps people engaged or hooked.
explanation_mandarin: 这是一句粤语俗语，字面意思是米饭黏一些更容易让人发胖。口语中有时也用作比喻，形容事物有黏性或吸引力，能让人留恋、依赖或上瘾。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally saying sticky rice makes people gain weight. In speech it can also be used metaphorically to describe something that is 'sticky' or attractive, keeping people attached, interested, or coming back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日講：飯黏啲食得人肥，唔好煮得太散。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 gong2: faan6 nim1 di1 sik6 dak1 jan4 fei4, m4 hou2 zyu2 dak1 taai3 saan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈常说：饭黏一点会让人发胖，别把饭煮得太散。
examples.english_sentence: Mom often says: sticky rice makes people gain weight, so don't cook the rice too loose.

mandarin_meaning: 被政府或官員收買／被收買而屈從（俚語）
english_meaning: to be bribed or co‑opted by officials; to have accepted payoffs from the authorities (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「饮咗门官茶」是粵語俚語，用來形容某人被政府或官員收買、受利益而對官府諂媚或聽命行事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression describing someone who has been bribed or co‑opted by government officials and therefore behaves submissively or does their bidding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講嗰位地產商喺政府面前好順從，大家話佢飲咗門官茶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 go2 wai2 dei6 caan2 soeng1 hai6 zing3 fu2 min6 cin4 hou2 seon6 cung4, daai6 gaa1 waa6 keoi5 jam2 zo2 mun4 gun1 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听说那位地产商在政府面前很顺从，大家说他被官员收买了。
examples.english_sentence: People say that developer is very deferential to the government — folks say he's 'drunk government tea' (i.e., been bribed/co‑opted).

mandarin_meaning: 先嘗第一口；比喻先經歷某種情況，常指先承受不利、困難或風險（先吃苦頭／先當第一個）
english_meaning: To take the first taste/first sip; figuratively, to be the first to experience something (often an unpleasant consequence) or to take the first blow/be a guinea pig.
explanation_mandarin: 「飲頭啖湯」字面意思是喝第一口湯，口語用法指某人先嘗到某種結果或後果，經常用來形容先受苦、先承擔損失或先被試驗的人。
explanation_english: Literally 'drink the first mouthful of soup.' Used figuratively to mean someone who is first to experience a result — often the first to suffer, take the blame, or act as a test subject.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事好危險，唔好叫佢去飲頭啖湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 hou2 ngai4 him2, m4 hou2 giu3 keoi5 heoi3 jam2 tau4 daam6 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事很危险，不要让他去第一个承受后果。
examples.english_sentence: This is dangerous — don't make him be the first to take the hit.

mandarin_meaning: 喝姜酒（用作坐月、祛寒和补身的传统做法）
english_meaning: to drink ginger wine (a traditional warming/remedial alcoholic drink, often used in postpartum care or to dispel cold)
explanation_mandarin: “饮姜酒”字面意思是喝以生姜和酒为主的饮品。在广东/香港等地区的传统习俗中，常用于坐月（产后调养）或当作驱寒、补身的民间疗法，也可泛指喝这种姜味药酒。
explanation_english: Literally 'to drink ginger wine.' In Cantonese-speaking areas this refers to consuming an alcoholic ginger-based drink used traditionally for postpartum recuperation (confinement), warming the body, dispelling cold, or as a home remedy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 坐月期間，阿嬸每日都要饮姜酒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: co5 jyut6 kei4 gaan1, aa3-sam2 mui5 jat6 dou1 jiu3 jam2 goeng1 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 坐月期间，婶婶每天都要喝姜酒。
examples.english_sentence: During her confinement, Aunt drinks ginger wine every day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冬天夜晚饮姜酒可以暖身，唔好饮太多啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dung1 tin1 je6 maan5 jam2 goeng1 zau2 ho2 ji5 nyun5 san1, m4 hou2 jam2 taai3 do1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 冬天晚上喝姜酒可以暖身，不要喝太多。
examples.english_sentence: Drinking ginger wine on winter nights can warm the body, but don't drink too much.

mandarin_meaning: 酒量好；能喝很多酒
english_meaning: can hold one's liquor; able to drink a lot; a good drinker
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語／形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 「饮得杯落」是廣東話的口語表達，用來形容一個人酒量好、能把杯中酒喝得下或能喝很多，常用於香港的日常對話，有時帶輕鬆或誇讚語氣。
explanation_english: “饮得杯落” is a Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone with a good tolerance for alcohol — able to down a drink or drink a lot. It’s commonly used in Hong Kong speech and can be said playfully or admiringly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿偉飲得杯落，成晚都跟住大家飲到凌晨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 wai5 jam2 dak1 bui1 lok6, seng4 maan5 dou1 gan1 zyu6 daai6 gaa1 jam2 dou3 ling4 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿偉酒量很好，整晚都跟大家喝到凌晨。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Wai can really drink; he spent the whole night drinking with everyone until the early morning.

mandarin_meaning: 喝剩的最後一口；比喻事情的收尾、殘留或善後部分
english_meaning: The last bit (literally the last sip of a drink); figuratively the finishing touches, leftovers, or follow-up/aftermath
explanation_mandarin: 「饮水尾」字面上指飲品最後剩下的一小部分（最後一口）。在香港粵語口語中也常用作比喻，表示某件事的收尾、剩餘或需要處理的善後工作。
explanation_english: Literally 'the tail of the drink' — the last sip or remnant. In Hong Kong Cantonese it is also used figuratively to mean the finishing touches, leftover matters, or follow-up tasks that need to be handled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 樽度仲有啲饮水尾，唔好倒晒啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: seon1 dou6 zung6 jau5 di1 jam2 seoi2 mei5, m4 hou2 dou2 saai3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 瓶子裡還有一些剩下的水，別全都倒掉。
examples.english_sentence: There's still a bit of water left in the bottle — don't pour it all out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個活動做好咗，但仲有啲饮水尾要處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 wut6 dung6 zou6 hou2 zo2, daan6 zung6 jau5 di1 jam2 seoi2 mei5 jiu3 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 活動做完了，但還有一些收尾工作要處理。
examples.english_sentence: The event is done, but there are still some follow-up tasks to handle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 人哋淨係見到成果，唔知道背後有幾多饮水尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jan4 dei6 zing6 hai6 gin3 dou3 sing4 gwo2, m4 zi1 dou3 bui3 hau6 jau5 gei2 do1 jam2 seoi2 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別人只看到成果，不知道背後有多少善後工作。
examples.english_sentence: People only see the results and don't know how much cleanup was required behind the scenes.

mandarin_meaning: 吃饱喝足；安逸享乐、游手好闲
english_meaning: to eat and drink one's fill; to live in comfort and indulgence (often implying idleness)
explanation_mandarin: 原意为吃饱喝足，引申为安逸享乐或只顾吃喝、游手好闲，常带有贬义或戏谑意味。
explanation_english: Literally 'eat and drink to fullness.' Figuratively it means to live comfortably and indulgently or to idle away time enjoying food and drink; often used pejoratively or teasingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都係飲飽食醉，唔做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dou1 hai6 jam2 baau2 sik6 zeoi3, m4 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天只知道吃饱喝足，不做事。
examples.english_sentence: He spends all day just eating and drinking and doesn't work.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）吃得很饱；夸张地说自己非常饱，常带幽默或讽刺意味
english_meaning: Slang for being extremely full after eating (often said humorously or sarcastically)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容词 / 感叹词（俚语）
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，字面是“被荷兰豆饱死”，用来夸张地表示自己吃得很饱，或讽刺某人吃得并不多却自称很饱。
