english_meaning: Not a standard Cantonese term; literally "yellow-green doctor." Not an official title — used jokingly or as a coined slang term with no fixed meaning.
explanation_mandarin: 「黄绿医生」並非標準詞彙，通常是朋友間的戲稱或網路上自創的俚語。字面上是「黃綠色的醫生」，但沒有固定指涉，需根據語境理解。
explanation_english: “黄绿医生” is not a standard expression. Literally “yellow-green doctor,” it is typically a joking nickname or a coined slang used among friends or online. It has no fixed definition and its meaning depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你哋叫佢做「黃綠醫生」係開玩笑啫，唔係真係職業。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 giu3 keoi5 zou6 wong4 luk6 ji1 sang1 hai6 hoi1 waan2 siu3 ze1, m4 hai6 zan1 hai6 zik1 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你们叫他“黄绿医生”只是开玩笑，不是真的职业称呼。
examples.english_sentence: You call him 'yellow-green doctor' as a joke; it's not a real professional title.

jyutping: wong4 zung2 goek3, bat1 siu1 tai4
mandarin_meaning: 形容情況糟到不值得一提或難以啟齒（多用作口語俗語）
english_meaning: An informal expression meaning the situation is so bad or embarrassing that it's not worth mentioning.
explanation_mandarin: 此廣東話俗語用來形容某事或某人糟糕、尷尬或慘淡到無需多說、難以啟齒。屬口語、地區性表達，常用於描述財務、健康或面子問題等令人尷尬的情況。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial phrase describes something so bad, embarrassing, or hopeless that it is not worth talking about. It is an informal, regional expression commonly used to refer to awkward or dire situations (e.g., finances, health, reputation).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢賭博輸晒錢，家境差到黃肿脚，不消提。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou2 bok3 syu1 saai3 cin2, gaa1 ging2 caa1 dou3 wong4 zung2 goek3, bat1 siu1 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他賭博把錢輸光，家境差得無法多提。
examples.english_sentence: He lost all his money gambling; his family's situation is so bad it's not worth mentioning.

cantonese: 黄连树下弹琴，苦中作乐
jyutping: wong4 lin4 syu6 haa6 daan6 kam4, fu2 zung1 zok3 ngok6
mandarin_meaning: 在苦难中寻找快乐；苦中作乐（自我安慰、在困境中逢闲寻乐）
english_meaning: To make the best of a bad situation; to find or make joy amid suffering; to take pleasure despite hardship.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻在艰苦或困境中自我安慰、寻找快乐，尽量在不利环境下维持乐观和快乐的态度。
explanation_english: An idiom meaning to take pleasure or find amusement amid hardship. It describes self-comforting behavior or maintaining optimism and small joys despite difficult circumstances.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家屋企經濟好差，佢都係黃連樹下彈琴，苦中作樂，日日同細路玩得好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 uk1 kei5 ging1 zai3 hou2 caa1, keoi5 dou1 hai6 wong4 lin4 syu6 haa6 daan6 kam4, fu2 zung1 zok3 ngok6, jat6 jat6 tung4 sai3 lou6 waan2 dak1 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在家里经济很差，他还是苦中作乐，每天和孩子们玩得很开心。
examples.english_sentence: Our family's finances are bad now, but he still makes the best of it—finding joy amid hardship and playing happily with the children every day.

cantonese: 黄鳝上沙滩，唔死一身潺（残）
jyutping: wong4 saan2 soeng5 saa1 taan1, m4 sei2 jat1 san1 caan4
mandarin_meaning: 黄鳝上沙滩，不死也会遍体鳞伤；比喻虽幸存但遭受重创或损失惨重。
english_meaning: If a yellow eel crawls onto the sandbank, even if it doesn't die it will be badly injured — used to say someone or something may survive but will be severely damaged or suffer heavy losses.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻处于危险或艰难境地，虽能活下来但会受到严重伤害或损失，多用来形容经历失败、受打击后遍体鳞伤的情况。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese proverb meaning that even if one survives a risky or harmful situation, one will be left badly hurt or damaged. Often used to describe heavy losses or severe consequences after an ordeal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次做生意蝕得好慘，真係黄鳝上沙滩，唔死一身残。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 zou6 saang1 ji3 sik1 dak1 hou2 caam2, zan1 hai6 wong4 saan2 soeng5 saa1 taan1, m4 sei2 jat1 san1 caan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这次做生意亏得很惨，真是黄鳝上沙滩，不死也遍体鳞伤。
examples.english_sentence: He lost terribly in this business deal — it's like a yellow eel on the sandbank: even if it survives, it'll be badly injured.

mandarin_meaning: （區域用語）指一種當地或野生的番薯、甘藷品種
english_meaning: (regional term) a local or wild variety of sweet potato (yam)
explanation_mandarin: 此詞為粵語某些方言或地方用語，常用來稱呼村落或鄉間栽種或天然生長的一種番薯（甘藷）。詞彙較為罕見，多見於口語或老一輩的說法。
explanation_english: A regional Cantonese expression used in some dialects to name a local or wild variety of sweet potato. The word is relatively rare and tends to appear in rural speech or older speakers' vocabulary.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋屋企後園有幾株黎峒藷，農曆新年會掘嚟煮嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2 hau6 jyun4 jau5 gei2 zyu1 lai4 dung6 syu4, nung4 lik6 san1 nin4 wui5 gwat6 lai4 zyu2 lai4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们家后园有几株黎峒藷，农历新年会挖来煮着吃。
examples.english_sentence: We have a few lei-dong-syu plants in our backyard; they'll be dug up and cooked for Lunar New Year.

mandarin_meaning: 裝傻；假裝糊塗或發呆
english_meaning: to play dumb; to act clueless; to be in a daze
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語表達，指故意或因恍惚而裝作不知情、裝傻或發呆。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to pretend to be clueless or to be in a daze — either deliberately playing dumb or actually being absent-minded.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好黎朦子啦，我知道你做過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lai4 mung4 zi2 laa1, ngo5 zi1 dou3 nei5 zou6 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別裝糊塗了，我知道你做過。
examples.english_sentence: Don't play dumb, I know you did it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日成日黎朦子，好似唔太清醒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 seng4 jat6 lai4 mung4 zi2, hou2 ci5 m4 taai3 cing1 sing2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天一直發呆，好像不太清醒。
examples.english_sentence: He's been spacing out all day; he doesn't seem fully alert.

mandarin_meaning: 愛耍脾氣、愛鬧彆扭或情緒低落的人／表現
english_meaning: Someone who sulks or is moody; sulky/moodiness (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「黎檬子」是廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人愛耍脾氣、情緒化、鬧彆扭或突然變得酸溜溜、不開心的狀態或行為。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term describing someone who sulks, acts moody, throws a tantrum or suddenly becomes sullen/sour. Can be used as a noun or adjective.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日黎檬子，唔想同人傾計。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 lai4 mung4 zi2, m4 soeng2 tung4 jan4 king1 gai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是耍脾氣，不想和人說話。
examples.english_sentence: He’s always sulking and doesn’t want to talk to people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好突然黎檬子啦，有咩唔開心講得清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 dat6 jin4 lai4 mung4 zi2 laa1, jau5 me1 m4 hoi1 sam1 gong2 dak1 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別突然耍脾氣，有不高興的事要說清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't suddenly start sulking — if something's bothering you, explain it clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 黏人；纠缠不放；黏着不走
english_meaning: clingy; to cling to someone and not let go; overly dependent or pestering
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語說法，形容一個人經常黏著別人、纏著別人不放，讓人覺得煩或不舒服。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who constantly clings to or follows others, being overly dependent or annoyingly persistent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日黐手𥹉腳，好令人煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ci1 sau2 ci1 goek3, hou2 ling6 jan4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天黏人，讓人很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He's always clinging to people; it's really annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 黏在網上 / 沉迷於網路
english_meaning: glued to the internet; addicted to the web; obsessed with online activities
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面意思是「黏在網上」，指沉迷互聯網或對網上事物過度著迷；有時也可泛指行為怪異或像發瘋一樣。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang literally meaning 'stuck to the net'. It describes being addicted to or obsessed with the internet/online activities. Occasionally used more broadly to imply someone is acting crazy or excessively absorbed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日黐網，日日對住部電腦，唔願出嚟同人傾計。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ci1 mong5, jat6 jat6 deoi3 zyu6 bou6 din6 nou5, m4 jyun6 ceot1 lai4 tung4 jan4 king1 gai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天黐網，天天對著電腦，不願出來和人聊天。
examples.english_sentence: He's always glued to the internet, at the computer every day, unwilling to come out and talk with people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果成日夜晚都上網，真係會黐網㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 seng4 jat6 je6 maan5 dou1 soeng5 mong5, zan1 hai6 wui5 ci1 mong5 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果總是在晚上上網，真的會黐網（上癮）。
examples.english_sentence: If you keep going online late every night, you'll really get addicted to the internet.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/俚語）形容人行為瘋狂、失去理智或失常，做事失控或過份激動。
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang term meaning to act crazy, lose control, or behave erratically; to be overreactive or irrational.
explanation_mandarin: 「黐總制（掣）」是香港粵語俚語，通常用來批評或描述某人行為失常、衝動或過火。語氣口語化，常與「黐線」「發癲」等詞互通使用，多見於非正式對話。
explanation_english: This Hong Kong Cantonese slang is used to describe someone acting crazy, irrational, or out of control. It's informal and often interchangeable with terms like 'go mad' or 'lose it' in casual speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁黐總制，冷靜啲再傾啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 ci1 zung2 zai3, laang5 zing6 di1 zoi3 king1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要這樣發瘋，冷靜一點再談吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so crazy; calm down and let's talk later.

mandarin_meaning: （粤语俚语）行为怪异、像发疯或神经质地乱跑/乱来
english_meaning: Cantonese slang meaning to behave crazily or erratically; to act irrationally or obsessively
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语，通常用来形容某人行为异常、神经质或像发疯似地到处乱转或做事不合常理。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe someone behaving oddly, nervously, or crazily — acting irrationally or wandering about in a frantic/obsessive way.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日黐車噉轉，大家都唔知佢發生咩事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 ci1 ce1 gam2 zyun2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zi1 keoi5 faat3 sang1 me1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近老是行为怪异（黐車噉轉），大家都不知道他发生了什么事。
examples.english_sentence: He's been acting crazy lately; nobody knows what's wrong with him.

mandarin_meaning: 整天吃喝不停；沉迷於飲食（口語、俚語，常帶貶義）
english_meaning: constantly eating and drinking; always snacking and drinking — a colloquial/slang phrase implying indulgence or lack of self-control
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，字面上是「黐」在「飲」「食」上，形容一個人總是吃吃喝喝、好吃好飲或無節制地飲食，常帶輕微貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally combining 'stick' with 'drink' and 'eat'; it describes someone who is always eating and drinking — often used to suggest indulgence or lack of restraint.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日黐飲黐食，成個月啲錢好快就冇晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ci1 jam2 ci1 sik6, seng4 go3 jyut6 di1 cin2 hou2 faai3 zau6 mou5 saat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天吃吃喝喝，一個月的錢很快就沒有了。
examples.english_sentence: He's always eating and drinking; his monthly money disappears quickly.

mandarin_meaning: （香港俚語）黐膠膠，形容人行為古怪、傻或黏人／黏糊糊，常帶貶義
english_meaning: Hong Kong slang meaning 'clinging/annoyingly clingy', 'crazy' or 'stupid/daft' (pejorative); used to scold or mock someone's behaviour
explanation_mandarin: 「黐𥹉𥹉」是粵語口語俚語，𥹉為膠的變體或次用字，整詞常用來形容人行為黏人、愚蠢或像發神經，語氣多半帶貶義或戲謔。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term (the middle character is a variant glyph often standing for 膠). It describes someone who is clingy, daft, or acting crazy; typically used pejoratively or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日都跟住人，真係黐𥹉𥹉喎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 dou1 gan1 zyu6 jan4, zan1 hai6 ci1 gaau1 gaau1 wo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是跟著人，真的很黐膠膠耶。
examples.english_sentence: You always follow people around — you're really being clingy/daft.

mandarin_meaning: 黑人僧（字面）
english_meaning: Black monk (literal)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思指皮膚較黑的僧侶或以黑色僧袍為特徵的僧人。在廣東話中並非常見的固定詞彙；視語境可能只是描述性用語，也可能帶有種族或戲謔意味，使用時需注意禮貌與敏感性。
explanation_english: Literally 'black monk' — a monk who is Black or characterized by black robes. Not a common fixed Cantonese expression; it may be used descriptively but can be racially sensitive or joking depending on context, so use with care.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 寺廟入面有位黑人僧，佢係來自非洲嘅出家人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zi6 miu6 jap6 min6 jau5 wai2 hak1 jan4 sang1, keoi5 hai6 loi4 zi6 fei1 zau1 ge3 ceot1 gaa1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 寺庙里有一位黑人僧，他是來自非洲的出家人。
examples.english_sentence: There is a Black monk in the temple; he is a monk from Africa.

mandarin_meaning: 人人都討厭 / 很不受歡迎
english_meaning: universally disliked; very unpopular; hated by everyone
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容某人或某事被很多人討厭、不受歡迎。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone or something is disliked by many people or is very unpopular.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講大話，真係黑人憎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6, zan1 hai6 hak1 jan4 zang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是說謊，真是人人都討厭。
examples.english_sentence: He lies all the time; he's really hated by everyone.

mandarin_meaning: 黑巧克力（口語、非標準寫法）
english_meaning: dark chocolate (colloquial/nonstandard)
explanation_mandarin: 口語或非正式寫法，常見於香港粵語中，屬於「黑朱古力／黑巧克力」的簡化或口語化形式。用來指可可含量較高、不太甜的巧克力。
explanation_english: A colloquial/nonstandard Cantonese form referring to dark chocolate (same idea as 黑朱古力 or 黑巧克力). Used in spoken Hong Kong Cantonese to mean chocolate with higher cocoa content and less sweetness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我鍾意食黑古勒，因為佢唔太甜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 ji3 sik6 hak1 gu2 lak6, jan1 wai6 keoi5 m4 taai3 tim4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我喜歡吃黑巧克力，因為它不太甜。
examples.english_sentence: I like eating dark chocolate because it's not too sweet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰盒係黑古勒定係牛奶朱古力？
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 hap6 hai6 hak1 gu2 lak6 ding6 hai6 ngau4 naai5 zyu1 gu2 lik6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那盒是黑巧克力還是牛奶巧克力？
examples.english_sentence: Is that box dark chocolate or milk chocolate?

mandarin_meaning: （用法不明或地區性俚語）字面為「黑＋咪＋麻」，為粵語口語俚語，常用作口語中的感嘆或責備，意指「別耍花招／別搞鬼／不要這樣做」。來源與確切語義於文獻中較少見，屬非正式用語。
english_meaning: (rare/colloquial) Literal reading 'black-mi-ma'. An informal Cantonese slang/interjection often used to scold or admonish—roughly 'don't play tricks / don't be sneaky / stop that'. Usage is regional and not well documented.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感嘆詞／口語俚語（非正式）
explanation_mandarin: 「黑咪麻」為粵語口語俚語，並非書面常用詞。字面上是三個字拼合，實際使用時常帶有責備或驚訝語氣，用於制止對方或表示不滿，例如讓對方不要耍花樣、不要搞鬼或不要再那樣做。由於詞源與確切語義在不同社群可能有所差異，使用時應注意語境與對象。
explanation_english: “黑咪麻” is an informal Cantonese slang phrase and is not commonly found in formal written sources. Literally the three characters read together, but functionally it is used as an admonishing or exclamatory expression—telling someone not to be tricky or to stop messing around. Because it is regional and colloquial, exact nuance can vary by speaker and context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好黑咪麻喇，講清楚啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hak1 mai1 maa4 laa3, gong2 cing1 co2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要黑咪麻了，說清楚一點。
examples.english_sentence: Don't '黑咪麻'—stop messing around; be clearer.

mandarin_meaning: 鬼祟、可疑（口語、俚語，地道用法）
english_meaning: sly/suspicious; acting shady (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「黑咪𠵼」為香港廣東話口語俚語，常用來形容一個人行為鬼祟、可疑或有偷偷摸摸的意味。此詞較口語化，屬地區性用法，書面上不常見。字形中第三字（𠵼）為較少見字，發音與寫法在不同社群中可能有變體。
explanation_english: “黑咪𠵼” is a colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to describe someone acting sly, sneaky, or suspicious. It is informal and regionally used; the third character (𠵼) is rare and the exact written form or pronunciation can vary among speakers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你見唔見到佢啲動作咁鬼祟，真係黑咪𠵼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gin3 m4 gin3 dou2 keoi5 di1 dung6 zok3 gam2 gwai2 seot1, zan1 hai6 hak1 mai1 ngaa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看不見他那些動作這麼鬼祟，真是可疑。
examples.english_sentence: Did you see how sneaky his movements were? He's really acting shady.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁黑咪𠵼啦，有事就講清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 hak1 mai1 ngaa5 laa1, jau5 si6 zau6 gong2 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要這麼鬼祟，如果有事就說清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so sneaky — if there's something up, just say it clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 黑色的沙子；也可特指澳門的黑沙海灘（Hac Sa）
english_meaning: black sand; (can also refer to Macau's Hac Sa / Black Sand Beach)
explanation_mandarin: 指顏色較深的沙粒，通常由火山岩或含鐵礦物形成；在地名上也可指澳門著名的黑沙海灘。
explanation_english: Refers to dark-colored sand, often formed from volcanic rock or iron-rich minerals; as a place name it can refer to Macau's famous Hac Sa (Black Sand) Beach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋去黑沙海灘玩啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 hak1 saa1 hoi2 taan1 waan2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们去黑沙海滩玩吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the Hac Sa (Black Sand) Beach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢度嘅黑沙主要係火山岩磨出嚟，摸落去好粗糙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 ge3 hak1 saa1 zyu2 jiu3 hai6 fo2 saan1 ngaan4 mo4 ceot1 lai4, mo2 lok6 heoi3 hou2 cou1 cou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这里的黑沙主要是火山岩磨出来的，摸起来很粗糙。
examples.english_sentence: The black sand here mainly comes from volcanic rock and feels coarse to the touch.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友喺黑沙度玩沙，家長要睇住佢哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 hai2 hak1 saa1 dou6 waan2 saa1, gaa1 zoeng2 jiu3 tai2 zyu6 keoi5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 孩子们在黑沙里玩沙，家长要看着他们。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are playing in the black sand; parents need to watch them.

mandarin_meaning: 卑鄙、無良或品行惡劣的人（口語罵人用）
english_meaning: scum; a despicable or low-life person (slang, pejorative)
partOfSpeech_english: noun (slang, pejorative) — can be used adjectivally
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語辱罵用語，形容品德低劣、做事卑鄙或對人不義的人，有時也可作形容詞使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang insult meaning a despicable, unscrupulous, or heartless person. Used as a noun and sometimes adjectivally to call someone 'scum' or a 'lowlife.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個人真係黑渣，唔值得信任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 jan4 zan1 hai6 hak1 zaa1, m4 zik1 dak1 seon3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個人真是黑渣，不值得信任。
examples.english_sentence: That person is really scum; not trustworthy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做黑渣啦，對朋友咁衰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 hak1 zaa1 laa3, deoi3 pang4 jau5 gam3 seoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別做黑渣，對朋友這樣壞。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be such a scumbag; don't treat friends so badly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢分手後變得好黑渣，成日玩弄人感情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan1 sau2 hau6 bin3 dak1 hou2 hak1 zaa1, sing4 jat6 waan6 nung6 jan4 gam2 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他分手後變得很黑渣，經常玩弄別人的感情。
examples.english_sentence: After the breakup he became a real scumbag, often playing with people's feelings.

mandarin_meaning: 粗俗的罵人話（類似「混蛋」「討厭的人」）
english_meaning: a coarse Cantonese insult meaning a nasty/unpleasant person (roughly "bastard" / "filthy bastard")
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 骂人词 / 侮辱性用語
explanation_mandarin: 「黑癦屎」是香港粵語中的粗俗罵人用語，用來指稱令人討厭、卑劣或可惡的人，語氣侮辱且帶有強烈情緒，通常用於口語和非正式場合。
explanation_english: “黑癦屎” is a coarse Cantonese slang insult used in Hong Kong to call someone nasty, despicable, or extremely unpleasant. It is vulgar and emotionally charged, used in spoken and informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你真係黑癦屎，成日遲到仲唔知錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 hak1 mong4 si2, seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3 zung6 m4 zi1 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你真是個黑癦屎，成天遲到還不覺得錯。
examples.english_sentence: You're such a black-mole-shit — always late and never admit it's your fault.

mandarin_meaning: 漆黑；一片黑暗（口語）
english_meaning: pitch-dark; very dark (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，形容光線非常暗或者一片黑，看不清楚的狀態，類似「黑漆漆」「漆黑」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese adjective describing something that is extremely dark or pitch-black (hard to see). Similar to '黑漆漆' or 'pitch-dark.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚停電，屋企入面黑窣窣，乜嘢都望唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ting4 din6, uk1 kei2 jap6 min6 hak1 suk1 suk1, mat1 je5 dou1 mong6 m4 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚停电，屋里一片漆黑，什么都看不到。
examples.english_sentence: There was a power cut tonight; the house was pitch-dark and we couldn't see anything.

mandarin_meaning: （魚名）鲩，一種鯉形目的淡水魚，可食用
english_meaning: a species of freshwater carp (huàn/鲩), edible
explanation_mandarin: 「黑鯇」指一種淡水魚，對應普通話的「鲩（鯇）」，常見於內陸河湖，可作食用魚或入饲料。
explanation_english: “黑鯇” refers to a freshwater carp species (Chinese 鲩/鯇). It is commonly found in inland rivers and lakes and is used as food.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條黑鯇好大，可以煲湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 hak1 wun6 hou2 daai6, ho2 ji5 bou1 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這條黑鯇很大，可以用來煲湯。
examples.english_sentence: This black huan is very large; it can be used to make soup.

mandarin_meaning: 漆黑、黑乎乎
english_meaning: very dark; pitch-black; blackish
explanation_mandarin: 表示非常黑暗或颜色很黑，常用来形容环境或物体呈一片黑暗或暗沉的样子。
explanation_english: Describes something that is very dark or black in appearance; often used to describe an environment or object that looks uniformly dark or dim.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚冇燈，條街黑黢黢，乜都睇唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 mou5 dang1, tiu4 gaai1 hak1 kuk1 kuk1, mat1 dou1 tai2 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上没有灯，整条街黑黢黢，什么都看不到。
examples.english_sentence: There were no lights at night; the whole street was pitch-black and you couldn't see anything.

mandarin_meaning: 怎么办 / 該怎麼辦
english_meaning: What to do? / What should (I/we) do?
explanation_mandarin: 用於表達對眼前問題或困境的不知所措，詢問應採取的辦法或表示無奈。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to ask what to do or to express helplessness when facing a problem or dilemma.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我遲到咗，老細會唔會嬲，點算好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ci4 dou3 zo2, lou5 sai3 wui5 m4 wui5 nau1, dim2 syun3 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我迟到了，老板会不会生气，怎么办？
examples.english_sentence: I'm late — will the boss be angry? What should I do?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 計劃變咗，資金又唔夠，點算好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gai3 waak6 bin3 zo2, zi1 gam1 jau6 m4 gau3, dim2 syun3 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 计划变了，资金又不够，怎么办？
examples.english_sentence: The plan changed and we don't have enough funds. What should we do?

mandarin_meaning: 怎么办 (zěnme bàn)
english_meaning: what to do; how to handle (a situation)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 疑问短语 / 动词短语
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示不知道應該如何處理某事或尋求解決辦法，常用於口語。
explanation_english: Used to express not knowing how to handle a situation or to ask for a solution; commonly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔知點辦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zi1 dim2 baan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不知道怎么办。
examples.english_sentence: I don't know what to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果手機壞咗，點辦啊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 sau2 gei1 waai6 zo2, dim2 baan6 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果手机坏了，怎么办？
examples.english_sentence: If the phone breaks, what should we do?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝老闆走咗，啲工作點辦？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 lou5 baan2 zau2 zo2, di1 gung1 zok3 dim2 baan6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天老板走了，这些工作怎么办？
examples.english_sentence: The boss left this morning; what about these tasks?

mandarin_meaning: 發霉的菜；（有時被誤寫或誤用為）梅菜（腌製的芥菜）
english_meaning: moldy vegetable; (sometimes mistakenly used for) mei cai (preserved mustard greens)
explanation_mandarin: 按字面指發黴的蔬菜。注意有時人會錯把「梅菜」（腌製芥菜，常見於菜餚如梅菜扣肉）寫作或說成「黴菜」，但兩者字義不同。
explanation_english: Literally 'moldy vegetable'. Note that some people mistakenly write or say this when referring to '梅菜' (mei cai), the preserved mustard greens used in dishes like braised pork with mei cai; the characters and meanings differ.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲菜發黴咗，已經變咗黴菜，扔咗佢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 coi3 faat3 mui4 zo2, ji5 ging1 bin3 zo2 mui4 coi3, reng1 zo2 keoi5 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些菜發霉了，已經變成發霉的菜，扔掉吧。
examples.english_sentence: These vegetables have gone moldy — they're moldy now, throw them away.

mandarin_meaning: 鼓槌蕉（某種蕉類的俗稱，果形較粗短或末端呈鼓槌狀）
english_meaning: drumstick banana (a common name for certain banana cultivars with a thicker, drumstick-like shape)
explanation_mandarin: 「鼓槌蕉」為對某些蕉類品種的俗稱，果實常較粗短，末端略呈鼓槌狀；此名稱在粵語地區用於指代局部常見的本地蕉種或某些植物學上可辨別的品種。
explanation_english: A colloquial name for certain banana cultivars whose fruits are relatively thick or short and have an end shaped somewhat like a drumstick. Used regionally in Cantonese-speaking areas to refer to local banana varieties.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市有冇人賣鼓槌蕉？我想買幾條嚟整甜品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 jau5 mou5 jan4 maai6 gu2 ceoi4 ziu1? ngo5 soeng2 maai5 gei2 tiu4 lai4 zing2 tim4 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 菜市場有沒有人賣鼓槌蕉？我想買幾根來做甜點。
examples.english_sentence: Is anyone selling drumstick bananas at the market? I want to buy a few to make desserts.

mandarin_meaning: 鼓气囊；（俚）爱吹嘘或满口空话的人
english_meaning: 1) Inflatable bag / air bladder. 2) (slang) A blowhard or someone full of hot air.
explanation_mandarin: 在字面上指可充气的袋子或囊（例如救生衣、气垫等内的气囊）。在口语或俚语中可用来形容常吹嘘、说大话或满口空话的人。
explanation_english: Literally an inflatable bag or air bladder (e.g., in a lifejacket or inflatable device). Informally, used as slang to describe someone who brags a lot or talks big — a blowhard.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 救生衣下面有個鼓氣袋，可以保持浮力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau3 sang1 ji1 haa6 min6 jau5 go3 gu2 hei3 doi2, ho2 ji5 bou2 ci4 fau4 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 救生衣下面有个鼓气囊，可以保持浮力。
examples.english_sentence: There's an air bladder under the life jacket that helps keep you afloat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度講到自己勁，根本係個鼓氣袋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai6 dou6 gong2 dou3 zi6 gei2 ging6, gan1 bun2 hai6 go3 gu2 hei3 doi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天到处吹嘘自己，根本就是个鼓气袋。
examples.english_sentence: He brags all the time; he's basically a blowhard.

mandarin_meaning: 鼠灰 / 鼠灰色 (shǔ huī / shǔ huīsè)
english_meaning: mouse-gray; a dull gray (sometimes grayish-brown) color
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，常用作顏色詞，指像老鼠毛色的灰色，通常偏暗淡或帶灰褐感。常用來形容衣物、汽車、傢俬等的顏色。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese color term (short for 鼠灰色) describing a mouse-like gray — typically a dull gray or grayish-brown. Commonly used to describe clothing, cars, furniture, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件外套係鼠灰色，夠低調。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 ngoi6 tou3 hai6 syu2 fui1 sik1, gau3 dai1 diu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件外套是鼠灰色，够低调。
examples.english_sentence: This coat is mouse-gray, quite low-key.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔鍾意嗰架車嘅顏色，睇落有啲鼠灰，冇精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 go2 gaa3 ce1 ge3 ngaan4 sik1, tai2 lok6 jau5 di1 syu2 fui1, mou5 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不喜欢那辆车的颜色，看起来有点鼠灰、没精神。
examples.english_sentence: I don't like that car's color; it looks a bit mouse-gray and dull.

mandarin_meaning: 占小便宜
english_meaning: to take petty advantage; to grab small freebies
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，形容某人常常佔小便宜、貪取微不足道的好處或免費物品，帶有貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase describing someone who habitually takes petty advantages or helps themselves to small free items; slightly derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鼠牙占，見到免費嘢就忍唔住拎走幾樣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 syu2 ngaa4 zim1, gin3 dou3 min5 fai3 je5 zau6 jan2 m4 zyu6 ling1 zau2 gei2 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是占小便宜，看到免费的东西就忍不住拿走几件。
examples.english_sentence: He always takes petty advantages; when he sees free stuff he can't help taking a few items.

mandarin_meaning: 鼠妖；比喻狡猾、愛偷竊、討人厭或小氣的人（俚語）
english_meaning: Literally 'rat demon'; slang for a sneaky or pesky person — e.g. someone who steals, is petty/stingy, or generally annoying.
explanation_mandarin: 「鼠魔」字面是老鼠的魔怪，廣東話口語中常用作戲稱或辱罵，形容像老鼠般狡猾、偷東西、令人討厭或小氣的人，也可指真實的鼠患情況。
explanation_english: The term literally means 'rat demon'. In Cantonese slang it's used jokingly or as an insult for someone who behaves like a rat — sneaky, a petty thief, stingy, or generally annoying. It can also be used more literally for rats/infestations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你呢個鼠魔又偷我啲零食！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ni1 go3 syu2 mo1 jau6 tau1 ngo5 di1 ling4 sik6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这个鼠魔又偷我的零食！
examples.english_sentence: You rat-demon stole my snacks again!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企有鼠魔喺廚房翻垃圾成晚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 jau5 syu2 mo1 hai2 cyu4 fong2 faan1 laap6 saap3 seng4 maan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家里有老鼠在厨房翻垃圾一整晚。
examples.english_sentence: There's a rat in the kitchen rummaging through the trash all night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢咁小器，真係鼠魔一個。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 gam3 siu2 hei3, zan1 hai6 syu2 mo1 jat1 go3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说话这么小气，真是个鼠魔。
examples.english_sentence: They're so stingy — really a rat demon.

jyutping: bei6 go1 lung4 dou1 mou5 juk6
mandarin_meaning: 骨瘦如柴 / 瘦得連鼻孔都沒有肉
english_meaning: Extremely thin; skin and bones (so thin there's not even flesh around the nostrils)
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話說法，用來形容人非常瘦、消瘦到連鼻孔附近也沒有肉，相當於「骨瘦如柴」或「皮包骨」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is extremely thin or emaciated—'skin and bones,' as if there's not even any flesh around the nostrils.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢病咗成個冬天，瘦到鼻哥窿都冇肉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 beng6 zo2 sing4 go3 dung1 tin1, sou3 dou3 bei6 go1 lung4 dou1 mou5 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他病了整個冬天，瘦到連鼻孔都沒有肉。
examples.english_sentence: He was sick the whole winter and got so thin there's not even any flesh around his nostrils.

mandarin_meaning: 少得可怜/微不足道（只有一点点）
english_meaning: a tiny amount; almost nothing; next to nothing
explanation_mandarin: 「鼻屎咁多」是廣東話口語，用來形容數量非常少、微不足道，字面上是比喻只有像鼻屎那麼一點點。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe a very small amount — essentially 'only a tiny bit' or 'next to nothing'. Literally compares the amount to the size of a booger.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你啲錢得鼻屎咁多，點夠用？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 di1 cin2 dak1 bei6 si2 gam2 do1, dim2 gau3 jung6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你的錢只有一點點，怎麼夠用？
examples.english_sentence: You only have a tiny amount of money — how will that be enough?

mandarin_meaning: 像鼻屎那麼小；微不足道
english_meaning: as tiny as a booger; very small/insignificant
explanation_mandarin: 俗語或俚語，用來比喻某物或某事非常小、微不足道，常帶輕蔑或戲謔語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang simile used to describe something very small or insignificant, often with a dismissive or humorous tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你俾我嗰筆錢淨係得鼻屎咁大，點夠我用？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 bei2 ngo5 go2 bat1 cin2 zing6 hai6 dak1 bei6 si2 gam2 daai6, dim2 gau3 ngo5 jung6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你給我的那筆錢只有鼻屎那麼大，怎麼夠我用？
examples.english_sentence: The money you gave me is only as big as a booger — how is that enough for me?

mandarin_meaning: 鼻塞；鼻子不通氣
english_meaning: stuffy nose; nasal congestion
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語詞，指鼻腔堵塞或呼吸不順，多用來形容感冒或過敏時的鼻子狀況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for a blocked or congested nose, used to describe the nasal condition often caused by a cold or allergies.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝起身成個鼻齆，呼吸唔太順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 hei2 san1 sing4 go3 bei6 ngong6, fu1 kap1 m4 taai3 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上起床鼻子整個塞住，呼吸不太順。
examples.english_sentence: I woke up this morning with a totally stuffy nose; breathing isn't very smooth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天氣轉涼，佢就開始鼻齆，仲流少少鼻水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 hei3 zyun2 leung4, keoi5 zau6 hoi1 ci2 bei6 ngong6, zung6 lau4 siu2 siu2 bei6 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天氣轉冷，他就開始鼻塞，還流一點鼻涕。
examples.english_sentence: When the weather turned cold he started getting a stuffy nose and a little runny nose.

mandarin_meaning: 鼻塞；鼻子不通（方言或口語）；亦可指短而塌的鼻子（少見）
english_meaning: stuffy nose; nasal congestion (colloquial); occasionally a short/snub nose (rare)
explanation_mandarin: 「齆」為一個較少見或方言用字，常用來形容鼻子堵塞、呼吸不暢或因此產生的鼻音，也有地區性用法指鼻子短塌。
explanation_english: 齆 is a less common/colloquial character used to describe a blocked or stuffy nose and related nasal sounds; in some dialectal uses it can refer to a short or snub nose.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家齆住鼻，聞唔到嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 ngong6 zyu6 bei6, man4 m4 dou2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在鼻塞，聞不到東西。
examples.english_sentence: My nose is stuffed right now; I can't smell anything.

mandarin_meaning: 整齐、井然有序（口语、强调）
english_meaning: neat and tidy; neat, well-ordered (colloquial, emphatic)
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示事物排列或收拾得很整齊，有強調語氣，常見於廣東話口語。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that things are arranged or tidied up very neatly. Colloquial Cantonese expression with an emphatic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢將屋企收得齊整整，冇嘢凌亂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoeng1 uk1 kei2 sau1 dak1 cai4 zing2 zing2, mou5 je5 ling4 lyun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他把家裡收得齊整整，沒有亂七八糟的東西。
examples.english_sentence: He/She has tidied the house neatly; there's nothing messy.

mandarin_meaning: （多用於）龍利魚，即巴沙/龍利魚，一種常見的白肉魚（魚片/魚柳）
english_meaning: pangasius / sole (commonly refers to pangasius/basa fillet used in cooking)
explanation_mandarin: 「龍利」常作「龍利魚」或「龍利魚柳」使用，指一種常見的白色魚肉（在超市或餐廳常見，亦稱巴沙魚或標示為龍利魚）。
explanation_english: Often short for 龍利魚 (pangasius/basa) or 龍利魚柳 (fillet). A common white-fleshed fish sold and used in cooking, frequently labeled as sole/pangasius in supermarkets and restaurants.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚買咗條龍利魚，打算煎嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 maai5 zo2 tiu4 lung4 lei6 jyu4, daa2 syun3 zin1 lai4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚买了条龙利鱼，打算煎来吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a pangasius/sole tonight and plan to pan-fry it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐廳有冇龍利魚柳？
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 teng1 jau5 mou5 lung4 lei6 jyu4 lau4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐厅有没有龙利鱼柳？
examples.english_sentence: Does the restaurant have pangasius/sole fillet?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 超市個標籤寫住龍利魚柳（巴沙）。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ciu1 si5 go3 biu1 cim1 se2 zyu6 lung4 lei6 jyu4 lau4 (baa1 saa1).
examples.mandarin_sentence: 超市的标签写着龙利鱼柳（巴沙）。
examples.english_sentence: The supermarket label says pangasius/basa fillet.

mandarin_meaning: （無廣泛記錄的粵語俗稱）地區性或口語用詞，可能用來指某種小豆類或街頭小食（例如花生或豌豆）；亦有可能是某地名產或家族俗稱，具體指向不一，屬俗稱/方言用語。
english_meaning: A regional/colloquial Cantonese term with no widely recorded meaning; likely a local nickname for a small bean or snack (for example, peanuts or peas). It is an informal/slang noun and usage varies by locality.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（俗稱 / 地方口語）
explanation_mandarin: 「龍牙豆」並非標準書面詞彙，在主流詞典中少見。根據口語語境，此詞常作俗稱使用，用來指代某種小型豆類或零食，具體含義會隨地區或說話者而異。遇到此詞時，通常需根據上下文或向說話者確認實際指代。
explanation_english: “龍牙豆” is not a standardized dictionary entry and is rarely recorded in major references. In colloquial use it appears as a regional nickname for a small bean or snack; the exact referent depends on locality and speaker. When encountered, its meaning usually requires contextual clarification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺街市買咗啲龍牙豆，但唔知係咪花生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 si5 maai5 zo2 di1 lung4 ngaa4 dau6, daan6 m4 zi1 hai6 mai6 faa1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在街市買了些「龍牙豆」，但不知道是不是花生。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some "lung ngaa dau" at the market, but I'm not sure if they're peanuts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿嬸話佢屋企有罐龍牙豆，好適合當下酒菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 san1 waa6 keoi5 uk1 kei5 jau5 gun3 lung4 ngaa4 dau6, hou2 sik1 hap6 dong1 haa6 zau2 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿姨說她家裡有罐龍牙豆，很適合當下酒菜。
examples.english_sentence: Auntie said she has a jar of lung ngaa dau at home — perfect as bar snacks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個詞可能係本地俗稱，聽人講對唔同地方代表唔同豆類。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ci4 ho2 nang4 hai6 bun2 dei6 zuk6 cing1, teng1 jan4 gong2 deoi3 m4 tung4 dei6 fong1 doi6 biu2 doi6 m4 tung4 dau6 leoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個詞可能是本地俗稱，聽說在不同地區代表不同的豆類。
examples.english_sentence: This term may be a local colloquialism; I've heard it stands for different kinds of beans in different areas.

mandarin_meaning: 龙目（字面：龙的眼睛；有时被误用为龙眼的俗称）
english_meaning: dragon eye (literal: the eye of a dragon); sometimes (nonstandard) used as a colloquial name for longan
explanation_mandarin: 「龍目」字面意思為「龍的眼睛」，可用來描述龍像或雕刻上的眼睛。有時有人將「龍目」誤用或俗稱為「龍眼」（即桂圓、龍眼果），但這並非標準稱呼，標準詞為「龍眼」。
explanation_english: Literally 'dragon eye' — the eye of a dragon. Used to refer to a dragon's eye in descriptions or carvings. Occasionally people use it colloquially to mean 'longan' (the fruit), but that is nonstandard; the correct term for the fruit is '龍眼' (longan).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廟入面個龍雕上面有一對好生猛嘅龍目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: miu6 jap6 min6 go3 lung4 diu1 soeng6 min6 jau5 jat1 deoi3 hou2 saang1 mang5 ge3 lung4 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 庙里龙雕上面有一对很生猛的龙目。
examples.english_sentence: The dragon sculpture in the temple has a pair of fierce dragon eyes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好用「龍目」去指代「龍眼」，兩者唔係相同嘅字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jung6 'lung4 muk6' heoi3 zi2 doi6 'lung4 ngaan5', loeng5 ze2 m4 hai6 soeng1 tung4 ge3 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要用“龍目”去指代“龍眼”，两者不是相同的字。
examples.english_sentence: Don't use '龍目' to refer to '龍眼'; the two terms aren't the same.

mandarin_meaning: 龙眼（果实），常指干龙眼/桂圆
english_meaning: longan (the fruit), often refers to dried longan (guiyuan) used in soups and desserts
explanation_mandarin: 指龍眼的果實（口語中常稱為龍眼子），常用於煲湯或糖水，民間認為有補血、補身的作用。也可以指乾燥的桂圓（龍眼乾）。
explanation_english: Refers to the longan fruit (colloquially called 'longan zi'), often used in soups and sweet desserts. Commonly the term can refer to the dried form (guiyuan), traditionally believed to be nourishing and blood-replenishing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日買啲龍眼子去煲湯，話可以補血。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 maai5 di1 lung4 ngaan5 zi2 heoi3 bou1 tong1, waa6 ho2 ji5 bou2 hyut3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈经常买龙眼子煲汤，说可以补血。
examples.english_sentence: Mom often buys longans to make soup, saying they can help replenish blood.

mandarin_meaning: 龍眼雞 / 龍眼雞湯（用龍眼乾與雞肉熬製的湯或菜餚）
english_meaning: Longan chicken (chicken cooked with dried longan; often a nourishing soup/dish)
explanation_mandarin: 指用雞肉與龍眼（通常為龍眼乾）一起熬煮成的湯或菜餚。此類湯品在粵式家常菜中常見，被視為滋補、補氣血的食療，常在坐月或冬天飲用。
explanation_english: A dish or soup made by cooking chicken together with longan (usually dried longan). Common in Cantonese home cooking, it is considered nourishing and is often served as a tonic for postpartum care or during colder months.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我整咗一鍋龍眼雞湯，飲落好補身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 zing2 zo2 jat1 wo1 lung4 ngaan5 gai1 tong1, jam2 lok6 hou2 bou2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我煲了一鍋龍眼雞湯，喝了很補身。
examples.english_sentence: I made a pot of longan chicken soup tonight; it's very nourishing to drink.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：龍芽蕉（lóng yá jiāo）。口語上為罕見或地區性粵語俚語，字面無固定標準含義，常用作戲稱某事或某人荒謬、可笑或古怪（使用上帶玩笑或貶義色彩）。
english_meaning: Literal: "dragon-bud banana". A rare/local Cantonese slang term with no fixed literal meaning; used jokingly or disparagingly to describe something or someone absurd, ridiculous, or silly.
explanation_mandarin: 「龍芽蕉」並非標準詞彙，而是一個較為地方性或口語化的用語／俚語。字面上結合了「龍」、「芽」、「蕉」三個字，但實際語用上常用來戲謔或貶稱某事物荒謬、可笑或不合常理。使用時語氣多半帶玩笑或貶義。此詞在不同社群間可能不被普遍理解。
explanation_english: "龍芽蕉" is not a standard lexical item but a regional/colloquial slang expression. Literally combining "dragon," "bud," and "banana," it has no stable literal meaning. In usage it is often employed jokingly or pejoratively to label something or someone as absurd, ridiculous, or nonsensical. It is a rare/local term and may not be widely understood across Cantonese speakers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣講嘢，真係龍芽蕉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 gong2 je5, zan1 hai6 lung4 ngaa4 ziu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣說話，真是荒謬／可笑。
examples.english_sentence: What you said is really absurd/ridiculous.

mandarin_meaning: 龙虎会（指高手、强者聚集或对决的场合；也可作组织或活动的名称）
english_meaning: Literally 'Dragon and Tiger Meeting' — a gathering or showdown of powerful people or formidable opponents; can also be used as a name for organizations/events/works.
explanation_mandarin: 「龍虎會」常用來形容高手雲集或強者相遇、勢均力敵的對決場面；有時也用作會社、比賽或作品的名稱。
explanation_english: The phrase denotes a meeting or clash of strong or outstanding figures — a scene where top people gather or contend. It can also appear as the name of societies, events, or creative works.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚有個龍虎會，唔少高手都會嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jau5 go3 lung4 fu2 wui6, m4 siu2 gou1 sau2 dou1 wui5 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚有个龙虎会，不少高手都会来。
examples.english_sentence: There's a 'Dragon and Tiger Meeting' tonight; many experts will attend.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次拳賽兩位選手打得好激，真係一場龍虎會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 kyun4 coi3 loeng5 wai2 syun2 sau2 daa2 dak1 hou2 gik1, zan1 hai6 jat1 coeng4 lung4 fu2 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次拳赛两位选手打得很激烈，真是一场龙虎会。
examples.english_sentence: This boxing match between the two fighters was very intense — truly a meeting of dragon and tiger (a clash of titans).

mandarin_meaning: 龙凤会（常指婚礼或婚宴，象征男女佳偶相聚、吉祥之意）
english_meaning: Literally "dragon-and-phoenix meeting"; an auspicious term referring to a wedding or wedding banquet, or the union/meeting of a matched couple
explanation_mandarin: 「龍鳳會」以龍代表男、鳳代表女，寓意吉祥和美滿，多用來指婚禮、婚宴或男女配對相聚，也可泛指美滿的一對或喜慶聚會。
explanation_english: The phrase pairs 'dragon' (male) and 'phoenix' (female) to symbolize an auspicious union. It commonly refers to a wedding or wedding banquet, a matched couple, or a celebratory gathering.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋星期六去參加佢哋嘅龍鳳會，大家要準時。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sing1 kei4 luk6 heoi3 caam1 gaa1 keoi5 dei6 ge3 lung4 fung6 wui6, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zeon2 si4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们星期六去参加他们的龙凤会（婚宴），大家要准时。
examples.english_sentence: We're going to attend their dragon-and-phoenix banquet (wedding) on Saturday; everyone should be on time.

mandarin_meaning: 龙凤饼
english_meaning: dragon-and-phoenix cake (traditional wedding pastry)
explanation_mandarin: 一種傳統的喜慶糕點，通常在婚禮或訂婚時作為禮餅分發，餅面常有龍、鳳圖案，象徵男女與夫妻和合、吉祥。
explanation_english: A traditional celebratory pastry often given at weddings or betrothals. The cakes are usually embossed with dragon and phoenix motifs, symbolizing the groom and bride and wishing the couple harmony and good fortune.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日話結婚要準備龍鳳餅，話係傳統嘅禮俗，代表夫妻和合。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 seng4 jat6 waa6 git3 fan1 jiu3 zeon2 bei6 lung4 fung6 beng2, waa6 hai6 cyun4 tung2 ge3 lai5 zuk6, doi6 biu2 fu1 cai1 wo4 hap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽常說結婚要準備龍鳳餅，說是傳統的禮俗，代表夫妻和合。
examples.english_sentence: My mum always says you should prepare dragon-and-phoenix cakes for a wedding; they're a traditional custom symbolizing a harmonious couple.

jyutping: lung4 cong4 bat1 jyu4 gau2 dau6
mandarin_meaning: 高位不一定比低位好；身居高位可能不如過簡樸自在的生活
english_meaning: Being in a high-status position isn't necessarily better than a humble life; high rank can bring more trouble than comfort.
explanation_mandarin: 字面上是說「當龍床（尊貴位置）不如當狗窦（卑微處所）」，用來表達高位未必帶來幸福，反而有可能更辛苦或不自由。
explanation_english: Literally 'a dragon's bed is not as good as a dog's den.' Used to express that high status doesn't always bring happiness or comfort; sometimes humble living is preferable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢雖然係公司嘅老闆，但壓力大到佢覺得龍床不如狗窦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 jin4 hai6 gung1 si1 ge3 lou5 baan2, daan6 aat3 lik6 daai6 dou3 keoi5 gok3 dak1 lung4 cong4 bat1 jyu4 gau2 dau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他雖然是公司的老闆，但壓力太大，他覺得當大老闆還不如做個普通人來得輕鬆。
examples.english_sentence: Although he's the company's boss, the pressure is so great he feels that being a big boss isn't as good as being an ordinary person.

synonyms: 金窝银窝，不如自家草窝

mandarin_meaning: 龍精虎猛（形容精力充沛、精神旺盛）
english_meaning: vigorous and full of energy; energetic and robust
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人精神非常旺盛、精力充沛，常用來稱讚即使年紀較大仍然很有活力的人。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is very vigorous and full of energy; often used to praise a person—sometimes an older person—who remains lively and robust.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢雖然年紀大，但仲係龍精虎猛，成日郁來郁去，做嘢好有精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 jin4 nin4 gei2 daai6, daan6 zung6 hai6 lung4 zing1 fu2 mung5, seng4 jat6 juk1 loi4 juk1 heoi3, zou6 je5 hou2 jau5 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他雖然年紀大，但仍然龍精虎猛，整天動來動去，做事很有精神。
examples.english_sentence: Although he's old, he's still vigorous and active—always moving around and very energetic at work.

jyutping: lung4 zau1 pou4 saat3, seoi2 (seoi1) san4
mandarin_meaning: （口语、讽刺）用来形容某人在水上活动总是倒霉、容易出事，像是带来水上厄运的人。
english_meaning: A colloquial/sarcastic label for someone who is jinxed around water or always causes/encounters mishaps in water-related activities (a 'water jinx').
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的口語說法，帶有戲謔或嘲弄的意味。把常在划船、游水等水上活動中出糗或招致意外的人，戲稱為「龍舟菩薩，水（衰）神」，意指他好像專門帶來水上的霉運。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression, often used teasingly or sarcastically. It mockingly calls someone who repeatedly has accidents or bad luck in boating/swimming activities a 'dragon-boat bodhisattva' or 'water (bad) god' — in other words, a person who brings water-related misfortune.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上次去划艇佢又跌落水，真係龍舟菩薩，水（衰）神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 ci3 heoi3 waak6 teng5 keoi5 jau6 dit3 lok6 seoi2, zan1 hai6 lung4 zau1 pou4 saat3, seoi1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上次去划艇他又掉进水里，真是龙舟菩萨，水（衰）神。
examples.english_sentence: Last time we went rowing he fell into the water again — he's a real 'dragon-boat bodhisattva', a water jinx.

jyutping: lung4 syun4 gwan3, ding2 seoi2 (seoi1) san4
mandarin_meaning: 骂人的口语：指沒用、常惹麻煩或带来霉运的人（“龍船棍”偏向骂人沒用，“頂水（衰）神”指倒霉或带衰的人）。
english_meaning: Colloquial Cantonese insult: describes someone useless or who brings bad luck/trouble ('lung4-syun4-gwan3' = useless/shabby person; 'ding2-seoi2 (seoi1)-san4' = unlucky person/jinx).
explanation_mandarin: 這是香港廣東話的口語或罵人用語，通常用來形容某人既沒用又常常惹事或帶來倒楣。可分為兩部分：“龍船棍”多作貶稱指人無能或可惡，“頂水（衰）神”指總是倒霉或像帶衰的人。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial insult used to describe a person who is useless and/or brings bad luck. The phrase combines two epithets: 'lung4-syun4-gwan3' (an insulting term for a useless or contemptible person) and 'ding2-seoi2 (seoi1)-san4' (someone who is unlucky or acts like a jinx).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係個龍船棍，成日頂水衰神，做乜嘢都出事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 go3 lung4 syun4 gwan3, sing4 jat6 ding2 seoi2 seoi1 san4, zou6 mat1 je5 dou1 ceot1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個龍船棍，總是倒霉，做什麼都會出事。
examples.english_sentence: He's really a 'lung-syun-gwan' — always unlucky/a jinx; everything he does goes wrong.

jyutping: lung4 syun4 zong1 zyu1 si2, jau6 coeng4 jau6 cau3
mandarin_meaning: 形容事情或說話冗長且讓人討厭、無聊
english_meaning: Describes something (a speech, story, event, etc.) that is dragged-out, tedious, and unpleasant/annoying
explanation_mandarin: 廣東俗語，用比喻方式形容某事或講話拖得很長，而且讓人覺得討厭或無趣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used metaphorically to describe something that goes on for too long and is unpleasant or boring.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個故仔聽落好悶，龍船裝豬屎，又長又臭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gu3 zai2 teng1 lok6 hou2 mun6, lung4 syun4 zong1 zyu1 si2, jau6 coeng4 jau6 cau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個故事聽起來很無聊，拖得又長又讓人討厭。
examples.english_sentence: This story sounds really boring — dragged-out and annoying.

jyutping: lung4 syun4 zoeng2, ok3 ceot1 jung2
mandarin_meaning: （口語）怒火湧上；突然大發雷霆（常用作形容某人立刻變得非常生氣）
english_meaning: colloquial expression meaning to suddenly become extremely angry or to erupt with rage
explanation_mandarin: 此短語為口語用法，構成上可分為兩部分：'龙船长'（直譯為龍舟隊長，可作稱呼或具體指人）與'恶出涌'（字面為“惡/怒意湧出/湧現”），合起來常用來描述某人突然間怒氣湧現、大发脾气。此短語在香港粵語或地區性口語中較為隨意、非正式，具情緒強烈的語氣。
explanation_english: This is a colloquial Cantonese expression. It breaks down into '龍船長' (literally 'dragon-boat captain', used as a form of address or reference) and '惡出湧' (literally 'badness/anger wells up'). Together it describes someone suddenly erupting in anger or becoming extremely furious. The phrase is informal and carries strong emotional tone; it is used conversationally rather than in formal writing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到隊友做錯，龍船長即刻惡出湧，對住佢哋發火。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 deoi6 jau5 zou6 co3, lung4 syun4 zoeng2 zik1 hak1 ok3 ceot1 jung2, deoi3 zyu6 keoi5 dei6 faat3 fo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到隊友做錯，龍船長立刻怒火中燒，對著他們發火。
examples.english_sentence: When he saw his teammates make a mistake, the dragon-boat captain immediately became furious and snapped at them.

mandarin_meaning: 未確認／非標準字形
english_meaning: unrecognized / non-standard glyph
explanation_mandarin: 「𠕄丨」並非常見或標準的粵語詞彙或漢字字形，可能是字形錯誤、罕用字或輸入異體。沒有固定讀音或通行釋義。如在文本中遇到，需參照上下文或查考來源判斷。
explanation_english: “𠕄丨” is not a commonly recognized or standard Cantonese word/character glyph. It is likely a corrupted glyph, extremely rare character, or input artifact. There is no established pronunciation or meaning. When encountered, consult context or original source for clarification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺字典見到「𠕄丨」，但唔識點讀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 zi6din2 gin3 dou3 '𠕄丨', daan6 m4 sik1 dim2 duk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在字典看到「𠕄丨」，但不知道怎麼讀。
examples.english_sentence: I saw "𠕄丨" in the dictionary, but I don't know how to read it.

mandarin_meaning: 哪位 / 誰
english_meaning: which person; who (polite)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用字（常見於香港），等同普通話的「哪位」或「誰」，用來詢問是哪一個人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial interrogative meaning 'which person' or 'who'. Common in Hong Kong usage to ask about someone's identity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 𠕄位喺度？
examples.jyutping_sentence: bin1 wai2 hai2 dou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哪位在這裡？
examples.english_sentence: Who is here?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 𠕄位係你嘅朋友？
examples.jyutping_sentence: bin1 wai2 hai6 nei5 ge3 pang4 jau5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哪位是你的朋友？
examples.english_sentence: Which one is your friend?

mandarin_meaning: 凹凹凸凸／凹凸不平（表面高低不平）
english_meaning: bumpy; uneven; full of dents and bumps
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容表面有凹陷和突起、不平整。常用來形容道路、地面或物件表面，有時也可用來形容皮膚或其他不平整的東西。
explanation_english: Colloquial expression describing a surface with dents and bumps—uneven or bumpy. Often used for roads, ground, objects' surfaces, and sometimes skin or other uneven textures.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢段路𠕄𠕄（凹凹）突突，好容易跣親。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dyun6 lou6 aau1 aau1 dat6 dat6, hou2 jung4 ji6 sin2 can1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這段路凹凹凸凸，很容易滑倒。
examples.english_sentence: This stretch of road is bumpy and uneven; it's easy to slip.

mandarin_meaning: 凹（āo）：表面向内凹陷、被撞出凹痕；亦可作动词表示使......凹下
english_meaning: concave; dented; to be dented/to dent
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容词 / 动词 / 名词
explanation_mandarin: 表示物体表面向內凹陷或有凹痕，可用作形容詞描述狀態，也可作動詞表示使物體凹下，或作名詞指凹陷處。
explanation_english: Describes a surface that is concave or dented. Can function as an adjective (concave/dented), a verb (to dent), or a noun (a dent/depression).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 架車個車門畀人撞凹咗，仲要拎去修理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaa3 ce1 go3 ce1 mun4 bei2 jan4 zong6 aau1 zo2, zung6 jiu3 ling6 heoi3 sau1 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 车门被人撞凹了，还要拿去修理。
examples.english_sentence: The car door got dented and needs to be taken for repair.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個碗底係凹嘅，未必穩陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 wun2 dai2 hai6 aau1 ge3, mei6 bat1 wan2 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个碗底是凹的，可能不稳。
examples.english_sentence: The bottom of this bowl is concave; it might be unstable.

mandarin_meaning: 討厭/令人煩惱的人或事；（口語、貶義）笨蛋、搞事的人
english_meaning: an annoying or troublesome person/thing; (colloquial, derogatory) a fool or someone who causes trouble
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語／俚語，名詞或感嘆詞
explanation_mandarin: 「𠝹嘢」是廣東話口語俚語，用來形容令人討厭、麻煩或愚蠢的人或事。有時用作罵人的短語，語氣可輕鬆或較粗魯，視語境而定。
explanation_english: “𠝹嘢” is Cantonese slang used to describe an annoying, troublesome, or foolish person/thing. It can be used as an insult or a dismissive remark; tone and context determine how strong it sounds.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做𠝹嘢啦，大家都唔想理你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 laap6 je5 laa1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 soeng2 lei5 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別做蠢事了，大家都不想理你。
examples.english_sentence: Stop acting like an idiot, nobody wants to deal with you.

mandarin_meaning: 割、切、扣減（口語）
english_meaning: to cut/slice; to split/divide; to deduct (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 這是一個廣東話的俗語或口語用字，常用來表示用利器切割、把東西分開，或在金錢/份額上扣減、分攤。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb used to indicate cutting or slicing with a sharp tool, splitting/dividing something, or deducting/sharing an amount (e.g., money or portions).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用刀𠝹咗條布。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 dou1 gaai1 zo2 tiu4 bou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他用刀把布割了。
examples.english_sentence: He used a knife to cut the cloth.

mandarin_meaning: 抓拿；逮捕
english_meaning: to seize; to arrest; to grab (forcefully)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語/口語，用來表示用武力或強制手段把人或物拿走、抓住或逮捕，常見於口語或網絡用語中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to seize, grab or arrest someone or something, often implying force or coercion; used in spoken Cantonese and online.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警察𠬪拏咗個小偷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 caat3 laap6 naa4 zo2 go3 siu2 tau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警察抓住了小偷。
examples.english_sentence: The police seized/arrested the thief.

mandarin_meaning: 畏缩
english_meaning: to cower; to shrink back; to be timid or reluctant
explanation_mandarin: 表示因害怕或膽怯而退縮、不敢面對或採取行動的狀態或行為。常用於口語，用作形容人遇到困難或危險時退避不前。
explanation_english: Indicates shrinking back or cowering out of fear or timidity; used to describe someone who hesitates or retreats when facing difficulty or danger. Commonly used in colloquial Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到狗就𠵇縮，唔敢郁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou2 gau2 zau6 wai6 suk1, m4 gam2 juk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到狗就畏缩，不敢动。
examples.english_sentence: He sees dogs and cowers, not daring to move.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 遇到困難唔好𠵇縮，要諗辦法解決。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu6 dou3 kwan3 naan4 m4 hou2 wai6 suk1, jiu3 nam2 baan6 faat3 gaai2 kyut3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 遇到困难不要畏缩，要想办法解决。
examples.english_sentence: Don't shrink back from problems; think of ways to solve them.

mandarin_meaning: 噎到喉嚨；哽住
english_meaning: to choke (on something); to have a lump in the throat; to be choked up
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指因食物或情緒而感到喉嚨被噎住或哽塞，可能導致咳嗽或聲音哽咽。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term meaning to choke (physically) or to feel a lump in the throat (emotionally), causing coughing or a choked voice.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我食嘢嗰陣𠵴喉，差啲嗆親。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik6 je5 go2 zan6 jit6 hau4, caa1 di1 hoeng3 can1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我吃東西的時候噎到，差點嗆到。
examples.english_sentence: I choked while eating and was almost choked.

mandarin_meaning: 可恶 / 该死（口语、粤语粗口）
english_meaning: damn; damn it; (vulgar/slang exclamation to express anger, annoyance or frustration)
explanation_mandarin: 「𠵼旗」是粤语口语俚语/粗口，用作感叹或咒骂，表示生气、懊恼或不满。语气强烈，常见于非正式场合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/vulgar interjection used to express anger, annoyance, or frustration. Strong colloquial language—used informally and can be offensive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 𠵼旗，你又遲到，做咩搞到成晚？
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 kei4, nei5 jau6 ci4 dou3, zou6 me1 gaau2 dou3 seng4 maan5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可恶，你又迟到了，怎么搞得这么晚？
examples.english_sentence: Damn, you're late again — why did it take you so long?

mandarin_meaning: 百分之 / 百分比（表示百分率）
english_meaning: percent / percentage
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（表示百分比的量詞／名詞）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語中從英語 percent 借來的表達，常寫作「巴仙」，用來表示百分比（即“%”）。例如「九十巴仙」即百分之九十。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial loanword from English "percent," commonly written as "巴仙" and used to indicate a percentage (i.e. "%"). For example, "九十巴仙" means 90 percent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份報告已經完成咗九十巴仙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 ji5 ging1 wan4 sing4 zo2 gau2 sap6 baa1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份報告已經完成了百分之九十。
examples.english_sentence: This report is 90 percent complete.

mandarin_meaning: 那个（口語）
english_meaning: that; that one (colloquial/filler)
explanation_mandarin: 「𠺪個」是廣東話口語中常用的指示代詞，等同於書寫或標準粵語的「嗰個」，用來指稱某事物或某人，有時也作語氣填充詞使用。
explanation_english: “𠺪個” is a colloquial Cantonese demonstrative equivalent to standard 嗰個 (go2 go3). It means “that” or “that one” and can also be used as a filler or discourse marker in casual speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 𠺪個人好唔守時。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 jan4 hou2 m4 sau2 si4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个人很不守时。
examples.english_sentence: That person is very unpunctual.

mandarin_meaning: 寄居
english_meaning: to lodge temporarily; to reside temporarily
explanation_mandarin: 表示暫時寄住在別人家或某處，不是長期定居。可作動詞使用。
explanation_english: Refers to staying temporarily at someone else's place or at a location rather than living there permanently. Used as a verb.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家𠺪居喺朋友屋企，未有地方自己住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 gei3 geoi1 hai2 pang4 jau5 uk1 kei2, mei6 jau5 dei6 fong1 zi6 gei2 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在寄居在朋友家，還沒有自己的住處。
examples.english_sentence: He is currently lodging at a friend's place; he doesn't have his own place to live yet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好多流浪動物都會𠺪居喺動物收容所度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 do1 lau4 long4 dung6 mat6 dou1 wui5 gei3 geoi1 hai2 dung6 mat6 sau1 jung4 so2 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 許多流浪動物會寄居在動物收容所。
examples.english_sentence: Many stray animals take up temporary residence in animal shelters.

mandarin_meaning: 你以為自己很了不起（諷刺用）
english_meaning: You think you're so clever / You're acting all clever (sarcastic)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俚語，帶有諷刺或嘲弄意味，用來指責或嘲笑對方自以為聰明、了不起。此詞含有方言字形，書面語少見，讀音與用法在不同地區可能有變體。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang/interjection used sarcastically to mock someone who thinks they're clever or impressive. The phrase uses rare/variant characters and is mainly spoken; pronunciation and form can vary regionally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 𠽤叻𡃈嘞，你以為自己做晒啲嘢就好叻咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: si6 lek1 gaai1 laak3, nei5 ji5 wai6 zi6 gei2 zou6 saai3 di1 je5 zau6 hou2 lek1 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以為自己做了很多事就很了不起嗎？
examples.english_sentence: You think you're so clever — do you really believe doing a few things makes you that great?

mandarin_meaning: 露馬腳
english_meaning: to give oneself away; to be exposed; to reveal a tell
explanation_mandarin: 比喻暴露破綻或真實身份、意圖，被人看穿或揭穿。
explanation_english: A metaphor meaning to expose a flaw, clue, or one's true identity/intentions — to be found out or to give oneself away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰啲藉口聽落唔可信，結果終於𠽤馬腳，真相被揭穿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 di1 zek3 hau2 teng1 lok3 m4 ho2 seon3, git3 gwo2 zung1 jyu1 lou6 maa5 goek3, zan1 soeng6 bei6 kit3 cyun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那些藉口聽起來不可信，結果終於露馬腳，真相被揭穿。
examples.english_sentence: His excuses sounded unconvincing, and in the end he gave himself away; the truth was exposed.

mandarin_meaning: 傻瓜／笨蛋；愚蠢的事或人（貶義、俚語）
english_meaning: idiot / stupid person; something stupid (slang, pejorative)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞 / 形容詞（俚語、貶義）
explanation_mandarin: 「𡃁嘢」是廣東話粗俗的口語用詞，用來罵人笨或形容某件事很愚蠢。帶有貶義，多見於口語或非正式場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar slang term used to call someone an idiot or to describe something as stupid. It is pejorative and typically used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你呢個𡃁嘢，做乜嘢咁蠢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ni1 go3 ngong6 je5, zou6 mat1 je5 gam2 cung2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這個笨蛋，為什麼這麼蠢？
examples.english_sentence: You idiot — why are you so stupid?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做𡃁嘢，諗清楚先好決定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 ngong6 je5, nam2 cing1 co2 sin1 hou2 kyut3 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別做傻事，先想清楚再決定。
examples.english_sentence: Don't do something stupid; think it through before deciding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好𡃁嘢，成日搞錯嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 ngong6 je5, sing4 jat6 gaau2 co3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很笨，經常弄錯東西。
examples.english_sentence: He's really clumsy/stupid at work; he always makes mistakes.

mandarin_meaning: 那家伙；那傢伙
english_meaning: that guy / that fellow (often colloquial, can be derogatory or playful)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來指代某個人，常帶輕蔑、抱怨或戲謔的語氣。此字形（𡃇）為口語書寫時出現的變體，常見同義詞為「嗰家伙/那家伙」。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression used to refer to someone (that guy/fellow). It often carries a slightly derogatory, complaining, or teasing tone. The character 𡃇 is a variant used in informal Cantonese writing; equivalent to 嗰/那.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 𡃇家伙又遲到喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaa1 fo2 jau6 ci4 dou3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那家伙又迟到了。
examples.english_sentence: That guy is late again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好理𡃇家伙，佢淨係識鬧人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lei5 go2 gaa1 fo2, keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 nau6 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別理那家伙，他只會罵人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't bother with that guy; he only knows how to pick fights/insult people.

jyutping: ngong6 ngong6 dou1 mou5 gam2 ngong6
mandarin_meaning: 笨到極點；愚蠢得不像話
english_meaning: extremely stupid; unbelievably foolish
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，用來強調某人或某事非常愚蠢，帶有貶義和誇張成分，常在廣東話日常對話中使用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to emphasize that someone or something is extremely foolish. It's derogatory and emphatic, commonly used in everyday spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢連最簡單嘅數學題都答錯，𡃇𡃇都冇咁𡃇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lin4 zeoi3 gaan1 daan1 ge3 sou3 hok6 tai4 dou1 daap3 co3, ngong6 ngong6 dou1 mou5 gam2 ngong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他連最簡單的數學題都答錯，笨到極點。
examples.english_sentence: He even got the simplest math problem wrong — unbelievably stupid.

mandarin_meaning: 低聲嘀咕／小聲抱怨
english_meaning: to mutter or grumble quietly; a soft, indistinct muttering sound
explanation_mandarin: 「𡄴𡄴聲」是廣東話的擬聲或俗語，用來形容小聲嘀咕、含糊地說話或悄悄抱怨的聲音或行為。
explanation_english: A Cantonese onomatopoeic/slang expression describing low, indistinct muttering or quiet grumbling; used for someone speaking under their breath or complaining softly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日𡄴𡄴聲唔講清楚，令人好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hap6 hap6 seng1 m4 gong2 cing1 co2, ling6 jan4 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是低聲嘀咕、不說清楚，讓人很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always mumbles under his breath and doesn't speak clearly, which is really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到廚房裡𡄴𡄴聲，好似有人唔滿意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 dou3 cyu4 fong1 leoi5 hap6 hap6 seng1, ho2 ci5 jau5 jan4 m4 mun5 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到廚房裡有低聲嘀咕，好像有人不滿意。
examples.english_sentence: I heard muttering in the kitchen; it sounded like someone was dissatisfied.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳／罕見粵語俗語（含義不確定）
english_meaning: Obscure Cantonese slang; meaning uncertain/not well documented
explanation_mandarin: 「𡄵牙𠾴哨」為罕見或方言性的粵語詞彙／俗語。現有資料不足以確定其標準讀音、詞性與確切含義，可能爲地方口語或古老用語，使用範圍極小或已不常見。
explanation_english: “𡄵牙𠾴哨” appears to be an obscure or dialectal Cantonese term/slang. There is insufficient documentation to determine its standard pronunciation, part of speech, or exact meaning. It may be a local colloquial or archaic expression with very limited or obsolete usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你聽過「𡄵牙𠾴哨」未？我從來未聽過呢個詞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 teng1 gwo3 '𡄵牙𠾴哨' mei6? ngo5 cung4 loi4 mei6 teng1 gwo3 ni1 go3 ci4. （註：詞中漢字之讀音不詳）
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你聽過「𡄵牙𠾴哨」嗎？我從來沒聽過這個詞。
examples.english_sentence: Have you heard of "𡄵牙𠾴哨"? I've never heard this term before.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）嚇呆、驚訝不知所措
english_meaning: slang for being shocked/stunned and momentarily at a loss
explanation_mandarin: 一個廣東話俚語，用來形容突然受驚、愣住或一時不知道怎麼反應的狀態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to describe being suddenly startled or stunned, momentarily not knowing how to react.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到個消息我𡗗乍咗，一時唔知點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 dou3 go3 siu1si6 ngo5 ngaap6-zaa3 zo2, jat1 si4 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到那個消息我嚇呆了，一時不知道怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: When I heard the news I was stunned; for a moment I didn't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 弄糟；搞砸
english_meaning: to mess up; to screw up; to ruin
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俚語，表示把事情弄壞或搞砸了（常指因粗心或失誤導致失敗）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to mess something up or to ruin something, often through carelessness or a mistake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做𡯨掉咗份報告，老細好唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 ngaak6 diu6 zo2 fan6 bou3 gou3, lou5 sai3 hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你把報告弄糟了，老闆很不高興。
examples.english_sentence: You messed up the report; the boss is very unhappy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再𡯨掉啲嘢，慢慢嚟就得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 ngaak6 diu6 di1 je5, maan6 maan6 lai4 zau6 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再把東西弄壞了，慢慢來就可以了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep ruining things; take your time and it'll be fine.

mandarin_meaning: 受庇护／被人罩着（受到保护或照顾）
english_meaning: to be under someone's protection or patronage; to be covered/looked after (often implying special favour or being coddled)
explanation_mandarin: 「𢆡罩」是廣東話俗語，指某人被有權勢或有關係的人保護、照顧或偏袒，做事較有後台，不需太擔心後果。有時帶有貶義，暗示不公平的優待或被寵着。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquialism means to be under someone's protection or patronage — to have a backer who shields or favours you. It often implies having special treatment or being coddled, sometimes with a negative connotation of unfair advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢有老細𢆡罩，做乜都唔會有咩事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau5 lou5 sai3 ngaap3 zaau3, zou6 mat1 dou1 m4 wui5 jau5 me1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他有老闆罩著，做什麼都不會有事。
examples.english_sentence: He has the boss's protection; he won't get into trouble no matter what he does.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個藝員有富商𢆡罩，拍戲工資高兼有資源。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ngai6 jyun4 jau5 fu3 soeng1 ngaap3 zaau3, paak3 hei3 gung1 zi1 gou1 gim3 jau5 zi1 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個藝人有富商罩著，拍戲工資高且有資源。
examples.english_sentence: This performer is backed by a wealthy patron, so they get high pay and opportunities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係靠𢆡罩，自己先要努力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 kaau3 ngaap3 zaau3, zi6 gei2 sin1 jiu3 nou5 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只靠被罩著，自己先要努力。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just rely on being under someone's protection — you need to work hard yourself first.

mandarin_meaning: 傻瓜、笨蛋（俚語）
english_meaning: silly person; idiot (slang, jocular/derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「𢭃欏柚」是一個廣東話的俚語，用來稱呼或戲稱某人笨拙、做事不靈光或傻乎乎。語氣可依語境變得較為親暱或帶貶義。
explanation_english: “𢭃欏柚” is a Cantonese slang term used to call someone silly or foolish — a jocular or mildly derogatory way to refer to someone acting dumb or clumsy. Tone depends on context; can be teasing or insulting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今朝連鑰匙都唔記得攞，真係𢭃欏柚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 ziu1 lin4 joek3 si2 dou1 m4 gei3 dak1 lo2, zan1 hai6 ngak3 laa1 jau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天早上連鑰匙都忘了，真是個傻瓜。
examples.english_sentence: You forgot your keys this morning — what a silly person.

mandarin_meaning: 耍脾氣；發脾氣；鬧情緒
english_meaning: to sulk; to be in a huff; to throw a tantrum (petty/moodiness)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容人因不滿或不如意而表現出嬌嗔、鬧情緒或故意耍脾氣的行為或態度。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who sulks, acts moody, or throws a petty tantrum when displeased or dissatisfied.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢又𢯎氣喇，唔知點解。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau6 ngaai3 hei3 laa3, m4 zi1 dim2 gaai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他又在耍脾氣了，不知道為什麼。
examples.english_sentence: He's sulking again; I don't know why.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好𢯎氣啦，我哋傾下解決辦法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 ngaai3 hei3 laa1, ngo5 dei6 king1 haa5 gaai2 kyut3 baan6 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別耍脾氣了，我們談談解決辦法。
examples.english_sentence: Don't sulk; let's talk about how to solve it.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見或未確認的粵語詞彙，沒有可靠記錄或現代用法
english_meaning: Rare or unverified Cantonese term; no reliable attestation or modern usage found
explanation_mandarin: 經查詢主要粵語詞典、語料庫和公開網路資源後，未能找到「𢱕拾拾」的可靠詞條、讀音或確切意義。此詞可能為方言變體、書寫/抄錄錯誤、罕見俗語或已失傳詞彙。故暫無法提供準確的讀音、詞性或自然例句。
explanation_english: A search of major Cantonese dictionaries, corpora, and public internet resources did not yield a reliable entry, pronunciation, or clear meaning for "𢱕拾拾". It may be a dialectal variant, a transcription/printing error, an extremely rare slang term, or an obsolete word.
